buy
buying
explanation: Cấu trúc “need + to V” diễn tả cần làm gì. Vì vậy: You need to buy new shoes.

question_text: If I were you, I ____ apologise.
options: will
would
can
explanation: Đây là mẫu lời khuyên giả định: “If I were you, I would...”. Dùng “would” vì đây là điều kiện loại 2.

question_text: We’re ____ in a beautiful holiday home at the moment.
options: stay
staying
stayed
explanation: “At the moment” cho thấy hành động đang diễn ra ở hiện tại. Với “we’re”, ta cần V-ing để tạo hiện tại tiếp diễn: “we’re staying”.

question_text: The shop ____ at 9 a.m. every day.
options: opens
is opening
opened
explanation: “Every day” diễn tả thói quen hoặc lịch cố định, nên dùng hiện tại đơn. Chủ ngữ “the shop” là số ít nên động từ thêm -s: “opens”.

question_text: If you heat water to 100°C, it ____.
options: boils
will boil
boiled
explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 0: If + present simple, present simple. Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

question_text: You look tired. You ____ take a break.
options: should
mustn't
needn't
explanation: Câu này đưa ra lời khuyên vì người nghe trông mệt. “Should” nghĩa là nên. “Mustn’t” là cấm, còn “needn’t” là không cần.

question_text: You ____ smoke in the hospital.
options: mustn't
don't have to
needn't
explanation: Trong bệnh viện, hút thuốc là điều bị cấm. “Mustn’t” diễn tả sự cấm đoán mạnh. “Don’t have to/needn’t” nghĩa là không cần, sai nghĩa.

question_text: The cake tastes ____ delicious.
options: very
many
much
explanation: “Delicious” là tính từ, nên dùng trạng từ “very” để bổ nghĩa: very delicious. “Many” dùng với danh từ đếm được số nhiều, “much” thường dùng với danh từ không đếm được hoặc so sánh.

question_text: The phone rang while I ____ dinner.
options: cooked
was cooking
cook
explanation: Một hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ thì hành động khác xen vào. “While I was cooking dinner” diễn tả việc tôi đang nấu ăn khi điện thoại reo.

question_text: When I got home, Jenny ____ on the telephone.
options: was speaking
speaking
speak
explanation: Một hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ khi hành động khác xen vào. “When I got home” là hành động xen vào, còn Jenny đang nói điện thoại nên dùng “was speaking”.

question_text: When I was at school I used ____ a good student.
options: to be
be
being
explanation: Cấu trúc diễn tả trạng thái/thói quen trong quá khứ là “used to + V”. Vì vậy dùng “to be”.

question_text: My brother is not as tall ____ me.
options: than
as
from
explanation: So sánh ngang bằng phủ định: not as tall as me.

question_text: He asked me if I ____ help him.
options: can
could
will
explanation: Đây là câu tường thuật. Khi chuyển từ lời nói trực tiếp sang gián tiếp, “can” thường lùi thành “could”: He asked me if I could help him.

question_text: The letters ____ every morning.
options: deliver
are delivered
delivered
explanation: Chủ ngữ “the letters” là vật nhận hành động, nên dùng bị động. “Every morning” chỉ thói quen, nên dùng bị động hiện tại đơn: “are delivered”.

question_text: Coffee ____ to be much cheaper a few years ago.
options: would
has
used
explanation: “Used to be” diễn tả một trạng thái trong quá khứ nhưng hiện tại không còn như vậy. Câu nghĩa là cà phê trước đây từng rẻ hơn nhiều.

question_text: She told me she ____ busy that day.
options: is
has been
was
explanation: Câu tường thuật lùi thì: is busy thành was busy.

question_text: They had finished dinner before I ____.
options: arrive
arrived
had arrived
explanation: “Had finished” diễn tả hành động đã xong trước một hành động quá khứ khác. Hành động đến sau dùng quá khứ đơn: before I arrived.

question_text: I’ve got no plans for the weekend. Maybe ____ visit my parents.
options: I
I’m
I’ll
explanation: “Maybe I’ll...” diễn tả một dự định chưa chắc chắn hoặc quyết định có thể xảy ra trong tương lai.

question_text: He denied ____ the window.
options: break
to break
breaking
explanation: Sau động từ “deny” dùng V-ing: deny doing something. Vì vậy câu đúng là “He denied breaking the window”.

question_text: It was ____ a nice day that we went swimming.
options: so
such
too
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “such + a/an + adjective + noun + that”: such a nice day that... “So” đi với tính từ/trạng từ, ví dụ “so nice that...”.

question_text: I wish I ____ more free time.
options: have
had
will have
explanation: Câu ước về hiện tại dùng dạng quá khứ: “I wish + S + V quá khứ”. Vì vậy dùng “had”, nghĩa là ước hiện tại có nhiều thời gian rảnh hơn.

question_text: They need someone ____ can work at weekends.
options: which
who
where
explanation: Someone chỉ người nên dùng who.

question_text: I’m not sure about my future. ____ I will start a business.
options: Perhaps
Shall
Might
explanation: “Perhaps” là trạng từ nghĩa là có lẽ, hợp với ý không chắc chắn. “Might” nếu dùng thì phải là “I might start...”, không đi với “I will” như câu này.

question_text: I'm thinking ____ moving to a bigger flat.
options: of
at
with
explanation: Cụm đúng là “think of + V-ing”, nghĩa là nghĩ đến việc làm gì. Vì vậy câu đúng là “I’m thinking of moving...”.

question_text: The museum ____ opened in 1998.
options: is
was
has
explanation: Câu có mốc quá khứ “in 1998” và nghĩa bị động: bảo tàng được mở cửa/khánh thành. Vì vậy dùng “was opened”.

question_text: The report ____ by the manager yesterday.
options: was checked
checked
is checking
explanation: Chủ ngữ “the report” nhận hành động kiểm tra, nên dùng bị động. Có “yesterday” nên dùng bị động quá khứ: “was checked”.

question_text: There were only ____ people at the meeting.
options: a few
much
any
explanation: “People” là danh từ đếm được số nhiều, nên dùng “a few”. “Much” dùng cho danh từ không đếm được.

question_text: I’m reading a really ____ book on the history of Europe.
options: interest
interesting
interested
explanation: “Book” là vật gây hứng thú nên dùng tính từ “interesting”. “Interested” dùng cho người cảm thấy hứng thú.

question_text: Neither Tom nor his friends ____ coming to the party.
options: is
are
be
explanation: Với “neither...nor...”, động từ thường chia theo chủ ngữ gần nhất. Chủ ngữ gần nhất là “his friends” số nhiều, nên dùng “are”.

question_text: He’s about 40, but in this photograph he looks much ____ .
options: young
younger
youngest
explanation: “Much” thường dùng để nhấn mạnh so sánh hơn. Vì vậy cần “younger”: trông trẻ hơn nhiều.

question_text: If I ____ enough money, I would travel more.
options: have
had
will have
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 2, diễn tả giả định không có thật hoặc khó xảy ra ở hiện tại. Cấu trúc: If + S + V quá khứ, S + would + V. Vì vậy dùng “had”.

question_text: I'd like ____ cup of tea, please.
options: a
an
explanation: A cup of tea là cách nói đúng: một tách trà.

question_text: I'm afraid I have ____ money left.
options: little
few
many
explanation: “Money” là danh từ không đếm được, nên dùng “little”. “Few” và “many” dùng với danh từ đếm được số nhiều.

question_text: A: Where is Lisa? B: She ____ be in her room; the light is on.
options: must
can't
needn't
explanation: Người nói suy luận chắc chắn Lisa ở trong phòng vì đèn đang bật. Dùng “must be” để diễn tả suy đoán chắc chắn.

question_text: They ate their lunch while they ____ coming home from school.
options: were
was
are
explanation: Chủ ngữ “they” đi với “were”. Cấu trúc quá khứ tiếp diễn “were coming” diễn tả hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ.

question_text: She bought it herself, ____ she?
options: hasn’t
didn’t
shouldn’t
explanation: Đây là câu hỏi đuôi. Mệnh đề chính là quá khứ đơn khẳng định “She bought...”, nên đuôi phải là phủ định với “did”: “didn’t she?”.

question_text: They decided ____ a new flat.
options: buy
buying
to buy
explanation: Sau “decide” dùng “to V”: decide to do something. Vì vậy câu đúng là “They decided to buy a new flat”.

question_text: She works ____ than her brother.
options: careful
more carefully
most carefully
explanation: “Works” cần trạng từ bổ nghĩa, và có “than” nên dùng so sánh hơn. Với trạng từ dài “carefully”, dạng đúng là “more carefully”.

question_text: She has ____ two books.
options: written
wrote
write
explanation: Sau “has” trong hiện tại hoàn thành cần quá khứ phân từ. Động từ “write” có V3 là “written”.

question_text: I haven't seen him ____ Monday.
options: for
since
at
explanation: “Monday” là một mốc thời gian, nên dùng “since”. Câu nghĩa là tôi đã không gặp anh ấy từ thứ Hai.

question_text: We were surprised ____ the news.
options: at
on
in
explanation: Cụm đúng là surprised at the news.

question_text: The room ____ cleaned before the guests arrived.
options: had been
has been
is being
explanation: Việc căn phòng được dọn xảy ra trước một mốc quá khứ khác: “before the guests arrived”. Vì vậy dùng quá khứ hoàn thành bị động: “had been cleaned”.

question_text: Do you know how long ____?
options: the film is
is the film
does the film
explanation: Đây là câu hỏi gián tiếp sau “Do you know”. Trong câu hỏi gián tiếp, dùng trật tự khẳng định: “how long the film is”, không đảo trợ động từ.

question_text: They asked us ____ late.
options: not to be
don't be
not be
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “ask someone not to do something”. Vì vậy: They asked us not to be late.

question_text: I don’t recommend driving in the morning because there’s too ____ traffic.
options: much
many
most
explanation: “Traffic” là danh từ không đếm được, nên dùng “too much traffic”. “Many” dùng với danh từ đếm được số nhiều.

question_text: Have you finished ____ the report?
options: write
writing
to write
explanation: Finish + V-ing, nên dùng finished writing.

question_text: If the dress ____ been so expensive, she would have bought it.
options: hadn’t
weren’t
aren’t
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 3: If + had not + V3, would have + V3. Vì vậy dùng “hadn’t been”.

question_text: She asked me where I ____.
options: live
lived
do live
explanation: Đây là câu tường thuật. Câu hỏi “Where do you live?” chuyển thành “where I lived”, dùng trật tự khẳng định và lùi thì.

question_text: She is afraid ____ spiders.
options: about
of
with
explanation: Cụm tính từ đúng là “afraid of”, nghĩa là sợ điều gì. Vì vậy: She is afraid of spiders.

question_text: The students ____ by the teacher now.
options: are being helped
helped
have helped
explanation: Bị động hiện tại tiếp diễn với now: are being helped.

question_text: I never do my homework ____ I hate studying at home.
options: so
because
although
explanation: Vế sau đưa ra lý do cho việc không làm bài ở nhà, nên dùng “because”.

question_text: I'm used to ____ early every day.
options: get up
getting up
got up
explanation: “Be used to + V-ing” nghĩa là quen với việc gì. Vì vậy dùng “getting up”, không dùng động từ nguyên thể.

question_text: The restaurant ____ we had lunch was very cheap.
options: who
where
which
explanation: “Restaurant” là nơi chốn, và mệnh đề sau diễn tả nơi chúng tôi ăn trưa, nên dùng “where”.

question_text: He promised ____ late again.
options: not being
not to be
don't be
explanation: Sau “promise” dùng “to V”. Dạng phủ định là “promise not to V”, nên câu đúng là “promised not to be late again”.

question_text: I ____ a great book this morning – I really want to finish it.
options: was reading
read
have read
explanation: Người nói muốn nhấn mạnh việc đang đọc dở cuốn sách vào sáng nay và hiện vẫn muốn đọc tiếp để hoàn thành. Vì vậy “was reading” phù hợp hơn “read” hoặc “have read”, vì “have read” thường gợi ý đã đọc xong.

question_text: I'll let you know when I ____ the answer.
options: find
will find
found
explanation: Sau “when” trong mệnh đề chỉ thời gian nói về tương lai, ta dùng hiện tại đơn, không dùng “will”. Câu đúng: when I find the answer.

question_text: It's the first time I ____ sushi.
options: try
tried
have tried
explanation: Với cấu trúc “It’s the first time...”, ta thường dùng hiện tại hoàn thành để nói về trải nghiệm đầu tiên: “I have tried”.

question_text: He has lived in this town ____ 2018.
options: for
since
during
explanation: Mốc thời gian 2018 dùng since. For dùng với khoảng thời gian.

question_text: I wish I ____ speak French fluently.
options: can
could
will
explanation: Câu ước về hiện tại dùng dạng quá khứ. Với khả năng, “can” chuyển thành “could”: I wish I could speak French fluently.

question_text: They’re so different. I ____ , there’s no way they’ll be happy together.
options: mean
decide
wish
explanation: “I mean” là cụm giao tiếp dùng để giải thích/nhấn mạnh ý vừa nói. Ở đây người nói giải thích rằng họ quá khác nhau nên khó hạnh phúc.

question_text: I'd rather ____ at home tonight.
options: stay
to stay
staying
explanation: Sau “would rather” dùng động từ nguyên thể không “to”: I’d rather stay. Nghĩa là tôi thích ở nhà hơn tối nay.

question_text: He didn't go to school ____ he was ill.
options: because
although
despite
explanation: Vế sau đưa ra lý do: anh ấy không đi học vì bị ốm. “Because” + mệnh đề là cấu trúc đúng. “Despite” đi với danh từ/cụm danh từ, không đi trực tiếp với mệnh đề như ở đây.

question_text: Excuse me? Can I try ____ this jacket to make sure it fits?
options: under
with
on
explanation: Cụm cố định khi mặc thử quần áo là “try on”. Vì vậy câu đúng là “Can I try on this jacket?”.

question_text: He is interested ____ photography.
options: in
on
at
explanation: Cụm tính từ đúng là “interested in”, nghĩa là quan tâm/hứng thú với điều gì.

question_text: I saw Wi Joo this morning and she ____ if you were free tomorrow.
options: told
asked
said
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “ask if...” nghĩa là hỏi liệu có... “Told” thường đi với tân ngữ và “that”, còn “said” thường đi với “that”, không hợp trực tiếp với “if” ở đây.

question_text: She is ____ person in the class.
options: smarter
the smartest
smart
explanation: So sánh nhất cần the + adj-est/most + adj: the smartest person.

question_text: Because of computers, many people don’t watch a lot of ____ now.
options: the television
a television
television
explanation: Khi nói chung về hoạt động xem TV, dùng “watch television” không cần mạo từ. “A television” là một cái TV, còn “the television” chỉ một TV cụ thể.

question_text: They have lived here ____ they got married.
options: since
for
during
explanation: “They got married” là mốc bắt đầu trong quá khứ, nên dùng “since”. “For” dùng với khoảng thời gian, ví dụ “for ten years”.

question_text: She can't come because she ____ her leg.
options: has broken
broke
was breaking
explanation: Việc gãy chân xảy ra trước đó nhưng kết quả còn ảnh hưởng hiện tại: cô ấy không thể đến. Vì vậy dùng hiện tại hoàn thành “has broken”.

question_text: There are two books here. Which one is ____?
options: your
yours
you
explanation: Sau động từ “is” cần đại từ sở hữu đứng độc lập: “yours” = của bạn. “Your” phải đi kèm danh từ, ví dụ “your book”.

question_text: I think, in the future, people ____ live much longer than they do now.
options: ought
will
would
explanation: “In the future” và “I think” cho thấy đây là dự đoán tương lai. Dùng “will live”.

question_text: This exercise is ____ than the last one.
options: difficult
more difficult
most difficult
explanation: Có “than” nên cần dạng so sánh hơn. Với tính từ dài “difficult”, ta dùng “more difficult”.

question_text: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ at home.
options: stay
stayed
will stay
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 1: If + hiện tại đơn, will + V. Mệnh đề kết quả dùng “will stay”.

question_text: When I go to university, I may ____ history.
options: study
to study
studying
explanation: Sau động từ khuyết thiếu “may”, dùng động từ nguyên thể không “to”. Vì vậy: may study.

question_text: I can't find the keys ____ I left on the table.
options: who
where
that
explanation: Keys là vật; mệnh đề quan hệ xác định có thể dùng that: the keys that I left.

question_text: The test was easier ____ I expected.
options: as
than
from
explanation: Trong so sánh hơn, ta dùng “than”: easier than I expected = dễ hơn tôi mong đợi.

question_text: The more you practise, the ____ you become.
options: good
better
best
explanation: Cấu trúc so sánh kép là “The more..., the better...”. Nghĩa là càng luyện tập nhiều thì càng giỏi hơn.

question_text: Call me tomorrow after 8.30, because I will just ____ at home.
options: about to relax
have relax
be relaxing
explanation: Người nói diễn tả hành động sẽ đang diễn ra vào thời điểm sau 8:30 ngày mai. Dùng tương lai tiếp diễn: “will be relaxing”.

question_text: The man ____ lives next door is a doctor.
options: who
which
where
explanation: “The man” là người và đại từ quan hệ làm chủ ngữ của mệnh đề “lives next door”, nên dùng “who”.

question_text: She asked him ____ he wanted coffee or tea.
options: whether
what
which
explanation: Có lựa chọn coffee or tea nên dùng whether.

question_text: I met a man ____ brother works with you.
options: whose
who
which
explanation: Cần đại từ quan hệ chỉ sở hữu: anh trai/em trai của người đàn ông đó. Vì vậy dùng “whose”.

question_text: It ____ be meat free – it tastes just like chicken!
options: could
can
can’t
explanation: Người nói suy luận món này không thể là đồ chay/không thịt vì nó có vị giống gà. Dùng “can’t be” để diễn tả suy đoán phủ định chắc chắn.

question_text: I'm not tall enough ____ the shelf.
options: reach
reaching
to reach
explanation: Cấu trúc “adjective + enough + to V” nghĩa là đủ... để làm gì. Câu đúng: tall enough to reach the shelf.

question_text: They stopped ____ lunch at 1 p.m.
options: have
having
to have
explanation: “Stop to do something” nghĩa là dừng việc đang làm để làm việc khác. Ở đây họ dừng lại để ăn trưa, nên dùng “to have lunch”.

question_text: You don't like spicy food, ____?
options: do you
don't you
are you
explanation: Câu hỏi đuôi: mệnh đề chính phủ định nên đuôi khẳng định: do you.

question_text: I was made ____ the room after the party.
options: clean
to clean
cleaning
explanation: Ở dạng chủ động, “make someone do something” không dùng “to”. Nhưng khi chuyển sang bị động, cấu trúc là “be made to do something”. Vì vậy dùng “to clean”.

question_text: The doctor says I will ____ much better by the end of the week.
options: to feel
be feeling
have felt
explanation: Câu nói về trạng thái/cảm giác dự kiến trong tương lai gần. “Will be feeling” là cách tự nhiên để nói sẽ cảm thấy khá hơn vào thời điểm đó.

question_text: It was a dark, moonlit night when the traveller ____ at the inn.
options: arrived
was arriving
had arrived
explanation: Đây là sự kiện chính trong câu chuyện ở quá khứ: người lữ khách đến quán trọ. Sự kiện chính dùng quá khứ đơn “arrived”.

question_text: The film was ____ boring that I fell asleep.
options: such
so
too
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “so + adjective + that”: so boring that I fell asleep. “Such” cần danh từ phía sau, ví dụ “such a boring film”.

question_text: I'm not used to ____ in big cities.
options: drive
driving
drove
explanation: Cấu trúc “be used to + V-ing/noun” nghĩa là quen với việc gì. Vì vậy: not used to driving.

question_text: He used to ____ tennis every weekend.
options: play
playing
played
explanation: “Used to + V nguyên thể” diễn tả thói quen trong quá khứ. Vì vậy dùng “play”, không dùng “playing” hay “played”.

question_text: It's time we ____ home.
options: go
went
going
explanation: Cấu trúc It is time + S + V quá khứ: It is time we went home.

question_text: I have my hair ____ every month.
options: cut
cutting
to cut
explanation: Cấu trúc nhờ ai làm gì là “have something + V3/ed”. Động từ “cut” có V3 vẫn là “cut”, nên câu đúng là “have my hair cut”.

question_text: She doesn't like coffee, ____?
options: does she
doesn't she
is she
explanation: Câu hỏi đuôi: mệnh đề chính phủ định thì đuôi khẳng định. “Doesn’t like” dùng trợ động từ “does”, nên đuôi là “does she?”.

question_text: The woman ____ you met yesterday is my aunt.
options: who
which
where
explanation: “The woman” là người, nên dùng đại từ quan hệ “who”. “Which” dùng cho vật/sự việc, còn “where” dùng cho nơi chốn.

question_text: If I hadn’t gone out last night, I ____ be so tired now.
options: won’t
wouldn’t
hadn’t
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện hỗn hợp: điều kiện trái với quá khứ “If I hadn’t gone out last night” và kết quả trái với hiện tại “I wouldn’t be so tired now”.

question_text: There's someone at the door, ____?
options: isn't there
is there
wasn't there
explanation: Câu hỏi đuôi với cấu trúc “There is...” ở dạng khẳng định sẽ dùng đuôi phủ định: “isn’t there?”.

question_text: ____ been reading this book now for a week and it isn’t getting any better!
options: I’ve
I’m
I’d
explanation: Cấu trúc hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn là “have/has been + V-ing”. Vì vậy: I’ve been reading this book for a week.

question_text: The garden is looking untidy– you need to get rid ____ the weeds.
options: from
out
of
explanation: Cụm đúng là “get rid of”, nghĩa là loại bỏ. Câu đúng: get rid of the weeds.

question_text: We need to find out ____ caused the problem.
options: what
which
whose
explanation: Cần từ để chỉ “điều gì” gây ra vấn đề. “What caused the problem” là cụm mệnh đề danh từ đúng trong câu này.

question_text: We have ____ finished our homework.
options: yet
already
still
explanation: Trong câu khẳng định hiện tại hoàn thành, “already” diễn tả việc đã hoàn thành rồi. “Yet” thường dùng trong câu phủ định/nghi vấn.

question_text: The film was ____ by millions of people.
options: watched
watching
watch
explanation: Bị động: was watched by millions of people.

question_text: He ____ be at home; his car isn't outside.
options: can't
must
should
explanation: Người nói suy luận rằng anh ấy không thể ở nhà vì xe không ở bên ngoài. Dùng “can’t be” để diễn tả suy đoán phủ định chắc chắn.

question_text: This is ____ useful advice.
options: a
an
explanation: “Advice” là danh từ không đếm được, nên không dùng “a/an”. Dù có tính từ “useful”, ta vẫn nói “useful advice”.

question_text: I ____ like mushrooms, but I can’t stop eating them now.
options: wouldn’t
didn’t use to
couldn’t
explanation: “Didn’t use to + V” diễn tả điều trước đây không xảy ra/không đúng nhưng hiện tại đã thay đổi. Câu nghĩa là trước đây tôi không thích nấm, nhưng bây giờ lại ăn nhiều.

question_text: We arrived late ____ the traffic.
options: because
because of
although
explanation: Sau chỗ trống là cụm danh từ “the traffic”, nên dùng “because of”. Nếu dùng “because” thì cần một mệnh đề, ví dụ “because the traffic was bad”.

question_text: We haven't finished the work ____.
options: already
yet
still
explanation: Trong câu phủ định hiện tại hoàn thành, “yet” thường đặt cuối câu để diễn tả “chưa”. Câu đúng: We haven’t finished the work yet.

question_text: I prefer tea ____ coffee.
options: than
from
to
explanation: Cụm so sánh sở thích đúng là “prefer A to B”. Vì vậy: I prefer tea to coffee.

question_text: I don't mind ____ early.
options: start
to start
starting
explanation: Sau “mind” dùng V-ing: mind doing something. Câu đúng là “I don’t mind starting early”.

question_text: The next meeting ____ on the sixth of June.
options: is holding
will be held
holds
explanation: Cuộc họp là thứ được tổ chức, nên cần bị động. Nói về tương lai, dùng “will be held”.

question_text: He worked hard ____ he could pass the test.
options: so that
because of
despite
explanation: So that diễn tả mục đích: He worked hard so that he could pass the test.

question_text: The newspaper China Today ____ published for over 60 years.
options: is being
has been
was being
explanation: “For over 60 years” diễn tả khoảng thời gian kéo dài từ quá khứ đến hiện tại. Chủ ngữ là tờ báo được xuất bản, nên dùng bị động hiện tại hoàn thành: “has been published”.

question_text: I regret ____ you that your application was unsuccessful.
options: tell
telling
to tell
explanation: Regret to tell dùng khi lịch sự báo tin xấu. Regret + V-ing nói về việc đã làm và hối tiếc.

question_text: She said she ____ call me later.
options: would
will
is going
explanation: Trong câu tường thuật, “will” thường lùi thành “would”. Vì vậy: She said she would call me later.

question_text: He made me ____ until midnight.
options: work
to work
working
explanation: Cấu trúc chủ động là “make someone + V nguyên thể không to”. Vì vậy dùng “work”: He made me work.

question_text: They said they ____ been studying for ages.
options: will have
are
had
explanation: Đây là câu tường thuật. Câu trực tiếp có thể là “We have been studying for ages”, khi tường thuật lùi thành “they had been studying for ages”.

question_text: ____ of China is very interesting.
options: history
A history
The history
explanation: Khi nói về lịch sử cụ thể của một quốc gia với cụm “of China”, cách tự nhiên là “The history of China”.

question_text: I don't know ____ to do next.
options: what
which
who
explanation: Cấu trúc “what to do” nghĩa là phải làm gì. “Which” dùng khi chọn giữa các lựa chọn cụ thể, còn “who” dùng cho người.

question_text: If she had studied harder, she ____ passed the exam.
options: would have
will have
had
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 3: If + had + V3, would have + V3. Vì vậy dùng “would have passed”.

question_text: My father, ____ is a dentist, told me not to drink sugary drinks.
options: who
which
that
explanation: Đây là mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định vì có dấu phẩy. Nói về người nên dùng “who”. “That” không dùng trong mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định có dấu phẩy.

question_text: The house ____ roof is red belongs to my uncle.
options: who
whose
which
explanation: Whose chỉ sở hữu: the house whose roof is red.

question_text: The teacher told us ____ carefully.
options: listening
listen
to listen
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “tell someone to do something”. Vì vậy: The teacher told us to listen carefully.

question_text: You ____ have bought that car. What a waste of money!
options: shouldn’t
mustn’t
couldn’t
explanation: “Shouldn’t have + V3” diễn tả việc lẽ ra không nên làm trong quá khứ. Người nói cho rằng mua xe là lãng phí tiền.

question_text: She has been learning English ____ she was ten.
options: for
since
during
explanation: “Since” dùng với mốc thời gian bắt đầu. “She was ten” là mốc bắt đầu, nên dùng “since”.

question_text: The train ____ at 7 p.m. tomorrow.
options: leaves
will leaving
is leave
explanation: Lịch trình cố định của phương tiện giao thông thường dùng hiện tại đơn, dù nói về tương lai. Vì vậy: The train leaves at 7 p.m. tomorrow.

question_text: The road was closed ____ an accident.
options: because
due to
although
explanation: Sau chỗ trống là cụm danh từ “an accident”, nên dùng “due to”. “Because” cần một mệnh đề đầy đủ, ví dụ “because there was an accident”.

question_text: This is a ____ train to London. It doesn’t stop on the way.
options: direction
directly
direct
explanation: Cần tính từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ “train”. “Direct train” nghĩa là chuyến tàu đi thẳng, không dừng giữa đường.

question_text: I don't know anyone ____ can fix this computer.
options: which
who
where
explanation: “Anyone” chỉ người, nên dùng đại từ quan hệ “who”. “Which” dùng cho vật, “where” dùng cho nơi chốn.

question_text: By the time the police arrived, the thief ____.
options: left
had left
was leaving
explanation: Hành động tên trộm rời đi xảy ra trước khi cảnh sát đến. Khi một hành động xảy ra trước một mốc quá khứ, dùng quá khứ hoàn thành: “had left”.

question_text: The book, ____ I borrowed from Mai, is excellent.
options: who
which
where
explanation: “The book” là vật, và mệnh đề có dấu phẩy là mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định. Dùng “which”, không dùng “that” trong loại mệnh đề này.

question_text: ____ memory of the day I met the president is very special to me.
options: The
A
explanation: Ở đây nói đến một ký ức cụ thể, được xác định bởi cụm “of the day I met the president”. Vì vậy dùng mạo từ xác định “The”.

question_text: If I had known your number, I ____ called you.
options: would have
will have
had
explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 3: If + past perfect, would have + V3/ed.

question_text: He has ____ visited London twice.
options: yet
already
still
explanation: Trong câu khẳng định hiện tại hoàn thành, “already” diễn tả việc đã xảy ra. Câu đúng: He has already visited London twice.

question_text: Describe the picture.
explanation: In the first picture, I can see several football players standing in a stadium. They look serious and ready for an important match. There are many spectators behind them, so the atmosphere seems exciting. In the second picture, a female athlete is jumping over a high bar or pole during a competition. Both pictures show sports events, but football is a team sport, while the second activity looks more individual and technical.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Both pictures show sports, but they are very different. In the first picture, I can see a football match. A player in a white shirt with the number ten is running fast with the ball at his feet. Two players in red and green shirts are trying to stop him. Behind them there are many spectators in a full stadium. In the second picture, a female athlete is doing the high jump. She is wearing blue and white and bending her back over a red bar. There is a big crowd behind her too. Both pictures show competition in front of many people, but football is a team sport, while the high jump is an individual and technical sport.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: The first picture captures a football match in full flow. A player in a white shirt with the number ten is sprinting with the ball at his feet, while two defenders in red and green kit chase him and try to win it back. Behind them a crowded stand rises up, so this looks like an important game. The second picture shows a single athlete in mid-jump, arching her back over a red high-jump bar in a blue and white kit, with a full stadium watching. She is entirely alone in the frame. What the pair captures is the difference between a sport you experience with others and one that comes down to a few seconds on your own. It is a neat pairing of two very different kinds of pressure.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: During my second year at university I lent my laptop to my roommate Minh for almost a fortnight. That does not sound dramatic, until you remember that a student's laptop holds their entire life. His had died two days before a major assignment deadline, and repairing it would have taken too long. So we worked out a timetable. He used it at night and I used it during the day, and somehow we both submitted on time. My feelings about it were mixed, and I would rather be honest than sound perfect. There was a real satisfaction in being useful to somebody who was clearly panicking. At the same time I was quietly anxious for the whole fortnight. That machine had cost me a year of saving, and every time I heard him carrying it downstairs I felt nervous. Nothing happened to it, of course. As it happens, I have already promised something for next month. My cousin is moving into her first flat in September with almost no furniture. She has been planning that flat for months. I am lending her my rice cooker, a small bookshelf and, rather more nervously, my camera. She wants to photograph the place before and after she decorates it. I have also offered to help her carry everything across the city on a Sunday. I suspect that will be the harder part. I feel relaxed this time, because a rice cooker is easy to replace.

He used my laptop at night, and I used it in the day. In the end we both finished our work on time. I felt happy about sharing it, because I could help a good friend. But I was also a little worried every day. That laptop cost me one year of saving money. Every time he carried it downstairs, I was nervous. Nothing bad happened, so now I am glad I said yes. He also bought me lunch to say thank you. I am planning to share something again soon. My cousin will move into her first flat next month. I will lend her my rice cooker and my small bookshelf. I will also help her carry the boxes on Sunday. She has very little furniture, so these things will be useful. She can keep them for one year.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: About eighteen months ago I was offered a job in Ho Chi Minh City. The salary was roughly forty per cent higher than what I was earning, and I had ten days to answer. The complication was my mother. She had just come out of hospital after a knee operation and was living alone in my home town. She had also just started using a walking stick. On one side there was the career I had been working towards. On the other there was the practical question of who would take her to her appointments. In the end what settled it was a conversation with my mother herself. She told me quite firmly that she had managed for sixty years without my supervision. So the guilt I had built the decision on was mine alone. I still turned the job down, but for a different reason. When I pictured myself in that office I felt nothing at all. When I pictured the drive home at weekends I felt something. It was instinct, once the noise had died down. As for having a lot of choices, I think it cuts both ways. More choice obviously means more freedom. I would never want a world where people simply inherited their parents' job. Yet a huge menu of options can be too much to handle. My generation spends a lot of energy worrying about the doors we did not walk through, and that helps nobody.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Back in 2023 I had to make a difficult choice about my job. A company in Ho Chi Minh City offered me a better salary. The salary was almost double my old one. But my family lives in my home town, and my mother was ill. I had one week to answer, and I could not sleep well. I asked my father and my best friend for advice. In the end I decided to stay at home. First, I made a list of good things and bad things. I wrote it in my notebook on a quiet evening. The list helped me see the truth clearly. Money was important, but my family was more important for me. I also talked to my mother, and she was very honest. She said she was fine, but I could see her face. So I said no to that company. For me, too many choices make life harder. Of course, choices give us freedom, and freedom is good. But too many options make us worried and slow. My lesson is simple. Now I choose only two options and I forget the others. This small rule saves me a lot of time. I still think about that day sometimes.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: In this picture I can see a young mother and her little child in the mountains. The child is sitting on the mother's shoulders, wearing a green top, and pointing at something far away with one hand. The mother has red hair and a grey shirt. She is holding the child's feet and smiling, and she is looking in the same direction. Behind them there are tall pine trees and very high grey mountains with some snow on the top. The sky is blue with white clouds, so I think the weather is good. They look happy, and I guess they are on a family trip or a walk in nature.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: This is a mother and her toddler on a walk in the mountains, and it looks like a perfect day for it. The child is riding on her shoulders in a green top, pointing excitedly at the peaks in the distance, while the mother holds his little shoes and smiles up at whatever he has spotted. She has red hair and a grey shirt, and she looks completely relaxed, as if carrying him this way is normal. Behind them there's a dense forest of tall pines and then huge grey mountains, with snow still on the summits and a few white clouds around them. I'd say it's late morning in summer. It's the kind of photo a father takes on a family holiday, and it captures that moment when a child discovers something for the first time.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: Last November I was asked to run a training session for new staff at my company. I was fairly nervous about it, because most of the audience were older than me. Afterwards my line manager Hoa stopped me in the corridor. She is not exactly generous with compliments, so I was surprised. She said my explanations were the clearest she had heard in years, and she wanted me to design the whole induction programme. It took me a moment to realise she was being serious. Honestly, it made my week. There was relief first, because I had spent three evenings preparing the slides. I genuinely thought I had rushed the second half. Then there was a kind of quiet pride that stayed with me for days. I remember walking home the long way just to enjoy it. What surprised me most was how much it changed my attitude at work. I started volunteering for things I would previously have avoided. That is exactly why I think positive feedback matters so much. People assume that others already know when they are doing well. In fact most of us are far more aware of our mistakes than our strengths. A few honest words can push somebody through a difficult period, and they cost nothing. Of course, praise has to be specific and deserved, otherwise it turns into empty flattery. Used properly, though, it is one of the cheapest and most powerful tools any manager has.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: I remember one day when my boss praised me in front of the whole team. It was at my office last year, on a Monday morning. I wrote a short report about our sales for one month. I used pictures and simple sentences, so it was easy to read. My boss read it before our meeting. He said it was clear and very useful for everyone. He also asked me to teach the same style to my colleagues. That was the first time he praised me in public. I felt very happy and a little shy at the same time. My face was hot and I did not know what to say. My colleagues smiled at me and said congratulations. After the meeting I called my mother and told her the news. I felt proud for the whole week after that. To me, positive feedback is very important at work. Many people work hard, but nobody says thank you to them. A few kind words can change someone's day completely. Feedback also helps people know that they are doing the right thing. So I always try to praise my friends when they do something well. For example, I sent a nice message to my colleague last week.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: In April I took the train up to Lao Cai to visit my grandmother. I had not seen her properly since Tet. She lives alone in a house that always smells of dried herbs. She had cooked far more food than two people could eat, which is her way of showing love. I stayed four days, mostly listening to stories about relatives I have never met. I also fixed her television aerial, which had been broken since January. She also gave me a bag of dried mushrooms to take home. As for guests behaving badly in my own home, I would find that really upsetting. A friend once brought somebody I did not know to my flat. He put his feet on the table, criticised the food and left the bathroom in a terrible state. I said nothing at the time, because I hate confrontation, but I never invited him back. Hospitality works both ways, and treating someone's home carelessly says a lot about a person. On the city or countryside question I am torn, though I lean towards the city at the moment. Cities offer work, hospitals, decent internet and the chance to disappear into a crowd. The countryside offers cleaner air, cheaper living and neighbours who actually know your name. Visiting my grandmother always makes me miss village life for about a week. Then I remember there is one bus a day, and my enthusiasm fades quite quickly.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: During Tet last year I visited my grandmother in the countryside. I took a bus for three hours on a Saturday morning. She lives alone in an old house with a big garden. She cooked chicken and rice for me, and it was too much food. I stayed two days, and I fixed her old electric fan. I brought her some fruit and warm socks. She gave me vegetables from her garden. She told me many stories about my father when he was young. We also walked to the market together on Sunday. If a guest was not respectful in my home, I would feel angry and sad. Once a friend brought a person I did not know to my flat. He put his shoes on my sofa and left rubbish everywhere. He also shouted on the phone late at night. I said nothing that day, but I never invited him again. To me, a guest should treat your home like their own home. Between a city and the countryside, I choose the city. The city has work, hospitals and good internet. My job and most of my friends are here. The countryside is quiet and the air is clean. But there is only one bus a day.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: Passing the final accounting paper at university is probably the thing I am proudest of, even though it happened three years ago. So I set myself one clear goal for that term: pass, whatever it took. I worked through three or four past papers a week, gave up my part-time job in a coffee shop, and revised in the university library from seven in the morning because my flat was far too noisy. When the results came out I was on a bus, and I actually shouted. The other passengers did not appreciate it. My first feeling, oddly, was not joy but relief. A huge weight slid off my shoulders after months of telling my family that I was not worried. The pride arrived later that evening, when I rang my mother and heard her go completely quiet. There was also a strange emptiness, because the person who had been getting up at six suddenly had nothing to get up for. As for why setting goals matters, I would say a goal turns a vague wish into a plan. Wanting to do well means nothing on a Tuesday morning, whereas a specific target tells you exactly what to do that day. A goal also gives failure a shape. When I failed the first time, I could see precisely how far I was from the line, and that gap was something I could close. Finally, reaching a goal changes how you see yourself. Since that exam I have assumed that most difficult things are possible with enough stubbornness, and so far that assumption has held.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Two years ago my goal was to pass my driving test. I failed the first time, because I was too nervous and made a small mistake at the end. After that I practised every Sunday morning with my uncle for three months. We drove around a quiet street near my house and practised parking many times. He is a very calm teacher. Then I took the test again in May, and I passed it. My marks were not high, but that was enough for me. When I heard the result, I felt relieved first. I sat in the car and I could not speak for a minute. After that I felt very proud, and I called my parents. In the evening I bought some cakes for my family. My mother was even happier than me. Now I drive to work every day without any problem. In my opinion, it is very important for people to set goals. First, a goal gives us a clear direction. When I had a test date, I knew exactly what to practise every week. Second, a goal helps us keep going when things are hard. After I failed, I wanted to give up, but the goal made me try again. Finally, when we reach a goal, we feel more confident. After my test, I believed that I could learn other difficult things too. So I think everybody should have a small goal for every month and a big goal for every year.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: My friend and I worked in a small team at my company last year. There were four of us in the group. We prepared a training day for the new staff. I made the slides, and my friend Nam booked the room. Another colleague wrote the questions for the test. We met twice a week for one month. The training day went well, and about thirty people came. Everyone said thank you at the end. How did I feel when working in the team? Most of the time I felt happy and full of energy. This is mainly because we shared the pressure, so nobody carried everything alone. When I was tired, Nam finished part of my work, and a colleague found a big mistake in my slides one day before the training. On the other hand, I sometimes felt annoyed when the meetings took too long. What are some benefits of working in a team? I think there are three main benefits. First, five people notice more than one person does, so mistakes are found early. Second, each person can do what they do best, because one person cannot be good at everything. I am good at slides, but I am bad at organising rooms and writing tests. Third, you can learn new skills from your teammates. So for me, working in a team makes the work faster and better.

extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Two summers ago I helped organise a charity book fair with five other volunteers, and that is still the clearest example of teamwork I can give. We had six weeks, almost no budget and a borrowed hall in the centre of Hanoi. I handled communication with the schools, another volunteer dealt with sponsors, and our leader, a retired teacher named Mr Bang, kept the whole thing from falling apart whenever two of us disagreed, which happened fairly often. How did I feel? For the most part, energised. There is a particular pleasure in watching a plan come together through six pairs of hands, and I felt supported, because I was never alone with a problem. I would be lying, though, if I said it was always comfortable: I was irritated by meetings that dragged on, and there was one person doing very little while another quietly did far too much. What are the benefits of teamwork? I would point to three main ones. The first is range: nobody is good at everything, so a team supplies a mix of skills no individual could have, and somebody usually catches a mistake before it becomes a disaster. The second is learning, since you pick up a great deal simply by watching how other people work, which has been more useful to me than any training course. And finally, a team keeps you accountable: when others depend on you, you finish what you promised. That book fair raised enough for four hundred textbooks, and I could not have managed that alone.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Both pictures show people spending a day outdoors, but the weather is completely different. In the first one, six young people in thick winter coats stand together in a pine forest. They are all looking down at a paper map that one of them is holding. In the second picture a woman in a white dress walks barefoot along the sea with three small children. The waves are washing over their feet. Tall white buildings stand behind them under a clear blue sky.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Both pictures show people spending a day outdoors, whereas the weather in them could hardly be more different. In the first, six young people who are wrapped in thick winter coats stand in a pine forest with large rucksacks. They have gathered around a paper map and they are all laughing. The second picture shows a woman in a white floral dress walking barefoot along the shoreline with three small children. Warm waves run over the wet sand, and tall white towers rise behind the beach.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Both pictures show two children playing a game, but the games are very different. In the first picture, a boy and a girl are sitting at a round metal table outdoors and playing chess. The boy on the left, in a dark blue T-shirt, is moving a piece. The girl on the right, in a white top, is resting her chin on her hand. Both of them are smiling. In the second picture, a girl and a boy are sitting on a sofa at home and playing a video game with black controllers. The girl has long blonde hair and a red checked shirt, and the boy wears a white T-shirt. They are laughing loudly. So the first game is quiet and slow, while the second is noisy and exciting.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Both pictures show a pair of children playing a game, but the mood is quite different in each. In the first, a boy and a girl of about ten sit opposite each other at a round metal table outdoors, with a wooden chess board between them. The boy on the left, in a navy T-shirt, is reaching across to move a piece, while the girl on the right, in a white top, rests her chin on her hand and watches him. Both are grinning, so it seems a friendly game rather than a serious contest. The second picture moves indoors: a blonde girl in a red checked shirt and a boy in a white T-shirt sit side by side on a sofa, gripping black wired controllers and laughing out loud. One game is slow and calm, the other fast and loud, but the children look equally happy in both.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Both pictures show people relaxing at home, but in very different ways. In the first picture, I can see a family of four sitting together on the grass in front of a light blue wooden house. There are two parents and two children, a boy and a girl. extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Both pictures show people enjoying a quiet moment at home, though the company could not be more different. The first shows a family of four sitting on the lawn in front of a pale blue wooden house: a mother, a father, a small boy in a blue shirt and a girl in white. The children are leaning against their parents, everyone is smiling at the camera, and pink flowers are blooming beside the house. The second picture shows a young woman with long wavy hair standing alone on a narrow balcony. She is wearing a white top, her face is tilted up towards the sunlight and one hand rests on her neck. Behind her stretch the grey rooftops and shuttered windows of an old European city. So one picture is about relaxing as a group, whereas the other is about choosing to be by yourself, and neither person looks lonely.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: The most recent present I got was a rather heavy one, a cast-iron frying pan. My younger sister gave it to me at the end of March, a few days before my birthday. She was flying back to Da Nang and could not wait for the actual day. She had noticed that every pan in my kitchen was scratched to death. So she decided to solve the problem herself, instead of buying me another scented candle I would never use. When it comes to presents in general, I lean towards handmade ones. A friend of mine once knitted me a scarf that was a bit crooked at one end, and I still keep it. Honestly, I cannot remember what I was given at my graduation. Handmade things carry the hours somebody spent on them, and that is hard to buy. That said, I would not be strict about it. If somebody needs a good pair of running shoes, a homemade card is not going to help them much. As for the near future, yes, I am planning something. My colleague Trang is leaving our office in September to study abroad. A few of us are putting together a photo album with short messages from everyone she has worked with. I am in charge of collecting the pictures, which means chasing about twenty people for old files. It is turning into far more work than I expected, but I think her reaction will make it worth the trouble.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Both pictures show places where people go on holiday, but they are very different. In the first picture, I can see a very crowded beach in a city. The sand is covered with colourful umbrellas in blue, red, yellow and green, and there are hundreds of people. Behind the beach there are tall apartment buildings. The place looks lively but very busy and noisy. In the second picture, two girls with long hair are sitting on a stone wall beside a calm lake. They are looking at a snow covered mountain and a dark green forest. The water is still and there is nobody else around. This place looks quiet and peaceful. I think the first place is fun with friends, but the second one is better for relaxing.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Both pictures show popular places to spend free time, but the atmosphere could not be more different. The first picture shows a city beach packed with people. Colourful umbrellas in blue, red, yellow and green cover almost every metre of sand, and a long line of tall buildings stands behind the beach. It looks like a hot public holiday, which would explain the crowd. The second picture shows two girls with long hair sitting side by side on a low stone wall beside a lake. They are looking across the still water towards a snow capped mountain and a dark pine forest, and there is nobody else in sight. One place is loud and social, whereas the other is silent and empty. Both are worth visiting, but I would choose the lake if I needed a real rest.

Behind them a man, probably the father, stands with a white acoustic guitar, so the whole family is joining in. The second picture shows a band on a large outdoor stage at a festival, seen from behind. Three musicians face a huge crowd sitting on the grass, with white tents and green trees in the distance, and one player in a red top has a guitar across his body. The first scene is private and relaxed; the second is a proper performance with cables, speakers and an audience.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: I changed jobs in early 2023. I left a small logistics company where I had worked for four years, and joined a much larger firm in the same industry. The decision was not really about money. My old team had shrunk from twelve people to five, and there was nowhere left for me to grow. I handed in my notice in January and started the new position three weeks later. That sounds smooth, but it certainly did not feel smooth at the time. The first two months were a mess of mixed feelings. I felt relieved to escape a company that was clearly going downhill. I felt guilty about leaving colleagues who had become friends. I was also quietly terrified that I had overestimated myself. In the old office I knew every system and every shortcut. In the new one I had to ask where the printer was. It took about half a year before I stopped feeling like a visitor. Why are big changes so hard for people? I think we underestimate how much of our confidence comes from familiarity rather than ability. When everything around you is new, you lose all those small daily wins. Those wins quietly tell you that you are doing fine. There is also the fear of regret, because with any change there is a version of your life you gave up. Most of us prefer something imperfect that we understand.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: I changed my job in January 2023. Before that, I worked at a small logistics company for four years. The company was getting smaller every year. The team lost people, and there was no chance to grow. So I applied to a bigger company in the same field. I sent my application in December, and I started the new job three weeks after I left. The new company has about two hundred staff, and the office is also nearer to my home. I had many different feelings at the same time. I felt happy, because the new office was modern and busy. But I also felt sad, because my old colleagues were my friends. In the first month I was nervous every morning. I did not know the systems, and I asked many simple questions. One kind colleague helped me with everything. After about six months I finally felt comfortable there. Why is change so hard for people? I think we love the things that we know well. When everything is new, we feel weak and slow. People are also afraid of making the wrong choice. For example, my brother stayed in a bad job for years, because he was simply afraid of a new start. But in my case, the change was worth it.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: Something that has stayed with me for years is a conversation with a taxi driver in Hue, during a work trip in 2019. It was a forty-minute journey from the airport. His taxi smelled of coffee, and there was a photograph on the dashboard. He told me, very calmly, as if it was normal, that he had been a secondary school teacher for eighteen years. Then his wife became seriously ill and he had to earn more. So he sold his motorbike, borrowed money and started driving. He was not bitter about it at all. He talked about his former students the way other people talk about a holiday they loved. At the time I felt genuinely uncomfortable, and I mean that as a compliment to him. I was twenty-four, and I was convinced that a career was a straight line you climbed. Listening to a man who had lost the thing he loved most made my own complaints sound ridiculous. There was admiration mixed in, and an embarrassment I could not shake off for days. What I learned is simple. You cannot read a person's life from their job. I had assumed a very ordinary story and I was completely wrong. Since then I ask far more questions of people I would once have walked straight past. The second lesson was about plans. Mine had been rigid until then, and he showed me a life can be rebuilt around whoever needs you.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: On a rainy Tuesday in 2019, I took a taxi from Hue airport. I was there for work, and the trip took forty minutes. The rain was heavy and the traffic was slow. He drove very carefully all the way. The driver told me that he was a teacher for eighteen years. His wife became ill, so he needed more money for the hospital. He sold his motorbike and started to drive a taxi. He works about twelve hours every day now. He talked about his old students with a big smile. He even remembered their names after all those years. At that moment I felt uncomfortable and very small. I was twenty-four, and I often complained about my easy job. His story showed me that my problems were not real problems. I also felt great respect for him, because he was not angry. From that day I learned that you cannot judge people from their job. Everyone has a long story behind them. Now I ask more questions and I listen more carefully. I also complain much less about small things at work. I still remember his face when I feel tired. I gave him a big tip at the hotel.

groups.question: Why do you think many people find it difficult to save money?

extra_data.sampleAnswer: My first proper experience of saving was for a second-hand Yamaha motorbike when I was twenty-one. It cost around eighteen million dong, and I was working part-time in a bookshop earning very little. It took me almost eleven months. I cut out coffee shops, which for a Vietnamese student is close to social suicide. I kept the money in a metal box at my aunt's house. I knew it would disappear if it sat in my bank account. I still remember counting the notes out on the seller's table. If somebody had offered to buy that bike for me, I think I would have felt grateful and slightly cheated at the same time. My uncle did offer to lend me the money halfway through, and I refused, which annoyed my mother enormously. The point was never the machine. It was proving to myself that I could stick to something for eleven months. A gift would have removed the only part that mattered. Why do so many people struggle to save? Partly it is simple maths. Rents and food have risen much faster than wages. Telling somebody to skip their coffee is insulting when the real problem is the rent. But there is a mental side too. One tap on a phone removes any real feeling of losing money, and adverts make us feel we are missing out. Saying no again and again for a reward months away is hard.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: The first time I saved money for something big, I was twenty-one. I wanted to buy an old motorbike for my daily trips. I worked part time in a bookshop, and my salary was small. So I stopped buying coffee and I cooked at home every day. I also walked to work instead of taking a bus. I kept my money in a box at my aunt's house. After about ten months I had enough money. I bought a second-hand Yamaha from a man near my school. The bike was red and quite old. It still runs well today. I was so happy on my first ride home. If someone bought it for me, I would say thank you. But I would also feel a bit strange. My uncle offered me money in the middle of that year. I said no, because the money was not the real point. I wanted to prove that I can finish a long plan. I think there are two main reasons why saving is hard. First, prices are high and salaries are low. So people spend everything before the end of the month. Then, shopping online is too easy today. You only touch your phone, and the money is gone.

groups.question: Why do you think fewer people read books nowadays?

extra_data.sampleAnswer: The last book I finished was The Remains of the Day by Kazuo Ishiguro. I read it over about three weeks in June, mostly on the bus to work. The novel is about three hundred pages long. A colleague had recommended it after I complained that I only ever read business books. She was right to. It follows an English butler looking back on decades of loyal service, and almost nothing dramatic happens in it. That is exactly the point. Reading it made me unexpectedly sad, which is not what I had expected from a book about a butler. He describes his life in careful, formal language. Underneath it you can see the loneliness and the wasted chances he will not admit to. That is especially true with a woman he worked with for years. I kept putting the book down every few pages, partly to think and partly because it made me uncomfortable. I hide behind work myself whenever something personal feels difficult. As for why fewer people read now, I do not think we have become lazy. It is competition. A novel asks for two or three hours of quiet attention. Our phones have trained us to check something new every minute. Reading is also slow to reward you, whereas a short video pays you back straight away. I have started leaving my phone in another room in the evenings, and my concentration comes back quickly.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: One evening after work, my colleague gave me a short novel. It was in June, and the book was about a Vietnamese family. I read it on the bus every morning on my way to work. I read about twenty pages each day. The story is about a mother and her son in a small village. Nothing exciting happens, but the story felt very real to me. The writer used simple words, so it was easy to read. The book has about two hundred pages. The son works in a city far away. I finished it in about three weeks. While I was reading it, I felt calm and a little sad. The mother in the book reminded me of my own mother. Some evenings I stopped reading and called her. I also felt relaxed, because the book was slow and quiet. Personally, I think phones are the main reason people read less. A book needs one hour of quiet time. But a short video only needs one minute, and it is easy. Also, people work long hours and feel too tired at night. Books are quite expensive here too. So I borrow them from my friends now. I gave the book to my sister after that.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: The last book I finished was The Remains of the Day by Kazuo Ishiguro. I read it over about three weeks in June, mostly on the bus to work. The novel is about three hundred pages long. A colleague had recommended it after I complained that I only ever read business books. She was right to. It follows an English butler looking back on decades of loyal service, and almost nothing dramatic happens in it. That is exactly the point. Reading it made me unexpectedly sad, which is not what I had expected from a book about a butler. He describes his life in careful, formal language. Underneath it you can see the loneliness and the wasted chances he will not admit to. That is especially true with a woman he worked with for years. I kept putting the book down every few pages, partly to think and partly because it made me uncomfortable. I hide behind work myself whenever something personal feels difficult. As for why fewer people read now, I do not think we have become lazy. It is competition. A novel asks for two or three hours of quiet attention. Our phones have trained us to check something new every minute. Reading is also slow to reward you, whereas a short video pays you back straight away. I have started leaving my phone in another room in the evenings, and my concentration comes back quickly.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: The Mid-Autumn Festival two years ago stands out for me. It was the first time I helped organise one rather than just watch. Our neighbourhood in Hanoi put on a lantern procession for the children. My aunt volunteered me to help build the star-shaped lanterns out of bamboo and coloured paper. We spent three evenings on the pavement outside her house, cutting frames and arguing about glue. On the night itself about sixty children walked the length of our street, with drums and a lion dance at the front. My aunt made sticky rice cakes for everyone that night. What I enjoyed most was not the event but the preparation. I ended up talking properly to neighbours I had been greeting for years without knowing their names. One of them was an elderly man who explained how the lanterns were made when he was a boy. That was before the plastic ones arrived from the shops. That kind of easy conversation normally never happens in a busy city. That is exactly why I think these events are worth protecting. They give people a reason to stand in the same place at the same time, which is rare now. For children they also create memories tied to a particular street and a particular group of adults. That gives them a sense of where they belong. Without days like that, a neighbourhood is just a collection of doors facing each other.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Not long ago my neighbourhood held the Mid-Autumn Festival. It was in September, and I helped the local group prepare it. We made paper lanterns for the children for three evenings. We used bamboo, coloured paper and a lot of glue. We finished the last lantern at midnight. The children carried them along the street. Some parents took a lot of photos. On the festival night about fifty children walked along our street. There was a lion dance and a lot of drums and music. My little nephew wore a mask and laughed all evening. I enjoyed the preparation more than the party itself. I talked to neighbours that I had never spoken to before. One old man showed me how to cut bamboo for the lanterns. He learned it from his father many years ago. We sat outside his house until ten o'clock. In my opinion, cultural events are really important for us. These events bring people together in one place. In a big city, people are busy and do not talk much. Also, children learn about their own culture from these days. For example, my nephew now knows why we make lanterns. So I will help the group again this year.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: About eight months ago I decided to become a morning person, which anyone who knows me would find quite funny. I used to work until one in the morning and then drag myself out of bed at nine, feeling half dead. Then my flatmate started swimming before work, and out of pure competitiveness I told her I would start getting up at half past five. The first fortnight was really miserable. I set three alarms, put my phone on the other side of the room, and still lay there arguing with myself in the dark. What I enjoyed most, once it settled, was the quiet. Nobody messages you at six in the morning. For the first time in years I had an hour that belonged completely to me. My concentration turned out to be much sharper then than it ever was at midnight, so I now do my hardest work first. The easy admin waits until the afternoon. Is it better to keep a fixed routine or to change it often? For me a fixed one wins, though not a rigid one. When the shape of the day is decided in advance, you stop wasting energy arguing with yourself. That energy goes into the work instead. People who rebuild their week constantly seem to spend a lot of time planning and rather less doing. Even so, a routine that never varies becomes a rut, so I keep one unpredictable day.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Last winter I changed my daily routine completely. Before that I worked until one in the morning every night. I woke up at nine and I always felt tired. Then my flatmate started swimming before work, and I wanted to try too. So I decided to get up at half past five. The first two weeks were terrible, and I used three alarms. I also put my phone far from my bed. The thing I enjoyed most was the quiet morning hours. Nobody sends you a message at six in the morning. That hour belongs to me, so I can read or plan my day. Some mornings I just drink tea and look out of the window. My mind is also clearer, so I do difficult work first. I finish the hard tasks before nine o'clock now. I'd say a fixed routine is much better than a changing one. When I plan my day early, I waste less time. I do not argue with myself about the next task. My body also knows when to sleep and when to wake up. Now I go to bed before eleven o'clock every night. But one free day a week is also important. On Sunday I get up late and I make no plans.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: Last March I was asked to prepare the annual report for my department, and honestly I nearly said no. My colleague Hang normally handled it, but she had gone on maternity leave. So the whole thing landed on my desk with barely three weeks' notice. I had to collect figures from five different teams, and some of them were very slow at answering emails. I ended up staying late almost every evening, living on instant noodles and rather bad coffee. While I was working on it I felt quietly annoyed, if I am honest, because it was not my job. Nobody had asked whether I had time for it. Underneath that there was real worry about putting my name on figures I had not collected myself. The one good moment came around day twelve, when the tables finally balanced. I remember sitting back in an empty office feeling almost powerful. If somebody had to take on the same thing, my advice would be very practical. First, break it into small pieces with your own deadlines. A three-week task with a single deadline turns into a three-day panic. Second, chase people early and in writing, and copy in their manager on the third reminder. It feels rude and it works. Third, agree with your own boss what you are allowed to drop, because something has to give. And finally, protect one evening a week completely. Otherwise you will hand the work in and be useless for a fortnight afterwards.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: This happened at my old job, in March last year. My manager asked me to write the yearly report for our department. My colleague Hang usually did that work, but she was on leave. So the job came to me, and I had only three weeks. I had to collect numbers from five different teams. Some people answered my emails very slowly, and that was stressful. I sent a short reminder every two days. I stayed late at the office almost every evening. I ate instant noodles at my desk and drank a lot of coffee. At first I felt angry, because it was not really my job. Then I felt worried about a mistake in the numbers. I checked every table two times, and I still slept badly. But on day twelve all the numbers were finally correct. At that moment I felt tired but very proud. My manager thanked me in front of the whole team. This task taught me a simple way to work. First, cut the big task into small parts with your own deadlines. Then, ask people for information early. After that, tell your boss which other work you will stop. Finally, rest one evening every week, or you will get ill.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Both pictures show people enjoying nature, but in very different places. In the first picture, four hikers are walking down a rocky mountain path. They are wearing warm jackets in blue and yellow and carrying backpacks. Below them there are thick white clouds, so they are very high up. In the second picture, a family of four is walking along a beach. The parents and the two children are all wearing matching white T-shirts with a blue cartoon shark on them, and black shorts. Both groups look happy in their own way.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Both pictures show people spending time outdoors, but the experiences could not be more different. In the first picture, four hikers in blue and yellow jackets are making their way down a steep, rocky slope. They carry backpacks and walking poles, and a thick layer of white cloud lies far below them, which shows that they have climbed very high. In the second picture, a family of four is strolling along a beach with turquoise water behind them. The parents and their two children all wear matching white T-shirts printed with a blue cartoon shark, black shorts, sunglasses and straw hats, and they are holding hands as they walk towards the camera. One picture is about effort and adventure, while the other is about rest and fun in the sun. Both groups seem to be enjoying their holiday, just at very different speeds.

groups.question: Do you think adults should keep learning new things? Why?

extra_data.sampleAnswer: Last winter I decided to learn to swim properly, at the slightly embarrassing age of twenty-eight. I had grown up near a river, but I had never done much more than splash about. So I signed up for lessons at a public pool near my office, twice a week at half past six in the morning. I bought a pair of goggles and a cheap swimming cap. My instructor was a former competitive swimmer in his fifties, and he had no patience for excuses. That turned out to be exactly what I needed. The first month was miserable, and I will not pretend otherwise. I felt clumsy, I swallowed a lot of chlorinated water, and children half my size were overtaking me in the next lane. What kept me going was a small improvement each week that nobody else noticed. One extra length, or one breath taken without panicking. By March I could swim continuously for half an hour. That change from frustration to competence was genuinely addictive. On whether adults should keep learning, absolutely, and not only for their careers, although updating your skills clearly matters. The bigger benefit is what learning does to your character. Being a beginner forces you to be humble and to accept looking foolish, and adults get very little practice at that. It also keeps the mind flexible. The older people I admire most are the ones still asking questions, not the ones who stopped at forty.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: About six months ago I learned to swim, at twenty-eight years old. I always felt shy about this, because most of my friends can swim. So I paid for lessons at a public pool near my office. I also bought goggles and a cheap swimming cap. The water was very cold in December. I went there twice a week, early in the morning before work. My teacher was an old man, and he was very strict with me. The first month was hard and I felt stupid. I drank a lot of water and my arms hurt. Small children in the next lane swam faster than me. I wanted to stop after the third lesson. But every week I could swim a little further. That small progress made me happy, so I did not give up. Now I can swim for thirty minutes without stopping. I'd say adults should definitely keep learning new things. The world changes fast, so we need new skills for our jobs. Learning also keeps our mind fresh and young. For example, my father learned to use a smartphone at sixty. Now he sends me photos every week. So I plan to learn something new every year. Now I swim there every Saturday morning.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: A fortnight ago I finally sorted out my mother's health insurance renewal, and I did the whole thing on my phone. I was sitting on the sofa at home. Before that, it would have meant a morning queuing at an office in District 3 with a folder of photocopies. Instead I logged into the portal, uploaded a photo of her card and paid by banking app. The confirmation email arrived within about twenty minutes. My mother, who is sixty-two, still does not quite believe it counts as official unless somebody stamps a piece of paper. Doing it that way felt slightly unreal, and I kept expecting something to go wrong. When the confirmation arrived I actually rang the insurance hotline to check it was genuine. That probably says more about me than about the system. Mostly, though, I felt relieved, because that job had been sitting on my list for weeks purely because I dreaded the queue. The benefits of handling everyday tasks online are obvious. The first one is time, since a whole morning became twenty minutes and I did not have to ask for leave. There is the cost as well, because I saved the fuel and the photocopying. Everything leaves a record too, so the receipt sits on my phone rather than in a drawer somewhere. Beyond that, it opens services to people who cannot easily travel, which matters a lot for the elderly.

I even called the hotline to check that it was real. The woman on the phone said everything was fine. My mother did not believe it without a paper and a stamp. So I printed the email for her, and then she was happy. After that, I felt very glad, because I saved a whole morning. The internet has clear benefits for these small tasks. First, you save a lot of time and money. Then, you can do it at night or at the weekend. Also, you keep a clear record on your phone. For example, I can find that email in five seconds. extra_data.sampleAnswer: The longest wait I can remember was for my visa results in 2021, when I applied for a two-week training programme in Singapore. The embassy said it would take ten working days. In the end it took nearly six weeks, because everything was still disrupted after the pandemic. My flight was already booked and my manager had approved the leave. There was nothing I could do except refresh an online tracking page that never changed. I even rang the embassy twice, and nobody could tell me anything. During that period I was much worse company than usual. I was irritable with my flatmate and I could not concentrate on ordinary tasks. I also kept planning two versions of my future at once, which is exhausting. What I found hardest was not the delay but the silence. If somebody had simply told me it would take six weeks, I could have accepted it. Not knowing is far worse than bad news. Are we less patient than before? I suspect so, though I would not blame people for it. Technology has trained us to expect instant results. Food in twenty minutes, films with no adverts, answers in one second. So any delay now feels like a fault rather than a normal part of life. My parents spent hours queuing for basic goods and thought nothing of it. My advice is to keep yourself busy while you wait, because patience is a skill you practise.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: My family and I waited a long time for my visa result in 2021. I applied for a short training course in Singapore. I applied in March and paid the fee online. The course was only two weeks long. The office said ten working days, but it took six weeks. My flight was already booked, and my manager gave me the days off. Every morning I opened the website, but there was no new information. My mother asked me about it every evening. While I was waiting, I felt worried and tired all the time. I could not concentrate on my normal work at the office. I was also not very kind to my flatmate that month. The hardest part was not the delay, but the silence. Nobody told me anything, so I made two plans in my head. I'd say people today are less patient, because everything is fast now. My advice is simple. Do not check your phone every hour, because that makes you nervous. Keep yourself busy with work or sport while you wait. Also, ask for a clear date, so you can plan. That advice really helped my sister last month. I finally got the visa in May.
