question_text: How did you feel while you were reading it?
What types of people live in these places?
explanation: People who live near pine forests are often those who enjoy a quiet lifestyle and nature. Some may work in forestry, tourism, farming, or environmental protection. They are usually used to cool weather and outdoor life. In desert areas, people must be strong and adaptable because the weather is very hot and dry. They may work in tourism, animal raising, mining, or small businesses that serve travelers every day.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: People who live near pine forests are often those who enjoy a quiet lifestyle and nature. Some may work in forestry, tourism, farming, or environmental protection. They are usually used to cool weather and outdoor life. In desert areas, people must be strong and adaptable because the weather is very hot and dry. They may work in tourism, animal raising, mining, or small businesses that serve travelers every day.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Different kinds of patience, I'd say. Around a pine forest you find people who work with wood, run guesthouses, or grow vegetables. Many of those families have lived there for generations. Desert communities are usually smaller and more mobile. They keep animals, guide travellers, or trade along the routes, and their whole day is planned around water and heat. Heat and cold shape work in opposite ways. Both groups know their land far better than any visitor. Their skills come from the landscape itself.

question_text: What did you enjoy most about taking part in it?
What did you enjoy most about the new routine?
How do most people in your country learn about world news?
explanation: In my country, there are many ways to learn about world news. You can watch or read the news online, you can read a newspaper, and you can listen to the radio. I think the most popular way of receiving news is online. There are many websites, but you can also get news through social media like Twitter and Facebook. It's very convenient for me. This can be improved step by step if people make small changes and choose practical solutions.

extra_data.imageDesc: Người đàn ông mặc vest cầm tờ báo đứng trước bức tường nhiều màn hình TV
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: In my country, there are many ways to learn about world news. You can watch or read the news online, you can read a newspaper, and you can listen to the radio. I think the most popular way of receiving news is online. There are many websites, but you can also get news through social media like Facebook and TikTok. It's very convenient because people can read the news on their phones anywhere, even on the bus. Older people, like my grandparents, still prefer to watch the news on TV at seven in the evening. So young people use their phones and older people use TV, but almost everyone knows about big world events on the same day.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: These days it's almost entirely through their phones. My generation gets it from Facebook and increasingly from TikTok, which I'm not proud of. You end up reading a serious headline over a piece of background music. Older people still watch the seven o'clock bulletin, and my grandfather has bought the same paper for thirty years. So two people in one house can have completely different pictures of the world. I'd trust almost none of it without first checking against a second, slower source.

question_text: How did you feel while you were working on it?
How do people learn to cook in your culture?
explanation: Most people learn cooking from family - parents or grandparents are the first teachers. They pass down traditional recipes, and it's usually a mix of watching, helping out, and eventually doing it yourself. Some learn by trial and error, experimenting with food at home. Nowadays, cooking shows, YouTube tutorials, and food blogs are very popular ways to pick up new skills or explore different cuisines. Schools sometimes offer cooking classes, too. It's a blend of tradition, curiosity, and adapting to modern resources.

extra_data.imageDesc: Người mẹ và bốn đứa trẻ đội mũ đầu bếp đang làm bánh trong bếp
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Most people learn cooking from family - parents or grandparents are the first teachers. They pass down traditional recipes, and it's usually a mix of watching, helping out, and eventually doing it yourself. Some learn by trial and error, experimenting with food at home. Nowadays, cooking shows, YouTube tutorials, and food blogs are very popular ways to pick up new skills or explore different cuisines. Schools sometimes offer cooking classes, too. It's a blend of tradition, curiosity, and adapting to modern resources.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: In my family it happened by standing nearby and being given jobs. Nobody explained anything; my grandmother would hand me the garlic and expect it to be finished. Recipes weren't written down, so you learnt by taste and by getting it wrong at Tet. My mother would say I still can't season properly, and she'd be right. That has changed for my generation. Most of my friends have learnt from YouTube, which is faster but flatter. You can copy a dish and not understand it.

I also love the quiet atmosphere because it is far from the busy traffic of the city center. The market and shops are close, so daily life is convenient. Beyond that, there's a woman selling banh mi who has remembered my order since 2021. Small recognitions like that make a big city feel manageable. I'd miss her more than the flat.

question_text: How do children go to school in your country?
explanation: In my country, children go to school in different ways. Some children walk to school if they live nearby, especially in small towns or villages. Others are taken by their parents on motorbikes or in cars. In big cities, some students use school buses or public buses, especially when the school is far from home. The choice depends on distance, family schedule, and traffic conditions. Parents usually choose the safest and most convenient way for their children.

School buses have appeared in the last ten years, though mainly at private schools that charge for them. In Hanoi the choice comes down to whose working hours are flexible.

question_text: Do you think walking is important?
explanation: Yes, walking is important because it keeps people active without costing money. We do not need special skills or expensive equipment to walk. It can improve physical health, support mental health, and reduce stress. Walking is also better for the environment when people use it for short distances. I think even ten or twenty minutes of walking each day can make a difference.

Beyond health, walking is when I actually think, whereas at my desk I mostly react to messages. Doctors have said for years that short daily walks help, and my own sleep clearly improves whenever I keep it up for a fortnight.

question_text: What are the benefits of growing a garden?
explanation: Growing a garden has many wonderful benefits. First, it allows people to have fresh vegetables, herbs, or beautiful flowers at home. I started with three pots and killed two, and even that taught me something. Patience is the real crop here. Nothing grows on your schedule.

extra_data.title: Consumer age

headings.text: Important lessons for all of us

paragraphs.text: In today's modern consumer age, people tend to own more than they used to. A worker only has 5-6 pairs of shoes in his entire life. And he will repair them when they break or wear out, not throw them away. Nowadays, if we have a phone, it is expected that you will use such electronic devices throughout your life.

Mrs. Judith Levine - a journalist and her husband decided to change their lifestyle to be as minimalist as possible. They only buy what is absolutely necessary, such as food for work. They do not go to the cinema, cafes, restaurants. As a writer, I can say that she is saving for a purpose of publishing her findings as a book.

To make this experiment as realistic as possible, Ms. Levine and her husband decided not to tell anyone, because they knew that once their friends knew about this plan, they would mention the issue of paying for the couple's share when they went out together. Therefore, the couple was determined to keep it a secret from friends, family and strangers.

Published in 2006, the book Not Buying It when reread 10 years later still holds its value. They believe that journalist Ms. Levine has the ability to predict future consumer trends. The minimalist lifestyle she mentioned has become a trend today.

The couple wanted to buy a gift as a gift. However, that went against their point of not buying unnecessary things. And they decided to make it themselves to have a lower spending level. However, none of them have any aesthetic talent, so they finally decided to give a meaningful and practical gift to the recipient, which is a piece of their jewelry.
Ms. Levine does not have an office, which is quite inconvenient when she has to meet partners in a coffee shop. When working alone, she often goes to the public library and finds it very convenient.
Lessons about minimalism in today's consumer trends: buy things that are really necessary, switch from driving cars and motorbikes to cycling and walking.

question_text: Digital
options: Redefining Leisure in the Digital era
Enhancing connectivity with mobile apps
Promoting essential digital literacy
Risks of Excessive Screen-Based Entertainment
Concerns About Data Privacy
Building Inclusive and Respectful Online Communities
Prioritize human-friendly designs
explanation:
1. Heading: Redefining Leisure in the Digital era Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói rằng thời gian giải trí không còn chỉ gắn với trò chơi ngoài trời, sách hay gặp gỡ trực tiếp, mà đã được định nghĩa lại trong bối cảnh kỹ thuật số. Vietnamese translation: Trong thế giới thay đổi nhanh hiện nay, thời gian rảnh không còn chỉ được gắn với trò chơi ngoài trời, sách hay những buổi gặp mặt trực tiếp. Cùng với sự phát triển của điện thoại thông minh, dịch vụ streaming và mạng xã hội, con người ngày nay dành phần lớn thời gian giải trí trên mạng. Sự chuyển dịch này không chỉ thay đổi cách mọi người thư giãn mà còn ảnh hưởng đến cách họ kết nối, học hỏi và giải trí.
2. Heading: Enhancing connectivity with mobile apps Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nhấn mạnh rằng ứng dụng di động đã thay đổi cách mọi người liên lạc và giúp họ kết nối tức thì với bạn bè, gia đình và đồng nghiệp. Vietnamese translation: Ứng dụng di động đã thay đổi cách mọi người giao tiếp và giữ liên lạc. Thông qua nền tảng nhắn tin, cuộc gọi video và ứng dụng mạng xã hội, người dùng có thể lập tức kết nối với bạn bè, gia đình và đồng nghiệp bất kể khoảng cách. Những công cụ này làm cho việc giao tiếp trở nên nhanh hơn, tiện lợi hơn và có tính tương tác hơn bao giờ hết.
3. Heading: Promoting essential digital literacy Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn khẳng định rằng digital literacy giúp con người tiếp cận thông tin, đánh giá nội dung trực tuyến và tự bảo vệ mình, nên đó là kỹ năng số thiết yếu. Vietnamese translation: Khi công nghệ số trở thành một phần trung tâm của cuộc sống hiện đại, khả năng sử dụng thiết bị và nền tảng trực tuyến một cách hiệu quả ngày càng quan trọng. Hiểu biết số giúp mọi người tiếp cận thông tin, đánh giá nội dung trên mạng, giao tiếp có trách nhiệm và tự bảo vệ mình trước tin sai lệch cũng như các rủi ro trực tuyến. Hiện nay, đây được xem là kỹ năng thiết yếu cho học tập, công việc và cuộc sống hàng ngày.
4. Heading: Risks of Excessive Screen-Based Entertainment Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cảnh báo rằng giải trí quá nhiều qua màn hình có thể giảm vận động, làm rối loạn giấc ngủ và hạn chế tương tác xã hội ngoài đời thực. Vietnamese translation: Mặc dù giải trí qua màn hình như chơi game, xem streaming và sử dụng mạng xã hội có thể rất thú vị, việc dành quá nhiều thời gian cho những hoạt động này có thể gây ra tác động tiêu cực. Sử dụng màn hình quá mức có thể làm giảm hoạt động thể chất, gây rối loạn giấc ngủ và hạn chế tương tác xã hội trong đời sống thật. Vì lý do đó, nhiều người lo ngại về việc cân bằng giải trí kỹ thuật số với những thói quen lành mạnh hơn.
5. Heading: Concerns About Data Privacy Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói rõ rằng nhiều người lo lắng về cách dữ liệu cá nhân của họ bị thu thập, lưu trữ và sử dụng trên các nền tảng số. Vietnamese translation: Khi ngày càng nhiều thông tin cá nhân được chia sẻ trên mạng, nhiều người dùng bắt đầu lo ngại về cách dữ liệu của họ bị thu thập, lưu trữ và sử dụng. Ứng dụng di động, website và các nền tảng mạng xã hội thường theo dõi hành vi người dùng, đôi khi không có sự đồng ý rõ ràng hoặc giải thích đầy đủ. Những thực hành này đã làm dấy lên những câu hỏi nghiêm túc về bảo mật, tính minh bạch và việc bảo vệ quyền riêng tư cá nhân.
6. Heading: Building Inclusive and Respectful Online Communities Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nhấn mạnh rằng không gian mạng chỉ thật sự hữu ích khi người dùng tương tác với nhau một cách tôn trọng, bao dung và hỗ trợ. Vietnamese translation: Internet kết nối con người từ nhiều bối cảnh, nền văn hóa và góc nhìn khác nhau, tạo ra cơ hội hợp tác và thấu hiểu lẫn nhau. Tuy nhiên, không gian trực tuyến chỉ thật sự có lợi khi người dùng giao tiếp theo cách tôn trọng và hỗ trợ. Việc khuyến khích sự tử tế, bao dung và giao tiếp có trách nhiệm là điều thiết yếu để xây dựng những cộng đồng trực tuyến hòa nhập và tôn trọng lẫn nhau.
7. Heading: Prioritize human-friendly designs Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn tập trung vào việc nhà thiết kế nên tạo ra hệ thống đơn giản, dễ tiếp cận và thoải mái, đồng thời tính đến nhu cầu, khả năng và trải nghiệm của người dùng. Vietnamese translation: Khi phát triển các nền tảng và công nghệ số, nhà thiết kế nên tập trung tạo ra những hệ thống đơn giản, dễ tiếp cận và thoải mái cho con người sử dụng. Thiết kế thân thiện với con người xem xét nhu cầu, khả năng và trải nghiệm của người dùng, qua đó làm cho công nghệ trở nên hòa nhập hơn và ít gây ức chế hơn. Cách tiếp cận này giúp bảo đảm công cụ số phục vụ con người một cách hiệu quả thay vì làm họ bị quá tải.

extra_data.title: Digital

headings.text: Redefining Leisure in the Digital era
Building Inclusive and Respectful Online Communities

paragraphs.text: In today's fast-changing world, free time is no longer defined only by outdoor games, books, or face-to-face gatherings. With the rise of smartphones, streaming services, and social media, people now spend much of their leisure time online. This shift has changed not only how people relax, but also how they connect, learn, and entertain themselves.

Mobile applications have transformed the way people communicate and stay in touch. Through messaging platforms, video calls, and social networking apps, users can instantly connect with friends, family, and coworkers regardless of distance. These tools make communication faster, more convenient, and more interactive than ever before.

As digital technology becomes a central part of modern life, the ability to use devices and online platforms effectively is increasingly important. Digital literacy helps people access information, evaluate online content, communicate responsibly, and protect themselves from misinformation and online risks. It is now considered an essential skill for education, work, and daily living.

Although screen-based entertainment such as gaming, streaming, and social media can be enjoyable, spending too much time on these activities may have negative effects. Excessive screen use can reduce physical activity, disrupt sleep patterns, and limit real-life social interaction. For this reason, many people are concerned about balancing digital entertainment with healthier habits.

As more personal information is shared online, many users have become worried about how their data is collected, stored, and used. Mobile apps, websites, and social platforms often track user behavior, sometimes without clear consent or explanation. These practices have raised serious questions about security, transparency, and the protection of personal privacy.

The internet connects people from different backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives, creating opportunities for collaboration and understanding. However, online spaces can only be truly beneficial when users interact in respectful and supportive ways. Encouraging kindness, tolerance, and responsible communication is essential for building inclusive and respectful online communities.

When developing digital platforms and technologies, designers should focus on creating systems that are simple, accessible, and comfortable for people to use. Human-friendly designs take into account users' needs, abilities, and experiences, making technology more inclusive and less frustrating. This approach helps ensure that digital tools serve people effectively rather than overwhelming them.

2. "finds their childhood games simpler" → Odilia: game hồi nhỏ "The rules were straightforward and easy to understand", còn game bây giờ "I have to think very hard every time we play".
3. "preferred reading books when they were a child" → Jan: "I had plenty of books, and the stories really gripped me... completely lost in a book". Bẫy: Shelly cũng được mẹ đưa sách nhưng "I didn't like sitting still and reading".
4. "wished to be outside more as a child" → Shelly: thích ra ngoài chơi nhưng trời hay mưa, "I would look gloomily out of the window and hope it would stop". Bẫy: Jan cũng ít ra ngoài nhưng không hề mong muốn ("I still don't go out a lot now").
5. "likes playing with their children" → Odilia: "I play board games with them... we laugh a lot while we do it".
6. "enjoyed doing arts as a child" → Shelly: "she gave me some pencils and paints instead... I couldn't stop drawing for hours". Bẫy: bố mẹ Jan muốn Jan học vẽ nhưng Jan "wasn't interested in it at all".
7. "enjoyed playing with other children in the past" → Chris: "I loved going outside to play with my peers. We just chased each other around". Bẫy: Odilia cũng chơi cùng người khác nhưng là chơi với CON của mình, không phải bạn hồi nhỏ.
👉 Mẹo: dạng 4 người luôn có một người "gần đúng" làm nhiễu. Phân biệt ai THÍCH thật với ai chỉ ĐƯỢC ĐƯA CHO hoặc BỊ BẮT làm.

people.name: Odilia
people.text: When I was a child, I would spend hours playing board games. The rules were straightforward and easy to understand. Now that I have children of my own, I want to distract them from using computers, so I play board games with them. I really struggle with the new ones, though. There are a lot of characters to remember and many choices to make, and I have to think very hard every time we play — even though we laugh a lot while we do it.

people.name: Chris
people.text: I was very lucky to grow up in a place with good weather. I loved going outside to play with my peers. We just chased each other around. If we had a ball, we would play football, and if we didn't, we would play catch until it got dark. Having had that experience, I find it hard to be alone even now, and some of those children are still my friends today.

people.name: Jan
people.text: I was unable to go outside much when I was little, and I still don't go out a lot now. I had plenty of books, and the stories really gripped me. My parents wanted me to do art, but I wasn't interested in it at all. There was a library near my house, and I could spend hours there, completely lost in a book. These days I really enjoy playing games, because I get so involved in them.

people.name: Shelly
people.text: When I was young, I loved going outside to play with my friends. When it rained, which it often did, I would look gloomily out of the window and hope it would stop. On days like that, my mother used to give me books, but I didn't like sitting still and reading. Then she gave me some pencils and paints instead. I realised that I was actually quite good at it, and I couldn't stop drawing for hours.

question_text: The Arrival of the Four-Day Work Week
options: A way of life now out of date
Benefits for employees
Undesirable financial consequences
Unforeseen challenges for employees
Difficult to change old habits
An unfair plan for some people
Alternative solutions worth considering
Businesses preparing for a new policy
explanation:
--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
1. "A way of life now out of date" → Henry Ford cắt từ 48 xuống 40 giờ tạo ra tuần 5 ngày, nhưng "what once looked progressive is no longer the norm for 21st-century workers" — nếp cũ đã lỗi thời.
2. "Benefits for employees" → cả đoạn là lợi ích cho nhân viên: "higher job satisfaction, lower stress", "balance work with personal life", chia sẻ việc chăm con.
3. "Undesirable financial consequences" → toàn số liệu tiền bạc của doanh nghiệp: "output falling by as much as 20%", "sharp rise in running costs", "pushes up spending on wages, training and supervision".
4. "Unforeseen challenges for employees" → những cái KHÔNG NGỜ xảy ra với chính người lao động: tưởng vui hơn nhưng "satisfaction settles back to where it started" (hedonic treadmill), rồi "working faster is how accidents happen", "more strained than they were on the old schedule". Không chọn "An unfair plan" vì đoạn này không so sánh nhóm nào được lợi hơn nhóm nào.
5. "Difficult to change old habits" → dù được nghỉ, người ta vẫn quay về nếp cũ: "some employees drifted back to the factory floor of their own accord", "others picked up a second job to fill the hours". Không chọn "Undesirable financial consequences" vì heading đó đã dùng cho đoạn 3 và đoạn 3 nói về tiền của doanh nghiệp, còn đây là thói quen của cá nhân.
6. "An unfair plan for some people" → nhân viên văn phòng được lợi còn "teachers gain nothing", bác sĩ y tá "how can doctors and nurses work any less?", lính cứu hoả vẫn phải trực; câu chốt "widening the gap between one kind of work and another" = bất công. Không chọn "Unforeseen challenges" vì đoạn này không nói về hậu quả bất ngờ, mà nói về ai được ai không.
7. "Alternative solutions worth considering" → đoạn liệt kê 3 cách khác thay cho tuần 4 ngày: "Raising basic pay", "Improving social welfare", "Adding more public holidays".
Nhiễu: "Businesses preparing for a new policy" — không đoạn nào nói doanh nghiệp đang chuẩn bị áp dụng chính sách; đoạn 3 chỉ nói doanh nghiệp bị tốn tiền.
👉 Mẹo: heading có "unfair" → tìm đoạn so sánh nhóm này được / nhóm kia không (đoạn 6). Heading có "challenges" → tìm đoạn nói hậu quả xấu xảy ra với chính người áp dụng (đoạn 4). Heading "old habits" → tìm hành động quay về cách cũ (đoạn 5).

extra_data.title: The Arrival of the Four-Day Work Week

headings.text: An unfair plan for some people
A way of life now out of date
Businesses preparing for a new policy

paragraphs.text: Proponents of the four-day workweek argue that shortening the working week is both realistic and overdue. History, they say, is on their side. During the era of industrialization, the car magnate Henry Ford cut his factories' schedule from 48 hours down to 40, without touching wages - a move that helped establish the five-day pattern still followed in most workplaces today. Yet what once looked progressive is no longer the norm for 21st-century workers. As technology and science advance, a growing number of jobs no longer require workers to be physically present in the office five days a week.

The clearest gains, advocates say, are felt by employees themselves. Workers report higher job satisfaction, lower stress and stronger motivation to contribute. An extra day off makes it easier to balance work with personal life, leaving room to care for family, rest properly or take up interests outside the office. Advocates also point to a wider effect at home: with an extra day free, employees can share the childcare that in many households falls almost entirely on their wives, who often have to give up employment and the chance to pursue a profession of their own. Others are unconvinced, arguing that child-care facilities can already handle this perfectly well.

The financial side is where doubts surface most quickly. When Japanese firms began trimming their schedules in the late 1980s, following a nationwide push to bring working hours down, some reported output falling by as much as 20% over the first year, along with a sharp rise in running costs. Companies in retail and hospitality face a particular difficulty, since their doors have to stay open whether or not staff numbers are cut. Covering those hours usually means taking on extra people, which pushes up spending on wages, training and supervision. For a small firm, these extra costs alone can be enough to rule the idea out.

Supporters argue that shorter hours simply make people happier. Others call that claim unfounded, pointing to the hedonic treadmill - the tendency for satisfaction to settle back to where it started, so that within months workers drift back to their usual level of contentment no matter how long or short their week has become. Worse, a shorter week may not even deliver the relief people expect. One French company recorded a rise in productivity after cutting its hours, though sceptics suspect the gain did not last. Fewer hours means working faster, and working faster is how accidents happen. Rushing through the same volume of tasks in less time can prove deeply stress-inducing, leaving employees more strained than they were on the old schedule.

There is the question of income. Fewer hours on the clock can mean a smaller income, and for workers on modest wages that difference matters. Others find the empty day harder to fill than they imagined, and boredom sets in when there is little to occupy them. Where shorter weeks have been tried on a national scale, the results have been telling: some employees drifted back to the factory floor of their own accord, while others picked up a second job to fill the hours they had just been given.

Not every job can bend that way. Office staff may do well out of a shorter week, but many roles simply cannot work like that. Schools stay open on the same timetable and students still have to be taught, so teachers gain nothing. Hospitals take in the same number of patients whether the week is four days or five, so how can doctors and nurses work any less? Fires still break out and emergencies still happen, and firefighters have to be there when they do. Crime rates do not fall just because the working week is shorter. Critics warn that a change like this would help those who are already comfortable and leave everyone else where they are, widening the gap between one kind of work and another.

Many people remain convinced that the case for cutting working hours is unfounded, and point instead to other ways of reaching the same goal. Raising basic pay would leave workers better off without touching the timetable at all. Improving social welfare - better healthcare, childcare and pensions - would ease the pressure on households more directly than an extra day at home. Adding more public holidays to the national calendar would give everyone extra rest without asking a single business to restructure the way it operates. Each of these, supporters argue, delivers what a shorter week promises while avoiding the problems it creates.

extra_data.title: Doggett’s coat and badge

headings.text: Not in it for the money
Origins of what the winner receives

paragraphs.text: In the early 18th century, London’s roads were often muddy, overcrowded, and difficult to travel on. As a result, the River Thames served as the main “highway” through the city. People frequently used water taxis-small boats rowed by trained professionals called watermen-to move around quickly. These water journeys were not only faster but often safer than traveling by road. For many Londoners, taking a boat was the most efficient way to attend work, markets, or social events. The Doggett’s race, therefore, celebrates not just rowing skill, but the essential role that watermen played in daily life during that time.

The Doggett’s Coat and Badge race was established in 1715 by Thomas Doggett, an Irish actor and theatre manager, who became well known in London. According to popular accounts, Doggett once narrowly escaped drowning while traveling on the River Thames. To express his gratitude for the boatman who saved him and to honor the newly crowned King George I, he created this race. It was open to young watermen who had recently completed their apprenticeships, giving them a chance to demonstrate their rowing skills. Over time, this event became not just a tribute to a personal event, but a long-standing tradition that celebrates both history and the craft of rowing on the Thames.

The prize awarded to the winner of the Doggett’s Coat and Badge race is unlike any ordinary trophy. Instead of money or medals, the champion receives a traditional red coat and a silver badge. These items are deeply symbolic and represent the pride and respect historically associated with watermen. Each piece is custom-made for the winner and presented in a formal ceremony that highlights the cultural importance of the event. The coat reflects 18th-century styles, while the badge often includes royal imagery and references to the Thames. This unique reward continues to connect the modern race with its historical roots and honors the profession’s heritage.

Although the Doggett’s race remains one of the oldest sporting events in the world, some have raised concerns about its future. With modern boats, technology, and shifting interests among younger generations, participation has declined in recent decades. Suggestions have been made to modernize the race to keep it relevant-perhaps by changing the route, updating the boats, or increasing promotion on social media. Others argue that preserving tradition is more important than making it popular. This ongoing discussion reflects broader challenges faced by many traditional events in the modern world: how to honor the past while adapting to the present.

Winning the Doggett’s Coat and Badge race is not just about rowing fast-it’s about gaining respect within a close-knit community. For many, this competition represents an important rite of passage. It is often the first time a newly qualified waterman competes on such a historic stage. Success in the race can lead to recognition, offers from exclusive rowing clubs, and opportunities to participate in ceremonial roles along the Thames. Even those who do not win often benefit from simply being involved. The reputation built through this race can carry weight throughout a rower’s career, especially in London’s traditional maritime circles.

One of the most heartwarming aspects of the Doggett’s race is its multi-generational appeal. In several families, competing in the race is a proud tradition passed from one generation to the next. It’s not uncommon to hear stories of grandfathers, fathers, and sons all having taken part over the years. Some families even have multiple winners across decades. These personal connections add emotional depth to the event and preserve its history in living memory. For these families, the race is more than a competition-it’s a legacy. The bond between relatives strengthens as they share stories, train together, and wear the symbolic red coat with pride.

Unlike many modern sports competitions, the Doggett’s Coat and Badge race offers no financial reward. The red coat and silver badge have cultural and emotional value, but not monetary. Contestants take part out of pride, tradition, and a deep respect for the waterman’s profession. Many dedicate months to training, not for riches but for the honor of winning one of Britain’s most historic races. The lack of financial incentive may even enhance the race’s prestige, showing that commitment to heritage and community can outweigh commercial interests. In today’s world, that kind of motivation stands out as truly admirable.

extra_data.title: Coffee

headings.text: A remedy of unjust revenue distribution
Coffee encourages the art of conversation
A habit that has become a big economy
Health risks versus health benefits debate
The custom of coffee drinking begins to spread

paragraphs.text: The custom of drinking coffee has been around for a long time, perhaps as long as 1500 years ago. There were times when drinking coffee was banned in many places. At that time, coffee houses were opened in some places in Egypt and Ethiopia. Later, the custom of drinking coffee spread to Italy and all over Europe. Not long after that, the Dutch introduced coffee to Asia. Later, the habit of drinking coffee became popular all over the world.

Coffee was first used in Africa but Europe is known as the largest coffee consuming region in the world. In the 18th century, many people from different professions such as writers, philosophers and politicians used coffee to stay awake during discussions and meetings. Coffee houses became meeting places for people to share ideas and debate hot topics in society. These places made it easy for people to share their intellectual thoughts and played an important role in business and society at that time.

Nowadays, many people have the habit of drinking coffee in the morning to wake up, or going to coffee shops in the evening to meet and socialize with each other. Coffee shops are popping up everywhere, providing places for people to relax and talk to each other. Coffee has become a global business, with personal coffee makers even appearing in households. Famous global coffee brands have become giant companies, using their brands and communication strategies to attract millions of coffee lovers around the world.

Coffee consumption in Europe accounts for about 90% of global coffee production, making it the largest market in the world. Meanwhile, some other countries in Africa such as Egypt and Ethiopia rely heavily on coffee exports to sustain their economies. However, there is a problem of injustice: workers in these African countries face terrible living and working conditions, with incomes as low as $1 a day. While wealthy European countries make huge profits from coffee, people in coffee-growing countries do not receive a fair share of their efforts and hard work.

To address this injustice, certification schemes for agricultural production have been introduced. If coffee meets certain certification standards, it can be sold at fair prices, preventing growers from having to sell at rock-bottom prices. However, there are problems with this solution. In reality, only about 5% of coffee meets the standards. Many small coffee producers in developing countries are too poor to pay the certification fees, leaving them even further behind in the global coffee market.

There is much debate about the effects of coffee on human health. It is true that coffee can help many people stay awake and concentrate. It contains antioxidants, which can help prevent diseases. But while drinking coffee, people often add sugar and milk and these can be harmful to your health. This can easily cause diseases such as diabetes or obesity for those who use it.

There is a legend about coffee. In the past, a monk observed that birds became more active and lively when they ate a small fruit. The monk then drank the juice from the fruit and stayed awake praying and talking until late at night. So it can be said that thanks to these birds, people knew about the coffee plant.

extra_data.title: Early Australia

headings.text: Technology helps uncover the ocean’s secret
A new evidence that leads to speculation
Determination of the explorers through the ages

paragraphs.text: Some researchers are rethinking the traditional narrative of how Australia was settled. While it is widely believed that the first people arrived via land bridges from Southeast Asia during the Ice Age, new theories suggest otherwise. Alternative histories propose that early humans may have used rudimentary boats to cross from distant shores far earlier than previously estimated. These claims are controversial but are supported by some archaeological findings and oral traditions of Indigenous communities. Such ideas challenge the Eurocentric view of exploration and emphasize the ingenuity of early seafarers long before written records existed.

The vast Australian outback and its harsh deserts have long posed a formidable challenge to resettlement and development. For thousands of years, the central areas of the continent were difficult to inhabit due to extreme heat, scarce water sources, and isolation. Even after European arrival, these natural barriers prevented deeper exploration and settlement for decades. Today, the environment still remains an obstacle, limiting infrastructure, agriculture, and population growth in these regions. The Australian landscape, while beautiful and iconic, continues to shape the way communities are formed and connected.

Advancements in marine technology have revolutionized our understanding of ancient migration routes to Australia. Underwater sonar mapping and satellite imaging have revealed submerged land masses and potential seafaring paths once used by early humans. Archaeologists are now uncovering tools and fossils deep beneath coastal waters, which provide new insights into how long ago people arrived on the continent. These discoveries would not be possible without modern equipment that allows exploration of areas previously inaccessible. As research continues, scientists hope to fill in many historical gaps that have puzzled historians for centuries.

It is now widely believed that the journey to Australia wasn't completed in one go. Instead, early humans likely reached the continent in stages, moving through island chains and coastal areas over generations. This theory is supported by the distribution of artifacts and remains across Southeast Asia and Northern Australia. The idea of gradual migration, rather than a single wave, helps explain the diversity of early populations found on the continent. This step-by-step approach also reflects how ancient peoples adapted to different environments as they moved closer to the Australian mainland.

In recent years, new evidence has emerged from both land and sea, prompting scientists to re-evaluate earlier assumptions. A set of ancient tools discovered in a Northern Territory cave doesn't match previously known Aboriginal designs, leading some to speculate about earlier migrations or even contact with other civilizations. Additionally, genetic studies hint at complex interactions with now-extinct human species. These findings, while not yet definitive, open the door to exciting discussions and possibilities about Australia's earliest human history.

Many of the first explorers to attempt crossing Australia's interior were ill-prepared for the harsh conditions they encountered. Without sufficient knowledge of the land or survival skills in such a hostile environment, numerous expeditions ended in tragedy. The lack of understanding of the Aboriginal methods of finding water, navigating terrain, and managing heat led to avoidable suffering. It wasn't until later that European settlers began to adapt, learning from Indigenous Australians how to travel and survive in such an unfamiliar landscape.

Despite the many difficulties, both ancient and modern explorers showed incredible perseverance in reaching and understanding Australia. Whether navigating unknown seas in simple rafts or trekking across searing deserts with limited supplies, their determination pushed the boundaries of what was thought possible. Stories of survival and discovery continue to inspire awe, reminding us of the strength and courage required to explore the unknown. Through the centuries, this spirit of exploration has become a core part of Australian history and identity.

question_text: Cultural Exchange
options: Redefining Global Cultural Understanding
Encouraging Cross-Cultural Festivals
Promoting Language Exchange Programs
Overemphasis on Commercial Tourism
Concerns About Cultural Preservation
Building Mutual Respect Among Communities
Focusing on Authentic Cultural Experiences
explanation:
1. Heading: Redefining Global Cultural Understanding Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cho thấy quá trình giao thoa văn hóa trong bối cảnh toàn cầu hóa đang thay đổi cách con người hiểu về văn hóa trên toàn thế giới. Vietnamese translation: Toàn cầu hóa đã thay đổi cách con người hiểu về văn hóa trên khắp thế giới. Ngày nay, giao lưu văn hóa cho phép mỗi cá nhân khám phá phong tục, niềm tin và giá trị vượt ra ngoài xã hội của chính mình. Quá trình này giúp định hình lại cách hiểu văn hóa toàn cầu bằng cách khuyến khích sự cởi mở, tính hiếu kỳ và nhận thức sâu sắc hơn về sự đa dạng trong đời sống hiện đại.
2. Heading: Encouraging Cross-Cultural Festivals Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói về các sự kiện quốc tế kết hợp âm nhạc, ẩm thực, nghệ thuật và truyền thống từ nhiều quốc gia để tôn vinh sự đa dạng và kết nối. Vietnamese translation: Nhiều cộng đồng hiện nay tổ chức các sự kiện quốc tế để tôn vinh sự đa dạng và sự kết nối. Những buổi gặp gỡ này quy tụ âm nhạc, ẩm thực, nghệ thuật và truyền thống từ nhiều quốc gia khác nhau. Bằng cách khuyến khích các lễ hội giao thoa văn hóa, xã hội tạo ra cơ hội để mọi người trân trọng sự khác biệt, tăng cường quan hệ và thúc đẩy sự hòa hợp giữa các nhóm văn hóa.
3. Heading: Promoting Language Exchange Programs Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nhấn mạnh rằng ngôn ngữ là công cụ mạnh mẽ để kết nối văn hóa và các chương trình trao đổi ngôn ngữ giúp người học vừa luyện giao tiếp vừa mở rộng hiểu biết văn hóa. Vietnamese translation: Ngôn ngữ là một trong những công cụ mạnh mẽ nhất để kết nối văn hóa. Trường học và các tổ chức thường tạo cơ hội để học sinh, sinh viên luyện nói với người đến từ các quốc gia khác. Bằng cách thúc đẩy các chương trình trao đổi ngôn ngữ, cộng đồng giúp người học cải thiện kỹ năng giao tiếp, đồng thời phát triển nhận thức văn hóa sâu sắc hơn và tình bạn quốc tế.
4. Heading: Overemphasis on Commercial Tourism Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cảnh báo rằng truyền thống đôi khi bị điều chỉnh để thu hút khách du lịch và tăng lợi nhuận, từ đó làm giảm tính chân thực của văn hóa. Vietnamese translation: Mặc dù du lịch có thể hỗ trợ giao lưu văn hóa, nó đôi khi cũng tạo ra những tác động tiêu cực. Ở nhiều nơi, các truyền thống bị thay đổi để thu hút du khách và tăng lợi nhuận thay vì giữ lại ý nghĩa nguyên gốc. Sự nhấn mạnh quá mức vào du lịch thương mại có thể làm giảm tính chân thực và khiến các thực hành văn hóa trở thành màn trình diễn hơn là sự biểu đạt bản sắc thực sự.
5. Heading: Concerns About Cultural Preservation Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nêu rõ nỗi lo rằng những phong tục truyền thống có thể mai một dần và thế hệ trẻ có thể mất liên kết với di sản địa phương. Vietnamese translation: Khi các nền văn hóa tương tác với nhau thường xuyên hơn, một số người lo sợ các phong tục truyền thống sẽ dần biến mất. Thế hệ trẻ có thể tiếp nhận lối sống nước ngoài và mất đi sự gắn kết với di sản địa phương. Những lo ngại về bảo tồn văn hóa này đã khiến nhiều cộng đồng chủ động bảo vệ ngôn ngữ, nghi lễ và các giá trị lịch sử của mình cẩn thận hơn trước đây.
6. Heading: Building Mutual Respect Among Communities Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cho thấy khi con người tìm hiểu truyền thống và niềm tin của nhau, họ thường thông cảm hơn và bớt phán xét hơn, từ đó xây dựng sự tôn trọng lẫn nhau. Vietnamese translation: Giao lưu văn hóa có thể đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc tạo ra những mối quan hệ hòa bình giữa các nhóm khác nhau. Khi con người tìm hiểu về truyền thống và niềm tin của nhau, họ thường trở nên thấu hiểu hơn và bớt phán xét hơn. Theo cách đó, các hoạt động văn hóa góp phần xây dựng sự tôn trọng lẫn nhau giữa các cộng đồng và khuyến khích sự hợp tác lâu dài.
7. Heading: Focusing on Authentic Cultural Experiences Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói rằng du khách hiện nay muốn trải nghiệm kết nối sâu hơn, tiếp cận đời sống và truyền thống địa phương thật hơn thay vì chỉ đi ngắm cảnh. Vietnamese translation: Du khách hiện đại ngày càng tìm kiếm những kết nối sâu sắc hơn thay vì chỉ tham quan đơn thuần. Thay vì đến những điểm đông đúc, họ muốn trải nghiệm đời sống hàng ngày, truyền thống địa phương và sự tương tác có ý nghĩa với người dân bản địa. Khi tập trung vào các trải nghiệm văn hóa chân thực, du lịch có thể trở nên tôn trọng hơn, mang tính giáo dục hơn và có giá trị hơn cho cả du khách lẫn cộng đồng sở tại.

extra_data.title: Cultural Exchange

paragraphs.text: Globalization has changed the way people understand culture around the world. Today, cultural exchange allows individuals to explore customs, beliefs, and values beyond their own societies. This process helps redefine global cultural understanding by encouraging openness, curiosity, and deeper awareness of diversity in modern life.

Many communities now organize international events to celebrate diversity and connection. These gatherings bring together music, food, art, and traditions from different countries. By encouraging cross-cultural festivals, societies create opportunities for people to appreciate differences, strengthen relationships, and promote harmony among various cultural groups.

Language is one of the most powerful tools for cultural connection. Schools and organizations often create opportunities for students to practice speaking with people from other countries. By promoting language exchange programs, communities help learners improve communication skills while also developing greater cultural awareness and international friendship.

Although tourism can support cultural exchange, it sometimes creates negative effects. In many places, traditions are changed to attract visitors and increase profits rather than preserve meaning. This overemphasis on commercial tourism may reduce authenticity and cause cultural practices to become performances instead of genuine expressions of identity.

As cultures interact more frequently, some people fear that traditional customs may gradually disappear. Younger generations may adopt foreign lifestyles and lose connection with local heritage. These concerns about cultural preservation have led many communities to protect their languages, rituals, and historical values more carefully than before.

Cultural exchange can play an important role in creating peaceful relationships between different groups. When people learn about each other's traditions and beliefs, they often become more understanding and less judgmental. In this way, cultural activities contribute to building mutual respect among communities and encourage long-term cooperation.

Modern travelers increasingly seek deeper connections rather than simple sightseeing. Instead of visiting crowded attractions, they want to experience daily life, local traditions, and meaningful interaction with residents. By focusing on authentic cultural experiences, tourism can become more respectful, educational, and valuable for both visitors and host communities.

explanation:
1. Đoạn mở đầu đối chiếu ngày trước phải ra phố, đi bộ giữa các cửa hàng và xếp hàng trả tiền, với việc ngày nay phần lớn mua sắm diễn ra trên mạng — rời xa cửa hàng truyền thống.
2. Đoạn liệt kê những cái lợi khiến thói quen này lan nhanh: so sánh chục người bán trong vài phút, xem số đo chính xác, giao tận nhà sau một hai ngày, mua bất kỳ giờ nào — vì sao thay đổi hấp dẫn đến vậy.
3. Đoạn nói người mua dựa vào đánh giá sao và bình luận của những khách lạ chưa từng gặp, tin họ hơn cả mô tả của người bán — để người lạ dẫn dắt lựa chọn của mình.
4. Đoạn nói khi thẻ đã lưu sẵn và chỉ cần chạm một cái là xong, khoảng dừng giữa lúc muốn và lúc trả tiền gần như biến mất, cộng thêm đồng hồ đếm ngược thúc giục — mua nhiều hơn dự định.
5. Đoạn nói chuyện trả hàng: khách đặt cùng một món ba cỡ rồi trả lại hai, chi phí xử lý và đóng gói lại rất tốn kém — cái giá của những kiện hàng không ai muốn.
6. Đoạn nói tác động không nằm trên hóa đơn: từng kiện hàng đi quãng đường xa hơn, dùng nhiều bìa carton và nhựa hơn, xe tải chạy đi chạy lại cùng một tuyến — thiệt hại khách không nhìn thấy.
7. Đoạn kết đưa lời khuyên: lập danh sách, chờ một ngày trước khi bấm đặt, đọc kỹ số đo — những cách đơn giản để giữ chừng mực.

extra_data.title: Shopping Online

headings.text: Buying more than you planned to
A move away from the traditional store
Damage that customers never see on the bill
Why the change proved so attractive
Simple ways to stay in control

paragraphs.text: Not long ago, buying a new coat or a birthday present meant a trip into town, a walk between shops and a queue at the till. Today a growing share of that activity happens on a phone screen during a lunch break or on the sofa in the evening. Retailers who once competed for the best position on a busy street now compete for the first row of results on a search page, and many have closed their town-centre branches altogether.

It is easy to see why the habit spread so quickly. A customer can compare a dozen sellers in a few minutes, read the exact measurements of an item, and have it delivered to the door within a day or two. Nothing ever closes, so people who work irregular hours are no longer limited by opening times. For those living far from a large town, the range of goods within reach has expanded enormously.

One feature that keeps buyers coming back is the opinion of people they have never met. Star ratings and written comments from previous customers often matter more than the description supplied by the seller. Sites also record what each visitor looks at and use that history to suggest further products, so the selection on offer quietly narrows to whatever a system predicts the shopper will like.

The ease of the process has a cost, however. When payment details are already stored and a purchase takes a single tap, the natural pause between wanting something and paying for it almost disappears. Countdown timers, messages announcing that only two items remain, and free delivery above a certain amount all encourage people to add extras to the basket. Many admit that their monthly total is higher than they realise.

Sending goods back creates another problem. Because clothing cannot be tried on in advance, some customers deliberately order the same item in three sizes and return two of them. Handling, checking and repackaging these parcels is expensive, and a surprising proportion never goes back on sale at all; damaged or out-of-season stock is sold off cheaply or destroyed. The price of that waste is eventually built into what everyone pays.

There is also an impact that rarely appears on the receipt. Individual parcels travel further and are packed in far more cardboard and plastic than a single trip to a shop would require, and vans making repeated journeys to the same street add to traffic and pollution. Some companies now group orders together or offer collection points, but progress is slow while customers continue to expect their goods the next morning.

None of this means people should stop buying from the internet, but a few habits help. Keeping a list and waiting a day before confirming an order removes much of the pressure to decide immediately. Reading the measurements carefully reduces the need to send things back, and choosing a slower delivery date allows several purchases to arrive together. Small adjustments of this kind protect both the budget and the environment.

extra_data.title: Children and Exercises

headings.text: Ways in which environment can influence behaviour
The success of a simple idea
A design for exercise and for study
The situation has the potential of being worst
The wider effects of regular activity

paragraphs.text: In recent years, children have been engaging in less physical activity. Instead, research has shown that the amount of time spent outdoors has decreased while the amount of time spent lounging on the sofa at home has increased significantly. While technology is often cited as the main cause, it is not the only reason. Urbanisation has limited the amount of space available for children to play. In today's world, children spend many hours doing homework. This forces them to spend more time indoors. The combination of screen time and lack of exercise is having a negative impact on children's physical fitness and overall health.

The phenomenon of children being sedentary is becoming more serious, largely due to the increase in time spent on electronic devices. The lure of smartphones and computers makes it difficult for both parents and children to reduce their screen time. As people become more aware of the benefits of exercise, it is imperative that we work together to find effective solutions to promote an active lifestyle.

An inspiring example is a teacher who started a program called Daily Mile, in which students are encouraged to run at least one mile every day. This simple idea quickly gained widespread support. Thanks to media coverage and positive feedback, the program has won numerous awards and is implemented in more than 3,500 schools in 36 countries. This initiative shows that small changes can have a big impact on children's exercise habits.

Daily Mile not only improves students' physical fitness, but also helps improve academic performance. Many teachers have noted that students who participate in this program become more focused and alert in class. Psychologists also agree that physical fitness contributes to mental clarity. The saying 'a healthy body is the foundation for a healthy mind' shows that regular exercise has a positive effect on children's ability to learn and remember.

The living and learning environment has a great influence on human behavior. For example, workplaces are often arranged to improve efficiency, while living spaces are designed to promote connections between members. Similarly, schools can be designed to encourage children to be active. Arranging open areas suitable for play and physical exercise can help students maintain an active lifestyle and fight the trend of being sedentary.

In Japan, an innovative architect designed a kindergarten in a very different way: the playground was built like a running track, allowing children to run and move freely. He said: “It is simple”, “Just start running” This innovative approach was not only successful but also won an award for its positive impact on children’s activity levels. Such thoughtful designs could inspire other schools to rethink how they create spaces that support learning while promoting physical activity.

Daily Mile and the Japanese architect’s playground design represent two different approaches to finance. The Daily Mile is virtually free, while the playground model requires a large investment. Local authorities need to consider many factors to balance promoting physical activity for children and managing their budgets appropriately. By finding creative but cost-effective solutions, communities can create environments that support children’s health and overall development.

2. Đoạn nói các quy tắc bàn ăn học từ nhỏ, không ai giải thích cho khách: người lớn tuổi ngồi quay ra cửa và ăn trước, rót trà cho người bên cạnh trước khi rót cho mình, gõ hai ngón tay để cảm ơn — luật bất thành văn.
3. Đoạn nói bữa sáng thường mua chứ không nấu: hàng quán gần chợ và ga tàu bán bánh bao, cháo, quẩy cho người đi làm trước 8 giờ — bữa sáng mua trên đường đi làm.
4. Đoạn nói vài món được chọn vì ý nghĩa chứ không vì vị: mì dài tượng trưng trường thọ, cá nguyên con ngày Tết mang ý dư dả — món ăn chọn vì ý nghĩa tượng trưng.
5. Đoạn về trà: luôn có mặt trong mọi dịp, mời trà là cách đón khách, rót cho người lớn tuổi còn là lời xin lỗi — thức uống mang theo thông điệp.
6. Đoạn nói thói quen đổi nhanh ở thành phố lớn: dân văn phòng trẻ đặt đồ ăn qua app và ăn tại bàn làm việc thay vì về nhà — nếp sinh hoạt mới của người trẻ đi làm.
7. Đoạn nói về lượng đồ ăn bỏ lại sau tiệc, nhà hàng thống kê con số khổng lồ, thực khách được khuyến khích gọi ít và mang phần thừa về — nhìn lại chuyện lãng phí thức ăn.

extra_data.title: Eating in China

headings.text: Breakfast bought on the way to work
New routines among young city workers
A meal designed around the group
Rethinking how much food is wasted
A drink that carries a message
Foods chosen for what they symbolise

paragraphs.text: In much of China a meal is not a set of separate portions but a collection of dishes placed in the centre of a round table for everyone to reach. Diners take a little at a time from the shared plates, and the person who invited the group usually orders on behalf of the whole table. Eating by yourself is regarded as slightly sad, and food is treated above all as a reason to bring family, colleagues or old classmates together.

Certain habits at the table are learned in childhood and are rarely explained to visitors. The oldest guest normally sits facing the door and starts first. Filling a neighbour's teacup before your own is a quiet mark of respect, and tapping two fingers on the wood is a way of saying thank you without interrupting the conversation. A guest is also expected to protest politely when the host insists on paying.

The first meal of the day is often bought rather than cooked. Before eight o'clock, small stalls near markets and metro stations sell steamed buns, rice porridge, fried dough sticks and bowls of noodles to people on their way to work. The food is cheap, served within a minute and frequently eaten standing up or carried away in a paper bag, which makes early morning one of the busiest moments on a Chinese street.

Several dishes are chosen less for their taste than for what they stand for. Long noodles served on a birthday suggest a long life, and a whole fish at New Year is linked to the idea of having more than enough in the year ahead. Families gather to fold dumplings together in the north, while the round cakes shared in autumn represent the reunion of relatives who live far apart. The meaning matters as much as the recipe.

Tea accompanies almost every occasion and carries responsibilities of its own. A pot is placed on the table before the food arrives and is refilled throughout the meal, and offering a cup is the standard way of welcoming a visitor to a home or an office. Pouring for an elder can also serve as an apology or a request for a favour, so a simple drink often does the work of an entire conversation.

Habits are changing quickly in the larger cities. Young office workers who once went home for a cooked lunch now order through an application and eat at their desks, and international chains have made burgers and fried chicken an ordinary weekday choice. Convenience has obvious advantages, but older relatives complain that a meal taken alone in front of a screen has lost the social purpose that once made it worthwhile.

Attention has recently turned to how much is left behind. Ordering generously has long been a way of showing respect for guests, yet restaurants report that enormous quantities are thrown away after banquets and celebrations. Diners are now encouraged to order smaller portions, ask for a box to carry the remainder home, or choose set menus sized for the number of people present. Doctors add that lighter cooking, with less oil and salt, would help too.

question_text: Here is the perspective of four people on the above topic. Please read the content and answer the question.
options: A
B
C
D
explanation:
--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
1. Chọn A vì đoạn A có câu "The job involves manual labour, so we're able to improve our physical health". Cụm "improve our physical health" là bằng chứng trực tiếp.
2. Chọn C vì đoạn C có câu "Each town has many people in need" và "we should use our time more meaningfully". Ý này cho thấy người nói nghĩ hoạt động tình nguyện nên giúp cộng đồng địa phương.
3. Chọn D vì đoạn D có câu "Making monthly donations is not a problem for me – it's how I show my support and contribution." Cụm "monthly donations" cho thấy người nói ủng hộ công việc thiện nguyện bằng tiền.
4. Chọn C vì đoạn C có câu "broaden our knowledge about local history, traditions, and culture". Đây là bằng chứng trực tiếp cho ý hiểu biết về văn hóa.
5. Chọn B vì đoạn B có câu "something that will benefit my future career." Cụm "future career" là từ khóa rõ nhất.
6. Chọn B vì đoạn B có câu "meeting new people helps me expand my network and create valuable connections". Đây là bằng chứng cho ý muốn gặp người mới và mở rộng quan hệ.
7. Chọn A vì đoạn A có câu "it's also a great way to travel while doing something meaningful." Cụm "a great way to travel" khớp trực tiếp với ý của câu hỏi.

people.name: A
people.text: I believe there are many ways we can show kindness through volunteering. I’m retired now, and I currently help build houses for people in need. I work with a volunteering organisation that already has clear plans in place. Through this work, I’ve had the chance to experience different foreign cultures. We’re often sent to various countries to carry out these projects, so it’s also a great way to travel while doing something meaningful. The job involves manual labour, so we’re able to improve our physical health – something that some people only begin to notice after a while.

people.name: B
people.text: My mother told me to do local volunteering because she is part of that organisation, but I’m not into it. I prefer volunteering abroad because I can develop soft skills – something that will benefit my future career. Also, meeting new people helps me expand my network and create valuable connections I can use later in my professional life.

people.name: C
people.text: Some people enjoy volunteering abroad, but honestly I feel most people are more interested in travelling. I believe we should use our time more meaningfully. Each town has many people in need. Their situations are difficult, and they don’t have the means to improve their quality of life. They are individuals who have contributed a lot to the country. Sharing stories with them helps us understand the differences between generations. We can also broaden our knowledge about local history, traditions, and culture through their experiences.

people.name: D
people.text: I’m too busy and rarely have any free time to do anything, so spending even a few hours volunteering is difficult. I would have to take half a day off work. I see many people in need and they genuinely require some extra financial support. That’s something I can help with because I earn a good salary. Making monthly donations is not a problem for me – it’s how I show my support and contribution.

2. Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nhấn mạnh việc học nhạc giúp rèn luyện trí nhớ và tạo ra các đường liên kết thần kinh mới.
3. Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói rằng tham gia dàn hợp xướng, dàn nhạc hay ban nhạc giúp con người gặp gỡ và kết nối với nhiều người khác.

Heading: Rèn luyện tính kỷ luật qua âm nhạc Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nhấn mạnh rằng học nhạc đòi hỏi “dedication and routine”, hình thành “self-discipline and patience” và cho thấy sự tiến bộ đến từ “consistency and effort over time”. Học sinh phải luyện tập thường xuyên, tham gia buổi tập và phát triển kỹ năng quản lý thời gian để cân bằng âm nhạc với những trách nhiệm khác. Cấu trúc này giúp hình thành tính kỷ luật và sự kiên nhẫn. Làm chủ một nhạc cụ cần nhiều tháng, thậm chí nhiều năm, và bao gồm việc lặp đi lặp lại các thang âm, sửa lỗi và dần dần tiến bộ. Những thói quen này cũng chuyển sang các lĩnh vực khác của cuộc sống, giúp người học nhạc duy trì sự tập trung và cam kết với các mục tiêu dài hạn. 5. Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn tập trung vào khả năng âm nhạc giúp con người diễn đạt những cảm xúc khó nói bằng lời.
6. Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cho thấy chơi nhạc cùng người khác giúp phát triển sự thấu cảm và trí tuệ cảm xúc.
7. Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nhấn mạnh lợi ích tinh thần và cảm xúc mà âm nhạc mang lại cho đời sống hằng ngày.

extra_data.title: Music

headings.text: A good way to boost your memory
A great opportunity to broaden your social circle
A creative outlet for expressing emotions
Develop a greater sense of well-being
Enhanced sensitivity to other people's feelings

paragraphs.text: While music is often associated with emotional expression, playing certain instruments can be surprisingly physical. Percussionists, drummers, and even pianists require strong coordination, stamina, and posture. Marching band musicians must walk in sync for long hours, often while carrying heavy instruments. String players need muscular endurance in their fingers and arms, and wind instrument players must have good lung capacity. Practicing regularly and performing under pressure also places physical demands on the body. In this way, music isn’t only mentally engaging—it can also be quite the workout.

Scientific studies have shown that learning to play music strengthens memory. When musicians play, they must recall notes, rhythms, and sequences, sometimes in real-time. Reading sheet music while coordinating hands or breath with timing challenges the brain, forming new neural pathways. This mental exercise has even been linked to improved academic performance in children and better memory retention in older adults. Whether memorizing entire pieces or remembering finger positions, the mental workout of music can benefit cognitive health across all age groups.

Music often brings people together, whether in choirs, orchestras, or bands. Being part of a musical group requires teamwork and offers regular opportunities to meet new people. This shared experience fosters a strong sense of community and belonging. For many, joining a music class or ensemble is not just about performance, but also about making friends and socializing in a relaxed, collaborative setting. Over time, these connections can turn into lasting friendships, broadening one's personal and professional network.

Learning music requires dedication and routine. Students must practice regularly, attend rehearsals, and develop time management skills to balance music with other responsibilities. This structure helps build self-discipline and patience. Mastering an instrument takes months, even years, and involves repeating scales, fixing mistakes, and gradually improving. These habits transfer to other areas of life, helping musicians stay focused and committed to long-term goals. Music teaches that progress comes through consistency and effort over time.

For many people, music is a deeply emotional experience. It offers a unique and personal way to express feelings that may be difficult to put into words. Composing melodies, writing lyrics, or simply playing with passion allows individuals to explore their emotional world and communicate it with others. Music can reflect joy, sadness, hope, or frustration. For this reason, it is often used in therapy to help people process emotions. In creative expression, music becomes both an emotional release and a form of personal storytelling.

Musicians often develop a heightened awareness of other people’s emotional states. In group settings, they must listen carefully and respond to changes in tone, tempo, or mood. This sensitivity helps them stay in harmony with others, both musically and socially. Playing music with others encourages empathy and understanding. Over time, this experience fosters emotional intelligence—a skill that benefits communication, relationships, and social awareness in everyday life.

Many people report feeling happier and more balanced when music is part of their daily life. Playing or listening to music can reduce stress, improve mood, and create a sense of inner peace. It provides a break from daily routines and offers something meaningful to focus on. Some use music to relax before bed, while others rely on it to energize their mornings. The emotional and psychological benefits are powerful, making music a simple yet effective tool for personal well-being.

  5. “These modern AI tools help businesses analyze data and make better decisions.” → “These modern AI” — từ chỉ định trỏ ngược về thứ vừa được nhắc.

▸ Mae the astronaut — thứ tự đúng:
  1. “Mae’s father worked as a nurse, and her mother was a teacher.” → câu mở đầu: nêu chủ thể và bối cảnh, không trỏ ngược về câu nào.
  2. “Her parents motivated Mae to pursue higher education and focus on scientific studies.” → bắt đầu bằng đại từ “Her” — bắt buộc phải có câu giới thiệu đứng trước.
  3. “Mae worked diligently and achieved several remarkable academic milestones.” → nối tiếp mạch nội dung của câu ngay trước.
  4. “These achievements eventually gave her the opportunity to join a training program in the United States.” → “These achievements eventually” — từ chỉ định trỏ ngược về thứ vừa được nhắc.
  5. “After completing the program, she joined a research team and contributed her skills and knowledge.” → mốc thời gian “After” — kể tiếp sự việc vừa xảy ra.

extra_data.title: Eating

paragraphs.text: Chinese culinary culture is like most other cultures in the world. It started with very basic hunting and gathering. Over time, society gradually developed, and with it, culinary culture developed. Gradually, cuisine became an art form and seemed to reach its peak in the 19th century. Although most Chinese people choose simple food with rice and vegetables, it is undeniable that Chinese culinary art has reached the level of exploiting the maximum flavor and each ingredient.

The concept of yin and yang has a complex influence on Chinese cuisine. In fact, this concept also appears in many other areas of life. It can be understood that yin and yang are opposite elements that complement each other to achieve a certain balance. Sweet and sour, cold and hot are typical examples of this concept. Some foods can be classified into hot or cold groups, such as lemon is considered cold and onion is considered hot. Based on this concept, Chinese people choose suitable foods to maintain the balance of the body.

In addition to the concept of yin and yang directly influencing the culinary culture, the Chinese also pay close attention to the availability of ingredients. Each region has its own ingredients, and this leads to differences in regional cooking styles. The coastal areas in the south of the country are famous for seafood dishes. In the north, the widespread cultivation of wheat has led to noodle dishes. The southwestern regions are famous for spicy soups, while some regions are famous for grilled meat.

Cooking methods are also regionally specific, in addition to the differences in food in these regions. However, there are some food techniques that are considered to be standard in Chinese culture. For example, vegetables are cut into small pieces and eaten with chopsticks. The Chinese have a long history of using chopsticks. The Chinese also often leave fish and meat with bones. According to them, this makes the food more delicious. Steaming is a very popular form of cooking. In addition, frying food with cooking oil is also commonly used.

The most common way for Chinese people to eat is street food. It is very common to see stalls selling all kinds of food on both sides of the road. This has become a part of the food culture. For large dining events, the food is often placed in the middle of the table so that guests can try different dishes. The meal is served with tea and sometimes rice wine from the local area.

There are signs that Chinese food culture and eating habits are changing. Chinese people now consume a wide variety of foods from many different countries. People in cities also prefer fast and convenient foods. In addition, some traditional products such as milk are consumed less by Chinese people than in the past.

The change in Chinese eating habits has a global impact. Due to its huge population, the food demand of the Chinese market will directly affect domestic and international food production. The change in diet leads to problems such as the increase in related diseases that a large economy like China is prone to. Therefore, achieving a balance like the yin-yang philosophy in Chinese culinary culture is clearly a big challenge.

extra_data.title: Early Australia

headings.text: Technology helps uncover the ocean's secret
A new evidence that leads to speculation
Determination of the explorers through the ages

paragraphs.text: Some researchers are rethinking the traditional narrative of how Australia was settled. While it is widely believed that the first people arrived via land bridges from Southeast Asia during the Ice Age, new theories suggest otherwise. Alternative histories propose that early humans may have used rudimentary boats to cross from distant shores far earlier than previously estimated. These claims are controversial but are supported by some archaeological findings and oral traditions of Indigenous communities. Such ideas challenge the Eurocentric view of exploration and emphasize the ingenuity of early seafarers long before written records existed.

The vast Australian outback and its harsh deserts have long posed a formidable challenge to resettlement and development. For thousands of years, the central areas of the continent were difficult to inhabit due to extreme heat, scarce water sources, and isolation. Even after European arrival, these natural barriers prevented deeper exploration and settlement for decades. Today, the environment still remains an obstacle, limiting infrastructure, agriculture, and population growth in these regions. The Australian landscape, while beautiful and iconic, continues to shape the way communities are formed and connected.

Advancements in marine technology have revolutionized our understanding of ancient migration routes to Australia. Underwater sonar mapping and satellite imaging have revealed submerged land masses and potential seafaring paths once used by early humans. Archaeologists are now uncovering tools and fossils deep beneath coastal waters, which provide new insights into how long ago people arrived on the continent. These discoveries would not be possible without modern equipment that allows exploration of areas previously inaccessible. As research continues, scientists hope to fill in many historical gaps that have puzzled historians for centuries.

It is now widely believed that the journey to Australia wasn't completed in one go. Instead, early humans likely reached the continent in stages, moving through island chains and coastal areas over generations. This theory is supported by the distribution of artifacts and remains across Southeast Asia and Northern Australia. The idea of gradual migration, rather than a single wave, helps explain the diversity of early populations found on the continent. This step-by-step approach also reflects how ancient peoples adapted to different environments as they moved closer to the Australian mainland.

In recent years, new evidence has emerged from both land and sea, prompting scientists to re-evaluate earlier assumptions. A set of ancient tools discovered in a Northern Territory cave doesn't match previously known Aboriginal designs, leading some to speculate about earlier migrations or even contact with other civilizations. Additionally, genetic studies hint at complex interactions with now-extinct human species. These findings, while not yet definitive, open the door to exciting discussions and possibilities about Australia's earliest human history.

Many of the first explorers to attempt crossing Australia's interior were ill-prepared for the harsh conditions they encountered. Without sufficient knowledge of the land or survival skills in such a hostile environment, numerous expeditions ended in tragedy. The lack of understanding of the Aboriginal methods of finding water, navigating terrain, and managing heat led to avoidable suffering. It wasn't until later that European settlers began to adapt, learning from Indigenous Australians how to travel and survive in such an unfamiliar landscape.

Despite the many difficulties, both ancient and modern explorers showed incredible perseverance in reaching and understanding Australia. Whether navigating unknown seas in simple rafts or trekking across searing deserts with limited supplies, their determination pushed the boundaries of what was thought possible. Stories of survival and discovery continue to inspire awe, reminding us of the strength and courage required to explore the unknown. Through the centuries, this spirit of exploration has become a core part of Australian history and identity.
