Woman: The window in the kitchen. It lets the cold in all winter, the frame is cracked, and I'm tired of taping it up every November. I called the fitters this morning — they can replace it next month.
Man: You already called them? So this isn't really a discussion, is it?
Woman: It's an announcement with discussion-flavoured decoration. The window is what we're changing.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – The window.
• Vì sao đúng: "The window in the kitchen... I called the fitters this morning — they can replace it next month", chốt lại "The window is what we're changing".
• The car sai: cô nói xe vẫn ổn, chỉ cần bảo dưỡng ("The car is fine, it just needs a service").
• The computer sai: cô chủ động loại trước ("no, not the computer either. It's slow, but it works").
👉 Mẹo: dạng "what will they change/buy" — người nói thường tự loại trừ bằng "X is fine", "not X either" rồi mới tiết lộ đáp án ở câu khẳng định cuối. Đừng chốt sớm.

question_text: Listen to the conversation between Douglas and Kay. Why does Douglas call Kay?
options: ask for a favor
suggest a meeting
say thank you
explanation:
Woman: Hello, Kay speaking.
Man: Kay! It's Douglas. Do you have a minute?
Woman: For you, always. Is this about borrowing my projector again?
Man: No no, no favors today, I promise. And before you ask — I'm not calling to arrange another meeting either; our calendar is full enough.
Woman: Now I'm curious!
Man: I'm calling to say thank you, properly. The report you helped me fix last week — the directors loved it. It got approved this morning, and that was your doing.
Woman: Douglas, that's so kind! You did the hard part.
Man: We both know better. Lunch is on me next week — no favors, no meetings, just gratitude.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – say thank you.
• Vì sao đúng: "I'm calling to say thank you, properly. The report you helped me fix last week — the directors loved it".
• ask for a favor sai: anh phủ nhận ngay từ đầu ("No no, no favors today, I promise").
• suggest a meeting sai: cũng bị anh loại trước ("I'm not calling to arrange another meeting either; our calendar is full enough").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "why does X call" — người gọi thường loại trừ hai mục đích giả trước. Nghe được cụm "I'm calling to..." là chốt được ngay.

question_text: Anna is calling her friend. Where will they meet?
options: At the marketplace
At the mall
At the park
explanation:
Woman: Hi! It's Anna. Are we still meeting tomorrow morning?
Man: Absolutely. Where suits you? The mall opens at nine — we could do breakfast there.
Woman: Honestly, the mall is chaos on Saturdays, all those queues. And the park... they're setting up a concert stage, half of it is fenced off this week.
Man: So the park is out too. Where then?
Woman: The marketplace! The farmers' stalls are there on Saturdays — we can buy cheese, look at the flowers, and there's that little coffee cart you liked.
Man: The one with the cinnamon buns! Sold. The marketplace at nine, by the fountain?
Woman: By the fountain at nine. Bring a shopping bag!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – At the marketplace.
• Vì sao đúng: "The marketplace! The farmers' stalls are there on Saturdays" và chốt "By the fountain at nine".
• At the mall sai: thứ Bảy quá đông và phải xếp hàng ("the mall is chaos on Saturdays, all those queues").
• At the park sai: đang dựng sân khấu ca nhạc, bị rào mất một nửa ("they're setting up a concert stage, half of it is fenced off this week").
👉 Mẹo: khi hai địa điểm đầu đều bị chê, hãy chờ câu bắt đầu bằng tên địa điểm kèm dấu chấm than — đó gần như luôn là đáp án.

question_text: A woman is talking to a police officer. What did she lose?
options: Wallet
Phone
Car
explanation:
Man: Good afternoon, madam. You said you've lost something?
Woman: Yes, officer, somewhere on the high street this morning. I was terrified it was my wallet at first, but no — the wallet is right here, thank goodness, cards and all.
Man: That's a relief. So what exactly is missing?
Woman: My phone. The new one, barely a month old. I had it at the bakery — I paid with it — and by the car park it was gone from my pocket.
Man: You didn't leave it in the car?
Woman: I checked the car twice, it's not there. It must have fallen out or... been taken.
Man: All right, let's file a report. Phone, black, one month old. We'll check the bakery's cameras first.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Phone.
• Vì sao đúng: "My phone. The new one, barely a month old" — và cảnh sát ghi biên bản "Phone, black, one month old".
• Wallet sai: ban đầu cô tưởng mất ví, nhưng ví vẫn còn nguyên ("I was terrified it was my wallet at first, but no — the wallet is right here, cards and all").
• Car sai: xe không mất; cô chỉ kiểm tra trong xe xem có bỏ quên điện thoại không ("I checked the car twice, it's not there").
👉 Mẹo: dạng khai báo mất đồ — món bị mất luôn được xác nhận lại ở cuối khi lập biên bản. Món xuất hiện kèm "but no / it's right here" là bẫy.

question_text: A man is seeking advice on future career. What is he going to do?
options: To work in business
To become a teacher
To study at college
explanation:
Man: Thanks for making time. I need advice — everyone keeps planning my future for me.
Woman: Let's hear it. What are the options?
Man: My mother wants me to become a teacher like her. Stable, holidays, respect — I understand the appeal, but standing in front of a class terrifies me.
Woman: And college? You mentioned applying last year.
Man: I did, and I got in — but honestly, three more years of exams is not what I want. I've made my decision, actually: I'm going to work in business. My uncle offered me a place at his trading company, starting from the bottom.
Woman: You sound sure.
Man: For the first time, I am. Business it is — I start next month.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – To work in business.
• Vì sao đúng: "I've made my decision, actually: I'm going to work in business. My uncle offered me a place at his trading company" và chốt "Business it is — I start next month".
• To become a teacher sai: đó là mong muốn của MẸ anh, còn anh thì sợ đứng lớp ("My mother wants me to become a teacher like her... standing in front of a class terrifies me").
• To study at college sai: anh đã đỗ nhưng từ chối vì không muốn thi cử thêm ("I got in — but honestly, three more years of exams is not what I want").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi dự định tương lai — ưu tiên câu có "I've made my decision / I'm going to". Nguyện vọng của bố mẹ và cơ hội đã từ chối đều là nhiễu.

question_text: A customer is calling the hotline of a department store. Which number to press in order to buy a computer?
options: One
Two
Three
explanation:
Woman: Thank you for calling Harrison's Department Store. How can I direct your call?
Man: Hello, yes — I want to order a computer I saw in your catalogue.
Woman: Of course, sir. Our automated line handles that. When you call back, listen carefully: press one for clothing and shoes.
Man: Not that, then.
Woman: Press two for furniture and home goods. And for electronics — computers, phones, televisions — you press three.
Man: So for the computer, three?
Woman: Exactly, press three, and the electronics team will take your order. They're open until eight tonight.
Man: Wonderful. Three it is. Thank you very much!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Three.
• Vì sao đúng: "for electronics — computers, phones, televisions — you press three", nhân viên xác nhận "Exactly, press three, and the electronics team will take your order".
• One sai: phím dành cho quần áo và giày ("press one for clothing and shoes").
• Two sai: phím dành cho nội thất và đồ gia dụng ("Press two for furniture and home goods").
👉 Mẹo: dạng tổng đài liệt kê phím bấm — nghe theo cặp "số + nhóm hàng", rồi xác định món cần mua thuộc nhóm nào (computer thuộc electronics). Đừng cố nhớ mỗi con số rời.

question_text: The woman is calling a friend about meeting for dinner. How long does it take to get to the station?
options: 30 minutes
40 minutes
50 minutes
explanation:
Woman: Hi! About dinner on Saturday — I'm trying to work out when to leave home.
Man: It depends how you're coming. Driving?
Woman: No, the train. How long does it take you to get to the station from your side?
Man: From mine, about thirty minutes on the bus. But you're further out, aren't you?
Woman: That's what I'm worried about. Someone told me it takes fifty minutes from my neighbourhood, which sounds like torture.
Man: Fifty? No, that's the old route, before they opened the new road. From yours it's forty minutes now, door to door. I did it last week visiting Tom.
Woman: Forty minutes — that's not bad at all. So if dinner is at seven, I'll leave at six.
Man: Leave ten minutes earlier to be safe. See you Saturday!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 40 minutes.
• Vì sao đúng: "From yours it's forty minutes now, door to door. I did it last week visiting Tom" — đây là thời gian từ nhà người phụ nữ (người đang hỏi) tới ga.
• 30 minutes sai: đó là thời gian từ nhà NGƯỜI ĐÀN ÔNG, không phải của cô ("From mine, about thirty minutes on the bus").
• 50 minutes sai: là con số cũ theo tuyến đường trước khi mở đường mới ("that's the old route, before they opened the new road").
👉 Mẹo: câu "how long" hay gài số của người khác hoặc số lỗi thời. Xác định rõ đại từ sở hữu ("from mine" vs "from yours") và loại số đi kèm "the old route / it used to be".

question_text: A man is talking to the shopping assistant. What color top does he buy?
options: Red
Blue
Black
explanation:
Woman: Welcome back! Did you decide on the top you looked at yesterday?
Man: Almost. The red one still calls to me — but my wife says red makes me look like a traffic light.
Woman: Ha! We do have it in blue, the exact same cut. Very popular this season.
Man: Blue... I tried it on. It's nice, but I own four blue tops already, according to this morning's wardrobe inspection.
Woman: Then may I suggest the black? Same fabric, and black never argues with anything in a wardrobe.
Man: Black. Safe, elegant, wife-approved. You know what, yes — the black one, size medium.
Woman: Excellent choice. Shall I wrap it, or will you wear the peace treaty home?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Black.
• Vì sao đúng: "You know what, yes — the black one, size medium", sau gợi ý "may I suggest the black? Same fabric, and black never argues with anything".
• Red sai: vợ anh chê trông như đèn giao thông ("my wife says red makes me look like a traffic light").
• Blue sai: anh đã có sẵn bốn áo xanh ("I own four blue tops already, according to this morning's wardrobe inspection").
👉 Mẹo: hội thoại mua quần áo hay dùng lý do hài hước để loại từng màu. Cứ chờ câu có cỡ áo đi kèm ("size medium") — màu ở câu đó là màu được mua.

question_text: Listen to the conversation about the directions. Where is the library located?
options: On the left of the square
In front of the square
Behind the square
explanation:
Man: Excuse me, could you help me? I'm looking for the city library.
Woman: Of course! You're almost there. You see the main square ahead?
Man: Yes, with the fountain. Someone told me the library is behind the square somewhere.
Woman: That's the old building — it's a museum now. And it's not the big white one in front of the square either; that's the town hall.
Man: So where do I go?
Woman: Look to the left of the square — the red brick building with the tall windows. That's the library, entrance under the arch.
Man: On the left, red brick. Wonderful, thank you so much!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – On the left of the square.
• Vì sao đúng: "Look to the left of the square — the red brick building with the tall windows. That's the library" và người hỏi nhắc lại "On the left, red brick".
• In front of the square sai: tòa nhà trắng phía trước là tòa thị chính ("it's not the big white one in front of the square either; that's the town hall").
• Behind the square sai: đó là tòa nhà thư viện CŨ, nay thành bảo tàng ("That's the old building — it's a museum now").
👉 Mẹo: bài hỏi đường luôn có hai tòa nhà nhiễu kèm chức năng khác (museum, town hall). Hãy ghép cặp "vị trí + đặc điểm tòa nhà" (bên trái + gạch đỏ) rồi mới chọn.

question_text: Singers can be good role models for young people.
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
Woman: Did you watch the interview with that young singer last night? She spoke about finishing school, refusing certain advertisements, donating her first big pay cheque. My daughter watched it three times — though honestly, I have known too many idols with beautiful interviews and ugly private lives to hand them my children's compasses.
Man: I saw it, and I would be kinder than that. A performer like her can show teenagers a way to carry themselves better than any lecture from me. What fascinates me more is how differently we all hear things. You adore those quiet piano albums that send me straight to sleep, and my heavy guitar records give you a headache. Nobody is right; the ear wants what it wants.
Woman: True enough — my sister and I grew up in one bedroom and cannot agree on a single record. Each pair of ears is its own country. And yet — here is the strange part — when I travelled through countries whose languages I could not speak a word of, a melody in a market square could still make every stranger around me sway together. Words need translating; a tune walks straight in.
Man: Sometimes, perhaps. I have also sat politely through foreign songs that meant nothing to me, so I will not sign that declaration. But here is something we should both be uneasy about: the people who understand exactly how a rising chord squeezes the heart — advertisers, film studios, campaign managers — use it on us daily.
Woman: Constantly. Play the right strings and you can steer a crowd wherever you wish. That power deserves more suspicion than we give it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: M-B-W-B (nữ nói trước như đề thật). Paraphrase:
1. "Singers good role models" → M: "A performer like her can show teenagers a way to carry themselves" — W từ chối ("hand them my children's compasses").
2. "Taste highly personal" → B: M "the ear wants what it wants" + W "Each pair of ears is its own country".
3. "Music universal language" → W: "a tune walks straight in" — M "I will not sign that declaration".
4. "Music manipulates feelings" → B: M "use it on us daily" + W "steer a crowd wherever you wish".

question_text: Children are interested in tech-based learning
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
W: How are your two getting on with that new tablet scheme at the school?
M: Rather well, actually, which honestly surprised me.
W: Same here. Put a lesson on a screen and they're suddenly wide awake — anything with an app or a game inside it and they'll happily sit there for an hour.
M: Exactly, I agree completely. My son will do twenty minutes of maths on a tablet without a murmur, then sulk for an hour over a paper worksheet.
W: It's the same story in every house I know.
M: What does worry me, though, is what happens the moment you take the screen away. A lot of them genuinely struggle to hold an ordinary conversation face to face.
W: Oh, I'm entirely with you there. My niece will type all evening quite happily, but ask her to order her own lunch in a café and she goes to pieces.
M: It's a proper skill, and they're simply not practising it any more.
W: Which is precisely why I think households need proper support with all this. Parents are left to work out the rules on their own, and most of them haven't the faintest idea where to start.
M: Hmm, I don't see it that way, to be honest. I'll accept that some parents find it hard going, but it isn't complicated — you set a time limit and you stick to it. You hardly need somebody coming round to explain that.
W: That's easy to say when you've only got the one at home.
M: Possibly. What I would say, though, is that children can be taught to manage their own behaviour online — to work out for themselves what's sensible and step away from it.
W: I'm not so sure about that at all. They're not old enough to see the harm coming, and every app has been designed by grown-ups to keep them hooked. That's hardly a fair fight.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Trẻ hứng thú với học qua công nghệ = Both · Trẻ khó giao tiếp ngoài đời = Both · Gia đình cần hỗ trợ quản lý công nghệ = Woman · Trẻ có thể tự điều chỉnh tương tác trực tuyến = Man

1. Children are interested in tech-based learning → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "Put a lesson on a screen and they're suddenly wide awake", người đàn ông tán thành rõ ràng: "Exactly, I agree completely."

2. Children find it difficult to communicate offline → Both: người đàn ông nêu "A lot of them genuinely struggle to hold an ordinary conversation face to face", người phụ nữ đồng ý: "Oh, I'm entirely with you there."

3. Families require help with management of technology → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "households need proper support with all this". Người đàn ông phản đối: "Hmm, I don't see it that way, to be honest."

4. Children can learn to regulate their online interactions → Man: người đàn ông nêu "children can be taught to manage their own behaviour online". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'm not so sure about that at all."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy chính ở ý 3 — người đàn ông mở đầu bằng "I'll accept that some parents find it hard going" nghe rất giống đồng ý, nhưng phần sau ("it isn't complicated") phủ nhận đúng việc gia đình cần được hỗ trợ, nên đáp án là Woman.

question_text: When did she become a Nutritionist?
options: When she did a biology degree.
After working in a hospital.
When she worked at a healthcare center.
explanation:
People often ask how I became a nutritionist, and my path was a little unusual. Most of my colleagues found this profession later in life — some decided to specialise after working in a hospital, where they saw every day how much food affects recovery, and others made the choice while employed at a local healthcare centre. My story is different. I qualified as a nutritionist while I was still completing my biology degree at university. During my second year, a professor invited me to join a research project on diet and energy, and I knew immediately that this was my field. So by the time I graduated, I already held my professional qualification — the degree and the career began together.
How I became well known is another story people usually get wrong. Some assume I appeared on a famous TV talk show, and others have heard a rumour that I invented some revolutionary new health food. Neither happened — I have never been on television, and I have never invented anything. The truth is quieter. For six years I answered calls on a national nutrition helpline, three evenings a week. I helped thousands of ordinary people solve their problems: a mother whose son refused vegetables, an athlete who kept feeling weak, an older man confused about his diabetes diet. Those callers told their friends, the friends told their doctors, and slowly my name spread. I became known not through cameras or products, but through years of solving one small problem at a time.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: When she did a biology degree. Bẫy: "hospital" và "healthcare center" là con đường của ĐỒNG NGHIỆP ("Most of my colleagues...").
2. Đáp án: After solving people's problems in a helpline. Bẫy: "TV show" và "inventing a new food" đều bị phủ định ("Neither happened").

question_text: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My company pays for our gym cards, and at first I thought it was just a nice perk. Six months later I understand their plan perfectly. On the days I swim before the office, I get through my inbox by ten and my ideas actually arrive when I need them. My boss noticed before I did — she said my reports read sharper. Exercise, for me, has become a work tool, as important as my laptop.
Speaker B: Everyone describes this wonderful energy after sport. Where is mine? Forty minutes of anything and I am a wrung-out towel — stairs become mountains, and my bed starts calling my name at eight in the evening. I still show up twice a week because the doctor insists, but let nobody tell you it feels light. For some of us, every single session is heavy from the first stretch to the last.
Speaker C: Book me for any sport, as long as there is a crowd. Wednesday volleyball with the neighbours, weekend badminton with my sisters — the score matters less than the laughing between points. Last week we spent more time imitating each other's serves than actually playing. Exercise alone feels like punishment; exercise with my favourite people is just a party where everyone happens to be sweating.
Speaker D: I will be the honest one here: I detest the whole business. The lycra, the counting, the mirrors, the smell of the changing rooms — every bit of it. My brother signs me up for things and I invent illnesses to escape. People say I simply have not found my sport yet. I have looked for forty years; my sport is reading on the balcony, and I am its champion.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Improve work performance (PARAPHRASE: "inbox by ten... reports read sharper... a work tool"). B = Find exercise tiring (PARAPHRASE: "a wrung-out towel... every session is heavy"). C = Have fun exercising with others (keyword "neighbours... sisters... laughing"). D = Hate exercising (keyword "I detest the whole business"). Nhiễu: alone, lose weight.

question_text: How much does a bus card cost?
explanation:
Quick announcement for the new students about the bus cards, since half of you overpaid last year! The monthly student card costs twenty dollars — twenty, from the machines at the depot or the app. Not thirty, that's the adult card the driver will happily sell you if you don't show your student ID. And forget the ten-dollar rumour — that's just the weekly card, useless maths for a whole term. Twenty dollars, student card, ID in hand. Your wallets can thank me later!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – $20.
• Vì sao đúng: "The monthly student card costs twenty dollars — twenty, from the machines at the depot or the app".
• $30 sai: đó là vé người lớn, tài xế sẽ bán nếu bạn không trình thẻ sinh viên — "Not thirty, that's the adult card the driver will happily sell you if you don't show your student ID".
• $10 sai: đó chỉ là vé tuần, vô dụng cho cả học kỳ — "forget the ten-dollar rumour — that's just the weekly card, useless maths for a whole term".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giá vé, mỗi con số gắn với một LOẠI vé (student / adult / weekly). Đọc kỹ câu hỏi hỏi loại nào rồi mới bắt số.

question_text: Four people are talking about running. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: Call me odd, but I do my kilometres right through the middle of town, on the pavements, dodging lamp posts and prams. I love running in the street — the shop windows, the smells from the bakeries, the little nods from the regulars I pass at the same corner every morning. Friends warn me about the traffic and the hard ground, and fair enough. But out there among the crowds and the noise, I never once feel bored.
Speaker B: I am lucky enough to live ten minutes from the coast, and that decides everything. Every morning I jog along the sand with the waves on one side and the cliffs on the other, gulls complaining overhead. When the tide is out I run on the firm wet sand, which is kind to the ankles. In winter the wind can be brutal, but watching the sun climb out of the water makes every frozen ear worth it.
Speaker C: I train for competitions, so guesswork is not good enough for me — I need exact distances and a clock I can trust. That is why you will find me at the stadium oval three evenings a week, counting laps on the rubber surface with my stopwatch. Four hundred metres, no surprises, no puddles, no dogs. My friends call it running in circles. I call it knowing precisely how fast I am getting.
Speaker D: I gave up on outdoor jogging the winter I turned forty — the dark evenings and icy paths defeated me. Now I do my five kilometres on the machine at the gym, warm and dry, with the television screens in front of me and a proper shower afterwards. The trainers there adjust my programme every month too. My friends tease me about running to nowhere, but nowhere has excellent air conditioning.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = prefer running in the street (keyword "running in the street"). B = at the seaside (PARAPHRASE: "along the sand... waves... tide" — không có chữ seaside). C = on the running track (PARAPHRASE: "stadium oval... counting laps... four hundred metres"). D = in the fitness center (keyword-lite: "machine at the gym" — bắt được qua gym). Nhiễu: in the park, mountain trail.

question_text: Four people are talking about listening to music. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My job empties me — eight hours of phone calls and complaints. So the first thing I do at home is drop onto the sofa, close my eyes, and let my favourite slow album wash the day away. Twenty minutes of those warm melodies and my shoulders finally come down from my ears. No wine, no television — just the speakers doing their quiet repair work. My wife says she can tell which song is playing by the look on my face.
Speaker B: My flatmates think I am strange, but my headphones go on the moment my books open. Instrumental only — words in songs fight with the words on the page. With the right quiet piano behind me, three hours of revision pass like one; without it, I check my phone every four minutes. I even match albums to subjects now: strings for history, soft electronic for maths. My exam playlist is basically a study partner.
Speaker C: In my family, music is not for listening — it is for joining in. The moment a song I know starts, my voice is already in it, harmonies and all. In the shower, over the cooking, in the car at full volume with the windows down. My neighbours have learned my entire repertoire through the walls, poor people. A song without my voice on top feels unfinished; that is simply how I enjoy music.
Speaker D: My alarm is set to silence — what actually starts my day is pressing play. Before my eyes fully open, the first song of my morning playlist is filling the bedroom, and by track three I am upright and human. Coffee, shower, dressing: all of it happens to music, every single morning. On the rare day the speaker battery dies, the whole house feels wrong until noon. Waking up without songs, to me, is only half waking up.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = To relax (PARAPHRASE: "wash the day away... shoulders come down... quiet repair work"). B = While studying (keyword "books open... revision"). C = While singing (PARAPHRASE: "my voice is already in it... my entire repertoire"). D = After waking up (keyword-lite "starts my day... morning playlist... waking up"). Nhiễu: while driving, before bed.

question_text: Community design can influence people's behavior.
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
Woman: Have you walked through the new quarter by the river? Benches facing each other, wide steps where people sit with coffee, one little square where three streets meet. Since it opened, strangers actually talk to each other there. The way a place is laid out quietly steers what people do in it.
Man: I noticed the same thing on my own street, oddly enough. When they widened the pavement and added those two long tables, neighbours who had nodded at each other for years finally sat down together. Bricks and benches really do write the rules of behaviour. What people forget, though, is the clock. Everyone expects a neighbourhood to feel like family within a season. From what I have seen, real bonds between neighbours grow the way trees do — years, not months.
Woman: Perhaps, though I have seen friendships spark quickly too, so I would not insist on the years. Here is a thought you will probably fight me on: I think the group you belong to at the office and the group you belong to on your street are basically the same animal. Same trust, same favours, same gossip.
Man: There I do fight you! One is held together by salary and deadlines, the other by choice. Leave a job and watch how many colleagues remain in your life. But let us end on common ground: our phones have completely rewritten how groups form at all. My cycling club found each other online before we ever met.
Woman: True — half my closest circle began as usernames. The front door is digital now.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: B-M-W-B (giữ nguyên). Paraphrase:
1. "Design influences behavior" → B: "the way a place is laid out quietly steers what people do" + "Bricks and benches write the rules".
2. "Creating community takes time" → M: "grow the way trees do — years, not months" — W "would not insist on the years".
3. "Work = social communities" → W: "basically the same animal" — M "There I do fight you!".
4. "Technology changed how community forms" → B: "phones have rewritten how groups form" + "half my closest circle began as usernames".

question_text: Continuity is very important in the workplace.
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
Man: It seems like every workplace is going through so many changes lately. But honestly, I think Continuity is still very important. When things are done consistently, it gives people a sense of security. If everything changes too fast, it is hard for employees to keep up and the organisation can lose its way. Continuity is important in keeping everyone focused
Woman: I get where you're coming from, but I feel like these days, nothing is certain. Job security isn't something we can rely on anymore. There's always the risk of layoffs, especially with the economy being unpredictable. People are moving from job to job more than ever before, and you can't always count on staying in one place for long
Man: That's definitely a concern. But regardless of job security or stability, one thing we both can agree on is that job satisfaction is a huge motivator. When people love what they do, they're more likely to stay even when times get tough. It's the main reason many of us keep pushing through the challenges.
Woman: Absolutely! I think when people are satisfied with their work, they're willing to go the extra mile. It's not just about the paycheck, it's about feeling fulfilled. That's what really makes the difference in the workplace.
Man: You're right. And another thing that's making a difference is technology. It's been a game-changer for the economy, making things more efficient. The growth we've seen in so many Industries is because of how we've embraced new technologies. It's definitely helping businesses thrive.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người nam nêu cao tính liên tục: "But honestly, I think Continuity is still very important."
2. Người phụ nữ nói công việc không còn an toàn ổn định tuyệt đối: "Job security isn't something we can rely on anymore."
3. Người nam gợi ý: "...one thing we both can agree on is that job satisfaction is a huge motivator." Người phụ nữ ủng hộ mạnh mẽ: "Absolutely! I think when people are satisfied with their work, they're willing to go the extra mile."
4. Người nam khẳng định vai trò của công nghệ: "technology. It's been a game-changer for the economy, making things more efficient."

question_text: Four people are talking about using the Internet. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: After a long shift, my routine never changes: dinner, sofa, screen. The internet replaced my television years ago — I follow three series at once and pick films by mood, from black-and-white classics to last month's releases. My flatmate and I have a Friday tradition of choosing the worst-reviewed film we can find and enjoying every terrible minute. Without the streaming sites, my evenings would be a lot quieter and a lot duller.
Speaker B: University turned me into a night-time typist. Every project, every essay, every group presentation runs through the online portal — I download the readings, join the shared documents, and submit everything before the midnight deadline. When I got stuck on statistics last term, a tutorial video explained in nine minutes what the lecture had failed to explain in ninety. My grades genuinely live or die by my connection.
Speaker C: My parents are back in the countryside and my brother works abroad, so the internet is really our dinner table now. Sunday evening video calls with the whole family, my mother showing me her garden through the camera, my father asking if I am eating properly. In between there are voice messages and photos of everything from new haircuts to burnt pancakes. Distance used to mean silence; now it just means a screen between us.
Speaker D: Before I even brush my teeth, I check the transport app. It tells me whether my usual bus is on time, which platform the train leaves from, and how the traffic is moving on the ring road. Twice last month it warned me about strikes before my colleagues had heard a word. Planning my route used to be guesswork and luck. Now the whole journey is arranged while the kettle boils.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Watch movies (keyword "films by mood... streaming"). B = Complete assignments (keyword "essay... submit"). C = Stay in touch with family (PARAPHRASE: "our dinner table now... Distance used to mean silence"). D = Find transport information (PARAPHRASE: "whether my usual bus is on time... journey arranged"). Nhiễu: news, games.

question_text: Housing space is more important than farming space.
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
W: Did you see the council's plan to put vegetable beds on the rooftops in the town centre?
M: I did, yes. And honestly, my first reaction was that we haven't got the land to spare. Every spare metre in this city ought to be going up as flats, not lettuce. People need somewhere to live before they need somewhere to grow beans.
W: I don't see it that way at all. Rooftops aren't competing with housing. Nobody is ever going to build a two-bedroom flat on the roof of a supermarket.
M: Hmm. I'm still not convinced the two can sit side by side.
W: And anyway, I find the whole idea rather lovely. Walking down a street where herbs are growing outside the chemist's makes a place feel alive.
M: See, that's where you lose me. I'm not so sure it's charming at all. To me it looks messy. Netting, plastic tubs, half of it brown and dying by August. I'd far rather have a proper park.
W: Well, we shall have to disagree on that one.
M: We shall.
W: There's a practical side too, though. This city genuinely hasn't got enough food coming into it. Supply is far tighter than people realise. One bad winter on the motorways and the shelves are empty.
M: I'll accept the figures you're quoting, but I don't read them that way. We aren't short of food. We're short of cheap food. Plenty is arriving; it's simply expensive. That's a completely different problem.
W: Hmm. Perhaps.
M: What I do think, though, is that it would do something real for jobs round here. Growers, deliveries, small shops buying direct from the roof next door.
W: Oh, absolutely, I agree with you there. Money going round the neighbourhood instead of off to a warehouse two hundred miles away.
M: Exactly. That's the part of it I'd actually vote for.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Chỗ ở quan trọng hơn chỗ trồng trọt = Man · Nông nghiệp đô thị hấp dẫn = Woman · Thành phố cần thêm lương thực = Woman · Nông nghiệp đô thị có lợi cho kinh tế = Both
1. Housing space is more important than farming space. → Man: Nam nêu "Every spare metre in this city ought to be going up as flats, not lettuce." Nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way at all. Rooftops aren't competing with housing."
2. Urban farming is appealing. → Woman: Nữ nêu "I find the whole idea rather lovely." Nam phản đối: "that's where you lose me. I'm not so sure it's charming at all."
3. Cities need more food. → Woman: Nữ nêu "This city genuinely hasn't got enough food coming into it." Nam phản đối: "I'll accept the figures you're quoting, but I don't read them that way. We aren't short of food."
4. Urban farming will benefit the urban economy. → Both: Nam nêu "it would do something real for jobs round here". Nữ tán thành: "Oh, absolutely, I agree with you there."
👉 Mẹo: Ý 3 là bẫy kinh điển — nam chấp nhận số liệu ("I'll accept the figures") nhưng bác bỏ kết luận, nên vẫn chỉ là Woman, không phải Both.

question_text: Future generations may struggle with information overload caused by technology.
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
Man: My little nephew asked me yesterday how people found addresses before phones, and I could not stop thinking about it afterwards. We built these tools, but the children who inherit them will swim in a flood we never knew. I worry the next generation will drown in the endless stream — more updates, more feeds, more alerts than any human mind was built to sort.
Woman: Funny, when I look at the same picture I mostly see the bright side. Since the digital wave arrived, whole industries have appeared out of nothing. My town alone has three software companies where the old mill used to stand, and the shops around them are full again. Whatever else these machines do, they have filled a lot of pay packets.
Man: The jobs are real, I will not argue there — though I notice you skipped my flood.
Woman: I did, because I trust people to build boats! And here is another hill I will stand on: nothing built from chips and wires will ever match what sits between our ears. A machine calculates; it does not wonder, doubt, or dream. The most powerful computer on earth is still a very fast filing clerk.
Man: I would be careful — the filing clerks are learning quickly. But let me raise the subject that actually keeps me up at night: everything we do is recorded by somebody. Our purchases, our routes, our conversations.
Woman: On that, no argument at all. The rules guarding our personal lives are years behind the machines. Both of us, for once, want the same thing: stronger walls around what belongs to each of us.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: M-W-W-B (giữ nguyên). Paraphrase:
1. "Future generations struggle with information overload" → M: "the next generation will drown in the endless stream" — W "I mostly see the bright side".
2. "Revolution good for economy" → W: "whole industries appeared... filled a lot of pay packets".
3. "No computer superior to human brain" → W: "nothing built from chips and wires will ever match what sits between our ears" — M "I would be careful".
4. "More should be done to protect privacy" → B: "everything we do is recorded" + "On that, no argument... stronger walls".

question_text: How many people live in the town?
explanation:
Welcome to Oakbridge, my friends! A little history before we enter the walls. A century ago this was a village of five thousand souls, mostly farmers and weavers. The mayor dreams aloud of reaching twenty thousand one day — you'll see his ambitious posters everywhere. But the honest number, from this year's census, is ten thousand residents exactly. Ten thousand people, two beautiful squares, and the best honey cake in the region, which we will taste in one hour!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 10,000.
• Vì sao đúng: "the honest number, from this year's census, is ten thousand residents exactly. Ten thousand people, two beautiful squares".
• 5,000 sai: đó là dân số của một thế kỷ trước ("A century ago this was a village of five thousand souls, mostly farmers and weavers").
• 20,000 sai: chỉ là mục tiêu thị trưởng mơ tới ("The mayor dreams aloud of reaching twenty thousand one day").
👉 Mẹo: số liệu dân số hay bị gài mốc quá khứ và mục tiêu tương lai. Chọn số đi kèm "today / this year's census / exactly".

question_text: A receptionist is checking the client list of a clinic. How many American clients are there?
options: Two
One
Three
explanation:
Let me run through Friday's bookings before I lock up. Morning block: Mr. Tanaka from Japan at nine, then Mrs. Almeida — she's Brazilian — at half past ten. After lunch we have the new patient, Mr. Harris from Chicago; he's our only American this week, I should flag his insurance forms. Then Miss Novak from Prague at three, and Doctor Rossi, Italian, closes the day at five. Five patients, one American. Forms printed tonight, coffee machine refilled — done!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – One.
• Vì sao đúng: "the new patient, Mr. Harris from Chicago; he's our only American this week" — và câu tổng kết "Five patients, one American".
• Two sai: bốn bệnh nhân còn lại đều không phải người Mỹ — "Mr. Tanaka from Japan", "Mrs. Almeida — she's Brazilian", "Miss Novak from Prague", "Doctor Rossi, Italian".
• Three sai: tổng cộng chỉ có năm bệnh nhân và người Mỹ duy nhất là Mr. Harris — "Five patients, one American".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi SỐ LƯỢNG theo tiêu chí (bao nhiêu người Mỹ), đừng chộp con số đầu tiên nghe được. Vừa nghe vừa đếm theo quốc tịch rồi đối chiếu câu tổng kết cuối bài.

question_text: A woman is calling her husband. What time is lunch ready?
options: 3pm
1pm
2pm
explanation:
Hi darling, it's me. Change of plan for lunch, listen carefully! I told you one o'clock this morning, but the plumber is still here fixing the sink, so the kitchen is a battlefield. I first thought I'd push everything to three, but then your mother called — she's dropping by at three thirty. So: lunch will be ready at two, on the dot. Two o'clock, and don't be late, the fish doesn't wait. Love you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 2pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "So: lunch will be ready at two, on the dot. Two o'clock, and don't be late, the fish doesn't wait".
• 1pm sai: giờ hẹn ban đầu, hỏng vì thợ sửa ống nước còn đang làm ("I told you one o'clock this morning, but the plumber is still here fixing the sink").
• 3pm sai: có nghĩ tới nhưng bỏ vì mẹ chồng ghé lúc 3h30 ("I first thought I'd push everything to three, but then your mother called").
👉 Mẹo: tin nhắn đổi giờ luôn theo mô-típ "giờ cũ – giờ định dời – giờ chốt". Chọn giờ đi kèm từ chốt "So:" và được nhắc lại ngay sau đó.

question_text: What occurs when things don't go according to plan in a team?
options: The team members lose confidence.
The team members become more assured.
The team members start again from the beginning.
explanation:
Before I became a business coach, I spent ten years leading software teams, and tonight I want to share the most important lesson from those years: what really happens when a project goes wrong. Picture the scene — the deadline arrives, the product is not ready, the client is unhappy. What do the team members do next? The comfortable answer is that they calmly return to the beginning and start the plan again, like scientists repeating an experiment. An even more comfortable answer is that failure makes a strong team more assured, more determined than before. I have watched this moment dozens of times, and I can tell you what actually happens: the team members lose confidence. Quietly, one by one, people start wondering whether they are good enough. Meetings become careful, ideas dry up, and the next piece of work takes twice as long — not because the task is harder, but because the belief is gone.
A leader's job in that moment is to rebuild belief, and there are two popular shortcuts that do not work. Pouring extra money in — increasing the project budget significantly — changes nothing about how people feel. And focusing on individual performance only, measuring each person against the others, just adds fear to the disappointment. What works is almost embarrassingly simple: set a realistic goal. Give the team a target they can genuinely reach this week, then another next week. Every small success returns a piece of the confidence that failure took away, and step by step, the team learns to trust itself again.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 09 bài 2 — cùng câu hỏi và đáp án, lời khác để hai đề không trùng script.)
1. Đáp án: The team members lose confidence. Bẫy: "start again from the beginning" và "become more assured" đều là "câu trả lời dễ chịu" bị bác bằng trải nghiệm thực.
2. Đáp án: Set a realistic goal. Bẫy: "increase the project budget" và "focus on individual performance only" là hai lối tắt "do not work".

question_text: Media exaggerates the benefits of the programme
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
M: There have been so many volunteer events recently that it's almost impossible not to talk about them on my podcast.
W: Fair enough.
M: First of all, these volunteer groups have become incredibly popular — the media everywhere is covering them. But honestly, I think what these events actually achieve is being blown out of proportion.
W: I agree with you there. The press keeps saying these groups are going to change the whole world and fix the environment, when in fact they only deal with a tiny part of the problem. There are plenty of other issues going on.
M: Like littering — for me that's one of the biggest problems in society today. People assume dropping one wrapper has a tiny effect, but it all adds up until it becomes a huge issue.
W: Hmm, I'm not sure it's as serious as you make out — there are far bigger things to worry about. But let's leave that to one side. What I want to say is that these volunteers are getting a lot of publicity — interviews, posts, articles — and I think that's a good thing. Whether they do it for fame, for personal reasons or for the community, it makes no difference to the result: it still draws more people into volunteering.
M: I don't see it that way. If people who volunteer for their own benefit get all that publicity, it doesn't just attract more volunteers — it can backfire. You end up with people volunteering to boost their ego rather than to help the community, and that does change what the programme achieves.
W: OK, let's go back to the litter problem, since you feel so strongly about it. What do you think should be done?
M: The best approach is to introduce penalties. Other countries have very tough punishments — heavy fines, even prison — and the figures show those countries have far lower rates of littering.
W: I'll accept the figures, but I don't think punishment is the most appropriate answer here. A fine changes behaviour for a week and then people forget. What actually works is education and making it easy to do the right thing — more bins, clearer signs, campaigns in schools. Change the habit, not just the price of breaking it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key theo đề thật 16/9: Media exaggerates = Both · Littering main problem = Man · Volunteers' motivations don't affect the outcome = Woman · Punishment most effective = Man.
1. Media exaggerates the benefits → Both: anh nói "blown out of proportion", cô "I agree with you there".
2. Littering is a major problem → The man: "one of the biggest problems in society today". Cô không đồng ý: "I'm not sure it's as serious as you make out".
3. Motivations do not affect the outcome → The woman: "Whether they do it for fame, for personal reasons or for the community, it makes no difference to the result". Anh phản bác: "it can backfire... that does change what the programme achieves".
4. Punishment is the most effective way → The man: "The best approach is to introduce penalties". Cô: "I don't think punishment is the most appropriate answer".
👉 Mẹo: câu 2 và 3 là bẫy — người nói đồng ý với SỐ LIỆU nhưng không đồng ý với KẾT LUẬN thì vẫn không phải Both.

question_text: What does the speaker say mostly affects concentration?
options: Concentration depends mostly on environment.
Concentration is primarily influenced by individual effort.
Concentration depends mainly on external distractions.
explanation:
Good morning. Today's lecture is about concentration — what really controls it, and what we keep getting wrong about it. Most people believe staying focused is mainly a matter of individual effort: try harder, be more disciplined, and the focus will come. Others blame everything on external distractions — the phone, the noisy colleague, the notifications. Both ideas contain a grain of truth, but research in psychology points somewhere else. What mostly affects concentration is your environment. The lighting in your room, the level of background noise, even the way your desk is arranged — these quiet factors decide how long your attention lasts, far more than willpower does. A tired student in a calm, well-lit library will usually focus better than a determined one in a chaotic cafe. If you want to concentrate, do not fight with yourself; redesign the space around you first.
The second misunderstanding is about our limits. We live in a culture that celebrates working non-stop, and I sometimes meet people who genuinely believe they excel at managing their own attention, or who claim they always recognise when their focus is running out. The evidence says otherwise. People often fail to consider the limits of concentration at all. Attention is a finite resource, like the battery in your phone, and it drains whether you notice or not. We push through hour after hour, wondering why the work gets slower and the mistakes pile up, when the honest answer is simple: the battery is empty, and only a real break can recharge it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Concentration depends mostly on environment. Bẫy: "individual effort" và "external distractions" đều được nhắc rồi bị hạ ("a grain of truth, but...").
2. Đáp án: People often fail to consider the limits of concentration. Bẫy: "excel at managing" và "always recognise" là niềm tin bị bác ("The evidence says otherwise").

question_text: What is she going to take with her?
options: games
books
food
explanation:
Hi Laura, it's me! I'm almost finished packing for the weekend at the lake house. I thought about bringing some books, but honestly, the bag is heavy enough already and I never open them anyway. And don't worry about food — Auntie says the kitchen there is full, so we don't need to carry anything to eat. What I AM going to take is the games — the cards and the big box of board games. Rainy evenings at the lake need games! See you at seven!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – games.
• Vì sao đúng: "What I AM going to take is the games — the cards and the big box of board games. Rainy evenings at the lake need games!".
• books sai: cô nghĩ tới rồi bỏ vì túi đã quá nặng — "I thought about bringing some books, but honestly, the bag is heavy enough already and I never open them anyway".
• food sai: không cần mang vì bếp ở nhà hồ đã đầy đồ — "Auntie says the kitchen there is full, so we don't need to carry anything to eat".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "mang theo gì", bám câu nhấn mạnh "What I AM going to take is...". Món đi kèm "I thought about... but" hay "we don't need to" là loại.

question_text: How many pages of the assignment?
explanation:
Before you all rush out — one last thing about the history assignment! I've had three emails asking about the length, so let's settle it now. The instructions sheet from last year said six pages, but that was for the old course — ignore it. Somebody also heard five pages from the other class; that's their topic, not ours. For this assignment, I want exactly four pages — no more, no less. Four pages, typed, on my desk by Friday morning. Have a good weekend!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 4.
• Vì sao đúng: "For this assignment, I want exactly four pages — no more, no less. Four pages, typed, on my desk by Friday morning".
• 6 sai: là số trang trong tờ hướng dẫn của khóa CŨ — "The instructions sheet from last year said six pages, but that was for the old course — ignore it".
• 5 sai: là yêu cầu của lớp khác với đề tài khác — "Somebody also heard five pages from the other class; that's their topic, not ours".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi số trang/số lượng, bám cụm "For THIS assignment, I want...". Số gắn với "last year", "the other class" đều bị loại.

question_text: Art is only suitable for the privileged few
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
W: Did you hear? The city has allocated 150 million dollars to fund arts programmes over the next year. That brings a lot of controversy among the residents.
M: I get why it's controversial. People pay taxes expecting their quality of life to improve - better infrastructure, cheaper public transport. Tax money should go towards the public interest. Only a small handful of people can actually afford those stage productions, concerts and painting exhibitions.
W: I don't see it that way. Anyone can just buy a ticket.
M: Those venues should run like any other business - deliver good service so customers keep coming back. From what I've seen, tickets to the theater and to art exhibits are really expensive. And if they're already taking in ticket money, why does the government keep pouring more in?
W: Actually, places like museums would have to close down without funding. If anything, I'd say those figures should be higher. And with that money, kids get the chance to encounter music and art from a young age.
M: That part I agree with. I'd like my own children to come across the arts at their school. Back then, it was pretty hard for our generation to get to see a musical.
W: Future generations will definitely find it much easier to reach those things.
M: OK, let's see.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
LƯU Ý: Đây là bản MỚI theo đề thi thật 25/8 (bài quỹ 150 triệu đô cho nghệ thuật), thay bản cũ. Key chuẩn: M-W-B-W.

1. Chỉ người ĐÀN ÔNG cho rằng nghệ thuật chỉ dành cho số ít: "Only a small handful of people can actually afford those stage productions, concerts and painting exhibitions." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way. Anyone can just buy a ticket."
2. Chỉ người PHỤ NỮ muốn chính phủ đầu tư thêm: "If anything, I'd say those figures should be higher." Người đàn ông ngược lại thắc mắc "why does the government keep pouring more in?"
3. CẢ HAI đồng ý trẻ em nên tiếp xúc nghệ thuật sớm. Người phụ nữ: "kids get the chance to encounter music and art from a young age." Người đàn ông: "That part I agree with. I'd like my own children to come across the arts at their school."
4. Chỉ người PHỤ NỮ tin tương lai nghệ thuật dễ tiếp cận hơn: "Future generations will definitely find it much easier to reach those things." Người đàn ông chỉ đáp "OK, let's see" — hoài nghi, không đồng tình.

question_text: Why does the brother find traveling meaningful?
options: Because it allows him to escape his professional responsibilities.
Because he wants to document his trips for social media influence.
Because it brings him joy and chances to learn about different cultures.
explanation:
My brother has always loved travelling, though people often misunderstand why he does it. Some of his colleagues believe he is simply trying to escape the pressure of his job — running away from deadlines by booking another flight. Others are sure he travels to feed his social media accounts, collecting beautiful photos to make his followers jealous. I can tell you that both guesses are wrong. He posts almost nothing online, and he plans his trips during his calmest months at work, not his busiest. The truth is much simpler: travelling brings him real joy and endless chances to learn about different cultures. He comes home full of stories about a cooking lesson in a small village or a festival he happened to walk into. Those moments of connection with local people and their traditions are, for him, the whole point of going anywhere.
I often tell him that his travelling is remarkably similar to my reading. Now, I do not mean they are alike because both are mandatory for academic success — no school forces you to wander through Vietnam or to finish a novel by Friday. Nor do they match because both demand great physical endurance; my sofa asks very little of me. The real similarity is deeper: both help people discover new worlds and grow as a person. Every country he visits changes him a little, and every book I finish changes me. When we compare notes at family dinners, we are really describing the same journey — his through places, mine through pages.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Because it brings him joy and chances to learn about different cultures. Bẫy: "escape responsibilities" và "social media" đều là suy đoán của người khác bị bác ("both guesses are wrong").
2. Đáp án: Both help people discover new worlds and grow as a person. Bẫy: "mandatory for academic success" và "physical endurance" đều bị phủ định hài hước.

question_text: Four people are talking about using the Internet. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My evenings have one ritual: lights off, snacks ready, and something good on the screen. The internet has turned my little bedroom into a cinema — old classics, new releases, series from Korea and Spain with subtitles. I have not bought a cinema ticket in two years, because why queue when the whole film library of the world sits behind my login? Saturday nights, my sister joins me and we argue for twenty minutes about what to watch.
Speaker B: Half the people I love live in other time zones now — university scattered us across three continents. So my internet hours are spent talking: video calls with my best friend in Toronto every Sunday, voice messages to the group that never sleeps, long chats with my old roommate about nothing. Without the connection, those friendships would have faded into birthday texts. With it, we still finish each other's sentences from opposite sides of the planet.
Speaker C: For me the internet is basically a homework machine. Every essay starts with the online library, every presentation leans on the journals my university subscribes to, and when the deadline panics arrive, the tutorial videos save my grade. Last term I wrote my entire dissertation without borrowing a single paper book. My classmates use it the same way — the night before submission, you can feel the whole class online, typing.
Speaker D: I check one thing before leaving the house, always: which bus is actually coming, and when. The app knows about the roadworks before the radio does, shows me where my bus is crawling on the map, and reroutes me when the trains misbehave. Since I started trusting it, I have stopped standing at stops in the rain guessing. My whole journey to work is planned by my phone before I finish my coffee.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = watch film (keyword "cinema... film library"). B = communicate with friends (PARAPHRASE: "spent talking... video calls... friendships"). C = complete school assignments (PARAPHRASE: "homework machine... essay... dissertation"). D = find transport information (keyword "which bus is coming... journey planned"). Nhiễu: online courses, games.

question_text: Four people are talking about protecting the environment. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My rule is simple: nothing usable leaves this house in a rubbish bag. The clothes my sons outgrow go to the church collection, the old bookshelf went to a student down the road, and my ancient laptop now lives at the community centre. Last month a young couple collected our spare bed within an hour of my posting it. Watching things start a second life in someone else's home feels far better than watching a skip swallow them.
Speaker B: I read labels the way detectives read clues. Before anything enters my basket, I check where it was made, what the packaging is, whether the company behaves itself. I pay a little more for washing liquid that rivers can forgive and coffee that farmers were fairly paid for. My husband groans at how long shopping takes, but every purchase is a small vote, and I intend to vote well.
Speaker C: In my kitchen, nothing with a lid gets thrown away. The big yoghurt pots hold my soup portions in the freezer, glass jars keep the rice and lentils, and the ice-cream tubs — washed, of course — carry my lunches to work. My cupboard looks like a museum of old packaging, I admit. But I have not bought a plastic box in six years, and my leftovers never see a rubbish bin.
Speaker D: I stopped trusting those bright bottles under the sink years ago. Vinegar and baking soda handle my kitchen, lemon juice brightens the taps, and the floors get plain hot water with a drop of olive soap. The chemical sprays with their skull warnings have not entered this flat since my daughter was born. My windows shine just as well, and the air in here smells of lemons instead of a laboratory.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = give away used items (PARAPHRASE: "second life in someone else's home" — cho đồ cũ). B = buy environmentally friendly products (PARAPHRASE: "washing liquid that rivers can forgive... every purchase is a small vote"). C = reuse containers for storing food (keyword "pots hold... jars keep... carry my lunches"). D = not buy commercial cleaning products (keyword "bright bottles... chemical sprays... not entered this flat"). Nhiễu: recycle waste, public transport.

question_text: People share similar ideas about beauty
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
M: You went to that photography exhibition at the weekend, didn't you? What was it actually like?
W: Fascinating, genuinely. Portraits from about twelve different countries. And what struck me was how much overlap there was. Deep down, I think we all recognise the same faces as attractive, wherever we happen to come from.
M: Hmm, I'm not so sure about that. I'd say what counts as attractive varies enormously from one place to another. It's almost entirely learned, in my view.
W: There's quite a lot of research suggesting otherwise, you know.
M: I'll accept the research exists, but I'm not convinced it proves very much. What I am certain of is that these things shift with the decades. Look at any family album and you'll see the standards moving.
W: Well, that rather depends what you're looking at. I'd argue the fashions change, the hair and the clothes, but the underlying face people admire stays remarkably steady.
M: We'll have to differ on that one, I think.
W: We will, clearly. Though there was one room I absolutely loved. Photographs of an old scrapyard, of all places, and they were genuinely lovely to look at.
M: Oh, I'm completely with you there. Some of the most striking things I've ever seen have been in spots you'd never think to look. Building sites, motorway bridges, that sort of thing.
W: Exactly my point. It turns up wherever it likes, and usually where nobody's expecting it.
M: It does. And that's partly why I think the old-fashioned standards are quietly on their way out. The next generation simply won't put up with them.
W: I don't see that happening, personally. People have been predicting exactly that for fifty years now, and the magazines still look much the same to me.
M: Give it another ten years and ask me again.
W: I'll believe it when I see it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Mọi người có quan niệm giống nhau về cái đẹp = Woman · Quan niệm về cái đẹp thay đổi theo thời gian = Man · Cái đẹp có thể tìm thấy ở nơi bất ngờ = Both · Quan niệm truyền thống về cái đẹp sẽ thay đổi = Man

1. People share similar ideas about beauty → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "Deep down, I think we all recognise the same faces as attractive, wherever we happen to come from." Người đàn ông phản đối: "Hmm, I'm not so sure about that. I'd say what counts as attractive varies enormously from one place to another."

2. Ideas about beauty change over time → Man: người đàn ông nêu "these things shift with the decades. Look at any family album and you'll see the standards moving." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'd argue the fashions change... but the underlying face people admire stays remarkably steady."

3. Beauty can be found in unlikely places → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "Photographs of an old scrapyard, of all places, and they were genuinely lovely to look at.", người đàn ông tán thành: "Oh, I'm completely with you there. Some of the most striking things I've ever seen have been in spots you'd never think to look."

4. Traditional ideas about beauty are going to change → Man: người đàn ông nêu "the old-fashioned standards are quietly on their way out. The next generation simply won't put up with them." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I don't see that happening, personally... the magazines still look much the same to me."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy ở ý 1 — "I'll accept the research exists" của người đàn ông chỉ là nhượng bộ một nửa, không phải đồng ý, nên ý 1 vẫn là Woman chứ không phải Both.

question_text: What are the critic's opinions about the restaurant?
options: The food is not fresh
The service is not good
The chief lack of experience
explanation:
I have reviewed restaurants for many years, so I was genuinely looking forward to my evening at La Bella Bistro. Let me be fair first. The food was perfectly fine — the fish arrived fresh, the vegetables were crisp, and nobody could complain about the plate in front of them. The chef clearly knows what he is doing; you can taste years of experience in the sauces. So no, the kitchen is not the problem. The problem, and it is a serious one, is the service. From the moment I sat down, the staff seemed either too busy or too poorly trained to look after their guests. I waited twenty minutes for a glass of water, my questions about the menu were answered in a hurry, and when the main course finally arrived, the waiter had already turned away before I could say thank you. Good cooking cannot rescue an evening like that.
And this matters more than ever, because restaurants today are competing with food delivery apps. Some owners think the answer is organic ingredients, and others are experimenting with ready-made packs that customers can finish cooking at home. Those ideas are fine, but they miss the real point. The one thing an app can never deliver is the feeling of being truly valued and welcomed. A warm greeting at the door, a waiter who remembers your name, the sense that your visit actually matters — that is what makes people leave their sofa and book a table. Until La Bella Bistro understands this, its dining room will stay half empty.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: The service is not good. Bẫy: "food is not fresh" bị phủ định ("arrived fresh"), "chef lacks experience" bị phủ định ("years of experience"). Phương án 3 sửa lại chính tả từ "The chief lack of experience".
2. Đáp án: Customers feel valued and welcome. Bẫy: "organic ingredients" và "ready-made pack" đều được nhắc là ý tưởng của chủ quán khác rồi bị gạt ("miss the real point").

question_text: Which sports is she good at?
options: Running
Swimming
Football
explanation:
Sports day is coming and everyone assumes I'll enter everything — if only they knew! Running? I look enthusiastic for exactly one hundred metres, then the wheels fall off. Swimming lessons were even worse; the instructor said I fight the water instead of moving through it. But football — football is my kingdom. Left wing, eight years, top scorer for the district two seasons running. Put me on the grass with a ball and everything suddenly makes sense.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Football.
• Vì sao đúng: "football is my kingdom. Left wing, eight years, top scorer for the district two seasons running".
• Running sai: chỉ giữ được sức đúng 100m rồi đuối ("I look enthusiastic for exactly one hundred metres, then the wheels fall off").
• Swimming sai: huấn luyện viên nhận xét cô chống lại nước chứ không bơi ("the instructor said I fight the water instead of moving through it").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "good at" — tìm bằng chứng thành tích cụ thể (số năm, vị trí thi đấu, top scorer). Lời tự trào hài hước luôn báo hiệu môn KHÔNG giỏi.

question_text: Four people are talking about their studying habits. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: The house is chaos until about ten — children, dishes, doorbells. So my textbooks wait, and they know they will get me when everyone else has surrendered to sleep. Between eleven and two, the flat is mine: no interruptions, no noise, just the desk lamp and my notes. My friends call those hours unnatural. I call them the only hours the world agrees to leave me alone, and my best marks were all born in them.
Speaker B: Ask my friends where I revise and they will laugh: everywhere. The train into college, the bench outside the sports hall, my aunt's kitchen, the launderette while my clothes spin. I have finished essays in waiting rooms and memorised vocabulary in a queue. One fixed desk makes my mind stiff; carrying my notes through the day keeps them alive. My record is studying in six locations before dinner — and remembering every page of it.
Speaker C: My secret weapon has wires: nothing enters my head without a soundtrack. Gentle jazz for heavy reading, film scores for essays, and one particular symphony that has carried me through every exam since I was sixteen. The melodies build a wall between me and the world, and inside that wall everything sticks. Silence, strangely, is what distracts me — my thoughts scatter without a rhythm to hold them in line.
Speaker D: I have one requirement, and it is absolute: no sound. I revise in the reading room where even a cough draws stares, or at home with everyone out and the windows shut. One barking dog can cost me a whole paragraph. My sister studies happily in noisy cafés and I genuinely do not understand how. For my brain, stillness is not a preference — it is the on switch.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = study late at night (PARAPHRASE: "between eleven and two... hours the world leaves me alone"). B = at various places (PARAPHRASE: "everywhere... six locations before dinner"). C = with music (keyword "soundtrack... melodies"). D = in a quiet place (keyword-lite "no sound... stillness"). Nhiễu: in a group, early morning.

question_text: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: Let me be the villain of this recording: sport and I are enemies, and we always have been. School athletics scarred me for life — the whistle, the shouting, the cold mud. As an adult I have politely tried yoga, tennis and one horrifying spinning class, and I walked out of each one certain of my truth. Some people were built to move; I was built to sit in a warm café watching them through the window.
Speaker B: I never cared about sport until my job nearly broke me. Endless reports, afternoon headaches, a brain like wet paper by Thursday. My doctor prescribed movement instead of pills, and the change shocked me: three morning swims a week, and suddenly my reports finish before lunch and my ideas queue up politely instead of hiding. My manager keeps asking what changed. The swimming pool changed, I tell her — everything else followed.
Speaker C: I admire people who bounce out of the gym glowing. My experience is the opposite: halfway through any session, my arms resign, my legs file complaints, and the last ten minutes happen in slow motion. Afterwards I do not glow — I collapse. Friends insist that one day the heaviness turns into energy. I have given it two years; the heaviness has only learned my name.
Speaker D: For me the magic ingredient is company. Saturday football with my old classmates, evening badminton with the people from my building — we play badly and laugh loudly, and that is exactly the point. Once, when everyone was away, I tried exercising by myself and quit in fifteen minutes from pure boredom. Put my friends on the court, though, and I will happily chase a ball until midnight.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---

C = find exercise tiring (keyword-lite "heaviness... collapse... slow motion"). D = has fun when exercising with friends (keyword "with my old classmates... laugh loudly"). Nhiễu: lose weight, alone.

question_text: Four people are talking about where they like to run. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: Rain, snow, heatwave — none of it matters to me anymore, because my kilometres happen indoors at the sports club. The machines measure everything, the physio works two doors down, and after my knee operation last year that safety means a lot. I book the same treadmill by the window every morning at six. My running friends call indoor running fake running. I call it running that my surgeon approves of.
Speaker B: I moved to the coast three years ago, and now I cannot imagine training anywhere else. Low tide gives me two kilometres of firm, flat sand, the salt air fills my lungs, and the sound of the water sets my rhythm better than any playlist. Some mornings I share the beach with nobody but the gulls and one old fisherman. My city friends visit, run one sunrise with me, and start checking property prices by lunchtime.
Speaker C: Give me the pavements, the crossings, the crowds — my route cuts straight through the busiest part of town. I time my runs by the bakery smells and wave at the flower seller setting up her stall. Yes, I stop for traffic lights, and yes, the ground is hard. But a city waking up around you is the best film ever made, and I get a free showing every single morning.
Speaker D: I train with a club, and we are spoiled: our sessions happen at the athletics stadium, on the proper red surface, under the floodlights. Marked lanes, exact distances, a coach with a whistle and no mercy. Interval nights are brutal — sprint, recover, sprint again, all measured to the metre. But when race day comes, I know my pace to the second, and that certainty was built lap by counted lap.
