question_text: What does the speaker say about the way of writing?
options: It is focused on technical details
It is exciting to read
It is more of a textbook than a biography
explanation:
I have just finished a new biography of a famous physicist, and I want to recommend it to all of you. Let me deal with the doubts first, because I had them too. When I picked it up, I was afraid it would be focused on technical details — page after page of equations that only a physicist could love. I also worried it might read more like a textbook than the story of a real person's life. I am happy to report that neither fear came true. The book is genuinely exciting to read. The author tells the scientist's life like an adventure story: the failed experiments, the rivalries, the night the famous discovery finally worked. I found myself reading until two in the morning, which almost never happens with science books.
Why does the book work so well? The secret is who it was written for. Some biographies of great scientists are really only suitable for experts in the field — full of special terms, with no explanations for the rest of us. And some, to be fair, are accurate but completely lack engaging storytelling. This one is different: it has been written for a general audience from the very first page. Complex ideas are explained through simple pictures from everyday life, so you need no scientific background at all. That choice explains why it has already become a bestseller, and why experts predict it will be as successful as the author's previous book. If you enjoyed that one, you will certainly enjoy this.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It is exciting to read. Bẫy: "focused on technical details" và "more of a textbook" đều là NỖI LO ban đầu và bị phủ định ("neither fear came true").
2. Đáp án: It has been written for a general audience. Bẫy: "only suitable for experts" và "lacks engaging storytelling" được nhắc là đặc điểm của các sách KHÁC ("Some biographies...").

question_text: What was one major problem the railways faced?
options: Not making enough money
Extreme weather damaging the tracks
The lack of qualified engineers and staff
explanation:
Welcome to today's talk on the history of our railways, and let me take you back to the middle of the twentieth century, the hardest period the network ever faced. When people guess what went wrong in those years, they usually mention extreme weather damaging the tracks, or a shortage of qualified engineers and staff. In fact, the tracks survived the storms well enough, and the railway schools were still producing plenty of capable engineers. The real problem was money — the railways were simply not making enough of it. Cars and trucks had become cheap and popular, so ticket sales and freight income fell year after year, while the cost of maintaining old bridges, stations and engines kept climbing. By the end of the decade, several lines were losing money every single day they operated.
What did the leadership do about it? This is the part of the story that historians still argue about. Some board members wanted to sell major assets to international investors, and one report even suggested suspending all operations for a complete restructure. The leader in charge rejected both ideas. Instead, he decided to continue the policies that had already been implemented in previous years — the same timetables, the same prices, the same structure — believing the economy would eventually turn and passengers would return by themselves. They did not. Most historians now agree that this decision to simply wait made the crisis longer and deeper than it needed to be, and it remains a warning for managers today.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Not making enough money. Bẫy: "extreme weather" và "lack of qualified engineers" đều bị phủ định ("survived the storms", "plenty of capable engineers").
2. Đáp án: Continuing policies that had already been implemented. Bẫy: "selling assets" và "suspending all operations" là đề xuất bị lãnh đạo TỪ CHỐI ("rejected both ideas").

question_text: What should students do when choosing a career?
options: Choose the same career as their friends
Be flexible and open minded
Focus only on the salary offered
explanation:
Good morning, graduates. Life after university can be exciting, but I will not pretend it is easy, so let me offer some honest advice about choosing a career. The most common mistake I see is students choosing the same career as their friends, simply because it feels safe to move in a group. The second mistake is looking only at the salary in the job advertisement and ignoring everything else about the role. I understand both temptations, but neither leads to a happy working life. A big salary in a job you hate becomes small very quickly, and your friends cannot live your career for you. What you should do instead is stay flexible and open-minded. Explore different industries, try roles you had never considered, and remember that your first job is only the first step on a much longer road. The people who do best after university are almost never the ones with a fixed plan; they are the ones who keep their eyes and options open.
Now, a word about the job market itself, because you deserve the truth. Yes, there are more opportunities for networking than ever before, with online platforms and career events everywhere. And yes, some jobs offer great benefits, from travel to flexible hours. But the single characteristic you must prepare for is this: the market is more competitive than it has ever been. Dozens of candidates apply for every good position, and a degree alone is no longer enough. Bring skills, bring experience, bring a positive attitude — and show clearly what makes you different.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Be flexible and open minded. Bẫy: "choose the same career as friends" và "focus only on the salary" đều được nhắc là SAI LẦM phổ biến.
2. Đáp án: More competitive. Bẫy: "networking" và "great benefits" đều được công nhận có thật nhưng đặc điểm phải chuẩn bị là tính cạnh tranh ("the single characteristic you must prepare for").

question_text: Listen to a voice message. How does Evan feel?
options: Happy
Tired
Sick
explanation:
Team, it's Evan, voice message because typing feels like mountaineering today. First — no, I'm not just tired, I wish! I slept ten hours and feel worse. And despite the beach photos from last week, nobody is happy over here anymore, believe me. The clinic confirmed it: a proper virus, fever, the full package. I'm in bed, contagious and useless, until Thursday minimum. Push my meetings, water my desk plant, and stay away from my office chair!

• Tired sai: chính anh bác bỏ ngay đầu bài — "no, I'm not just tired, I wish! I slept ten hours and feel worse".
• Happy sai: chỉ được nhắc để phủ định — "despite the beach photos from last week, nobody is happy over here anymore".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi cảm xúc/trạng thái luôn thả đủ 3 tính từ. Chọn tính từ nằm trong câu KHẲNG ĐỊNH có bằng chứng cụ thể (bác sĩ, triệu chứng); bỏ tính từ đi kèm "not", "I wish", "despite".

question_text: How does the speaker recommend saving money effectively?
options: Saving a large amount only on a daily basis.
Save a fixed amount regularly.
Use credit cards to manage expenses.
explanation:
Good afternoon, everyone. Today I want to share some simple ideas about managing your money, because saving is a skill anyone can learn. Let me start with the most common questions I get. Some people try to save a large amount in one go — they put aside a big sum after a bonus, feel proud for a week, and then save nothing for months. Others believe the answer is using credit cards to manage their expenses, telling themselves they will pay everything back later. In my experience, both approaches usually end in disappointment. What actually works is much less exciting: save a fixed amount regularly. Choose a number you can manage, even a small one, and move it into your savings account every single month. Better still, make the transfer automatic, so the money is gone before you have a chance to spend it. If you wait until the end of the month and save whatever is left, there will usually be nothing left. Regular beats big, every time.
And who actually succeeds with money? I have watched hundreds of savers over the years. It is not the people who keep all their savings in one account, and it is certainly not the ones who avoid making any long-term plans because planning feels stressful. The people who save most successfully are the ones who get advice from people with real experience — a parent who has managed a household budget for thirty years, a colleague who has already bought a home, or a professional adviser. Money wisdom is learned fastest from those who already have it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Save a fixed amount regularly. Bẫy: "saving a large amount" và "use credit cards" đều được nhắc rồi bị loại ("both approaches usually end in disappointment").
2. Đáp án: Get advice from people that have experience. Bẫy: "keep all savings in a single account" và "avoid long-term plans" đều bị phủ định trực tiếp.

question_text: A man is talking about his eating habit. What time does he usually eat?
options: 8 o'clock
7 o'clock
5 o'clock
explanation:
My eating schedule confuses every dinner guest we've ever had! Most of my friends eat at eight, fashionably late, wine and candles. My brother's family sits down at five like clockwork, farmers' hours, he calls it. Me? Seven o'clock, every single evening, rain or shine. It started with my old night shifts and simply stayed. Seven — early enough to digest, late enough to cook properly. My stomach could replace the town clock, my wife says!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 7 o'clock.
• Vì sao đúng: "Me? Seven o'clock, every single evening, rain or shine" — và "Seven — early enough to digest, late enough to cook properly".
• 8 o'clock sai: đó là giờ ăn của bạn bè anh — "Most of my friends eat at eight, fashionably late, wine and candles".
• 5 o'clock sai: đó là giờ ăn của gia đình ông anh trai — "My brother's family sits down at five like clockwork, farmers' hours".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi thói quen của NGƯỜI NÓI, bắt tín hiệu đổi chủ ngữ "Me?", "As for me". Giờ gắn với "my friends", "my brother" chỉ là nền so sánh.

question_text: There is too much information on the Internet
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
M: How did you get on with that evening course you signed up for — the online one?
W: I scraped through it, just about. Honestly, the worst part is that there's an endless mountain of stuff online — far more than any human being could ever wade through.
M: I'm not so sure that's the real trouble, though. I'll grant you it looks overwhelming at first glance, but a decent city bookshop holds more than you'd read in ten lifetimes and nobody ever moans about that.
W: Hang on, a bookshop has been filtered by somebody who knows what they're doing. Which brings me to my next point, actually — fishing out something you can actually trust online is a proper skill in its own right.
M: Oh, I agree with you there completely. Choosing the right search terms, spotting when a site is quietly selling you something — none of that comes naturally to anybody.
W: Exactly. My students click whatever sits at the top of the page and take it as gospel.
M: Mine do the same. And I'd go a step further, actually — I think all this scrolling is genuinely rewiring the way we reason things out.
W: Hmm, I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. I'll accept our habits have shifted — nobody reads a newspaper cover to cover any more. But our actual reasoning? No, that's much as it ever was.
M: You say that, but I can't hold an argument in my head the way I used to.
W: That's called being forty, I'd say.
M: Fair enough. One thing I am certain of, mind you — youngsters today simply won't wait for anything.
W: Now that I do agree with, one hundred per cent. If a video takes four seconds to load, they've swiped away and forgotten it ever existed.
M: My nephew watches entire films on double speed. I find it baffling.
W: I've caught myself doing exactly that, to be honest. Perhaps it isn't only the young after all.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Quá nhiều thông tin trên Internet = Woman · Tìm thông tin cần kỹ năng = Both · Internet ảnh hưởng cách ta tư duy = Man · Internet khiến giới trẻ thiếu kiên nhẫn = Both

1. There is too much information on the Internet → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "there's an endless mountain of stuff online — far more than any human being could ever wade through". Người đàn ông phản đối: "I'm not so sure that's the real trouble, though."

2. Finding information on the Internet requires skills → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "fishing out something you can actually trust online is a proper skill in its own right", người đàn ông tán thành rõ ràng: "Oh, I agree with you there completely."

3. The use of the Internet affects the way we think. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "I think all this scrolling is genuinely rewiring the way we reason things out". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "Hmm, I don't see it that way, I'm afraid."

4. The Internet makes young people less patient. → Both: người đàn ông nêu "youngsters today simply won't wait for anything", người phụ nữ đồng ý: "Now that I do agree with, one hundred per cent."

👉 Mẹo: Cả ý 1 và ý 3 đều có bẫy nhượng bộ một nửa —"I'll grant you it looks overwhelming" và "I'll accept our habits have shifted" nghe như tán thành, nhưng ngay sau đó người nói bác bỏ đúng phần cốt lõi, nên không phải Both.

question_text: What does the speaker say about short-term goals?
options: It helps people adjust their priorities when circumstances change.
It creates pressure and limits creativity
It only apply to specific situations or certain types of people
explanation:
Today I want to talk about making plans, and especially about short-term goals, because they have an unfair reputation. Many people believe short-term goals only apply to specific situations or certain types of people — students before exams, perhaps, or athletes before a competition. Others complain that these goals create pressure and limit creativity, as if writing down a target somehow locks your imagination in a box. Both views miss what short-term goals actually do best. Their real strength is flexibility: they help people adjust their priorities when circumstances change. Say you plan to read three books this month, and then a busy project lands on your desk. A short-term goal bends easily — you read one book instead, and set a fresh target next month. Nothing is broken, nothing is lost, and you are still moving forward. Long plans crack when life changes; short goals simply bend.
Now let me widen the picture to goal setting in general, because here too the common opinions are wrong. You will hear that having goals leads to confusion and distraction, with too many targets pulling you in different directions. And optimistic people love to say that goals bring about wonderful opportunities. My view, after years of coaching, is more practical than either: goal setting can prevent you from making mistakes. When your goal is written clearly, you check every decision against it, and you notice bad choices before you make them. The person without goals says yes to everything and discovers the mistake afterwards. The person with goals sees it coming.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It helps people adjust their priorities when circumstances change. Bẫy: "create pressure and limit creativity" và "only apply to specific situations" đều được nhắc là quan niệm sai ("Both views miss...").
2. Đáp án: It can prevent you from making mistakes. Bẫy: "confusion and distraction" là lời phàn nàn của người khác, "bring about opportunities" là lời của "optimistic people" — người nói chọn ý thực dụng hơn cả hai.

question_text: Four people are talking about their studying habits. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: People laugh when they see my rucksack — my books live in it because my study spot changes daily. Monday might be the kitchen table, Tuesday the bus, Wednesday a café, Thursday the steps outside the lecture hall if the sun is out. Staying in one seat makes my brain fall asleep; a fresh background keeps the material fresh too. My record is five different spots in a single day of revision, and that was my best exam ever.
Speaker B: For me, the enemy is sound. One conversation through the wall, one motorbike outside, and the sentence I was holding shatters. So I have built myself a little fortress: the back corner of the top floor of the library, behind the old journals nobody touches. Not a whisper reaches there. My friends know that between two and six I simply disappear from the world — that silence is where my concentration lives.
Speaker C: My housemates find it strange, but I cannot open a textbook without my headphones on. Soft piano for reading, something with a beat for writing notes — the melodies wrap around me like a wall and the hours slide by. In a silent room my thoughts wander everywhere; give them a soundtrack and they march in line. My playlist for the final exams lasted nine hours, and I knew every note by the end.
Speaker D: My day belongs to everyone else — work, family, dinner, dishes. My books only get me after the house goes quiet, usually from eleven until two in the morning. There is something magical about being the only mind awake on the street: no messages, no doorbells, just me and the pages in a pool of lamplight. My mother worries about the dark circles under my eyes. I tell her that is when my brain finally switches on.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = At various places (PARAPHRASE: "study spot changes daily... five different spots"). B = In a quiet place (PARAPHRASE: "little fortress... Not a whisper reaches there"). C = With music (keyword "headphones... melodies... playlist"). D = Late at night (keyword "from eleven until two in the morning"). Nhiễu: in a group, early morning.

question_text: How much money is left in the kitchen?

question_text: Who does she live with? / A woman is talking about her vacation. What is the relationship between Lisa and the speaker?

The truth: we met at our first job, twenty-two years old, sharing one tiny desk and one stapler. The stapler caused our first argument and our friendship. Two decades of holidays together since. • 22 sai: chỉ là phỏng đoán của người chồng — "My husband, typically, insisted she must be at least twenty-two because she seems so responsible".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi tuổi, con số đúng luôn có NGUỒN GIẤY TỜ (student card, ID, passport). Số gắn với "thought", "insisted", "misread" là nhiễu.

question_text: According to the speaker, how should we learn to work?
options: Effectively
Independently without any guidance
By following strictly fixed instructions
explanation:
In today's fast-moving workplace, the old ways of training are no longer enough, so let me share two ideas that I believe matter most for your career. The first is about how we work. Some people think the goal is to work independently, without any guidance at all — to prove you never need help. Others go the opposite way and follow strictly fixed instructions for every task, never asking whether the instructions still make sense. Neither approach will carry you far. What we should really learn is how to work effectively. That means organising your day around the tasks that create the most value, instead of simply staying busy. An effective worker asks: which two hours of my day actually matter? Master that question and you will stand out in any company, because busy people are everywhere, but effective people are rare.
The second idea is about progress. Efficiency alone will keep you employed, but it will not move you forward. If you want real growth, you must be willing to experiment. Try a new method, test an unfamiliar tool, volunteer for the project nobody understands yet. I know many people prefer to maintain a predictable daily routine, because routines feel safe. And I know others believe the wise strategy is to avoid any risks in the workplace. But think honestly: have you ever met a successful person whose whole story was "I kept my routine and avoided every risk"? Progress belongs to the people who try things, fail politely, learn quickly, and try again.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Effectively. Bẫy: "independently without any guidance" và "following strictly fixed instructions" đều được nhắc rồi bị loại ("Neither approach will carry you far").
2. Đáp án: Experiment. Bẫy: "maintain a predictable daily routine" và "avoid any risks" đều được nhắc rồi bị phản bác bằng câu hỏi tu từ.

question_text: A man is talking about his job. Where is he working now?

explanation:
My career took a turn nobody predicted, least of all me! After graduation I nearly stayed at the university — they offered me a teaching assistant role, flattering, but the pay was pocket money. Then came two years in a big trading company: great salary, endless hours, my weekends fed to spreadsheets. So last spring I jumped again, and now I work in a bank. The mortgage department, regular hours, proper holidays, and my own desk by the window. Third time lucky — this one I'm keeping!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – In a bank.
• Vì sao đúng: "So last spring I jumped again, and now I work in a bank. The mortgage department, regular hours, proper holidays".
• At a university sai: chỉ là lời mời sau tốt nghiệp mà anh không nhận vì lương bèo — "they offered me a teaching assistant role, flattering, but the pay was pocket money".
• In a big company sai: là chỗ làm trước đó, đã nghỉ — "two years in a big trading company: great salary, endless hours, my weekends fed to spreadsheets".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "Where is he working NOW?" phải bám thì hiện tại. Chỗ nào đi kèm "after graduation", "then came", "two years" đều thuộc quá khứ.

question_text: What is the speaker's opinion about security cameras at work?
options: People are unnecessarily worried about them
Most people don't even realize cameras are present.
Cameras should be placed to ensure complete coverage.
explanation:
I have noticed that some of my co-workers get nervous about the security cameras in our office. They say things like, "It feels like we are being watched all the time," or "I do not like feeling that I am not trusted." Some of them even walk a longer way to the printer just to avoid the camera in the corridor — as if anyone were sitting there watching them collect paper. And before you ask: no, people certainly do notice the cameras; the idea that most staff do not even realise they are present is simply not true in our office. There is also a colleague who keeps saying the cameras should be placed to cover every single corner of the building, which I find equally unnecessary. My honest opinion is different from all of these: people are unnecessarily worried about them. The cameras are not there to spy on us or to catch small mistakes. They are there to keep us safe.
Think about what the cameras actually do. If a theft or an accident happened, would you not want a record of it? And their presence quietly prevents trouble before it starts. I know some people find them intimidating, and others insist they are only useful after something bad has already happened. I would ask those colleagues to look at it differently. Instead of feeling watched, we should feel reassured about their presence. The company is not doubting us — it is looking after us. Once you see the cameras that way, walking past one stops feeling uncomfortable and starts feeling, honestly, a little safer.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: People are unnecessarily worried about them. Bẫy: "most people don't realize cameras are present" bị phủ định ("simply not true"), "cameras should be placed to ensure complete coverage" là ý của một đồng nghiệp và bị chê ("equally unnecessary").
2. Đáp án: People should feel reassured about their presence. Bẫy: "intimidating and invasive" và "only useful after incidents" đều là quan điểm của người khác mà người nói phản bác.

question_text: A man is talking about his old school days. What was the man's favorite thing about school?

explanation:
School days, what a question! My wife loved the maths classes — equations were her music, strange woman. Me? Old maps, battles, kings poisoning each other! Mr. Elwood telling the French Revolution like a thriller, chalk flying. I chose my degree because of that classroom. History — the only lessons I ever ran to.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – History classes.
• Vì sao đúng: "But the history classes — those were mine... I chose my degree because of that classroom. History — the only lessons I ever ran to".
• Math classes sai: là môn vợ anh mê, còn anh thì sợ — "My wife loved the maths classes"; "Numbers were my weekly punishment".
• Sports sai: bị chê thẳng là còn tệ hơn toán — "sports even worse: always picked last, always in goal, always freezing".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi sở thích, tách rõ ai thích gì. Bám sở hữu "those were mine"; môn gán cho "my wife" là nhiễu.

question_text: What career did he choose?

My professor pushed research; the laboratory route, publications, conferences. Fascinating, but the university salary made my landlord laugh. So I chose business, and I've never once regretted it. question_text: What is the main issue with the product's promotion campaign?
options: It is using outdated advertising methods
They use exaggerated claims
It is not targeting the correct market
explanation:
Let me use a real example in today's marketing class: a fitness supplement called PowerBoost, launched three months ago. Its promotion campaign is in trouble, and it is worth understanding why. Some students suggested the company was using outdated advertising methods — but no, the campaign runs on all the modern channels, from short videos to influencer posts. Others guessed it was not targeting the correct market — wrong again; the ads reach exactly the young, active audience the product is made for. The real issue is that the advertisements make exaggerated claims. They promise a dramatic increase in strength within days, and when customers do not feel that miracle, they stop trusting the brand. A bold promise gets attention, but a broken promise loses a customer forever, and the online reviews now say exactly that.
The product has a second problem: it is struggling to stand out on the shelves. You might assume it is priced too high, but its price is almost identical to its competitors. You might think it is hard to find, but it is already available in most big stores. The truth is less comfortable: PowerBoost is simply too similar to many existing products. Same ingredients, same packaging style, same promises as a dozen other supplements. When customers cannot see what makes a product unique, they pick whichever one they already know. So the lesson for the company is clear — stop shouting louder, and start being genuinely different. Honest claims plus a real point of difference: that is what this campaign needs.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They use exaggerated claims. Bẫy: "outdated advertising methods" bị phủ định ("runs on all the modern channels"), "not targeting the correct market" bị phủ định ("wrong again").
2. Đáp án: It is too similar to many existing products. Bẫy: "priced too high" bị phủ định ("almost identical"), "not available in enough stores" bị phủ định ("available in most big stores").

question_text: What was the lecturer's opinion about both authors' past work?
options: They have both been overlooked by ACADEMICS.
They make reference to each other's work.
One was less successful than the other.
explanation:
Today I want to talk about two writers who shaped modern literature, one from England and one from Argentina. Let me correct two common ideas about them straight away. First, some students think these authors have been overlooked by academics. In fact, universities on both sides of the Atlantic have studied their books for decades. Second, people sometimes assume that one of them was far less successful than the other. Not true either — both enjoyed large audiences during their lifetimes and both are still in print today. What genuinely connects them is something much more interesting: they make references to each other's work. In one writer's short stories you will find characters and ideas borrowed, with respect, from the other; and in the second writer's essays, whole passages reply to the first. Reading them side by side feels like listening to a long, friendly conversation carried on across an ocean.
There is one more thing every new reader should know. Some critics argue their reputation now goes far beyond their original target audience, and others complain that, given their talent, they should have been even more popular. Perhaps. But the honest warning is this: their books are not always easy, and the meanings are not always easily identified. Both writers loved symbols, hidden jokes and ideas buried under the surface of the story. You may need to read a chapter twice, or come back to a book years later, before it opens up. That difficulty is not a fault. It is exactly why readers and critics still argue about these two writers today.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They make reference to each other's work. Bẫy: "overlooked by academics" bị phủ định ("universities have studied their books for decades"), "one was less successful" bị phủ định ("Not true either").
2. Đáp án: It is not always easy for the meanings to be identified. Bẫy: "reputation beyond target audience" và "should have been more popular" đều là ý kiến của người khác ("Perhaps") — người nói chốt ở độ khó của tác phẩm.

question_text: What should people do to maintain a healthy environment?
options: Replace all personal vehicles with electric bicycles
Make a daily effort to recycle, reduce waste, and use energy carefully.
Limit industrial production to strictly rural areas
explanation:
Protecting our planet has become more urgent than ever, so today I want to talk about what ordinary people can actually do. Whenever this topic comes up, someone always suggests something dramatic. Replace every car with an electric bicycle! Move all the factories out of the cities and limit industry to the countryside! Ideas like these sound impressive, but they are neither realistic nor, honestly, necessary. What experts actually recommend is much closer to home: make a daily effort to recycle your rubbish, reduce unnecessary waste, and use energy carefully around the house. Turn off the lights you are not using, repair things instead of replacing them, carry a reusable bag. One person doing this changes little — but millions of people doing it, day after day, change a great deal. The environment is not saved by grand gestures; it is saved by small habits repeated everywhere.
At the same time, we cannot ignore what large-scale human activities are doing. Take deforestation. A few business voices still claim that clearing forests primarily benefits the local economy, and I have even heard the strange argument that it somehow creates more resilient ecosystems for the future. The research says the opposite. Activities like deforestation harm nature directly and cause serious problems — climate change accelerates, floods become more common, and communities suffer long-term health issues from dirtier air and water. Forests are the planet's natural filters, and every hectare we lose makes the daily efforts of ordinary people harder. We need both: small habits at home, and real protection for what remains.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Make a daily effort to recycle, reduce waste, and use energy carefully. Bẫy: "electric bicycles" và "limit industry to rural areas" được nhắc là ý tưởng "neither realistic nor necessary".
2. Đáp án: They harm nature and cause problems like climate change and health issues. Bẫy: "benefit the local economy" và "resilient ecosystems" là lập luận bị bác ("The research says the opposite").

question_text: What occurs when things don't go according to plan in a team?
options: The team members lose confidence.
The team members become more assured.
The team members start again from the beginning.
explanation:
Leading a team toward a shared goal is never a straight road, and today I want to talk about what happens when a project runs into trouble. Imagine your team misses an important deadline. What happens next? You might expect everyone to calmly go back to the beginning and start the plan again. Some managers even assume that a good team simply becomes more confident, more determined, after a setback. My twenty years of experience say otherwise. In most cases, the opposite happens: morale drops sharply, people begin to doubt their own abilities, and the team members lose confidence. That loss of belief, not the delay itself, is the real damage, because a team that stops trusting itself works slower and makes more mistakes.
So how should a leader respond? I often hear two answers. The first: increase the project budget significantly, as if money could buy back motivation. The second: watch each person closely and focus on individual performance only, turning the office into an examination room. Both methods fail, and usually quickly, because neither touches the real problem. What genuinely helps a leader maintain team motivation is far simpler — set a realistic goal. Break the big target into steps the team can actually reach, and let people feel the taste of success again, even a small one. Each completed step rebuilds the confidence that the setback destroyed. Money runs out and supervision creates fear, but realistic goals create momentum — and momentum is what carries a team through hard times.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: The team members lose confidence. Bẫy: "start again from the beginning" là điều "you might expect", "become more assured" là giả định của một số quản lý — cả hai bị bác ("My experience says otherwise").
2. Đáp án: Set a realistic goal. Bẫy: "increase the project budget" và "focus on individual performance only" đều được nhắc rồi bị loại ("Both methods fail").

question_text: Why does the brother find traveling meaningful?
options: Because it allows him to escape his professional responsibilities.
Because he wants to document his trips for social media influence.
Because it brings him joy and chances to learn about different cultures.
explanation:
People at work keep asking about my brother, the one who is always at an airport somewhere. And I have heard every theory about why he travels so much. His manager is convinced it is escape — that he books flights to run away from his professional responsibilities. My aunt is equally sure it is all for social media, that he wants dramatic photos to impress strangers online. I find both theories funny, because his accounts have been silent for two years, and he actually clears his work completely before every trip precisely so that nothing follows him. The real reason is the one nobody guesses because it is so ordinary: travelling makes him genuinely happy, and it gives him chances to learn about different cultures. He learns ten phrases of every language, eats where the locals eat, and comes home with stories instead of souvenirs.
Here is the funny thing — I never travel, yet I understand him perfectly, because what he does with a backpack, I do with books. People sometimes assume reading and travelling belong together because both are somehow mandatory for success at school. They are not; nobody grades you on either. And clearly neither depends on physical endurance — one of us climbs mountains while the other sits in an armchair. What truly makes them similar is this: both help a person discover new worlds and grow. His borders are on maps and mine are on pages, but we cross them for exactly the same reason.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 10 bài 1 — cùng câu hỏi và đáp án, lời khác để hai đề không trùng script.)
1. Đáp án: Because it brings him joy and chances to learn about different cultures. Bẫy: "escape responsibilities" (thuyết của manager) và "social media" (thuyết của bà cô) đều bị bác.
2. Đáp án: Both help people discover new worlds and grow as a person. Bẫy: "mandatory for academic success" và "physical endurance" đều bị phủ định.

question_text: Why is an 'important customer' valuable to a company?
options: Because they guarantee the company's stock prices will never fall.
Because they provide steady money, influence others, and help improve services.
Because they are responsible for hiring and training new employees.
explanation:
In business school we talk a lot about "key accounts" — the important customers — so let me explain why they matter so much. First, let me clear away two wrong ideas. Some analysts talk as if these customers were part of the company itself, responsible for internal tasks like hiring and training new employees. They are not; they are outsiders. And no customer, however large, can guarantee that the company's stock prices will never fall — markets simply do not work that way. The real value of an important customer has three layers. They provide steady money, giving the business a reliable stream of income it can plan around. They influence others, recommending the brand to friends and partners more convincingly than any advertisement could. And through their honest feedback, they help improve services, pointing out problems before thousands of smaller customers ever meet them.
This leads to my second point: customer behaviour today is genuinely unpredictable. Tastes shift, apps change habits, and last year's bestseller gathers dust. Some managers respond by cutting the marketing budget to avoid financial risks, which only makes the company invisible. Others try to standardise every product and ignore individual preferences, hoping one size will fit everyone. It never does. The wise response is the simplest: businesses should monitor customer habits closely and update their services whenever the data shows a change. Watch what customers actually do, not what they said last year, and adjust quickly. In a market that never stands still, the companies that survive are the ones that keep moving with it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Because they provide steady money, influence others, and help improve services. Bẫy: "hiring and training" và "stock prices" đều bị phủ định ngay đầu.
2. Đáp án: Businesses should monitor customer habits and update their services when needed. Bẫy: "reduce the marketing budget" và "standardize all products" đều được nhắc rồi bị chê ("only makes the company invisible", "It never does").

question_text: Why do modern buildings stand out?
options: They associate with modern cityscapes
They prioritize traditional materials over steel
They are primarily built in rural environments
explanation:
Let us talk about modern architecture, because our cities are changing in front of our eyes. Why do modern buildings stand out? Some people expect me to say it is because architects now prioritise traditional materials — wood, brick and stone — over steel. Others assume the most striking new buildings are primarily built in rural environments, away from the crowds. Neither is true. Walk through any city centre and you will see the real answer: modern buildings stand out because they associate so closely with modern cityscapes. Glass surfaces, straight lines, minimal decoration — each new tower is designed to match the clean, uniform look of the contemporary city around it. They are recognised not as individual masterpieces but as pieces of one large visual identity, the way letters belong to the same alphabet.
But being recognisable is not the same as being impressive, and here I must be honest. Architecture magazines love to claim that today's buildings represent the peak of architectural innovation, and city councils like to boast that every new project focuses on maximising public green spaces. Look closely and both claims fall apart. What many new buildings actually display is a clear lack of ambition. Developers choose efficiency, low cost and fast construction over creativity, so the same glass box appears in London, Dubai and Singapore with only the address changed. Our skylines are filling with buildings that are tall, clean, profitable — and instantly forgettable. Until developers reward imagination again, the cities of this century will all look like each other.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They associate with modern cityscapes. Bẫy: "traditional materials" và "rural environments" đều bị phủ định ("Neither is true").
2. Đáp án: They often display a lack of ambition. Bẫy: "peak of architectural innovation" và "public green spaces" là tuyên bố của tạp chí/chính quyền bị bác ("both claims fall apart").

question_text: What makes the video stand out from others?
options: The high marketing budget involved.
Its production techniques.
The participation of famous celebrities.
explanation:
The sudden success of this short video has puzzled a lot of marketing experts, so let me break it down. When something gets thirty million views, people jump to the usual explanations. Some assume famous celebrities must have taken part — but watch it yourself: every face in the video is an unknown amateur. Others guess the creators spent a huge marketing budget pushing it across social media. In fact, the team has confirmed they spent almost nothing on promotion. What really makes this video stand out is its production techniques. The camera work is inventive, the editing is smooth in a way you rarely see outside professional studios, and the sound design pulls you in from the first second. Viewers may not know the technical terms, but they feel the quality instantly — and that feeling is what they share with their friends.
This leads to a bigger question: what makes videos succeed more generally? Some creators believe the secret is translating their work into multiple languages, and others chase whatever long-term trend the industry is predicting. Both strategies sound sensible, but the evidence points elsewhere: videos become more successful when they are released at the right time. The same clip that disappears on a quiet Tuesday can explode on a holiday weekend when millions are scrolling. Timing decides whether the spark meets dry wood or wet ground. So my advice to creators is simple: polish your craft, certainly — but study your audience's calendar just as carefully as your camera settings.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Its production techniques. Bẫy: "celebrities" bị phủ định ("every face is an unknown amateur"), "marketing budget" bị phủ định ("spent almost nothing").
2. Đáp án: They should be released at the right time. Bẫy: "translated into multiple languages" và "follow long-term trends" được nhắc là chiến lược của người khác ("Both strategies sound sensible, but...").

options: Man
Woman

question_text: What does the speaker say about many new buildings?
options: They often display a lack of ambition.
They represent the peak of architectural innovation
They focus on maximizing public green spaces

question_text: The Internet makes young people less patient.
options: Man
Woman
Both

question_text: More should be done to protect individual privacy.
options: Man
Woman
Both

question_text: What time is dinner?
explanation:
Family meeting via voicemail, everyone listen up! Tonight's dinner time has been a battlefield of opinions. Your brother wanted eight thirty after his gym — vetoed, the roast would be sad and dry by then. Grandpa lobbied for nine thirty, which is frankly a midnight snack, not dinner. The kitchen has ruled: dinner is at seven thirty! Seven thirty, table set, hands washed, phones in the basket. The roast waits for no one. Love you all, chef mum out!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 7:30 pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "The kitchen has ruled: dinner is at seven thirty! Seven thirty, table set, hands washed, phones in the basket".
• 8:30 pm sai: là đề xuất của cậu em sau buổi gym, bị bác vì món quay sẽ khô — "Your brother wanted eight thirty after his gym — vetoed, the roast would be sad and dry by then".
• 9:30 pm sai: là ý của ông, bị chê là ăn khuya chứ không phải bữa tối — "Grandpa lobbied for nine thirty, which is frankly a midnight snack, not dinner".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giờ ăn, mỗi mốc gắn với một người đề xuất. Chỉ lấy mốc do người quyết định chốt — nghe "the kitchen has ruled", "vetoed".

question_text: According to the reviewer, when can videos become more successful?
options: If they are translated into multiple languages.
They should be released at the right time.
When they strictly follow long-term trends.

question_text: Urban farming will benefit the urban economy.
options: Man
Woman
Both

question_text: Listen to a man calling his friend. Why does he make the call?
options: To ask for directions
To invite her out
To tell her he will be late
explanation:
Hey Claire, it's Rob! No, don't worry, I'm not lost this time — I actually know the way to the restaurant, no directions needed, miracle of miracles. And I'm not calling to invite you anywhere new either, we're already meeting tonight, aren't we? The thing is... I'm still stuck at the office. The report went back for changes at the last minute, so I'll be about forty minutes late. Order the starters without me — I'll run all the way. Sorry, sorry, sorry!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – To tell her he will be late.
• Vì sao đúng: "The thing is... I'm still stuck at the office. The report went back for changes at the last minute, so I'll be about forty minutes late".
• To ask for directions sai: anh khẳng định biết đường — "I'm not lost this time — I actually know the way to the restaurant, no directions needed".
• To invite her out sai: hai người vốn đã hẹn gặp tối nay — "I'm not calling to invite you anywhere new either, we're already meeting tonight, aren't we?".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi mục đích cuộc gọi, người gọi loại 2 khả năng bằng "I'm not calling to...". Lý do thật nằm ngay sau "The thing is...".

question_text: What do the students need to do every Tuesday?
options: write a note
write a report
go camping
explanation:
Good morning, everyone, before you open your textbooks — one new rule for this term. Every Tuesday, each of you will write a report about the experiment we did that week. One page is enough: what you did, what you observed, and what you learned. You will hand it to me at the start of Wednesday's lesson. This is every single Tuesday, so put it in your diaries now. The reports will count towards your final mark, so please take them seriously.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – write a report.
• Vì sao đúng: "Every Tuesday, each of you will write a report about the experiment we did that week. One page is enough".
• write a note sai: bài chỉ nói "report", hoàn toàn không nhắc tới việc viết note — đây là nhiễu bằng từ gần nghĩa.
• go camping sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
👉 Mẹo: dạng thông báo nhiệm vụ định kỳ, khoanh cụm "Every + thứ trong tuần" rồi bắt đúng ĐỘNG TỪ + DANH TỪ ngay sau đó (write a report), đừng đoán theo từ na ná.

question_text: What country will they study next semester?
options: Germany
Spain
France
explanation:
Big news from the exchange office today, everyone! The placements for next semester are finally decided. I know half of you dreamed of Germany, but Munich took no one from our faculty this year — their quota filled instantly. And Spain, sadly, suspended the partnership until the paperwork clears. But the good news is golden: we're going to France! Lyon, to be exact — the full semester, language course included, September to January. Start practising your bonjour, people!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – France.
• Vì sao đúng: "the good news is golden: we're going to France! Lyon, to be exact — the full semester, language course included, September to January".
• Germany sai: Munich không nhận ai từ khoa của họ vì chỉ tiêu đầy ngay — "Munich took no one from our faculty this year — their quota filled instantly".
• Spain sai: chương trình hợp tác bị tạm dừng chờ giấy tờ — "Spain, sadly, suspended the partnership until the paperwork clears".
👉 Mẹo: dạng thông báo địa điểm, nghe cụm đảo hướng "But the good news is". Nước nào đi kèm "took no one", "suspended", "filled" thì gạch.

question_text: Where does Malik want to go?
options: The town hall
The library
The park
explanation:
It's Malik, leaving a message about this afternoon. Everyone keeps suggesting places and I want to be clear about where I actually need to go! The library — no, I returned all my books on Tuesday, nothing for me there. And the park picnic can wait for the weekend, tell the others. I need the town hall, before it closes at four! My residence permit is ready for collection, and if I miss today the office closes until Monday. So: town hall, half past three. Who's driving me?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – The town hall.
• Vì sao đúng: "I need the town hall, before it closes at four! My residence permit is ready for collection" và chốt "So: town hall, half past three".
• The library sai: cậu đã trả hết sách hôm thứ Ba, không còn việc gì ở đó ("I returned all my books on Tuesday, nothing for me there").
• The park sai: buổi picnic để cuối tuần ("the park picnic can wait for the weekend, tell the others").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "where does he WANT to go" — chọn nơi gắn với động từ nhu cầu "I need..." và một việc gấp có hạn chót. Nơi đi kèm "can wait" là nhiễu.

question_text: A man is talking about the environment of the countryside. What is the main cause of poor air quality?
options: Factories
Cars
Fires from the countryside
explanation:
People romanticise our countryside air, but let me tell you the truth from my porch! Everyone blames the factories first — we have exactly one, the little dairy plant, cleaner than most kitchens. Then they point at cars; forty vehicles pass on a busy day, hardly a highway. No — the real trouble comes every autumn, from the fires. Farmers burning the fields after harvest, smoke rolling in for weeks, the whole valley coughing under a grey blanket. Those countryside fires — that's what steals our clean air.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Fires from the countryside.
• Vì sao đúng: "the real trouble comes every autumn, from the fires. Farmers burning the fields after harvest, smoke rolling in for weeks, the whole valley coughing".
• Factories sai: cả vùng chỉ có một nhà máy sữa nhỏ và rất sạch — "we have exactly one, the little dairy plant, cleaner than most kitchens".
• Cars sai: lượng xe quá ít để gây ô nhiễm — "forty vehicles pass on a busy day, hardly a highway".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi nguyên nhân chính, đáp án nằm sau "No — the real trouble is". Thứ mà "everyone blames" hoặc "they point at" thường là nhiễu.

question_text: A man has a new job. How many days does the man have to work?
options: 3 days
4 days
5 days
explanation:
Signed the contract this morning — the new job is official! And before the family panics about my health: the schedule is civilised. The old warehouse job ate five days a week plus overtime, never again. They first offered me a four-day arrangement, but that included Saturdays, so I pushed back. Final deal: three days — Monday, Wednesday, Friday, eight to four. Three days of work, four days of life! The garden, the grandkids and the fishing rod will finally see me. Retirement rehearsal, I call it!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 3 days.
• Vì sao đúng: "Final deal: three days — Monday, Wednesday, Friday, eight to four. Three days of work, four days of life!".
• 5 days sai: là lịch của công việc CŨ ở kho hàng — "The old warehouse job ate five days a week plus overtime, never again".
• 4 days sai: là đề nghị đầu tiên của công ty, anh từ chối vì có cả thứ Bảy — "They first offered me a four-day arrangement, but that included Saturdays, so I pushed back".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi số ngày làm, bám cụm chốt "Final deal", "in the end". Số gắn với "the old job", "they first offered" là nhiễu.

question_text: Mary is talking to her friend about her new home. What does she ask her friend about?
options: Where to buy a new table
The furniture
Mirror
explanation:
Hi! It's Mary, calling about my endless apartment project! The living room is nearly human now — the mirror question you can forget, my mother donated her big gold one, drama included, free of charge. And the furniture is all chosen, delivered, assembled; my thumbs survived the instruction manuals. But one mystery remains, and you're my expert: where does one buy a proper dining table these days? Solid wood, seats six, doesn't cost a kidney? You bought yours somewhere clever — call me back with the address!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Where to buy a new table.
• Vì sao đúng: "one mystery remains, and you're my expert: where does one buy a proper dining table these days?" — và cô nhờ "call me back with the address!".
• The furniture sai: đồ đạc đã mua, giao và lắp xong — "the furniture is all chosen, delivered, assembled".
• Mirror sai: mẹ cô đã cho một cái miễn phí nên khỏi bàn — "the mirror question you can forget, my mother donated her big gold one, drama included, free of charge".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "cô ấy hỏi bạn về việc gì", tìm CÂU HỎI thật sự trong bài. Món đi kèm "you can forget", "all done" là việc đã xong.

question_text: Why did she return to the shop?
options: To exchange a shirt
To buy a skirt
To exchange a dress
explanation:
You won't believe my afternoon. Remember the blue shirt I bought for Dad's birthday on Saturday? When he opened the box, it turned out to be a medium, and Dad has worn a large for thirty years. So today I went back to the shop to exchange the shirt for the right size. The assistant was lovely about it — found the large straight away and even wrapped it again for free. Second try at the birthday present tomorrow. Wish me luck!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – To exchange a shirt.
• Vì sao đúng: "today I went back to the shop to exchange the shirt for the right size" — vì áo mua là size medium trong khi bố mặc size large.
• To buy a skirt sai: bài không hề nhắc tới váy ngắn; "skirt" chỉ là nhiễu gần âm với "shirt", và cô đi ĐỔI chứ không mua mới.
• To exchange a dress sai: món đồ trong bài là chiếc áo sơ mi xanh — "the blue shirt I bought for Dad's birthday", không phải váy liền.
👉 Mẹo: bộ ba shirt / skirt / dress là bẫy nghe gần âm. Nghe kỹ phụ âm đầu, đồng thời bám manh mối bối cảnh (quà cho bố, size medium/large) để loại nhanh.

question_text: Listen to a girl calling the cafe. Where did she ask the coffee shop to look for her lost item?
options: On the counter
Near the door
In the corner
explanation:
Hello, Riverside Café? Thank goodness you picked up. I was there an hour ago and I've lost my purse — small, red leather. Could you check for me? Not by the counter where I paid, I already know I had it after that. And I doubt it's near the door, we didn't stop there. Please look in the corner, at the little table under the lamp where we sat all afternoon — I think it slipped behind the cushion. Yes, the corner table. I'll hold, thank you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – In the corner.
• Vì sao đúng: câu hỏi hỏi nơi cô NHỜ tìm — "Please look in the corner, at the little table under the lamp where we sat all afternoon... Yes, the corner table".
• On the counter sai: cô khẳng định sau khi trả tiền ở quầy thì ví vẫn còn ("Not by the counter where I paid, I already know I had it after that").
• Near the door sai: cô cho là khó xảy ra vì họ không dừng ở đó ("I doubt it's near the door, we didn't stop there").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "where did she ASK them to look" — chỉ lấy nơi đi kèm lời nhờ ("Please look in..."), không lấy những nơi cô tự loại trừ dù chúng cũng được nhắc tên.

question_text: What did she like best about the film?
options: the mountain scenes
the action scenes
the ending
explanation:
The film last night — let me tell you my honest ranking! Everyone praises the action scenes, and yes, the chase across the rooftops was well made, but my heart was beating for another reason entirely. The ending? Frankly, it collapsed — twenty minutes of explanations nobody needed. No, what I loved, what I still see when I close my eyes, were the mountain scenes. Those silent shots of the peaks at dawn, the tiny climbers against all that snow... I'd watch the whole film again just for those.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – the mountain scenes.
• Vì sao đúng: "what I loved, what I still see when I close my eyes, were the mountain scenes... I'd watch the whole film again just for those".
• the action scenes sai: cô công nhận làm tốt nhưng đó không phải điều cô thích nhất ("the chase across the rooftops was well made, but my heart was beating for another reason entirely").
• the ending sai: cô chê thẳng là hỏng ("Frankly, it collapsed — twenty minutes of explanations nobody needed").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "liked BEST" — một phương án được khen nhẹ (well made) vẫn là bẫy. Chọn thứ gắn với ngôn ngữ cảm xúc mạnh nhất: what I loved, I still see, I'd watch again.

question_text: What does he advise young people to do to save money?
options: Use public transportation
Buy second-hand items
Cook for yourself
explanation:
Young listeners keep writing in: how do I actually save money on a first salary? Honest answer time. Public transport passes help, but the savings are pocket change unless you're currently driving a limousine. Second-hand shopping? Fine for furniture, though the hunting eats your weekends. The advice that truly moves the needle is this: cook for yourself. Those daily lunches out and delivery dinners quietly eat a third of a young salary. Learn five simple recipes, pack your lunch — watch your account grow within one month.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Cook for yourself.
• Vì sao đúng: "The advice that truly moves the needle is this: cook for yourself... Learn five simple recipes, pack your lunch — watch your account grow within one month".
• Use public transportation sai: có tiết kiệm nhưng không đáng kể — "Public transport passes help, but the savings are pocket change".
• Buy second-hand items sai: chỉ hợp đồ nội thất và ngốn hết cuối tuần — "Fine for furniture, though the hunting eats your weekends".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi lời khuyên, tìm cụm nâng mức độ: "the advice that truly...", "what really works". Ý đi kèm "help, but", "fine, though" chỉ là lời khuyên hạng hai.

question_text: Listen to the radio program about a new restaurant. What does the man complain about?
options: the place was cold
the place was hot
the place was ugly
explanation:
And now our weekly restaurant review! Our reporter visited the new grill house on Station Road last night. The food? Excellent — he says the steak was the best he's had all year, and the prices were fair too. But there was one serious problem: the temperature. The heating was broken, the big windows let in every draught, and he sat through dinner in his coat and scarf. The place was freezing cold from starter to dessert. Fix the heating, he says — and he'll happily come back!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – the place was cold.
• Vì sao đúng: "The heating was broken, the big windows let in every draught, and he sat through dinner in his coat and scarf. The place was freezing cold from starter to dessert".
• the place was hot sai: ngược hẳn với bài — hệ thống sưởi hỏng nên quán lạnh cóng, khách phải mặc áo khoác quàng khăn ăn tối.
• the place was ugly sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu; bài chỉ khen đồ ăn và giá — "the steak was the best he's had all year, and the prices were fair too".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "phàn nàn điều gì", bỏ qua mọi thứ được KHEN ở đầu bài và bám cụm đảo hướng "But there was one serious problem".

question_text: How much are the eggs?
options: 2 pounds
3 pounds
1.50 pounds
explanation:
Fresh eggs, lovely people, fresh from the farm this morning! Yes dear, let me explain the prices, everyone asks. The supermarket across the road charges two pounds for eggs that saw a chicken last month, maybe. That fancy organic place? Three pounds, and they gift-wrap the box like jewellery! Mine — golden yolks, laid at dawn — one pound fifty. One fifty, honest price for honest eggs. Two boxes, my dear? I'll pick you the biggest ones!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 1.50 pounds.
• Vì sao đúng: người bán nói về trứng của MÌNH — "Mine — golden yolks, laid at dawn — one pound fifty. One fifty, honest price for honest eggs".
• 2 pounds sai: đó là giá của siêu thị đối diện — "The supermarket across the road charges two pounds".
• 3 pounds sai: đó là giá cửa hàng organic — "That fancy organic place? Three pounds, and they gift-wrap the box like jewellery!".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giá, mỗi con số luôn gắn với một NƠI BÁN khác nhau. Bám từ sở hữu "Mine", "ours", "here" để biết giá nào là của người đang nói.

question_text: What area is he describing?
options: A shopping district
A university area
A residential neighborhood
explanation:
Let me describe my new neighbourhood, because people keep guessing wrong! It's not a shopping district — there's one bakery and a kiosk, that's the entire retail empire. And despite the quiet streets, it's no ordinary residential area either; nobody here is retired, believe me. This is a university area through and through: two faculties within walking distance, cheap cafés full of laptops, bicycles chained to every fence, and the streets buzzing with students until midnight. The average age must be about twenty-one!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – A university area.
• Vì sao đúng: "This is a university area through and through: two faculties within walking distance, cheap cafés full of laptops, bicycles chained to every fence".
• A shopping district sai: cả khu chỉ có một tiệm bánh và một ki-ốt ("there's one bakery and a kiosk, that's the entire retail empire").
• A residential neighborhood sai: bị phủ định thẳng vì dân cư toàn người trẻ ("it's no ordinary residential area either; nobody here is retired").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "what area" — nghe các chi tiết định danh (faculties, students, bicycles) thay vì chờ tên gọi. Hai phương án nhiễu thường bị bác bằng "it's not... either".

question_text: What is not original?
options: Furniture
Home
Bicycle
explanation:
Welcome to the open house! Let me be transparent about this property, as the family asked. The home itself — walls, roof, those beautiful ceilings — all completely original from 1925, never rebuilt. Even the old bicycle in the garden shed belonged to the first owner; his grandson insists it stays with the house, original and still working! The furniture, however, is another story: everything you see was bought new by the current owners — not a single original piece remains. Shall we begin upstairs?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Furniture.
• Vì sao đúng: câu hỏi hỏi thứ KHÔNG nguyên bản — "The furniture, however, is another story: everything you see was bought new by the current owners — not a single original piece remains".
• Home sai: bản thân ngôi nhà nguyên bản từ 1925 ("walls, roof, those beautiful ceilings — all completely original from 1925, never rebuilt").
• Bicycle sai: chiếc xe đạp cũ cũng là đồ nguyên bản của chủ đầu tiên ("belonged to the first owner... original and still working").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi phủ định "What is NOT original?" — nghe từ nối đảo hướng "however", "but". Thứ đứng ngay sau nó chính là ngoại lệ cần chọn.

question_text: A woman is calling her husband. What time is lunch ready?
options: 3pm
1pm
2pm
explanation:
Darling, listen before your next meeting! Lunch plans have moved twice, so here's the final version. One o'clock is dead — the oven decided to sulk and the repairman only just left. I nearly said three, but your father called; he's picking us up at three fifteen for grandma's, remember? So lunch lands at two. Two o'clock sharp, soup and the good bread, and if you're late I'm starting without you. Two! Love you, bye!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 2pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "So lunch lands at two. Two o'clock sharp, soup and the good bread" — cuối bài cô ấy còn nhắc lại "Two!".
• 1pm sai: đã hủy vì lò nướng hỏng, thợ vừa mới về — "One o'clock is dead — the oven decided to sulk and the repairman only just left".
• 3pm sai: suýt chọn rồi bỏ, vì 3h15 bố đến đón đi nhà bà — "I nearly said three, but your father called; he's picking us up at three fifteen".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giờ, bắt cụm chốt "lands at", "sharp" và con số được LẶP LẠI. Mốc đi kèm "is dead", "I nearly said", "but" là mốc bị loại.

question_text: The woman is discussing her new exercise routine. How much time does she spend cycling?
options: 45 minutes
35 minutes
60 minutes
explanation:
My new exercise routine is finally settled, and my body has opinions! Monday and Thursday I swim for forty-five minutes — that part everyone knows. The gym circuit takes a full hour on Saturdays, sixty sweaty minutes, don't remind me. But the cycling, my favourite part: every morning before work, thirty-five minutes along the river path. Thirty-five exactly, timed by my watch — enough to wake up, not enough to need a second shower. The routine of a genius, if I say so myself!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 35 minutes.
• Vì sao đúng: "the cycling, my favourite part: every morning before work, thirty-five minutes along the river path. Thirty-five exactly, timed by my watch".
• 45 minutes sai: đó là thời gian BƠI thứ Hai và thứ Năm — "Monday and Thursday I swim for forty-five minutes".
• 60 minutes sai: đó là buổi tập gym thứ Bảy — "The gym circuit takes a full hour on Saturdays, sixty sweaty minutes".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi thời lượng của MỘT môn cụ thể, vừa nghe vừa ghép cặp môn–số phút. Chỉ lấy con số đứng cạnh đúng từ khóa trong câu hỏi (cycling).

question_text: Why can't he do the job today?
options: He sicks
He has another appointment
He has to eat
explanation:
Mr. Kowalski, it's Ben the handyman, about your fence today — I'm so sorry, I have to reschedule! No, I'm not sick, thank goodness, healthy as a horse, don't cancel me forever! And it's not about lunch either, I can hammer and chew at the same time, ask anyone. The real problem: the dentist finally called with a cancellation slot, and this tooth has bullied me for three weeks. My appointment is at two, right across town. Tomorrow morning, first thing, your fence gets my full attention — promise!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – He has another appointment.
• Vì sao đúng: anh phải đi khám răng đúng giờ làm — "the dentist finally called with a cancellation slot, and this tooth has bullied me for three weeks. My appointment is at two, right across town".
• He sicks sai: anh khẳng định vẫn khỏe — "No, I'm not sick, thank goodness, healthy as a horse".
• He has to eat sai: bị gạt thẳng, anh vừa làm vừa ăn được — "it's not about lunch either, I can hammer and chew at the same time".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi lý do hoãn/hủy, người nói loại 2 lý do trước rồi mới nói thật. Bám cụm "The real problem:" và danh từ chỉ lịch hẹn (appointment, slot).

question_text: An expert is talking about lack of satisfaction at work. What should be the solution?
options: Request a transfer
Take a vacation
Find a new job
explanation:
A listener asks: I'm deeply unhappy in my role — what now? Careful, friend. Everyone's first instinct is a vacation, but two weeks on a beach only postpones the Monday you dread; the problem waits at your desk, tanned and rested. Quitting entirely for a new job? Drastic, and risky before you've diagnosed the illness. My advice: request a transfer first. Same company, different team, new manager — often the role was wrong, not the workplace. A transfer costs nothing and answers everything. Try that door before the exit.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Request a transfer.
• Vì sao đúng: "My advice: request a transfer first. Same company, different team, new manager" — và "A transfer costs nothing and answers everything".
• Take a vacation sai: chỉ trì hoãn vấn đề chứ không giải quyết — "two weeks on a beach only postpones the Monday you dread; the problem waits at your desk".
• Find a new job sai: bị đánh giá quá vội và rủi ro — "Quitting entirely for a new job? Drastic, and risky before you've diagnosed the illness".
👉 Mẹo: dạng chuyên gia tư vấn, đáp án nằm ngay sau "My advice:". Phương án bị gắn nhãn tiêu cực ("only postpones", "drastic", "risky") là nhiễu.

question_text: Listen to a man talking about the game he is playing. What is the game stopping him from doing?
options: Play
Change characters
Win
explanation:
Okay, I need to talk about this game, because it's driving me crazy. Playing it is not the problem — I play every single evening, two hours minimum. And changing characters? Easy, I've tried all twelve of them, from the knight to the little wizard. But winning? That's another story. Whatever I do, that final level beats me every time. The game simply will not let me win. Forty-three attempts. Forty-three! One day, my friends. One day.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Win.
• Vì sao đúng: "Whatever I do, that final level beats me every time. The game simply will not let me win. Forty-three attempts".
• Play sai: việc chơi hoàn toàn không phải vấn đề — "Playing it is not the problem — I play every single evening, two hours minimum".
• Change characters sai: đổi nhân vật rất dễ, anh đã thử hết — "Easy, I've tried all twelve of them, from the knight to the little wizard".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "stopping him from doing" là hỏi việc KHÔNG làm được. Gạch mọi việc đi kèm "not the problem", "easy"; đáp án nằm sau "But...".

question_text: Listen to a writer talking about her job. What is her first job?
options: Writer
Librarian
Teacher
explanation:
People often think I've been writing all my life, but my road here was longer than that. After university, my first job was actually as a teacher — I taught English to teenagers for six years, and I loved reading stories aloud to my classes. Later I worked in the town library for a while, surrounded by other people's books, and that's when I started writing my own. My first novel came out ten years ago, and I've been a full-time writer ever since.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Teacher.
• Vì sao đúng: "After university, my first job was actually as a teacher — I taught English to teenagers for six years".
• Librarian sai: đó là công việc SAU đó — "Later I worked in the town library for a while, surrounded by other people's books".
• Writer sai: là nghề hiện tại, đến sau cùng — "My first novel came out ten years ago, and I've been a full-time writer ever since".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "her FIRST job" là hỏi trình tự thời gian. Vẽ nhanh trục khi nghe: "After university / my first job" → "Later" → "ever since".

question_text: Stephanie is looking for a job taking care of children. How old is she?
explanation:
Hello! I'm Stephanie, answering your childcare advertisement — let me introduce myself properly! People often guess I'm twenty-five because I'm tall, and my mother jokes I have the patience of a thirty-year-old. But no — I'm twenty-one, in my third year of nursery education studies. Twenty-one, with four younger siblings, so children hold no mysteries for me! I'm free every weekend, I cook, I do first aid, and I know forty fairy tales by heart. References ready — call me anytime!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 21.
• Vì sao đúng: "But no — I'm twenty-one, in my third year of nursery education studies. Twenty-one, with four younger siblings".
• 25 sai: chỉ là phỏng đoán của người khác vì cô cao — "People often guess I'm twenty-five because I'm tall".
• 30 sai: là câu đùa của mẹ cô về tính điềm đạm — "my mother jokes I have the patience of a thirty-year-old".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi tuổi, gạch ngay số đi kèm "guess", "jokes", "people think". Tuổi thật nằm sau "But no — I'm..." và thường được nhắc lại lần hai.

question_text: A girl is calling her mother. Which dress does she want?
options: Short and blue
Long and white
Long and red
explanation:
Mum, it's me, calling from the dress shop — I need your yes before they close! Remember the short blue one from the catalogue? I tried it — awful on me, we bury that idea. The long white one fits beautifully, but Aunt Vi says white at a wedding is war with the bride, so no. Which leaves the one I'm wearing right now: long, deep red, and mum — I look like a film star. It's the red one I want. Can I? Call me back in five minutes!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Long and red.
• Vì sao đúng: "the one I'm wearing right now: long, deep red, and mum — I look like a film star. It's the red one I want".
• Short and blue sai: cô mặc thử và thấy rất tệ ("I tried it — awful on me, we bury that idea").
• Long and white sai: dáng đẹp nhưng mặc trắng đi đám cưới là phạm kỵ với cô dâu ("Aunt Vi says white at a wedding is war with the bride, so no").
👉 Mẹo: mỗi phương án là cặp "dáng + màu". Đừng chốt khi mới nghe đúng một nửa; đợi câu có đủ cả hai đặc điểm kèm "It's the... I want".

question_text: Listen to a woman explaining why she was late. What is the main reason she gets late?
options: Car broke down
Heavy traffic
Missed the train
explanation:
I owe the whole team an explanation for this morning's chaos! No, the car didn't break down — she's running beautifully since the service, thank you. And the traffic was actually kind for a Monday, moving the whole way. My disaster happened at the station: I watched my train close its doors from the top of the escalator. Missed it by eight seconds! The next one came forty minutes later, packed with everyone else's bad morning. So: guilty, one missed train, endless apologies — cake for everyone at lunch!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Missed the train.
• Vì sao đúng: "My disaster happened at the station: I watched my train close its doors from the top of the escalator. Missed it by eight seconds!".
• Car broke down sai: xe vẫn chạy tốt sau khi bảo dưỡng — "No, the car didn't break down — she's running beautifully since the service".
• Heavy traffic sai: hôm đó đường lại thông thoáng — "the traffic was actually kind for a Monday, moving the whole way".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi lý do đi trễ, người nói loại trừ trước rồi mới nêu lý do thật. Đáp án nằm sau "The real problem/My disaster was...".

question_text: A woman is calling her son. What time will the mother meet the son?
options: Six o’clock
Two o’clock
Three o'clock
explanation:
Sweetheart, it's mum, listen carefully because plans moved again! Forget two o'clock — grandma's doctor visit ran over and we're still in the waiting room. I thought we'd manage six, but that's too late, the shops will be closing and we still need your suit fitted. So: three o'clock, at the fountain entrance of the shopping centre. Three, on the dot! I have your measurements, grandma has opinions, and we have one hour to make you elegant. Don't be late, my love!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Three o'clock.
• Vì sao đúng: "So: three o'clock, at the fountain entrance of the shopping centre. Three, on the dot!".
• Two o'clock sai: bị hủy vì buổi khám của bà kéo dài — "Forget two o'clock — grandma's doctor visit ran over and we're still in the waiting room".
• Six o'clock sai: quá muộn, cửa hàng sắp đóng mà còn phải đo vest — "I thought we'd manage six, but that's too late, the shops will be closing".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giờ hẹn, gạch mốc đi sau "Forget..." và mốc bị chê "too late". Giờ đúng thường kèm địa điểm cụ thể và cụm "on the dot".

question_text: An author is talking about her daily routine. When does she usually write?
options: In the afternoons
In the mornings
At night
explanation:
Readers imagine my writing life as candlelit midnights — the truth is far less romantic! Mornings are hopeless: before eleven I'm a zombie with a teacup, answering emails and staring at the garden. And night writing, which sounds so poetic? I tried it for a whole winter and deleted every word the next day — tired sentences, all of them. My real work happens in the afternoons. One o'clock to six, phone in the drawer, same chair, same desk. Every book I've published was written after lunch.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – In the afternoons.
• Vì sao đúng: "My real work happens in the afternoons. One o'clock to six, phone in the drawer, same chair, same desk. Every book I've published was written after lunch".
• In the mornings sai: cô thừa nhận buổi sáng vô dụng — "Mornings are hopeless: before eleven I'm a zombie with a teacup".
• At night sai: đã thử suốt một mùa đông rồi xóa sạch — "I tried it for a whole winter and deleted every word the next day — tired sentences, all of them".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi thời điểm làm việc, bám cụm "My real work happens...". Khung giờ gắn với "hopeless", "I tried... and deleted" là mồi nhử.

question_text: What did she advice for people who lack motivation at work?
options: Attend a time management workshop
Request a transfer
Take on additional responsibilities
explanation:
A listener asks what to do when motivation at work disappears — a question I hear every week! First, what NOT to do. Don't pile on additional responsibilities hoping pressure will wake you up; a tired mind just drowns faster. And a time management workshop? Useful for the organised, useless for the unmotivated — you'll plan beautifully and still feel empty. What actually works, in case after case: request a transfer. A new team inside your own company restarts the engine while keeping your security. Try that first.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Request a transfer.
• Vì sao đúng: "What actually works, in case after case: request a transfer. A new team inside your own company restarts the engine while keeping your security".
• Take on additional responsibilities sai: bị bác vì càng thêm áp lực càng đuối ("Don't pile on additional responsibilities hoping pressure will wake you up; a tired mind just drowns faster").
• Attend a time management workshop sai: chỉ hữu ích với người đã ngăn nắp, vô dụng với người mất động lực ("Useful for the organised, useless for the unmotivated").
👉 Mẹo: bài tư vấn thường tuyên bố rõ "First, what NOT to do". Mọi ý sau câu đó là nhiễu; đáp án nằm sau "What actually works".

question_text: A man is talking to a friend about his plan to move abroad. What is his biggest problem?
options: Finding the right house
Persuading his family
Getting the financing
explanation:
The Canada plan is moving, my friend, but let me tell you where it hurts. The money side, surprisingly, is solved — the bank approved my financing last week, better rate than I hoped. Finding the right house? Easy, my cousin in Vancouver has already shortlisted three near his street. No, the wall I keep hitting is at my own dinner table. My wife's parents call it abandonment, my daughter cries about her friends. Persuading my family — that is the whole battle now.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Persuading his family.
• Vì sao đúng: "the wall I keep hitting is at my own dinner table... Persuading my family — that is the whole battle now".
• Finding the right house sai: anh họ ở Vancouver đã chọn sẵn ba căn ("my cousin in Vancouver has already shortlisted three near his street").
• Getting the financing sai: ngân hàng đã duyệt với lãi suất tốt hơn kỳ vọng ("the bank approved my financing last week, better rate than I hoped").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "biggest problem" — mọi thứ đi kèm "solved / already / approved" đều bị loại. Vấn đề thật đi kèm ẩn dụ khó khăn: the wall, the battle, the mountain.

question_text: How does she go to school?
options: She drives
She takes the bus
She walks
explanation:
My journey to school surprises everyone at the office when I mention it. No, I don't drive — I sold the car in spring, parking near the school was theft in slow motion. And the bus? I tried it for a term: two changes, twenty minutes of waiting, packed like sardines. So now I simply walk. Thirty-five minutes through the old town, past the bakery that gives me the day's first smile. I arrive awake, warm and cheerful — my colleagues arrive from traffic jams looking like storm clouds!
