Woman: Eight was a disaster, remember? The kitchen was closing and we ate like racehorses.
Man: True. Seven, then? That's the classic hour.
Woman: Seven I'm still on the bus from my mother's, I'd arrive frazzled and starving.
Man: Then let's split the difference backwards — six thirty. The restaurant is quiet then, we get the window table, and the whole evening is ours.
Woman: Six thirty is perfect, actually. Early dinner, long talk, home before eleven like the adults we pretend to be.
Man: Six thirty, window table. Booked!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 6.30pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "let's split the difference backwards — six thirty. The restaurant is quiet then" và chốt "Six thirty, window table. Booked!".
• 8.00pm sai: lần trước 8h là thảm họa vì bếp sắp đóng cửa ("Eight was a disaster, remember? The kitchen was closing and we ate like racehorses").
• 7.00pm sai: giờ đó cô còn trên xe buýt từ nhà mẹ về ("Seven I'm still on the bus from my mother's, I'd arrive frazzled and starving").
👉 Mẹo: giờ chốt thường đi kèm hành động đặt chỗ ("Booked!", "I'll book a table"). Nghe thấy động từ này là dừng phân vân, không cần nghe lại.

question_text: What will they bring to the picnic?
options: Drinks
Food
Snacks
explanation:
Man: Sunday picnic is confirmed! Now, who brings what? I heard Tom's already claimed something.
Woman: Tom's bringing all the drinks — lemonade, juice, his famous iced coffee. Don't touch drinks.
Man: And Priya said something about snacks yesterday?
Woman: Crisps, nuts, those little crackers — all hers, it's decided. So guess what's left for us.
Man: The main event. The actual food!
Woman: Exactly — sandwiches, the cold chicken, my potato salad, and fruit for after. The serious food is our department.
Man: I'll do the chicken tonight and the sandwiches in the morning. We're the kitchen heroes of this picnic!
Woman: Heroes with cool bags. Eleven o'clock at the gate!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Food.
• Vì sao đúng: "The main event. The actual food!" – "Exactly — sandwiches, the cold chicken, my potato salad... The serious food is our department".
• Drinks sai: Tom đã nhận phần đồ uống ("Tom's bringing all the drinks — lemonade, juice, his famous iced coffee. Don't touch drinks").
• Snacks sai: Priya lo phần này ("Crisps, nuts, those little crackers — all hers, it's decided").
👉 Mẹo: dạng chia việc mang đồ — ghép nhanh "tên người + món" khi nghe. Phần của người nói nằm sau "what's left for us / our department".

question_text: Jana is talking to her friend. What does Jana’s sister look like?
options: Blonde
Tall
Short
explanation:
Woman: Jana! Your sister lands tomorrow, right? I'm collecting her from the airport — describe her so I don't hug a stranger!
Man: Ha! People always expect us to look alike. They think she's blonde like me — no, her hair is dark brown, almost black.
Woman: Dark hair, got it. And is she tall? You're practically a lighthouse.
Man: Everyone assumes that too! No — the height gene skipped her completely. She's short, barely reaches my shoulder, and furious about it since childhood.
Woman: Short with dark hair. Anything else?
Man: She'll be the one laughing loudest at the arrivals gate. You literally cannot miss her.
Woman: Short, dark, loud and wonderful. I'll bring the welcome sign!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Short.
• Vì sao đúng: "No — the height gene skipped her completely. She's short, barely reaches my shoulder, and furious about it since childhood".
• Blonde sai: bị bác ngay, tóc cô ấy nâu sẫm gần như đen — "They think she's blonde like me — no, her hair is dark brown, almost black".
• Tall sai: cũng bị bác, chỉ người kể mới cao — "Everyone assumes that too! No — the height gene skipped her".
👉 Mẹo: dạng tả ngoại hình, bám cấu trúc phủ định "People think... — no, actually...". Đặc điểm của NGƯỜI KỂ (blonde, tall) hay bị gán nhầm sang người được hỏi.

question_text: Four people are talking about their journey to work. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My office is twenty-five minutes from home on foot, and my neighbour Marta works in the same building, so every morning at eight we set off together. We solve the world's problems before nine — her divorce, my roses, everyone's politics. Honestly, the conversation is better exercise than the walking. On days she is ill, the same pavement feels twice as long, and I arrive at my desk with nobody's opinions but my own.
Speaker B: I am a devoted passenger of the seven-forty. Top deck, second row, window seat — my little office in the sky. While the traffic crawls underneath, I read my novel or answer messages, and somebody else worries about the driving. A monthly ticket costs less than a week of parking in my part of town. Colleagues complain about their steering wheels; I turn pages. I know who wins.
Speaker C: My commute is my meditation, and it only works because I do it with nobody. Thirty-five minutes on foot, headphones optional, thoughts wandering where they like. I rehearse difficult conversations, plan the weekend, sometimes just count magpies. People offer me lifts constantly and I refuse them all — those solitary steps between home and work are where I become ready for other humans.
Speaker D: I resisted for years, but the school run defeated me: two children, two schools, one office, three different directions. So now it is the family wagon every morning — bags in the boot, arguments about the radio station, goodbye kisses at two different gates, then the ring road to work. Parking costs a fortune and the traffic tests my soul. But with our timetable, four wheels are not a choice; they are survival.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Walk with friends (PARAPHRASE: "set off together... conversation is better exercise"). B = Go by bus (PARAPHRASE: "passenger of the seven-forty... top deck... monthly ticket"). C = Walk alone (PARAPHRASE: "on foot... with nobody... solitary steps"). D = Drive car (keyword-lite "family wagon... parking... four wheels"). Nhiễu: bike, train.

question_text: Listen to a woman explaining why he was late. What is the main reason he gets late?
options: Overslept
Forgot something
Missed the train
explanation:
Let me explain about my husband before you all judge him — he'll be here any minute! It's not what you think. He didn't oversleep; he was actually up at six, I heard him making coffee before my alarm even rang. And he didn't forget anything either — the presents, the flowers, the folder for later, everything was packed by the door since last night. What happened is simpler: he missed the train. The one before it was cancelled, the platform was packed, and he just couldn't squeeze on. The next train gets in at ten past — save him some cake!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Missed the train (lỡ tàu).
• Vì sao đúng: người vợ nói thẳng "What happened is simpler: he missed the train" — tàu trước bị hủy, sân ga đông nghịt nên anh không chen lên được.
• Overslept sai: bị phủ định ngay từ đầu "He didn't oversleep; he was actually up at six" — anh dậy từ 6 giờ, còn pha cà phê.
• Forgot something sai: cũng bị phủ định "he didn't forget anything either" — quà, hoa, tập hồ sơ đã xếp sẵn ở cửa từ tối hôm trước.
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi LÝ DO thường liệt kê đủ 3 phương án nhưng phủ định 2 cái bằng "didn't...", "it's not..."; chỉ khoanh phương án đi kèm câu khẳng định như "What happened is..." hoặc "The reason is...".

question_text: A woman is chatting with a friend about her afternoon plans. What is she going to do this aftermoon?
options: Go on a city tour
Visit a museum
Relax at home
explanation:
Perfect timing, I was just about to text you my plans! So, this afternoon. Mum suggested the museum — there's a new exhibition — but queues on a school holiday? An hour of waiting with a hundred toddlers, no thank you. And yes, relaxing at home sounds tempting, but I've been indoors all week with that report; my sofa and I need a break from each other. So I've booked the city tour! The walking one with the funny guide everyone recommends — old town, rooftop views, secret courtyards. Three o'clock start. Jealous?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Go on a city tour (đi tour tham quan thành phố).
• Vì sao đúng: cô nói "So I've booked the city tour! The walking one with the funny guide everyone recommends — old town, rooftop views... Three o'clock start".
• Visit a museum sai: là gợi ý của mẹ nhưng bị loại vì xếp hàng "queues on a school holiday? An hour of waiting with a hundred toddlers, no thank you".
• Relax at home sai: cô đã ở nhà cả tuần "I've been indoors all week with that report; my sofa and I need a break from each other".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi KẾ HOẠCH CHIỀU NAY, đáp án là hoạt động ĐÃ ĐẶT/ĐÃ ĐẶT CHỖ ("I've booked...") kèm giờ cụ thể; hai lựa chọn kia luôn có câu chê ngay sau đó.

question_text: What is her favorite thing to do in her spare time?
options: watching a movie at home
going to the theatre
playing sports
explanation:
People assume I spend my evenings on the sofa watching films at home, and yes, that happens on lazy Sundays — but it's not what I love most. My brother keeps dragging me to play sports with his team, and I go sometimes, mostly for the pizza afterwards. But my real passion, the thing I save my money for, is going to the theatre. Live actors, the lights, that moment when the curtain rises — nothing on a screen comes close. I've already booked three plays for next month!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Going to the theatre.
• Vì sao đúng: "my real passion, the thing I save my money for, is going to the theatre" — đã đặt vé ba vở cho tháng sau.
• Watching a movie at home sai: chỉ xảy ra vào Chủ nhật lười và bị hạ thấp ngay ("it's not what I love most").
• Playing sports sai: đi cùng anh trai cho có, chủ yếu vì bữa pizza sau đó ("mostly for the pizza afterwards").
👉 Mẹo: hỏi sở thích SỐ MỘT, tìm cụm cường độ mạnh "my real passion", "what I love most"; ý gắn với "sometimes" luôn bị loại.

question_text: A woman is chatting with a friend about her afternoon plans. What is she going to do this afternoon?
options: Sleep at home
Go to the cinema
Go on a city tour
explanation:
You caught me at the perfect time — I'm just deciding my afternoon! My body says sleep at home, honestly, after this crazy week — but if I nap now I'll be awake until three in the morning, so no. My neighbour invited me to the cinema, but it's that three-hour war film, and I'm not in the mood for explosions. So I've decided: I'm going on the city tour! The open-top bus one — I've lived here six years and never done it. Tourist in my own town, here I come!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Go on a city tour.
• Vì sao đúng: "So I've decided: I'm going on the city tour! The open-top bus one — I've lived here six years and never done it."
• Sleep at home sai: cô tự loại vì ngủ giờ này sẽ thức tới 3 giờ sáng ("if I nap now I'll be awake until three in the morning, so no").
• Go to the cinema sai: hàng xóm rủ nhưng đó là phim chiến tranh dài ba tiếng, cô không có hứng.
👉 Mẹo: hỏi kế hoạch, bám "So I've decided"; ý gắn với "My body says..." hoặc lời rủ của người khác đều là nhiễu.

question_text: A man is talking about his job. Where is he working now?
options: At a university
In a big company
In a bank
explanation:
My career path confuses everyone at reunions, so here's the short version! Yes, I spent six years at the university — teaching economics, marking essays at midnight — but I left that world behind two winters ago. Then came a strange year at a big company, one of those glass-tower places; interesting money, soulless meetings, we parted as friends. These days? I work in a bank. The old red-brick one on Market Street — I manage the loans department, regular hours, actual weekends. My students would laugh, but honestly, I've never been happier.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – In a bank (làm ở ngân hàng).
• Vì sao đúng: anh nói "These days? I work in a bank. The old red-brick one on Market Street — I manage the loans department, regular hours, actual weekends".
• At a university sai: đã nghỉ từ hai năm trước "I spent six years at the university — teaching economics... but I left that world behind two winters ago".
• In a big company sai: chỉ làm đúng một năm rồi nghỉ "Then came a strange year at a big company... we parted as friends".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi HIỆN TẠI LÀM Ở ĐÂU, bài kể theo trình tự sự nghiệp. Bám mốc thời gian "These days", "Now", "Today" và loại mọi nơi có "left", "spent... years" ở thì quá khứ.

question_text: A man is calling his teacher to meet for the assignment. When is the meeting?
options: On Thursday afternoon
On Tuesday morning
On Thursday morning
explanation:
Good afternoon, Professor Hale, this is Victor from your research methods group — about our assignment meeting. Thank you for offering the slots! I checked my timetable carefully. Thursday afternoon, your first suggestion, clashes with my lab session — I can't move that, unfortunately. And Tuesday morning I'm at the hospital placement all day, so that's out too. But your third option works perfectly: Thursday morning. I'll take Thursday morning, ten o'clock, your office — and I'll bring the draft AND the questions this time. Thank you again, Professor!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – On Thursday morning (sáng thứ Năm).
• Vì sao đúng: Victor chốt "But your third option works perfectly: Thursday morning. I'll take Thursday morning, ten o'clock, your office".
• On Thursday afternoon sai: là gợi ý đầu tiên nhưng trùng buổi thí nghiệm "clashes with my lab session — I can't move that".
• On Tuesday morning sai: cậu đi thực tập bệnh viện cả ngày "I'm at the hospital placement all day, so that's out too".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi LỊCH HẸN có 3 lựa chọn giáo viên đưa ra, nghe theo thứ tự "first suggestion / second / third option". Chỉ chọn phương án đi kèm "works perfectly", "I'll take..." và có giờ cụ thể.

question_text: Listen to an instruction. Which light shows that the computer is on?
options: Green
Red
Blue
explanation:
Before I leave you with your new office computer, one important lesson: the three lights on the tower, because the manual explains them terribly. The green light near the cable? That only tells you power is arriving from the wall — the machine itself can still be fast asleep. The little red one blinks when something needs attention, usually a low battery in the backup. The one you actually want every morning is the blue light: blue shining means the computer is on and working. No blue, no work. Any questions?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Blue.
• Vì sao đúng: "The one you actually want every morning is the blue light: blue shining means the computer is on and working. No blue, no work."
• Green sai: chỉ báo có điện từ ổ cắm, máy vẫn có thể đang tắt ("the machine itself can still be fast asleep").
• Red sai: là đèn cảnh báo, nháy khi có gì đó cần chú ý, thường là pin dự phòng yếu.
👉 Mẹo: dạng hướng dẫn thiết bị, ghi nhanh cặp màu–chức năng rồi chọn đúng chức năng câu hỏi hỏi (ở đây là trạng thái "on").

question_text: Four people are talking about listening to music. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My nervous system has an off switch, and it is shaped like a record player. After the children are in bed, I pour a tea, lower the needle on something slow, and let the day's knots untie themselves one by one. No screens, no talking — just twenty quiet minutes while the melodies do their gentle housework inside my head. My husband says he can measure my week by which record I reach for on Friday night.
Speaker B: I wake up before my alarm just to beat it to the speaker. The first song goes on while my eyes are still half closed, and it walks me through the whole morning — louder for the shower, brighter for breakfast, something cheerful for finding my keys. By the time I close the front door, side one is finished and I am fully human. A morning that starts in silence feels broken to me all day.
Speaker C: My voice is not good, and I could not care less — every song I know is a duet the moment it starts. I harmonise with the kettle-side radio, perform full choruses into the hairbrush, and my car is a one-woman concert hall on the motorway. The neighbours applauded from their balcony once, only half joking. Listening quietly feels like watching a dance and refusing to move; joining in with my own voice is the entire pleasure.
Speaker D: Exam season turned me into a musical creature. My revision only works with a instrumental stream in my ears — the notes hold my attention on the page the way a fence holds sheep. Lyrics ruin it: the words on the page and the words in the song start fighting. Four hours of formulas pass gently when the piano is playing. In silence, I last twenty minutes before my phone wins.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = To relax (PARAPHRASE: "off switch... knots untie themselves... gentle housework"). B = After waking up (PARAPHRASE: "wake up before my alarm... walks me through the morning"). C = While singing (PARAPHRASE: "every song is a duet... my own voice is the pleasure"). D = While studying (keyword "revision... formulas"). Nhiễu: while exercising, before bed. (Variant khác lời 16/18.)

question_text: A man is talking about his trip. What did he enjoy last year?
options: Hiking
Cycling
Swimming
explanation:
People keep asking about my trip last year, so here's the honest version. The hotel offered three activities. I tried hiking on the first day — beautiful views, but my knees complained for a week afterwards. Swimming was on the list too, but the lake was freezing even in July, so I gave up after one dip. What I really enjoyed was the cycling. They gave me a good bike, the paths were flat and quiet, and I rode for hours every day. I've even bought my own bike since!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Cycling.
• Vì sao đúng: "What I really enjoyed was the cycling" — cấu trúc nhấn mạnh cho biết đây mới là hoạt động anh thích; họ còn cho mượn xe tốt và anh đạp hàng giờ mỗi ngày.
• Hiking sai: có thử ngày đầu nhưng đau gối cả tuần sau đó ("my knees complained for a week afterwards").
• Swimming sai: nước hồ lạnh cóng dù đang tháng Bảy, anh bỏ cuộc sau một lần xuống ("the lake was freezing even in July").
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "thích hoạt động nào" luôn nêu đủ 3 hoạt động. Chỉ chọn cái đi sau cụm nhấn mạnh "What I really enjoyed/loved was...", bỏ mọi cái đứng trước "but".

question_text: A man calls the teleshop. What is the teleshop number?
explanation:
Hello, hello — is this thing recording? Right. I'm calling about the blender from your TV advert, and I want to check I've got the right number, because I've dialled wrong twice already. The first time I tried one-zero-two-zero-three-zero, which turned out to be a pizza place — nice people, wrong products. Then somebody gave me three-zero-one-zero-two-zero, also wrong, that's a taxi firm. The number on my screen right now says: two-zero-one-zero-three-zero. Two, zero, one, zero, three, zero. If this is finally the teleshop — call me back about the blender!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 201030.
• Vì sao đúng: "The number on my screen right now says: two-zero-one-zero-three-zero. Two, zero, one, zero, three, zero." — tức 201030.
• 102030 sai: là số ông gọi nhầm lần đầu, hóa ra là tiệm pizza ("which turned out to be a pizza place").
• 301020 sai: là số người khác đưa, hóa ra là hãng taxi ("also wrong, that's a taxi firm").
👉 Mẹo: dạng dãy số, ghi cả ba dãy rồi mới chọn; đáp án là dãy gắn với hiện tại ("right now") và được đọc lại lần hai.

question_text: Four people are talking about their studying habits. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My friends joke that my textbooks have frequent flyer miles. Monday finds me at the kitchen counter, Tuesday in the corner café, Wednesday on the top floor of the faculty building, and sunny days pull me onto the grass by the fountain. A single fixed desk makes my thoughts go stale within an hour; every change of scenery presses a refresh button in my head. During finals I once revised in five spots in one day — my best results ever followed.
Speaker B: One squeaking chair can end my whole session, so I have searched the city for perfect stillness and found it: the archive room on the fourth floor, past the old maps, where even footsteps apologise. Nobody speaks, phones die at the door, and the loudest event of the afternoon is a page turning. My friends revise in the noisy common room and call me a monk. Fine — this monk remembers what he reads.
Speaker C: My revision has a sound engineer: me. Soft strings under heavy reading, low steady beats when the essay needs momentum, and one particular film soundtrack reserved for the night before every exam — my little superstition. Inside the headphones, the world disappears and the words on the page stand still. Take the melodies away and my eyes slide off every paragraph. My library is wherever my playlist is.
Speaker D: The house only becomes mine after midnight, and that is when the books open. One lamp, cold tea, absolute quiet from eleven until two — my brain does its finest work while the whole street sleeps. Morning people preach their sunrise routines at me, and I have honestly tried. Before nine, I read the same sentence six times; after midnight, I read it once and own it forever.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = In various places (PARAPHRASE: "textbooks have frequent flyer miles... change of scenery"). B = In a quiet place (PARAPHRASE: "perfect stillness... even footsteps apologise"). C = With music (keyword-lite "headphones... melodies... playlist"). D = Late at night (keyword-lite "after midnight... eleven until two"). Nhiễu: with friends, classroom. (Variant khác lời 09/15.)

question_text: Four people are talking about protecting the environment. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: People are surprised when I call my armchair shopping an environmental habit, but do the sums with me. My orders arrive in one van that serves the whole neighbourhood — one engine replacing the thirty cars that would each have driven to the retail park and circled for parking. I batch everything into a single weekly delivery, so no extra trips, no impulse petrol. My sister burns a litre of fuel to buy a toothbrush; my toothbrush shares a van with her street's groceries.
Speaker B: My car has learned to live without me on weekdays. Since March I catch the six-fifty into the centre — no fuel burned in my name, no half hour hunting for parking, and the queue of single-driver cars I sail past confirms my choice every morning. My colleagues thought the novelty would wear off before summer. Instead my car now spends its weekdays under a cover, and the planet and my wallet both breathe easier.
Speaker C: My electricity meter used to spin like a fan; now it crawls, and that is my proudest achievement this year. Every lamp in the house went low-energy, the heating drops two degrees at night, and the television no longer sleeps with one glowing eye — everything goes off at the wall. My teenagers complained for a week, then turned it into a competition. Last month's usage was barely half of last year's.
Speaker D: In my bathroom hangs a four-minute hourglass, and the family showers race it. The washing-up happens in a basin, never under a running stream, and the rinsing water ends its life in my flowerpots. I fitted the little flow-savers on every tap the day the utility report showed what an average family pours away. My children think I am obsessed. I tell them: electricity can be made tomorrow, but the well does not refill on demand.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Shopping online (PARAPHRASE: "armchair shopping... orders... single weekly delivery"). B = Not driving to work (PARAPHRASE: "car has learned to live without me... catch the six-fifty"). C = Using less electricity (keyword-lite "electricity meter... low-energy... usage half"). D = Using less water (keyword-lite "showers race it... running stream... well"). Nhiễu: planting trees, recycling bottles. (Variant khác lời Đề 03.)

question_text: Why do residents oppose this plan?
options: It will remove several public parks in the area
It makes public transportation more expensive for residents
It doesn't do enough to promote alternatives to driving
explanation:
Good evening, and thank you for joining tonight's town hall about the Regional Development Plan. Before we open the floor, let me address what people are actually angry about, because the newspapers have confused things. No, the plan will not remove any public parks — I have read all two hundred pages, and every park in this district is protected. And no, it will not make public transportation more expensive; fares are set by a different authority entirely. The genuine complaint, the one written on the posters outside, is that the plan does not do enough to promote alternatives to driving. Page after page describes new roads and bigger junctions, yet the sections on bus routes, cycle paths and walkable streets are thin. Residents who hoped to leave their cars at home feel the city is planning a future with even more traffic, not less, and frankly, reading the document, it is hard to argue with them.
The council members I have spoken to have a different, quieter worry. It is not about opposition from local businesses — most shops along the high street actually welcome the plan. Nor has the project exceeded its budget; the accounts are still healthy. Their concern is about land. The city centre is full of empty warehouses and abandoned plots that could be rebuilt first, yet the plan pushes outward into green fields at the edge of town. Several councillors argue that this is simply not an efficient use of the land we already have, and they intend to demand changes before any vote takes place.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 06 bài 1 — cùng câu hỏi và đáp án, lời khác để hai đề không trùng script.)
1. Đáp án: It doesn't do enough to promote alternatives to driving. Bẫy: "remove public parks" và "more expensive" đều bị bác ngay đầu.
2. Đáp án: The plan is not making efficient use of existing land. Bẫy: "opposition from businesses" và "exceeded budget" đều bị phủ định.

question_text: Four people are talking about using the Internet. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My travel budget is small, so the world comes to me through my screen instead. Friday nights are for cinema at home — I work through the classics one director at a time, and my watchlist currently holds two hundred titles. Last month it was old Japanese films; this month, French comedies with subtitles. My local cinema shows six films; my laptop shows sixty thousand. For the price of one ticket a month, I have the largest screen-room in history.
Speaker B: When my best friend moved to Australia, I thought our friendship would shrink to birthday messages. Instead, we talk more now than when she lived two streets away. Sunday morning calls over breakfast — her dinner time — the running joke chat that never sleeps, photos of everything from her new beach to my old dog. The distance is nine thousand kilometres; the conversation has never been closer. The connection is what keeps us next-door neighbours.
Speaker C: My degree happens as much online as in the lecture hall. The reading lists live on the portal, my group project shares one document across five laptops, and the deadline uploads happen at two minutes to midnight, always. When the statistics module nearly defeated me, a professor in another country rescued my grade through a free video series. Ask what the internet is to me and I will answer honestly: it is where my homework gets done.
Speaker D: I refuse to stand at a bus stop hoping anymore. Before my shoes are on, the app has told me which line is running late, where my bus is on the map, and whether the trains are behaving. When the bridge closed last month, my phone had redrawn my whole route before the radio mentioned it. My colleagues arrive complaining about their journeys. I arrive having read a book, exactly on time.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = watch films (PARAPHRASE: "cinema at home... watchlist... largest screen-room"). B = communicate with friends (PARAPHRASE: "we talk more now... conversation has never been closer"). C = complete assignments (keyword "homework gets done... deadline uploads"). D = find transport information (keyword-lite "which line is running late... redrawn my route"). Nhiễu: news, games. (Variant khác lời Đề 10/12.)

question_text: Four people are talking about listening to music. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: Sunday evenings are sacred in my flat: phone in the drawer, lights low, and one full album from start to finish on the good speakers. That hour dissolves whatever the week left in my muscles — I can feel the tension draining somewhere around the third track. Doctors talk about massages and hot baths; my medicine has always been melodies and a closed door. By the final song I am a calmer, kinder version of myself.
Speaker B: My study desk has three permanent residents: my laptop, my coffee, and my headphones. The moment revision starts, so does my instrumental playlist — nothing with lyrics, because sung words elbow the textbook words out of my memory. With the right background running, formulas settle in quietly and essays untangle themselves. My study group finds it funny that I refuse to revise in silence. Silence, for me, is where concentration goes to die.
Speaker C: I cannot keep a tune to myself — the moment I recognise a song, I am part of it. Full performances happen in my shower, duets with the radio while I cook, and my long drives are basically concerts where I hold every part. My family bangs on the bathroom door; my colleagues have votes about my humming. I accept all criticism and change nothing. Music you only listen to is music half-enjoyed.
Speaker D: The first thing my hand touches in the morning is not the snooze button — it is the play button. My wake-up playlist starts gentle and grows louder, and by the fourth song even my teenage son is vertical. Breakfast has a soundtrack, brushing teeth has a soundtrack, finding lost keys has a dramatic soundtrack. Mornings without that music feel like films with the sound off: technically functional, but joyless.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = To relax (PARAPHRASE: "dissolves whatever the week left... tension draining... calmer version"). B = While studying (keyword "revision... textbook... study group"). C = While singing (PARAPHRASE: "I am part of it... performances... hold every part"). D = After waking up (PARAPHRASE: "first thing my hand touches in the morning... wake-up playlist"). Nhiễu: while driving, before bed. (Variant khác lời Đề 16/22.)

question_text: A girl is talking about a show she will attend. What will end with?
options: A dance performance
A big celebration
A surprise performance
explanation:
Guess who got tickets to the summer gala — me! Saturday night, and I've done my homework on the programme. My cousin swears it ends with a dance performance, but she's thinking of the spring show — the dance troupe is touring abroad this month. The newspaper called it 'a big celebration', but that's just their fancy words for the whole evening, not the finale. The actual ending, according to the organisers themselves, is a surprise performance — a mystery guest that nobody, not even the staff, will know until the curtain. I love secrets like this!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – A surprise performance (một tiết mục bất ngờ).
• Vì sao đúng: cô dẫn nguồn chính thức "The actual ending, according to the organisers themselves, is a surprise performance — a mystery guest that nobody... will know until the curtain".
• A dance performance sai: người chị họ nhớ nhầm sang chương trình mùa xuân "she's thinking of the spring show — the dance troupe is touring abroad this month".
• A big celebration sai: chỉ là cách báo chí gọi cả buổi tối, không phải màn kết "that's just their fancy words for the whole evening, not the finale".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi KẾT THÚC BẰNG GÌ, so nguồn tin: lời đồn của người thân và báo chí thường sai. Chỉ tin nguồn "according to the organisers" và bám từ khóa chỉ phần cuối (ending, finale).

question_text: A woman is talking about her weekends. What did she do last week?
options: Went out with friends
Stayed at home
Visited a café
explanation:
My weekends are usually quite busy, but last week was different. My friends did call about going out on Saturday — there was a birthday dinner in town — but I was so tired after the work week that I said no. I even walked past that new café everyone talks about and didn't go in. Instead, I stayed at home the whole weekend: slept late, cooked slowly, watched two films under a blanket. And you know what? It was exactly what I needed.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Stayed at home.
• Vì sao đúng: "Instead, I stayed at home the whole weekend: slept late, cooked slowly, watched two films under a blanket".
• Went out with friends sai: có lời rủ nhưng cô từ chối vì quá mệt — "there was a birthday dinner in town — but I was so tired after the work week that I said no".
• Visited a café sai: cô chỉ đi ngang qua chứ không vào — "I even walked past that new café everyone talks about and didn't go in".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "làm gì cuối tuần", bám cụm đảo hướng "Instead, I...". Việc đi kèm "I said no", "didn't go in" là việc KHÔNG làm.

question_text: A woman is talking about shopping places. Where is she going to go shopping?
options: At the mall
At a boutique
At a new shopping center
explanation:
Saturday is shopping day, and this time I have a plan! Normally I just go to the mall — it's close, but honestly I know every shop in there by heart now. My sister keeps talking about that little boutique on Rose Street, but their prices make my eyes water, one dress costs my whole weekend budget. So instead I'm going to the new shopping centre by the river — it opened last month, over a hundred shops, and everything has opening discounts. I'll be there when the doors open!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – At a new shopping center.
• Vì sao đúng: "I'm going to the new shopping centre by the river — it opened last month, over a hundred shops, and everything has opening discounts".
• At the mall sai: cô đã chán vì quá quen ("I know every shop in there by heart now").
• At a boutique sai: là gợi ý của chị gái nhưng giá quá đắt ("their prices make my eyes water, one dress costs my whole weekend budget").
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi nơi chốn, đáp án thường nằm sau "So instead I'm going to..."; hai nơi nêu trước chỉ để loại trừ.

question_text: Louis is having dinner in a new restaurant. What does he complain about?
options: The price is cheap
The food is delicious
The service is slow
explanation:
Reporting live from my table at the new bistro — this is Louis, your unofficial food critic! The verdict so far. The menu prices genuinely surprised me — main courses cheaper than the pizzeria across the road, no complaints there. And the food? My lamb was perfect, herbs, crispy edges, the works — the kitchen clearly knows its business. BUT. I ordered dessert twenty-five minutes ago. My water glass has been empty for half an hour. Three tables are waving at nobody. The service here is painfully slow — that's my one real complaint tonight!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – The service is slow (phục vụ chậm).
• Vì sao đúng: cả bài khen rồi bẻ lái bằng chữ "BUT", và Louis chốt lại nhận xét trọng tâm "The service here is painfully slow — that's my one real complaint tonight", kèm bằng chứng: đợi tráng miệng 25 phút, cốc nước cạn nửa tiếng.
• The price is cheap sai: anh có khen giá "main courses cheaper than the pizzeria across the road", nhưng đó là chi tiết phụ, không phải nhận xét chính anh muốn nêu.
• The food is delicious sai: món ăn cũng được khen "My lamb was perfect, herbs, crispy edges", nhưng vẫn nằm ở phần trước chữ "BUT".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi NHẬN XÉT/ĐÁNH GIÁ, nghe tới chữ "BUT" là biết trọng tâm nằm ở vế sau. Câu có "my one real complaint", "the only problem" chính là ý người nói muốn nhấn.

question_text: Four people are talking about travelling to work. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My mornings start at the stop outside the flower shop, seven-fifteen sharp. The number twelve carries me and my thoughts across town while somebody else handles the gears and the traffic lights. I have a regular seat, a regular crossword, and a nodding acquaintance with the whole upper deck. Driving would save me ten minutes, my brother insists. Those ten minutes would cost me my crossword and my calm, so the twelve keeps winning.
Speaker B: Our house runs on a military timetable — two school drop-offs, then my clinic across town by eight-thirty. Only the family car makes that mathematics work. The children argue over the radio in the back, I drink my coffee at red lights, and the parking bill at the end of each month makes my eyes water. Friends preach about buses and bicycles. With our mornings, I would need three of each.
Speaker C: Between my front door and the office lie two parks and one bridge, and I cross them all on foot, by myself, every day. Those forty minutes are the only true silence I get — no passengers, no colleagues, just my own footsteps sorting out my thoughts. Offers of lifts come daily and I decline them all politely. By the time I reach my desk, the day's problems have already been walked into order.
Speaker D: My commute doubles as my social hour. My colleague Anh lives three doors down, so we cover the thirty minutes to the office side by side, on foot, dissecting yesterday's meetings and planning our lunches. When she is away I genuinely feel the difference — the same streets, half the fun. Our boss says he can hear us laughing from his window before we reach the gate. Best part of the working day, both of us agree.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = travel by bus (PARAPHRASE: "the number twelve carries me... upper deck"). B = travel by car (PARAPHRASE: "family car... parking bill... red lights"). C = walk alone (PARAPHRASE: "on foot, by myself... own footsteps"). D = walk with a friend (PARAPHRASE: "cover the thirty minutes side by side, on foot"). Nhiễu: bicycle, motorbike. (Variant khác lời Đề 17.)

question_text: Why is identifying the correct market so important for a company?
options: It helps the company focus its resources and avoid wasting time on low-demand areas.
It guarantees that the business will operate without any rival firms.
It provides a justification for lowering product standards to maximize profit.
explanation:
Welcome to week three of our business strategy course. Today's topic: why identifying the correct market matters so much. Let me first remove two dangerous ideas. Some new founders believe that once they choose a specific market niche, their business will somehow operate without any rival firms. That protection does not exist — competitors follow wherever money appears. Even worse, I occasionally hear that focusing on one market justifies lowering product standards to squeeze out more profit, since customers there have fewer choices. Companies that try this are usually punished within a year. The real reason market identification matters is efficiency: it helps the company focus its resources and avoid wasting time on low-demand areas. A small business has limited money, limited staff and limited hours. Point them at the customers who genuinely want your product, and every dollar works harder. Spread them across markets that barely care, and even a good product dies quietly.
Our second word today is profitability, which is widely misunderstood. Reaching profit does not signal that the company no longer needs market research — customers keep changing whether you study them or not. Nor does it suggest you can now disregard your competitors; they read your success as an invitation. What profitability really proves is more basic and more important: the company can cover its own costs, and its position in the market is strengthening. Profit is oxygen. It does not tell you where to swim, but without it, no other strategic question matters at all.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It helps the company focus its resources and avoid wasting time on low-demand areas. Bẫy: "without any rival firms" và "lowering product standards" đều bị bác ("That protection does not exist", "punished within a year").
2. Đáp án: It proves the company can cover costs and strengthen its position. Bẫy: "no further need for market research" và "disregard competitors" đều bị phủ định.

question_text: Listen to an announcement. Which platform to wait for the train?
options: Platform 2
Platform 5
Platform 8
explanation:
Your attention please, passengers for the fourteen twenty service to the coast. Please note the platform information, as there have been changes this afternoon. This train normally departs from platform five — not today; platform five is closed for urgent repairs. Earlier announcements mentioned platform eight; that arrangement has also been cancelled. The fourteen twenty will now depart from platform two. Platform two, at the far end of the main hall, past the ticket office. Please allow extra time to reach it. Thank you.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Platform 2.
• Vì sao đúng: thông báo chốt "The fourteen twenty will now depart from platform two. Platform two, at the far end of the main hall".
• Platform 5 sai: đó là sân ga thường ngày nhưng hôm nay đóng cửa "platform five is closed for urgent repairs".
• Platform 8 sai: là thông báo cũ đã bị hủy "Earlier announcements mentioned platform eight; that arrangement has also been cancelled".
👉 Mẹo: dạng thông báo nhà ga, chú ý trạng từ thời gian: "normally/earlier" = thông tin cũ, "now" = thông tin đúng. Chỉ khoanh số đi kèm "will now depart from".

question_text: Four people are talking about their favourite sports. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: Eleven of us, one captain's armband, and a league table we take far too seriously — that is my Sunday. I have played with the same club since school, and the best part was never the goals; it is the changing-room jokes, the shared bus to away games, the feeling of covering for a teammate having a bad day. Individual training bores me stiff. Give me a squad, a formation and someone to celebrate with.
Speaker B: I grew up beside the sea, and my sport never left it. Four mornings a week I am in the pool before work, counting lengths, and summer weekends belong to the open bays — goggles, cap, and an hour of open blue. The weightlessness resets whatever the week has bent. Dry-land sports have never tempted me; if my sport does not involve getting wet, I fundamentally do not trust it.
Speaker C: Our neighbourhood has an unofficial stadium: the flat stretch of tarmac between the bakery and the parked cars. Every evening the kids and half the adults gather there — jumpers for goalposts, chalk lines redrawn weekly, matches interrupted respectfully for passing motorbikes. No membership, no schedule, no referee except the old man on the balcony. The fancy pitches charge by the hour; our tarmac has been free for thirty years.
Speaker D: My teammates have four legs. Saturday means the riding school: grooming my horse, checking tack, then jumping practice in the sand arena and long rides through the hills when weather allows. People assume the horse does all the work — let them try holding a canter for an hour. The partnership is the point: two heartbeats negotiating every fence together. No gym machine has ever nuzzled my pocket for apples afterwards.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = plays in a team sport (PARAPHRASE: "Eleven of us... squad, formation... teammate"). B = spends time in the water (PARAPHRASE: "in the pool... open bays... getting wet"). C = plays in the street (PARAPHRASE: "flat stretch of tarmac... jumpers for goalposts"). D = does sports with animals (PARAPHRASE: "teammates have four legs... riding school... horse"). Nhiễu: alone, running.

question_text: Louis is having dinner in a new restaurant. What does he complain about?
options: The price is cheap
The food is delicious
The service is slow
explanation:
So here I am at that new restaurant everyone's been posting about, and I have thoughts. Credit where it's due: the food is delicious — my soup was perfect, and this steak melts like butter. The price is fair too, cheaper than I expected for this part of town. But the service! I waited forty minutes for the starter, another thirty for the main, and I've been holding this empty glass for a quarter of an hour. The service is just too slow. Lovely food — bring a book!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – The service is slow.
• Vì sao đúng: "But the service! I waited forty minutes for the starter, another thirty for the main" và anh chốt "The service is just too slow".
• The price is cheap sai: giá đúng là rẻ nhưng đó chỉ là lời khen dạo đầu trước "But" ("The price is fair too, cheaper than I expected").
• The food is delicious sai: đồ ăn ngon thật ("the food is delicious"), nhưng ý kiến Louis muốn nhấn mạnh nằm sau "But".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi nhận xét về nhà hàng/dịch vụ, hai ý đầu thường là khen; quan điểm bài muốn hỏi nằm sau "But" và được nhắc lại ở câu chốt.

question_text: Four people are talking about protecting the environment. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: Open my cleaning cupboard and you will find exactly four things: white vinegar, baking soda, a block of plain soap and old cloths cut from worn-out shirts. The supermarket sprays with their skulls and warnings left this house when my asthma got worse, and honestly, nothing has been dirtier since. My mother-in-law inspects my kitchen on every visit hoping to win the argument. Five years running, the vinegar is still champion.
Speaker B: My loft was a museum of forgotten things until last spring. Now there is a rule: whatever we no longer use must find a new owner within the month. The children's bicycles went to the refugee centre, my old tools to the young man fixing up the house opposite, and four boxes of books to the hospital library. Selling never crossed my mind — watching the neighbour's boy ride off on my son's old bike paid better than money.
Speaker C: I have become that person who studies packaging in the supermarket aisle. If the label cannot tell me the cotton was grown responsibly or the paper came from managed forests, the product stays on the shelf. My weekly shop takes twice as long and costs a little extra, but my basket is my ballot paper. Companies count every purchase, so I make every purchase say something.
Speaker D: Nothing that once held food gets binned in my kitchen. The tall pasta jars now organise my whole pantry, margarine tubs stack in the freezer full of portioned stews, and the biscuit tins carry cakes to every school fair in the district. My wife jokes that our shelves are a graveyard of other products' packaging. Perhaps — but we have not bought storage boxes in a decade, and our food waste fits in a teacup.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Does not use commercial cleaning products (PARAPHRASE: "supermarket sprays... left this house... vinegar is champion"). B = Give away used items (PARAPHRASE: "find a new owner... paid better than money"). C = Buy environmentally friendly products (keyword-lite "grown responsibly... managed forests"). D = Reuse containers for storing food (keyword "jars organise my pantry... tubs... tins"). Nhiễu: walk instead of driving, reusable bags.

infoItems.text: Does not use commercial cleaning products

question_text: Four people are talking about online shopping. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: I broke my ankle in January, and that is when internet shopping saved my winter. Everything I needed simply appeared: the courier brought my groceries to the third floor, the pharmacy package came the next morning, and even my new crutch pads arrived faster than my sister could visit. Two months without leaving the flat, and I never missed a meal or a birthday present. The doorbell became my favourite sound in the house.
Speaker B: My grandmother taught me never to pay the first price, and the internet is her lesson made easy. I watch items for weeks, wait for the seasonal sales, stack the discount codes, and strike when the price bottoms out. The winter coat I am wearing cost me less than half the shop price. My colleagues call me stingy, but my bank account calls me clever — same product, same label, very different receipt.
Speaker C: I run my own bakery, which means my day off is Tuesday and only Tuesday. Spending it in queues would be a small tragedy, so my entire household shops itself online in stolen minutes — flour suppliers compared while the ovens heat, birthday gifts chosen on the bus, groceries ordered during my lunch break. The hours other people spend pushing trolleys, I spend by the river with my dog. That trade is the best bargain the internet ever offered me.
Speaker D: My daughter has unusual feet — one size larger than the other, if you can believe it. Every shoe shop in our city offers the same fifteen models and shrugs. Online, I found a maker who sells single shoes in mixed sizes, three colours, her exact fit. The same story repeats with everything unusual we need: left-handed scissors, extra-long trousers, that discontinued ink my husband swears by. The high street stocks the middle of the road; the internet stocks everyone else.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = The products are delivered (PARAPHRASE: "simply appeared... courier... doorbell became my favourite sound"). B = It is cheaper (PARAPHRASE: "less than half the shop price... different receipt"). C = It saves time (PARAPHRASE: "stolen minutes... hours other people spend pushing trolleys"). D = There are more choices (PARAPHRASE: "single shoes in mixed sizes... stocks everyone else"). Nhiễu: easy to return, safe to pay. (Variant khác lời Đề 05/06.)

infoItems.text: The products are easy to return
It is safe to pay online

question_text: A man is talking about his holiday. How is he going to travel to the city?
options: By car
By bus
By train
explanation:
The holiday is booked at last — one week in the capital! Now, the travel plan. Driving is out: parking in the city costs a fortune, and I'd spend half the holiday looking for a space. The train was my first choice, honestly, but there are engineering works that week and the line is closed on both weekends. So I'm going by bus — the express coach, six in the morning, straight to the city centre in four hours. Cheap ticket, and I'll sleep the whole way!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – By bus.
• Vì sao đúng: "So I'm going by bus — the express coach, six in the morning, straight to the city centre in four hours".
• By car sai: bị loại ngay từ đầu ("Driving is out: parking in the city costs a fortune").
• By train sai: tuần đó thi công đường ray, tuyến đóng cả hai cuối tuần ("the line is closed on both weekends").
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi phương tiện, săn cụm loại trừ "is out", "is closed"; đáp án đi với "So I'm going by...".

question_text: Language is the biggest difficulty when people try to understand a local culture
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
Woman: Back from my month in the highlands, and I have one conclusion: you can smile, point and share meals all you like, but until you can speak with people in their own words, the real life of a place stays behind glass. I watched ceremonies I half-understood and jokes I missed entirely. The tongue is the door, and mine stayed locked.
Man: Funny — I have travelled wordless through plenty of places and felt the doors open anyway, through markets and music and shared work. A phrasebook helps, but I would not call it the main wall. What did strike me on my own trips is how the same shops, the same songs and the same screens now greet you everywhere. The world is blending.
Woman: That blending was everywhere in the highlands too — teenagers in global fashion under grandmother's roof, festival dances rehearsed from online videos. The old patterns are being stirred into one big pot, village by village. We watched it happen in different countries and brought home the same photograph.
Man: We did. And I will say the harder thing: the grandchildren are letting go. The old crafts, the ceremonies, the recipes — the young people I met shrugged at all of it. Their eyes point at the cities and the future, not the family altar.
Woman: Some shrug, but I met plenty of young people fighting to keep the old flames lit — recording the songs, learning the weaving. I refuse to sign their surrender yet. So how should an outsider truly learn another way of life, in your view?
Man: Boots on the ground — nothing else comes close. One week walking someone's streets teaches more than a shelf of books or a hundred documentaries. Go there, eat there, get lost there.
Woman: Books and films have taught me plenty from my own sofa, so I will keep both tickets, thank you.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: W-B-M-M (giữ nguyên). Paraphrase:
1. "Language biggest difficulty" → W: "The tongue is the door, and mine stayed locked" — M "I would not call it the main wall".
2. "Globalisation changing local traditions" → B: "The world is blending" + "stirred into one big pot... same photograph".
3. "Younger generation does not care" → M: "the grandchildren are letting go... shrugged at all of it" — W "I refuse to sign their surrender".
4. "Visiting in person most effective" → M: "Boots on the ground — nothing else comes close" — W "I will keep both tickets".

question_text: Four people are talking about outdoor activities. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My Saturdays begin at the stables before the mist lifts. Brushing her down, checking her hooves, then two hours through the fields with only hoofbeats for conversation — my mare knows the route better than I do by now. People ask if it frightens me, trusting an animal that size. It is the opposite: those two hours of moving together are the calmest partnership in my week. The saddle is my favourite chair in the world.
Speaker B: Rain or shine, my trainers hit the path along the canal at seven. Nothing complicated — just me, my breathing, and five kilometres of towpath before the world wakes up properly. I started to lose my temper less, honestly, and kept going because the mornings felt unfinished without it. Last month I entered my first ten-kilometre race and finished grinning like a fool. Simple legs, simple happiness.
Speaker C: My weekends are vertical. My club drives out to the crags every Sunday, ropes and helmets rattling in the boot, and we spend the day solving the rock face metre by metre. Fingertips ache, forearms burn, and the moment you pull over the top edge repays every scrape. People call it dangerous; done properly, it is chess with your whole body. I have never trusted people more than the ones holding my rope.
Speaker D: Two wheels, fat tyres, forest trails — that is my religion. Saturday mornings I load the bike, drive to the hills, and spend four muddy hours flying down tracks and pushing back up them. The bruises are a fair tax on the joy. My wife inspects the scratches on my arms every weekend and sighs; I remind her the alternative was golf, and she agrees the mud is better.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = horse riding (PARAPHRASE: "stables... my mare... saddle"). B = going for a run (PARAPHRASE: "trainers hit the path... five kilometres... race"). C = climbing (PARAPHRASE: "vertical... crags... ropes and helmets... rock face"). D = mountain biking (keyword-lite "Two wheels... bike... forest trails"). Nhiễu: swimming, camping.

question_text: Four people are talking about where they study. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: I like studying somewhere with sunshine and fresh air. It doesn't have to be completely quiet — in fact, when it's too quiet I don't feel inspired at all, which is why I never study in the library or in a classroom. What I love is the park near my university. I take my books, sit on the grass, and read. Nice weather and a light breeze — what could be more perfect than that?
Speaker B: Every day I spend about an hour on the train, and that's when I do most of my homework. A lot of people ask me how anyone can concentrate on public transport, but honestly the background noise is exactly what helps me focus. Quite often I can finish an important assignment in that one hour, before I even get to campus.
Speaker C: I have a real problem with noise. I did think about the university library, but there's always something — cups clinking, people sipping coffee, and someone dragging a chair across the floor. I live with my parents, and they're usually out at work during the day, so the house is completely silent. That's when I sit on the sofa and get my assignments done.
Speaker D: I actually need background sound to concentrate. There's a coffee shop near my house that a lot of people go to, and I love the atmosphere there. I can sit in a corner with my laptop, enjoy a cup of coffee, and somehow the buzz of the place lets me focus completely on my work.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A → In the park: "What I love is the park near my university... sit on the grass". Bẫy: A NHẮC library và classroom nhưng là để loại ("never study in the library or in a classroom").
B → On public transport: "about an hour on the train... background noise is exactly what helps me focus".
C → At home: "I live with my parents... the house is completely silent... sit on the sofa". Bẫy: C nhắc library nhưng để chê (cups clinking, chair dragging).
D → In the coffee shop: "There's a coffee shop near my house... enjoy a cup of coffee".
Nhiễu: In the library (A và C đều nhắc nhưng đều KHÔNG học ở đó), In the classroom (A loại).
👉 Mẹo: người nói nhắc một địa điểm để CHÊ rồi mới nói nơi mình học — chờ câu có "what I love / that's when I".

question_text: How to maximise productivity?
options: Effective time management
Effective allocation of resources
Effective utilization of personnel
explanation:
Everyone wants to be more productive these days, and there is plenty of advice about how to get more done. Some managers say the answer is to allocate resources more carefully — making sure that money and equipment go where they are needed most. Others believe it is all about how you use your personnel, giving each employee the task that suits them best. Both ideas can help in a large company, but for one person working alone, I don't think either of them is the key. In my experience, what really maximises productivity is effective time management. When you plan your day carefully, decide what is most important, and keep those hours free from interruptions, you simply get more done with the same energy. Studies show the same thing: people who organise their time well perform better than people who only work when they feel motivated.
Having said that, these strategies are not easy. Some people give up because the systems look complicated at the start, although most methods are actually simple once you have tried them for a week. Others say that a method designed for office work will not fit their particular job, and sometimes that is true. But the real problem, the one that catches almost everyone, is that using these strategies well takes real, continuous effort. Writing a plan is easy; following it on a busy afternoon, when emails keep arriving, is much harder. In the end, it is not about being clever — it is about doing the same simple things every day.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Effective time management. Bẫy: "allocation of resources" và "utilization of personnel" đều được nhắc rồi gạt ("neither of them is the key").
2. Đáp án: Using them effectively requires effort. Bẫy: "too complicated for beginners" bị hạ ("actually simple once you have tried"), "not suitable for every kind of job" được công nhận một phần nhưng không phải vấn đề chính ("the real problem... is effort").

question_text: There is too much information on the Internet
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
W: Have you seen the digital skills course they've just put on at the community centre?
M: I have, and I'd say it's long overdue. If you ask me, the real trouble with the web now is the sheer quantity of material — there's far more of it out there than anybody could ever wade through.
W: Hmm, I'm not so sure about that. There's a lot out there, I'll give you that, but I honestly don't think volume is the enemy. Nobody stands in a supermarket complaining that the shelves are too full.
M: In a supermarket you pick one shelf and walk away. Online you've got ten thousand shelves shouting at you at once.
W: Even so. What I'd say the course is genuinely for is that pulling anything useful out of the web is a proper craft. You have to be taught how to do it.
M: Yes, exactly, I'd go along with that entirely. Narrowing a search sensibly, working out whether a site can be trusted — none of that comes naturally to anyone at all.
W: Quite. My dad types a whole sentence into the box and then gives up when the first result is rubbish.
M: Mine reads the advert at the top of the page and treats it as gospel truth.
W: Actually, there's something rather bigger going on as well. I'm convinced that all this scrolling is quietly reshaping the way our minds work — how we reason, how we hold on to an idea.
M: Hang on, I can't go along with that one. Our routines have changed beyond recognition, obviously, and I'll accept that much happily. But the underlying thinking itself? No, I'd say that's much as it ever was.
W: You would say that. I certainly can't follow a complicated argument the way I could ten years ago.
M: That might just be your workload, to be honest. What I will sign up to, though, is that waiting for anything at all has become unbearable for most of us now.
W: Oh, completely, I'm right with you there. A page takes four seconds to load and I've already shut the tab.
M: Same with a queue, or a kettle. We've lost the knack of standing still.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Quá nhiều thông tin trên Internet = Man · Dùng Internet cần kỹ năng = Both · Internet đang thay đổi cách ta tư duy = Woman · Internet khiến người ta kém kiên nhẫn = Both

1. There is too much information on the Internet → Man: người đàn ông nêu rõ "the real trouble with the web now is the sheer quantity of material — there's far more of it out there than anybody could ever wade through." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "Hmm, I'm not so sure about that. There's a lot out there, I'll give you that, but I honestly don't think volume is the enemy."

2. Using the Internet requires skills → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "pulling anything useful out of the web is a proper craft. You have to be taught how to do it." Người đàn ông tán thành rõ ràng: "Yes, exactly, I'd go along with that entirely."

3. The Internet is changing the way we think → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "I'm convinced that all this scrolling is quietly reshaping the way our minds work — how we reason, how we hold on to an idea." Người đàn ông phản đối: "Hang on, I can't go along with that one... But the underlying thinking itself? No, I'd say that's much as it ever was."

4. The Internet has made people less patient → Both: người đàn ông nêu "waiting for anything at all has become unbearable for most of us now", người phụ nữ đồng ý: "Oh, completely, I'm right with you there."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy nằm ở ý 1 và ý 3 — cả hai lần người nghe đều nhượng bộ một phần ("I'll give you that", "I'll accept that much happily") rồi bác bỏ đúng phần cốt lõi, nên đáp án chỉ là Man hoặc Woman chứ không phải Both.

question_text: Where does he want to go tomorrow?
options: The park
The cinema
The town hall
explanation:
Tomorrow is my only free day this month, and everyone has suggestions. My sister says the park — but I was there twice last week with the dog, I know every bench by name now. My flatmate is pushing for the cinema, except there's nothing good on until the new releases on Friday. No — tomorrow I want to go to the town hall. They've opened the old tower to visitors for the first time in years, and you can climb right to the clock. The view over the whole town — I've waited months for this!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – The town hall.
• Vì sao đúng: "tomorrow I want to go to the town hall. They've opened the old tower to visitors for the first time in years, and you can climb right to the clock."
• The park sai: chị gái gợi ý nhưng anh đã đi hai lần tuần trước ("I was there twice last week with the dog").
• The cinema sai: bạn cùng nhà rủ nhưng không có phim hay đến tận thứ Sáu.
👉 Mẹo: hỏi nơi muốn đến, bỏ nơi do người khác đề xuất; đáp án nằm sau "No — tomorrow I want to go to".

question_text: Greg is talking about a working day in his life. How does he go to work?
options: By bus
By car
By bike
explanation:
People often ask how I manage my mornings, so here's my working day. I used to drive, but since the office moved to the centre, the car just sits in traffic for an hour, so that's finished. My wife keeps saying I should cycle — good exercise, she says — but with our winters, I'd arrive soaked three days out of five. So now I go to work by bus. Twenty minutes, a warm seat, and I read my book the whole way. Best decision I've made in years.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – By bus.
• Vì sao đúng: "So now I go to work by bus. Twenty minutes, a warm seat, and I read my book the whole way".
• By car sai: đã bỏ vì văn phòng chuyển vào trung tâm, xe kẹt cả tiếng — "I used to drive, but since the office moved to the centre, the car just sits in traffic for an hour, so that's finished".
• By bike sai: chỉ là gợi ý của vợ, bị loại vì mùa đông — "My wife keeps saying I should cycle... but with our winters, I'd arrive soaked three days out of five".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi phương tiện đi lại, bám cụm "So now I...". Phương tiện gắn với "I used to" (quá khứ) hay "my wife says I should" (ý người khác) đều là nhiễu.

question_text: Future generations may struggle to keep up with information technology development.
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
M: They've rolled out three new systems at our office since January. I can barely keep track of them.
W: It's the same everywhere, I think. Nobody's given any time to learn anything properly.
M: To be honest, it makes me wonder how our grandchildren will manage. The pace is so fierce now that I'd say the generation after us will really struggle to stay on top of it all.
W: Do you think so? I'm not so sure. Children absorb this sort of thing in an afternoon — my niece set up my phone faster than I could open the manual. If anything they'll find it easier than we do.
M: They handle the gadgets, certainly. Understanding the systems underneath is quite another matter.
W: Well, we'll see. What does worry me is employment. I'm fairly convinced all this clever software is going to leave an enormous number of people without a job.
M: Hmm, I don't see it that way at all. I'll accept that particular trades disappear, of course — that's always happened. But the overall number of jobs? No, that doesn't fall. Roles shift, and new ones turn up.
W: Tell that to the staff at the sorting warehouse down the road.
M: Half of them are driving the vans now, from what I hear.
W: Possibly. But here's the thing — I still believe machines will end up as helpers rather than substitutes. A tool sitting on the desk beside you, not somebody in your chair.
M: No, I genuinely can't agree with that. In a great many skilled jobs they won't be assisting anyone at all; they'll be doing the entire task themselves while we glance at the odd result.
W: That's a rather bleak picture.
M: Realistic, I'd call it. Mind you, the thing that actually keeps me awake is privacy. We badly need much tougher rules about what firms are allowed to do with our personal details.
W: Oh, absolutely, I'm with you completely on that one. You tick a single box and your information is sold on to forty companies you've never heard of.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Thế hệ sau khó theo kịp công nghệ = Man · Công nghệ cao khiến nhiều người mất việc = Woman · Máy móc chỉ hỗ trợ chứ không thay thế con người = Woman · Cần biện pháp mạnh hơn để bảo vệ dữ liệu cá nhân = Both

1. Future generations may struggle to keep up with information technology development. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "the generation after us will really struggle to stay on top of it all." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "Do you think so? I'm not so sure. Children absorb this sort of thing in an afternoon... If anything they'll find it easier than we do."

2. Advanced technology could put many workers out of a job. → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "I'm fairly convinced all this clever software is going to leave an enormous number of people without a job." Người đàn ông phản đối: "Hmm, I don't see it that way at all. I'll accept that particular trades disappear, of course... But the overall number of jobs? No, that doesn't fall."

3. Machines will only support people rather than replace them at work. → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "I still believe machines will end up as helpers rather than substitutes. A tool sitting on the desk beside you, not somebody in your chair." Người đàn ông phản đối: "No, I genuinely can't agree with that... they'll be doing the entire task themselves while we glance at the odd result."

4. Stronger measures are needed to keep personal data private. → Both: người đàn ông nêu "We badly need much tougher rules about what firms are allowed to do with our personal details", người phụ nữ đồng ý: "Oh, absolutely, I'm with you completely on that one."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy chính ở ý 2 — người đàn ông nói "I'll accept that particular trades disappear, of course" nghe rất giống đồng ý, nhưng ngay sau đó ông phủ nhận kết luận (tổng số việc làm không giảm), nên đáp án là Woman chứ không phải Both.

question_text: What is the speaker's advice?
options: Be well informed of the places you are going to visit.
Always carry extra water and food supplies.
Avoid cycling on rough terrain.
explanation:
Last year I cycled from Vietnam to Portugal, and since then everyone asks me for advice about long cycling trips. Most people expect me to talk about equipment. They assume the golden rule is to always carry extra water and food supplies, enough for several days. Others tell me the secret must be planning a route that avoids rough terrain completely. Honestly, neither is my main advice. You can buy water in almost every village on Earth, and some of my best days were on terrible roads. My real advice is this: be well informed about the places you are going to visit. Before I set off, I spent two months reading about every region on my route — where the borders close early, which areas flood in spring, where to find a mechanic. That knowledge saved me more times than any spare tyre ever did.
And if I zoom out to the bigger lesson of the whole journey, it is about people. Some cyclists plan trips around the weather, only visiting places in the perfect season. Others tell you to just cycle at your own pace and not worry about the destination. Fine — but both miss what actually makes a trip unforgettable: knowing the people and cultures of the different countries you cross. Learn twenty words of each language. Accept the tea you are offered. Ask the old man at the petrol station about his village. The kilometres disappear from your memory within a year; the people never do.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Be well informed of the places you are going to visit. Bẫy: "extra water and food" và "avoid rough terrain" đều bị gạt ("neither is my main advice").
2. Đáp án: Knowing the people and cultures in the different countries. Bẫy: "good weather conditions" và "cycle at your own pace" được nhắc rồi bị loại ("both miss what actually makes a trip unforgettable").

question_text: What does he advise young people to do to save money?
options: Use public transportation
Buy second-hand items
Cook for yourself
explanation:
Young listeners keep writing to ask how to save money, so here's my honest advice after thirty years of budgets. Everyone tells you to use public transport, and sure, it helps — but a bus ticket here and there is small change. Buying second-hand is fine too, though a cheap broken chair is no bargain, believe me. The real saver, the one that changes everything, is this: cook for yourself. Eating out three times a week quietly eats half a salary. Learn five simple dishes, and watch your bank account grow.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Cook for yourself.
• Vì sao đúng: "The real saver, the one that changes everything, is this: cook for yourself." — ăn ngoài 3 lần/tuần ngốn nửa tháng lương.
• Use public transportation sai: có giúp nhưng chỉ là tiền lẻ ("a bus ticket here and there is small change").
• Buy second-hand items sai: cũng ổn nhưng đồ rẻ mà hỏng thì không hời ("a cheap broken chair is no bargain").
👉 Mẹo: dạng lời khuyên, đáp án là ý được nâng lên bằng so sánh nhất "The real saver", "the one that changes everything".

question_text: Four people are talking about art. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: I moved to this city knowing exactly one person, so I signed up for the Thursday sketching circle out of pure loneliness. Best decision of the year. Twelve strangers drawing the same bowl of fruit, laughing at the results, then staying for coffee long after the easels are packed. Two of them are now my closest friends here. I came for the pencils, honestly — I stayed for the people around the table.
Speaker B: Rainy Sundays in our house mean one thing: the paint boxes come out and my daughters take over the kitchen. We do handprint chickens, cardboard castles, glitter everywhere including the butter. The results are objectively terrible and we frame them anyway. My phone stays in another room for those two hours — just three of us, aprons on, making a happy mess. Their grandmother receives every masterpiece by post.
Speaker C: My sketchbook pays my bills — I design patterns for a textile company, so drawing is what I do from nine to six with a lunch break. Deadlines, client corrections, colour charts: the romance wears thin some weeks, and I understand now why my art teacher warned me. Still, when a stranger walks past wearing a scarf born in my sketchbook, the office desk feels worth it. Few people get paid for their doodles.
Speaker D: My easel faces the window in the spare room, and what happens there is strictly between me and the canvas. I paint when the flat is empty, show nobody, and stack the finished work behind the wardrobe. My husband stopped asking to see them years ago. It is not shyness exactly — it is that the hour is mine, the mistakes are mine, and an audience would change everything. Some pleasures work best unwitnessed.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = social activity (PARAPHRASE: "signed up out of loneliness... stayed for the people"). B = with children (PARAPHRASE: "my daughters take over the kitchen... three of us"). C = part of their job (PARAPHRASE: "sketchbook pays my bills... nine to six"). D = alone (PARAPHRASE: "strictly between me and the canvas... unwitnessed"). Nhiễu: competitions, online classes. (Variant khác lời Đề 04.)

question_text: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: I have made my peace with an unpopular truth: physical activity and I were never meant to be together. The bicycle my wife bought me rusts elegantly in the garage, the yoga mat became the cat's bed, and my single visit to her aerobics class is a story her friends still request at parties. I have stopped apologising. My heart belongs to slow breakfasts and crossword puzzles, and it is very happy there.
Speaker B: Sport entered my life through the office door, oddly enough. Our director introduced walking meetings and lunchtime badminton, and within a month I noticed the difference at my desk: the afternoon fog lifted, my proposals came out cleaner, and I stopped rereading the same paragraph four times. Now I guard my lunchtime game like an appointment with a client. Whatever it costs in sweat, it repays in finished work.
Speaker C: Every trainer I have ever had says the same thing: it gets easier. It does not. Twenty minutes into any class, my lungs demand negotiations, my legs vote to go home, and the mirror shows a tomato in sportswear. I complete every session — pride insists — but I complete it the way one completes a tax return: slowly, painfully, and with relief that it is over for another week.
Speaker D: The trick nobody told me for years: bring your people. My cousin and I turned our runs into gossip sessions, my old classmates and I have a Sunday football ritual that ends in a noisy café, and even the neighbours join our badminton evenings now. Surrounded by friendly faces, two hours of sport disappear like ten minutes. Alone, I would not last one lap of the park — together, we forget to stop.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = hate exercising (PARAPHRASE: "never meant to be together... stopped apologising"). B = help improve work performance (PARAPHRASE: "afternoon fog lifted... repays in finished work"). C = find exercise tiring (PARAPHRASE: "lungs demand negotiations... tomato in sportswear"). D = has fun when exercising with friends (keyword "with friendly faces... together"). Nhiễu: lose weight, alone. (Variant khác lời 02/11/14.)

infoItems.text: has fun when exercising with friends

question_text: The man is talking about his key. Where did he find the key?
options: In his car
In the front door
In the bedroom
explanation:
The great key mystery of this morning — you'll enjoy this! Picture me, eight am, late for work, turning the flat upside down. First suspicion: the car, obviously — I checked every seat, under the mats, the glove box. Nothing. Then the bedroom, because keys love hiding in yesterday's trousers — I emptied every pocket in the wardrobe. Also nothing! And then, walking out defeated... there it was. The key was in the front door. OUTSIDE. It had spent the entire night in the lock, waving at the neighbours. New rule: pocket check before bed!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – In the front door (cắm ở ổ khóa cửa trước).
• Vì sao đúng: anh kể "there it was. The key was in the front door. OUTSIDE. It had spent the entire night in the lock".
• In his car sai: đã tìm nhưng không có "First suspicion: the car... I checked every seat, under the mats, the glove box. Nothing".
• In the bedroom sai: cũng tìm hụt "I emptied every pocket in the wardrobe. Also nothing!".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi TÌM THẤY Ở ĐÂU, các nơi được tìm trước đều kết thúc bằng "Nothing", "no luck". Đáp án nằm sau cụm bất ngờ "And then... there it was".

question_text: Where does she go shopping?
options: at a new shopping mall
at a department store
at a local market
explanation:
Saturday means shopping, and everyone always asks where I go. The old department store in the centre? I stopped going years ago — same clothes on the same racks since forever. The local market is charming for vegetables, but you can't buy shoes between the tomatoes, can you? No — I do my shopping at the new shopping mall by the motorway. It has everything under one roof, the parking is free, and there's a lovely café on the top floor for when my feet give up!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – At a new shopping mall.
• Vì sao đúng: "I do my shopping at the new shopping mall by the motorway. It has everything under one roof, the parking is free".
• At a department store sai: cô bỏ từ nhiều năm vì hàng không đổi mới ("same clothes on the same racks since forever").
• At a local market sai: chỉ hợp mua rau, không mua được giày ("you can't buy shoes between the tomatoes, can you?").
