question_text: Why is identifying the correct market so important for a company?
options: It helps the company focus its resources and avoid wasting time on low-demand areas.
It guarantees that the business will operate without any rival firms.
It provides a justification for lowering product standards to maximize profit.
explanation:
Let us open today's strategy seminar with the question I ask every new client: who exactly is your market? Founders often resist this question, and usually for one of two mistaken reasons. Some believe that choosing a narrow market means their business will operate without rival firms — a safe little island. There is no such island; if a market makes money, competitors will arrive by the next boat. Others privately think that dominating a small market justifies lowering product standards to maximise profit. Try it, and watch your reviews destroy you within months. The real reason market identification matters is discipline: it helps the company focus its resources and stop wasting time on low-demand areas. Small firms do not fail from lack of ideas; they fail from spreading thin. Know your market, and every hour and every dollar starts pulling in the same direction.
Our second concept is profitability, and I want to correct how people read it. When a company finally turns a profit, some managers celebrate as if market research were now unnecessary — as if the customers had been permanently understood. Others relax about their competitors, assuming success means safety. Both reactions are dangerous. What profitability actually signifies is this: the company can cover its costs, and its position in the market is strengthening. That is all — and that is everything. Profit buys you time, options and credibility. But the moment you treat it as permission to stop paying attention, it begins to disappear.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 17 bài 1.)
1. Đáp án: It helps the company focus its resources and avoid wasting time on low-demand areas. Bẫy: "without any rival firms" ("no such island") và "lowering product standards" đều bị bác.
2. Đáp án: It proves the company can cover costs and strengthen its position. Bẫy: "no further need for market research" và "disregard competitors" là hai phản ứng "dangerous".

question_text: What will this musician do in the near future?
options: He will probably retire from singing
He plans to release a new album
He wants to collaborate with younger artists
explanation:
Hello and welcome back to our celebrity news hour. The question on every fan's lips this month: what will the great man of song do next? The internet has its theories. Young stars have lined up to say how much they dream of collaborating with him, and the fan forums are certain a new album is being recorded in secret. I hate to spoil the party, but his interview with us this morning settled it. There is no album, he told me, and no collaborations either — his studio days are finished. After his farewell concert next month, he will almost certainly retire from singing altogether. His voice, he admits, has grown weaker with the years, and he would rather leave the stage while the applause is still real than let it fade politely away.
And when he looks back across forty years, what does he see? I expected easy answers and got honest ones. Does he regret choosing music? Never — he called it the only life he could have lived. Did he peak too early, as one critic famously wrote? He found that idea funny; his own favourite work came late, not early. But one thought does follow him, he said, on quiet evenings: he could have been more successful. The world tour he cancelled out of fear, the songs he left unrecorded, the years lost to fighting with his record label. Even a legend, it turns out, keeps a private list of the doors he never opened.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 16 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: He will probably retire from singing. Bẫy: "new album" và "collaborate with younger artists" là theory của fan bị chính ca sĩ bác.
2. Đáp án: He could have been more successful. Bẫy: "regrets choosing profession" ("Never") và "peaked too early" ("found that idea funny") đều bị phủ định.

question_text: Why didn't he go to college immediately after finishing school?
options: He was not ready to start higher education.
He could not afford the tuition fees.
His grades were not good enough.
explanation:
People still ask why I did not go to college immediately after finishing school, so let me tell the story properly. My grades were perfectly fine — good enough for every course I applied to later. And although tuition worried my parents at first, money was never the deciding factor; we would have managed. The truth is simpler and harder to admit at eighteen: I was not ready for higher education. Years of examinations had emptied me. I could not name what I wanted to study, and starting a degree without knowing why felt like boarding a train without reading its destination. So I made the decision that shocked my teachers: I bought a backpack instead of textbooks.
For two years I travelled, and I want to be precise about my reasons, because people guess them wrong. I was not running away from studying — I read constantly on the road, more than I ever had at school. And it was never simply about seeing new places; the sightseeing grew ordinary within months. I travelled because I wanted to become more independent. I took temporary jobs in three countries, arranged my own rooms, stretched a thin budget through expensive cities, and solved every emergency with nobody to call. When I finally walked into university at twenty, I arrived knowing how to run a life — which made learning how to run a career remarkably easy.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 20 bài 2 — ngôi thứ nhất, chi tiết khác.)
1. Đáp án: He was not ready to start higher education. Bẫy: "tuition fees" ("never the deciding factor") và "grades" ("perfectly fine").
2. Đáp án: To become more independent. Bẫy: "avoid studying" ("read constantly") và "simply to travel" ("grew ordinary within months").

question_text: According to the reviewer, what is one benefit of school sports?
options: They help promote students' overall health.
They are designed to limit physical exertion.
They primarily focus on academic competition.
explanation:
As an education reviewer, I visit dozens of schools every year, and the place I always ask to see first is not the library — it is the sports field. Let me explain why, and clear up two misreadings while I am at it. School sports are sometimes accused of being designed to limit physical exertion, keeping children safe by keeping them slow. Nonsense; a good programme works young bodies properly and progressively. Others suspect sport in schools mainly feeds academic competition, another arena for rankings. Also wrong — the field is where rankings matter least. The benefit my reviews document year after year is simpler: school sports promote students' overall health. Regular training builds stronger hearts and better sleep, and the healthiest schools in my files are, without exception, the sportiest ones.
Yet health is only half the story, and the other half is routinely underrated. Worried parents sometimes fear sport encourages extreme specialisation — the child who becomes only a swimmer, only a striker. Coaches occasionally worry it teaches individual glory over team success. In well-run schools I find the opposite of both. What sport gives students, above everything, is balance. It is the counterweight to hours of sitting, memorising and testing; the place where a stressed mind empties and refills. Take sport out of a school and the timetable still functions — but the children tilt, like a ship that has lost its ballast. Keep it in, protect it, and everything else in the building works better.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 42 bài 1.)
1. Đáp án: They help promote students' overall health. Bẫy: "limit physical exertion" ("Nonsense") và "academic competition" ("Also wrong").
2. Đáp án: It provides balance. Bẫy: "extreme specialization" và "individual over team" — "I find the opposite of both".

question_text: Why is an 'important customer' valuable to a company?
options: Because they provide steady money, influence others, and help improve services.
Because they are responsible for hiring and training new employees.
Because they guarantee the company's stock prices will never fall.
explanation:
Today's sales seminar is about a phrase you will hear in every boardroom: the important customer. First, let us kill two myths, because new account managers repeat them constantly. Myth one: important customers are somehow involved in company operations, even in hiring and training new employees. They are not — they are clients, not colleagues. Myth two: holding a few big customers guarantees the company's stock prices will never fall. No customer on Earth has that power; markets move for a hundred reasons. So why are these customers genuinely valuable? Three reasons, and you should memorise them. They provide steady money — reliable orders a business can plan its year around. They influence others — one recommendation from a respected client wins more deals than a month of advertising. And they help improve services, because they tell you honestly what is broken while smaller customers simply leave in silence.
Second topic: unpredictability. Modern customer behaviour changes faster than any forecast, and I have watched companies respond in two disastrous ways. Some cut the marketing budget to avoid financial risk — and disappear from the customer's mind within a season. Others standardise every product, ignoring individual preferences, hoping that one offer will suit the whole market. It never does. The response that actually works is continuous attention: monitor your customers' habits, study what the data tells you, and update your services the moment real behaviour shifts. In a market that refuses to stand still, standing still is the only guaranteed way to lose.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 13 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: Because they provide steady money, influence others, and help improve services. Bẫy: "hiring and training" và "stock prices" là hai "myth" bị giết ngay đầu.
2. Đáp án: Businesses should monitor customer habits and update their services when needed. Bẫy: "reduce the marketing budget" và "standardize all products" là hai cách "disastrous".

question_text: What is the importance of advertising?
options: It increases the product price
It can help reach new customers
It can build brand recognition
explanation:
In tonight's business class I want to talk honestly about advertising, because opinions are so divided. Small business owners always tell me the same two worries. First, that advertising will push up their product prices, since the marketing money has to come from somewhere. Second, that advertising is really just about building brand recognition — getting a logo remembered — which feels like a luxury when budgets are tight. I understand both concerns, but they miss the main point. The real importance of advertising is that it can help a business reach new customers. Your existing customers already know you; advertising is the bridge to the thousands of people who have never walked past your shop. A modest, well-aimed campaign brings in buyers you could never have met otherwise, and that — not fame, not recognition — is what pays the bills and grows the company.
Sponsorship of sports tournaments, however, deserves a separate warning. When companies hesitate, they usually give the wrong reasons. Some say sponsorship is simply too expensive, though packages now exist at every price level. Others fear it creates unfair competition, giving big brands an advantage smaller firms cannot match. Neither of those is the real danger. The true risk is that sponsorship can generate negative publicity for the sport itself. One doping scandal, one match-fixing story, one ugly incident in the stands — and the sponsor's name is printed right next to the bad news in every report. Before you put your logo on a tournament, ask yourself one question: whose mistakes am I prepared to share?

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 04 bài 1 — cùng đáp án, nhiễu khác: expensive / unfair competition.)
1. Đáp án: It can help reach new customers. Bẫy: "increases the product price" và "build brand recognition" là hai lo ngại bị gạt ("they miss the main point").
2. Đáp án: They can generate negative publicity for the sport. Bẫy: "too expensive" và "unfair competition" đều bị bác ("Neither of those is the real danger").

question_text: What attracts readers to this novel?
options: It is different from his earlier works
It is romantic and soft
It is less famous than his earlier works
explanation:
Welcome to tonight's book programme. Our subject: Shadow in the Night, the novel the whole country seems to be carrying around. Now, why are readers so drawn to it? Remember, James Parker built his name on soft, romantic stories, and when this book was announced, industry voices predicted disaster — some even said it would end up less famous than his earlier works, a forgotten experiment. Instead, the bookshops cannot keep it on the shelves, and the reason is exactly what the doubters feared: it is completely different from everything he has written before. Gone are the gentle love stories; in their place, a dark mystery that tightens page by page. Readers who thought they knew Parker are discovering a new writer inside the old one, and that surprise is precisely what attracts them.
So what happens next — and what do I think he should do? His new fans beg him to continue in this thrilling genre. His loyal old readers write letters asking him to go back to romance, where he made his name. My opinion sides with neither camp. Before Parker writes a single page of his next book, he should sit down with the critics' reviews and truly listen. They have mapped his weaknesses honestly — the rushed middle chapters, the thin secondary characters — and they have named his new strengths just as clearly. A writer at a crossroads does not need cheering fans. He needs honest maps, and the critics have drawn them.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 01 bài 1, câu hỏi khác: "What attracts readers" / "opinion about this novel".)
1. Đáp án: It is different from his earlier works. Bẫy: "romantic and soft" là phong cách CŨ, "less famous" là dự đoán bị chứng minh sai.
2. Đáp án: He should listen to critics before writing his next work. Bẫy: "continue this genre" (fan mới) và "go back to original genre" (độc giả cũ) — "My opinion sides with neither camp".

question_text: Why do residents oppose this plan?
options: It will remove several public parks in the area
It makes public transportation more expensive for residents
It doesn't do enough to promote alternatives to driving
explanation:
This is City Radio's planning special, and tonight we examine why the Regional Development Plan is in trouble. Let me sort the rumours from the facts, because both are flying. Rumour one: the plan removes several public parks. False — I have checked the maps myself, and every park stays exactly where it is. Rumour two: it makes public transportation more expensive. Also false; fares are not even mentioned in the document. The real opposition, the reason hundreds of residents packed last week's meeting, is that the plan does not do enough to promote alternatives to driving. It funds new roads generously while offering almost nothing for buses, bicycles or pedestrians. People who want to leave the car at home read this plan and see a city telling them not to bother. That is the complaint — and it is written on every protest sign outside the town hall.
The city council, meanwhile, wrestles with a different problem. Not opposition from local businesses; the chamber of commerce actually endorsed the plan last month. Not the budget either, which remains on target. Their difficulty is land use. The plan builds outward into farmland while entire blocks of the city centre sit empty — disused factories, abandoned car parks, buildings waiting for demolition. Several councillors keep asking the same question in every session: why are we buying new land when we are not using the land we already own? Until the planners answer it, the council's votes are not there, and the plan stays stuck.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant thứ 3 của Regional plan — khác lời Đề 06 và Đề 16.)
1. Đáp án: It doesn't do enough to promote alternatives to driving. Bẫy: "remove parks" và "more expensive" là rumour bị bác bằng kiểm chứng.
2. Đáp án: The plan is not making efficient use of existing land. Bẫy: "opposition from businesses" ("endorsed") và "exceeded budget" ("on target") đều bị phủ định.

question_text: Why do many readers find the book interesting?
options: It uses simple language to describe complex ideas.
It relies heavily on technical vocabulary.
It avoids explaining abstract concepts.
explanation:
My book club chose the new biography of the famous physicist this month, and the discussion was the liveliest we have had all year. Why do readers find it so interesting? Not for the reasons you might fear. The book does not rely on technical vocabulary — I counted perhaps five specialist terms in four hundred pages, each explained on arrival. Nor does it avoid the abstract concepts, the truly strange corners of physics; it walks straight into them, holding the reader's hand. The answer is the author's great gift: using simple language to describe complex ideas. Time slowing near the speed of light is explained through two brothers and a railway journey. Particle behaviour becomes a story about letters posted into two boxes at once. Our least scientific member finished the book first and talked about it longest.
As for why it has become quite so popular — topping the charts for eleven weeks — the answer surprised me. It is not despite but because of its similarity to the author's previous book about the same scientist. That earlier biography built an audience of devoted readers, and this new volume gives them exactly the pleasure they remember: the same warm voice, the same rhythm of story and science. Publishers call this brand loyalty; readers just call it comfort. Critics grumble that it is too familiar — nobody, however, calls it too difficult, and nobody calls it too long. The queue in the bookshop settles that argument.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant vật lý #3 — câu 2 hỏi lý do NỔI TIẾNG, đáp án "similar to the previous book".)
1. Đáp án: It uses simple language to describe complex ideas. Bẫy: "technical vocabulary" và "avoids abstract concepts" đều bị phủ định.
2. Đáp án: It is similar to the previous book about the scientist — sự quen thuộc giữ chân độc giả cũ. Bẫy: "too difficult" và "too long" — "nobody calls it...".

question_text: Why hasn't he gone to college?
options: He wasn't ready to start higher education
He couldn't afford the tuition fees.
He didn't get good enough grades
explanation:
People keep asking why I am not at university like the rest of my class, so let me explain properly. It is not about money — my parents had saved for years, and the tuition fees were never a problem. And it is not about my grades either; my results were actually good enough for every course I looked at. The honest reason is simpler: I just was not ready to start higher education. After thirteen years of school, my head was full and my motivation was empty. I knew that if I walked straight into a lecture hall that September, I would waste both the money and the opportunity. So I made a choice that surprised everyone: I stopped.
For the next two years I travelled through Asia and Europe, and I want to be clear about why. It was not simply for the travelling itself — the buses and the beaches were never the point. And I certainly was not trying to avoid studying; I actually read more books on the road than I ever did at school. I travelled because I wanted to become more independent. I wanted to cook my own food, fix my own problems, manage my own money in places where nobody knew me. Two years later, I can say it worked. I am starting university this autumn, and I am arriving as someone who can stand on his own feet — which, I think, is worth more than arriving two years earlier.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: He wasn't ready to start higher education. Bẫy: "tuition fees" bị phủ định ("never a problem"), "grades" bị phủ định ("good enough for every course").
2. Đáp án: To be more independent. Bẫy: "to travelling" bị gạt ("the buses and the beaches were never the point"), "to avoid studying" bị phủ định ("read more books on the road").

question_text: Why did the new podcast fail?
options: The content was too long.
The creators did not promote their show effectively.
It faced too much competition.
explanation:
Our media studies class today examines a small case study: the podcast that launched with a party last spring and shut down before the year ended. What went wrong? The team themselves first blamed the length of their episodes — too long, they thought, for busy listeners. But their own analytics told a different story: the people who pressed play stayed to the end, so the content itself was holding attention. Outside observers pointed at the crowded market and said the show simply had too many rivals. Yet in the very same months, smaller podcasts in busier categories were growing steadily, so competition alone explains nothing. The autopsy points to one clear cause: the creators did not promote the show effectively. No social media presence, no guest appearances, no outreach to communities who might have loved it. A show nobody hears about is a show nobody hears.
Before you conclude that podcasting itself is a bad bet, let me give you my view of the medium. Critics dismiss it as a waste of time, and even some fans treat it as nothing deeper than entertainment for the daily commute. I think both sell it short. Done well, a podcast is one of the best community-building tools ever invented. Listeners return every week, write in with their stories, meet each other in comment sections and live events. A microphone and honest conversation can gather thousands of strangers around a shared interest — and that, not download numbers, is the real measure of the medium.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 18 bài 2. Phương án nhiễu đã thay "too many listeners" bằng "It faced too much competition".)
1. Đáp án: The creators did not promote their show effectively. Bẫy: "content too long" bị bác bằng analytics, "competition" bị bác bằng ví dụ đối chứng.
2. Đáp án: It is a great way to build a community. Bẫy: "waste of time" và "only entertainment" — "both sell it short".

question_text: What does the speaker say is a key benefit of making plans?
options: They make life more predictable.
They help you make decisions.
They reduce the need for communication.
explanation:
People often misunderstand planning, so tonight let me clear a few things up. When I ask people what a plan gives you, I hear the same answers. Some say plans make life more predictable — you always know what happens next. Others joke that a good plan reduces the need for communication, because everyone can just read the document instead of talking. There is a small truth in both, but neither is the real prize. In my experience, the key benefit of making plans is that they help you make decisions. Planning forces you to think about your priorities in advance, so when two options appear on a busy Tuesday, you already know which one serves your goal. Instead of reacting at the last minute, you choose calmly — and you can explain to yourself exactly why. That clarity, not predictability, is what a plan is really for.
Of course, I will not pretend planning is all sunshine. Some critics claim it discourages people from taking risks, but I have found that a well-made plan actually gives you the safety to take bigger ones. Others insist planning only works in professional situations, which anyone who has planned a wedding or a family trip knows is untrue. The genuine difficulty is different: planning requires you to set yourself certain limits. A real plan means saying no — no to extra projects, no to attractive distractions, no to keeping every option open forever. Choosing your limits is uncomfortable. But without limits, what you have is not a plan; it is only a wish.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They help you make decisions. Bẫy: "more predictable" và "reduce the need for communication" được nhắc rồi hạ cấp ("neither is the real prize").
2. Đáp án: It requires you to set yourself certain limits. Bẫy: "discourages taking risks" và "only works in professional situations" đều bị bác.

question_text: How did the writer finish his book?
options: It was completed much faster than his previous work
The plot was very strong
By incorporating feedback from a famous editor
explanation:
The writer's new novel is finally on the shelves, and everyone asks the same question: how did he actually finish it, after all those public struggles? Some rumours claim he completed it much faster than his previous work — untrue; this book took nearly six years, twice as long as any before. Others whisper that a famous editor rescued the manuscript with heavy feedback — also wrong; he famously works alone and rejected every offer of editorial help. By his own account, what carried the book to the final page was the strength of the plot itself. The storyline was so well built, so alive in his head, that it pulled him through every difficult month. When a writer knows exactly where the story must go, he says, the only job left is to keep walking toward it. A strong plot, in other words, finished the book as much as the author did.
The readers, of course, have delivered their verdict too, and it is mixed. Interestingly, nobody complains about the physical quality of the hardback edition — the binding and paper have been widely praised. Nor is the vocabulary too academic; the language is plain and welcoming. What some readers do criticize is more uncomfortable: the novel is very similar to the author's other books. The lonely hero, the seaside town, the buried family secret — loyal fans recognise every ingredient. Supporters call it a signature. Critics call it a formula. The truth, as usual, probably depends on how many of his books you have already read.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: The plot was very strong — chính cốt truyện chắc tay đã kéo nhà văn hoàn thành sách. Bẫy: "faster than previous work" ("untrue") và "feedback from a famous editor" ("also wrong") đều bị phủ định.
2. Đáp án: It is very similar to the author's other books. Bẫy: "hardback quality" ("widely praised") và "academic vocabulary" ("plain and welcoming") đều bị loại.

question_text: What does the reviewer say about the characters in the novel?
options: They are too difficult for readers to understand.
They feel realistic and emotionally engaging.
They are less important than the storyline.
explanation:
Good evening, book lovers — tonight, the novel everyone is talking about. Let me start with the characters, because opinions online are noisy. Some reviewers call them too difficult to understand; I disagree — spend ten pages with them and they open up. Others dismiss them as less important than the storyline. Wrong again, in my view. For me, the characters are the beating heart of this book: they feel realistic and emotionally engaging, people you recognise from your own kitchen table, with flaws that make you wince and hope.

And what about the novel's impact? Some academics predict it will mainly appeal to their own seminar rooms — too clever for the general public, they say. Others warn it may divide readers' opinions, with its unusual ending. I see something simpler and bigger: this book will establish the author's popularity. Mark my words — the bookshop queues, the reading clubs, the translations already being negotiated. Within a year, hers will be a household name, and this novel will be the reason.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They feel realistic and emotionally engaging — "too difficult" và "less important than the storyline" đều được nhắc rồi bác bỏ ("I disagree", "Wrong again").
2. Đáp án: It will establish the author's popularity. Bẫy: "appeal to academic audiences" là dự đoán của giới học thuật bị gạt, "divide readers' opinions" chỉ là cảnh báo của người khác; người review chốt "this book will establish the author's popularity".

question_text: How often do you make changes to your room?
explanation: I think there are two main reasons. Firstly, photographs and paintings carry memories and meaning. A photo of a holiday or of family members reminds people of happy moments every time they walk past it, so the house feels more personal and less like an empty space. Secondly, pictures are one of the cheapest and easiest ways to make a room look attractive. A large blank wall can look cold, but adding a few frames immediately gives the room colour and character. In addition, the pictures people choose often say something about their taste and interests, so visitors can learn about them just by looking around.

extra_data.imageDesc: Đôi vợ chồng treo bộ khung ảnh lên tường phòng khách
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Not very often, to be honest. I make small changes about once or twice a year, and a big change only every few years. For example, at the beginning of this year I painted my walls soft grey, bought a new bookshelf and put some family photos on the wall next to the door. It took me a whole weekend, so I will not do it again soon. Between those big changes, I only move the desk or buy a new lamp when I feel bored with the room. I think small changes like that are enough to make a room feel fresh again.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Rarely, and usually only when the room starts to annoy me. A proper change happens every two or three years. The last one was in January, when I painted the walls soft grey over one weekend and swapped the ceiling light for a warmer one, which made a bigger difference than the paint did. In between, I limit myself to small things: moving the desk to the window, or rearranging the books by height, which drives my sister mad every time she visits. I would like to redecorate more often, but the cost and the mess put me off.

question_text: What is the expert's opinion about sports competitions?
options: Identify and recruit professional athletes for national teams.
Prepare students for a competitive work environment
Attract significant funding from international sponsors.
explanation:
As a specialist in youth development, I am often asked to defend sports competitions in schools, and my defence may surprise you. Some administrators value competitions mainly as a way to identify and recruit professional athletes for national teams. Others love them because trophies attract significant funding from international sponsors. Both benefits exist, but both miss what competitions actually teach. In my expert opinion, sports competitions prepare students for a competitive work environment. On the field, a young person learns to perform under pressure, to lose on Saturday and return on Monday, to win without humiliating the loser. Those are precisely the skills the adult workplace demands and no textbook can supply. The scoreboard is a classroom — arguably the most honest one a school owns.
That said, my advice for schools comes with a warning about extremes. One headteacher I know wants to enforce athletic participation as a strict graduation requirement — forcing unwilling teenagers onto the track achieves nothing but resentment. Another school went the opposite way, restricting physical activities to protect what they called academic excellence. Equally mistaken. What sport should give students is balance in their lives. After six hours of screens, formulas and silent concentration, the body needs to run and the mind needs to empty. Schools that protect that daily balance — without turning sport into either a punishment or a forbidden luxury — consistently produce their calmest and, in the end, highest-achieving students.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Prepare students for a competitive work environment. Bẫy: "recruit professional athletes" và "funding from sponsors" — "both miss what competitions actually teach".
2. Đáp án: Provides them with a balance in their lives. Bẫy: "strict graduation requirement" và "restrict physical activities" là hai thái cực bị bác.

question_text: What does the announcer say about the new novel?
options: It is different from his earlier works
It is romantic and soft
It is less famous than his earlier works
explanation:
Good evening, and welcome to the books segment. Tonight: James Parker's Shadow in the Night, the novel that has surprised the whole publishing world. Longtime readers know Parker as the king of soft, romantic stories — and before this release, more than one magazine predicted the new book would end up less famous than his earlier works, an experiment his fans would politely ignore. The announcer of every bestseller list can now tell you how wrong that was. The novel's defining quality is that it is completely different from everything Parker has written before. The romance is gone; in its place, a dark thriller of secrets, false identities and midnight chases. Critics who once called him predictable are writing apologies, and the first print run sold out in nine days.
The question dividing his readership now is what Parker owes them next. The newcomers, who met him through this thriller, demand he continue in the genre. The faithful, who followed him for twenty years of love stories, want him back in his original territory. In my view — and I have reviewed every book he has published — he should ignore both crowds and listen carefully to the critics before starting his next manuscript. The professional reviews of this novel are unusually detailed: they praise his new command of tension, and they document exactly where the middle chapters sag. That is not noise; that is a map. Writers grow by studying honest maps, not by following the loudest cheers.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 01 bài 1 và Đề 37 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: It is different from his earlier works. Bẫy: "romantic and soft" (phong cách cũ) và "less famous" (dự đoán sai).
2. Đáp án: He should listen to critics before writing his next work. Bẫy: "continue this genre" và "go back to original genre" là đòi hỏi của hai nhóm độc giả bị gạt.

question_text: What happened when the TV series first aired?
options: The plot was based on a globally famous novel
It failed to engage the audience from the start
It utilized a massive celebrity marketing budget
explanation:
Today I want to talk about a drama series whose road to success was anything but smooth. Cast your mind back to its premiere. Some viewers assumed the plot came from a globally famous novel and expected instant success; in fact, the story was entirely original. Others imagined a massive celebrity marketing budget carrying it to popularity; the real launch budget was modest. The truth is harsher: when the series first aired, it failed to engage the audience from the start. The opening episodes were confusing, the timeline jumped without warning, and thousands of viewers switched off before episode three. Only a determined rewrite in the second half of the season — clearer storytelling, sharper focus on two central characters — slowly won the audience back, and by the finale the series had become the year's unlikeliest hit.
Success, however, brought its own disease, and here is my warning as a reviewer. The problem is not diversity in the casting, which the producers handled admirably. Nor is production quality inconsistent — every episode looks equally polished. The problem is overexposure. The moment the ratings soared, the series was everywhere: advertisements on every platform, interviews on every channel, merchandise in every shop. Audiences tire of what they cannot escape, and the affection the show fought so hard to earn is being spent on saturation. Television history is clear on this point: series are damaged by overexposure, and the wisest producers know when to let a hit breathe.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It failed to engage the audience from the start. Bẫy: "famous novel" và "celebrity marketing budget" đều bị phủ định.
2. Đáp án: Series are damaged by overexposure. Bẫy: "diversity in casting" ("handled admirably") và "inconsistent quality" ("equally polished") đều bị loại.

question_text: Why do modern buildings stand out?
options: They prioritize traditional materials over steel
They are primarily built in rural environments
They associate with modern cityscapes
explanation:
Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the final lecture of our architecture course. Let us end with a question students love: why do modern buildings stand out? In your essays, some of you argued that architects today prioritise traditional materials — brick, timber, stone — over steel and glass. Walk through any financial district and you will see how wrong that is. Others wrote that the most striking modern buildings are primarily built in rural environments. Also incorrect — the countryside is where you find the least contemporary architecture, not the most. The true answer is that modern buildings stand out through their association with modern cityscapes. Their glass walls, clean lines and minimal decoration are designed to mirror the city around them. A modern tower is recognised the way a word is recognised in a sentence — not alone, but as part of the language of the whole skyline.
Now for my honest closing thought, which may surprise you after a term of studying these structures. The industry press insists that today's buildings represent the peak of architectural innovation, and every city council brochure promises new projects that maximise public green spaces. Believe neither claim too quickly. Look carefully at what is actually being built, and many new buildings display a plain lack of ambition. Developers reward speed and cheapness, so identical glass boxes rise in every city on Earth. My challenge to you, the next generation of architects, is simple: be the ones who make our cities surprising again.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 12 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: They associate with modern cityscapes. Bẫy: "traditional materials" và "rural environments" đều bị bác trong bài giảng.
2. Đáp án: They often display a lack of ambition. Bẫy: "peak of innovation" và "green spaces" là tuyên bố bị nghi ngờ ("Believe neither claim too quickly").

question_text: According to the passage, how does work benefit an individual beyond just earning money?
options: It helps develop skills, contribute to society, and provide a sense of purpose.
It primarily serves as a way to avoid social interactions
It focuses on maximizing leisure time during the weekends
explanation:
People often ask me, as a career counsellor, why work matters beyond the salary — and the answer shapes every session I run. Some cynics say a job's main value is giving people a way to avoid social interactions, hiding behind a desk all day. Others treat work as merely the price we pay to maximise weekend leisure. Both views sell working life badly short. Beyond the money, work helps a person develop skills, contribute to society, and build a sense of purpose that no payment can replace. Solving real problems sharpens the mind, serving customers or patients ties us into the community, and finishing something difficult gives shape to our days. Ask a retired person what they miss, and they rarely say the salary. They say the purpose.
Alongside work, I always prescribe books, and I am asked why reading deserves equal billing. Not because keeping professional and private interests completely separate is healthy — that wall, in my experience, starves both sides. And not because reading reduces the need for formal education over time; books complement teachers, they do not replace them. The real result of balancing work and books is growth in every area of a person's life. Work develops what you can do; reading expands what you can imagine. One without the other produces either a dreamer with idle hands or a worker with a closed mind. Together, they build the rarest thing of all: a person who is both capable and curious.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It helps develop skills, contribute to society, and provide a sense of purpose. Bẫy: "avoid social interactions" và "maximize leisure time" — "Both views sell working life badly short".
2. Đáp án: Growth in every area of a person's life. Bẫy: "complete separation" và "decrease need for formal education" đều bị bác.

question_text: Why is the book so popular?
options: It uses simple language to describe complex ideas
It was endorsed by a famous celebrity
It contains many colorful illustrations
explanation:
If you visit any bookshop this month, you will see a pyramid of copies of the new biography of the century's greatest physicist. Why has it sold so well? The rumours give the wrong answers. No, a famous celebrity did not endorse it on a talk show — the publicity budget was tiny. And no, it is not filled with colourful illustrations; apart from one photo section, it is plain text. The book's popularity rests on a simple achievement: the author uses simple language to describe complex ideas. Readers who fled physics at school suddenly find themselves understanding relativity over breakfast, because every concept arrives wrapped in an everyday story — a train, a torch, a falling apple. Making difficulty feel easy is the hardest trick in writing, and this author performs it on every page.
Naturally, success invites criticism, and the critics have found their angle. Interestingly, nobody accuses the book of choosing entertainment over facts — the science has been verified by specialists. Nobody calls it too short to matter either; it is a substantial volume. The recurring criticism is that it is remarkably similar to the author's previous book about the same scientist. Same structure, same rhythm, several of the same anecdotes retold in fresher clothes. Loyal readers defend the familiarity as a signature style. Reviewers call it repetition. If you never read the first book, the debate will not trouble you — but if you did, expect a strong feeling that you have walked this road before.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 26 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: It uses simple language to describe complex ideas. Bẫy: "celebrity" và "illustrations" đều bị phủ định.
2. Đáp án: It is similar to the previous book about the scientist. Bẫy: "entertainment rather than facts" và "too short" — "nobody accuses...".

question_text: What should students do when choosing a career?
options: Choose the same career as their friends
Be flexible and open minded
Focus only on the salary offered
explanation:
Welcome, final-year students. Today we talk honestly about life after graduation, starting with the biggest decision: choosing a career. Every year I watch the same two mistakes. A group of friends all apply to the same company, because choosing the same career as your friends feels safer than choosing alone. And other students scan job advertisements looking only at the salary, as if the number were the whole story. Please avoid both paths. Your friends' perfect job may be your nightmare, and a high salary in the wrong field buys you comfortable unhappiness. What you should be is flexible and open-minded. Explore industries you know nothing about, accept that your first job is a starting point rather than a destination, and let your career surprise you. The best professional lives I know were never planned in a straight line.
When you actually apply for jobs, let me correct two rumours going around. No, companies do not prefer handwritten applications — that advice died decades ago, and everything is digital now. And no, it is not true that most jobs no longer require qualifications; your degree still opens the door. But here is what you must truly pay attention to: the job market is becoming more competitive every year. For every position you want, dozens of graduates with similar degrees are applying. The degree gets you considered — it no longer gets you chosen. Skills, experience, a genuine attitude, and something that makes you memorable: build those now, before you need them.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 07 bài 1 — nhiễu câu 2 khác: handwritten / no qualifications.)
1. Đáp án: Be flexible and open minded. Bẫy: "same career as friends" và "focus only on salary" là hai sai lầm bị cảnh báo.
2. Đáp án: They are becoming more competitive. Bẫy: "handwritten applications" và "no longer require qualifications" đều là tin đồn bị bác.

question_text: What is the speaker's advice?
options: Always carry extra water and food supplies.
Avoid cycling on rough terrain.
Be well informed of the places you are going to visit.
explanation:
Before you set off on a long cycling expedition, let me — as someone with three continental crossings behind him — offer the advice I wish I had received. New riders always fixate on the same two things. They want to carry extra water and food for every possible emergency, loading their bikes until the wheels groan. Or they spend weeks redrawing their route to avoid every stretch of rough terrain. I understand the instinct, but neither obsession is my advice. Shops exist everywhere, and rough roads teach you more than smooth ones. What I tell every rider is this: be well informed about the places you are going to visit. Know when the mountain passes close, which regions require permits, where the monsoon arrives early, which towns have a bike mechanic. On the road, information weighs nothing and saves everything.
If you ask for my advice in the broadest sense — the one lesson above all others — it is not about the machine or the map. Some riders chase perfect weather from country to country, and others tell you to simply cycle at your own pace and forget the destination. Fine ideas, but they miss the heart of the journey: get to know the people and cultures of the countries you ride through. Say yes to the invitation for dinner. Learn how to say thank you in every border you cross. Years from now, you will have forgotten the hills that nearly killed you — but not the family that took you in when it rained.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 19 bài 1.)
1. Đáp án: Be well informed of the places you are going to visit. Bẫy: "extra water and food" và "avoid rough terrain" là "obsession" bị gạt.
2. Đáp án: Knowing the people and cultures in the different countries. Bẫy: "good weather" và "own pace" — "Fine ideas, but they miss the heart".

Man: I've been thinking about how future generations might really struggle with all the information technology throws at them. With the sheer volume of data available, it's easy to see how they could feel overwhelmed and unsure of what to trust.
Woman: I get that, but I actually think this technological revolution is beneficial for our economy. It's opened up new job opportunities and streamlined many industries, driving growth in ways we haven't seen before.
Man: I understand your point, but we also need to consider the potential downsides. As automation increases, many traditional jobs could disappear and not everyone will be able to transition to new roles. We have to ensure that the workforce is prepared for these changes. Woman: Still, we should recognize that no matter how advanced they get, computers can't replicate the complexity of the human brain. Our ability to think critically and empathize is irreplaceable, and we need to nurture those qualities even as we embrace new technologies. Man: I see. However, while we're advancing I believe we both see the need for stronger protections around individual privacy. As where more on the internet safeguarding personal information becomes increasingly important.
Woman: Exactly! Protecting privacy is essential in this digital age. We have to ensure that people maintain control over their data balancing innovation with the right to privacy.

Whether it's colleagues at work or friends outside, the essence is the same-feeling seen, supported, and involved, whichever the size or type of group doesn't matter as much as the emotional connection people have within it
Man: That's an interesting point. I'm not so sure I'm the best person to judge that. I've mostly kept my work life and personal life pretty separate. Though these days, a lot of those connections don't even happen face-to-face anymore.
Woman: Totally. Online platforms are redefining what community means. I've seen people build strong support networks without ever meeting in person.
Man: Same here. I joined a language exchange group online, and it's actually one of the most engaging communities I've been part of. Technology really has changed the game.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người phụ nữ nói: "...the way a space is designed can actually change how people relate to each other." Người nam cũng nhận thấy điều đó qua trải nghiệm của mình: "I noticed how different things felt... ended up chatting with neighbors..."
2. Người nam cho rằng kết nối cần thời gian: "it takes a while before you really feel integrated. It's a gradual growth, not something that just clicks."
3. Người phụ nữ nói: "Whether it's colleagues at work or friends outside, the essence is the same—feeling seen, supported, and involved..."
4. Người phụ nữ nhận xét: "Online platforms are redefining what community means." Người nam đồng ý hoàn toàn: "Same here. ... Technology really has changed the game."

question_text: People share similar ideas about beauty
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
Woman: Hi David. You look so serious reading while watching that beauty show. What happened?
Man: You know, I've been thinking a lot about beauty lately. It seems like so many people share similar ideas about it, especially with social media showing the same types of looks and trends everywhere. It's almost like there's a formula for what's considered beautiful.
Woman: That's a good point. However, I believe that ideas about beauty change over time. What we find beautiful today might not be the same in a few years. Just look at how fashion and beauty standards have shifted over the decades! Remember how popular certain hairstyles or clothing styles were?
Man: It's fascinating to see how those perceptions evolve. And I think beauty can be found in unexpected places too. For instance, when I walk through my neighborhood, I notice beauty not only in nature, like the way the sun sets or flowers bloom, but also in everyday moments like a street musician playing a beautiful tune or people sharing a laugh.
Woman: Those little things can be incredibly beautiful. And I think traditional ideas of beauty are going to change even more. People are starting to value authenticity and unique qualities rather than just sticking to old standards.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người nam nhận xét: "It seems like so many people share similar ideas about it..." (Rất nhiều người có những ý tưởng giống nhau về [vẻ đẹp]).
2. Người phụ nữ cho rằng chuẩn mực luôn thay đổi: "I believe that ideas about beauty change over time."
3. Người nam nhận định cái đẹp có mặt ở những nơi bất ngờ: "beauty can be found in unexpected places too." Người phụ nữ đồng ý việc có thể cảm nhận cái đẹp qua những điều giản đơn: "Those little things can be incredibly beautiful."
4. Người phụ nữ khẳng định về thay đổi chuẩn mực truyền thống: "I think traditional ideas of beauty are going to change even more."

question_text: Housing space is more important than farming space.
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
M: Did you see they're turning that old multi-storey car park into growing plots?
W: I did, and I think it's a shocking waste, frankly. In a city this crammed, putting up somewhere for people to live matters far more than finding room for rows of lettuce.
M: I don't see it that way at all. I'll grant you that housing is desperately tight, but you're talking about a rooftop nobody could put flats on anyway. It isn't one or the other.
W: In practice it usually is, though. Somebody always has to choose.
M: Well, I'll be honest with you, I find the whole idea rather lovely. Tomatoes on a warehouse roof, herbs growing over a bus depot — there's something genuinely charming about the whole business.
W: It leaves me completely cold, I'm afraid. To me it looks like a hobby for people with plenty of spare time and very little to worry about.
M: That's a bit harsh. Anyway, charm aside, there's a hard practical case as well. Towns are simply going to need far more food than they can currently lay their hands on, and it has to come from somewhere.
W: I'm not convinced that's the real problem, though. We already produce more than enough — a third of it ends up in the bin. Growing a few extra courgettes on a roof doesn't fix any of that.
M: Fair enough, but the supply lines into cities are terribly fragile.
W: Maybe so. There is one thing I'll happily give it, mind you — a proper network of city farms would put real money back into the area. Jobs, shops buying produce grown half a mile away, that sort of thing.
M: Exactly, I agree with you entirely there. Every pound stays in the neighbourhood instead of disappearing off to some enormous distributor two hundred miles away.
W: That's the bit I'd put funding behind, then. Just not at the expense of somebody's flat.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Không gian ở quan trọng hơn không gian canh tác = Woman · Nông nghiệp đô thị hấp dẫn = Man · Thành phố cần thêm thực phẩm = Man · Nông nghiệp đô thị có lợi cho kinh tế đô thị = Both

1. Housing space is more important than farming space. → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "putting up somewhere for people to live matters far more than finding room for rows of lettuce". Người đàn ông phản đối: "I don't see it that way at all."

2. Urban farming is appealing. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "I find the whole idea rather lovely". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "It leaves me completely cold, I'm afraid."

3. Cities need more food. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "Towns are simply going to need far more food than they can currently lay their hands on". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'm not convinced that's the real problem, though."

4. Urban farming will benefit the urban economy. → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "a proper network of city farms would put real money back into the area", người đàn ông tán thành: "Exactly, I agree with you entirely there."

👉 Mẹo: Chỗ dễ sập bẫy nhất là "I'll grant you that housing is desperately tight" (ý 1) — nghe như đồng ý nhưng là nhượng bộ một nửa rồi bác kết luận, nên ý 1 vẫn là Woman. Ý 3 cũng vậy: người đàn ông nêu, người phụ nữ chỉ công nhận một phần rồi phản đối.

question_text: There is too much information on the Internet
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
M: Have you read that piece about how the Internet has changed us? It's been on my mind all week.
W: Go on then. Though my first thought is always the same: there's simply far too much material sitting out there. Nobody could ever get through a fraction of it.
M: I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. You can't really have too much of it. It's just there, quietly waiting. Nothing is forcing you to open all of it.
W: Fair enough, but it does leave me feeling swamped before I've even started.
M: Well, here's what I would say. Digging out something decent takes proper technique. You have to know how to word a search, where to look, when to give up on a page.
W: Exactly, I agree with you there completely. Half the people in my office type in a whole sentence and then wonder why they get rubbish back.
M: Right. It's a skill like any other, and almost nobody sits down and teaches it.
W: Nobody teaches it at school either, which is odd.
M: Here's my bigger worry, though. I reckon all this has genuinely reshaped the way our minds work. We skim, we jump about, we never follow an argument through to the end any more.
W: I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. I'll accept that our habits have shifted, but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap. People were easily distracted long before any of this existed.
M: Hmm. I still think something has changed in here.
W: What I will say is that youngsters now have almost no tolerance for waiting. My nephew sighs if a video takes three seconds to load.
M: Oh, I completely agree with you on that one. I see it constantly at work. If a page doesn't open instantly, they've already given up and wandered off.
W: It's the on-demand culture, isn't it. Everything now, or not at all.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Quá nhiều thông tin trên mạng = Woman · Tìm thông tin cần kỹ năng = Both · Internet ảnh hưởng cách ta suy nghĩ = Man · Internet khiến giới trẻ kém kiên nhẫn = Both
1. There is too much information on the Internet → Woman: Nữ nêu "there's simply far too much material sitting out there". Nam phản đối rõ: "I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. You can't really have too much of it."
2. Finding information on the Internet requires skills → Both: Nam nêu "Digging out something decent takes proper technique." Nữ tán thành: "Exactly, I agree with you there completely."
3. The use of the Internet affects the way we think. → Man: Nam nêu "I reckon all this has genuinely reshaped the way our minds work." Nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. I'll accept that our habits have shifted, but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap."
4. The Internet makes young people less patient. → Both: Nữ nêu "youngsters now have almost no tolerance for waiting". Nam tán thành: "Oh, I completely agree with you on that one."
👉 Mẹo: Bẫy nằm ở ý 3 — nữ nói "I'll accept that our habits have shifted" nghe như đồng ý, nhưng ngay sau đó bác bỏ kết luận ("but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap"), nên đáp án là Man chứ không phải Both.

question_text: Art is only suitable for the privileged few
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
W: You came round that exhibition with me on Sunday and barely said a word. Go on, what did you really think of it?
M: Honestly? I felt out of place the whole time. That's the trouble with art — it's really a pastime for a small, comfortable set of people, and everyone else is expected to nod politely and move along.
W: I don't see it that way at all. The gallery was free, it was full of perfectly ordinary families, and half the room had wandered in straight from the market.
M: It still felt like a private club to me.
W: Well, that's precisely why I think the government ought to be putting a good deal more money into the arts. Funding is exactly what keeps those doors open to everybody.
M: I'm not convinced, I have to say. I'll accept that the arts do matter — I'm not a complete philistine. But public money, when hospitals are struggling? No. Let the people who enjoy it pay for it themselves.
W: And there you've just described how it ends up belonging to the wealthy.
M: Hmm. Point taken, but I'd still spend the money elsewhere. Where I do agree with you, mind you, is on the children. They ought to be meeting paintings and music when they're tiny, not at sixteen.
W: Absolutely, I couldn't agree more. My nephew was sitting drawing in a gallery at four, and it has never once occurred to him that it might not be for him.
M: That's the bit that sticks, isn't it. Start late and you feel like a visitor forever.
W: Which makes me rather hopeful, actually. I reckon in twenty years art will be far easier for ordinary people to get at than it is now — whole collections online, work turning up in shopping centres and stations.
M: I don't share your optimism there, I'm afraid. A photograph of a painting on a phone simply isn't the same thing, and the real galleries will still be sitting in the same handful of expensive cities.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Nghệ thuật chỉ hợp với số ít có đặc quyền = Man · Chính phủ nên đầu tư nhiều hơn cho nghệ thuật = Woman · Trẻ em nên tiếp xúc nghệ thuật sớm = Both · Tương lai nghệ thuật sẽ dễ tiếp cận hơn = Woman

1. Art is only suitable for the privileged few → Man: người đàn ông nêu "it's really a pastime for a small, comfortable set of people". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way at all."

2. The government should invest more in arts → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "the government ought to be putting a good deal more money into the arts". Người đàn ông phản đối: "I'm not convinced, I have to say."

3. Children should be exposed to art early → Both: người đàn ông nêu "They ought to be meeting paintings and music when they're tiny, not at sixteen.", người phụ nữ tán thành: "Absolutely, I couldn't agree more."

4. In the future, art will become more accessible → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "in twenty years art will be far easier for ordinary people to get at than it is now". Người đàn ông phản đối: "I don't share your optimism there, I'm afraid."

👉 Mẹo: Ý 2 có bẫy "I'll accept that the arts do matter" — nghe như hai người cùng phe, nhưng người đàn ông bác bỏ đúng chuyện tiền ngân sách; ngược lại ở ý 3 anh ta chủ động đồng ý thật, đây mới là ý Both duy nhất.

question_text: Auditions are most important for an actor's career.
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
Man: You know, I've always believed that auditions are the most important part of an actor's career. I mean, that's where the magic happens. It doesn't matter how great you are in rehearsals or even in the final performance, if you can't nail that audition, you're not getting anywhere.
Woman: Yeah, but it's not just about the audition. I've seen actors who can absolutely shine when they're given the right material to work with. Strong scripts really bring out the best in them. If the writing's weak, even a talented actor might struggle to connect. I think actors respond best when they feel inspired by what's on the page.
Man: That's true, but whether it's a strong script or a weak one, they still have to nail that first audition to even get the chance to perform, right?
Woman: Sure, the audition is key, but once they're in, the script can make or break their performance. It's kind of a balance between both.
Man: I agree with that. But I also think there's a huge difference between theater acting and screen acting. The two require completely different skill sets. In theater, you've got to project and be larger than life, whereas on screen, it's all about subtlety, keeping everything smaller and more contained.
Woman: Absolutely! They're such different worlds. The way you use your body, your voice, even how you interact with your fellow actors-it's all completely different depending on whether you're on stage or in front of a camera.
Man: Right, and that's why actors deserve as much praise as possible. They're constantly shifting between styles and adapting to new roles. It's tough!
Woman: Couldn't agree more. I mean, whether it's theater or film, acting is such an emotional and demanding job. Encouragement and praise go a long way. They need to feel appreciated for all the work they put in.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người nam đánh giá cao tầm quan trọng của vòng thử vai: "I've always believed that auditions are the most important part of an actor's career."
2. Người phụ nữ cho rằng kịch bản mới quan trọng: "I think actors respond best when they feel inspired by what's on the page." (Strong scripts really bring out the best in them).
3. Người nam so sánh sự khác nhau: "...huge difference between theater acting and screen acting." Người phụ nữ hoàn toàn đồng ý: "Absolutely! They're such different worlds."
4. Người nam nói: "actors deserve as much praise as possible." Người phụ nữ đồng tình: "Couldn't agree more. ... Encouragement and praise go a long way."

It's also a great way to explore nature and stay fit. I try to hit the trails at least a few times a month because it's such a thrilling experience for me. It's become my go-to form of exercise whenever I have the time. Speaker B: When it comes to staying active, I've tried lots of different things, but I've found that I get the most out of a good jog. It's a great way to keep my energy levels up, and I enjoy how it clears my mind. I usually jog around the park or along the river near my home. It's not too fast, but it still gets my heart pumping and helps me unwind. I try to fit it into my routine as often as I can, even if it's just for twenty minutes. Speaker C: I prefer something more low-key and calming when it comes to exercise. I'm not really into intense activities like running or biking. Instead, I find walking to be the perfect balance for me. It allows me to relax while still staying active. Whether it's in the park or just around my neighborhood, I try to get my steps in every day. It's also a nice way to clear my head after a long day at work. Speaker D: I've been involved in different sports over the years, but one thing that stands out for me is horse riding. There's something about being with horses that feels both calming and exciting. Riding through open fields or along forest paths is an amazing way to stay active. It's not just a workout, but also a chance to connect with animals and nature. I try to go riding whenever I have a free weekend. It's definitely my favorite way to keep fit.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
• Going for a run → Speaker B: "I get the most out of a good jog", chạy quanh công viên hoặc dọc bờ sông.
• Mountain biking → Speaker A: "nothing more exciting than mountain biking", thích địa hình gồ ghề và lao xuống dốc.
• Walking → Speaker C: "I find walking to be the perfect balance", thích vận động nhẹ nhàng, đi bộ mỗi ngày.
• Horse riding → Speaker D: "one thing that stands out for me is horse riding", cưỡi ngựa qua đồng và đường rừng.
• Hiking và Swimming là 2 phương án nhiễu — hiking chỉ được A nhắc để LOẠI ("some of my friends prefer running or hiking"), còn swimming không ai nói.

question_text: Cultural Exchange
options: Redefining Global Cultural Understanding
Encouraging Cross-Cultural Festivals
Promoting Language Exchange Programs
Overemphasis on Commercial Tourism
Concerns About Cultural Preservation
Building Mutual Respect Among Communities
Focusing on Authentic Cultural Experiences
explanation:
1. Heading: Redefining Global Cultural Understanding Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cho thấy quá trình giao thoa văn hóa trong bối cảnh toàn cầu hóa đang thay đổi cách con người hiểu về văn hóa trên toàn thế giới. Vietnamese translation: Toàn cầu hóa đã thay đổi cách con người hiểu về văn hóa trên khắp thế giới. Ngày nay, giao lưu văn hóa cho phép mỗi cá nhân khám phá phong tục, niềm tin và giá trị vượt ra ngoài xã hội của chính mình. Quá trình này giúp định hình lại cách hiểu văn hóa toàn cầu bằng cách khuyến khích sự cởi mở, tính hiếu kỳ và nhận thức sâu sắc hơn về sự đa dạng trong đời sống hiện đại.
2. Heading: Encouraging Cross-Cultural Festivals Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói về các sự kiện quốc tế kết hợp âm nhạc, ẩm thực, nghệ thuật và truyền thống từ nhiều quốc gia để tôn vinh sự đa dạng và kết nối. Vietnamese translation: Nhiều cộng đồng hiện nay tổ chức các sự kiện quốc tế để tôn vinh sự đa dạng và sự kết nối. Những buổi gặp gỡ này quy tụ âm nhạc, ẩm thực, nghệ thuật và truyền thống từ nhiều quốc gia khác nhau. Bằng cách khuyến khích các lễ hội giao thoa văn hóa, xã hội tạo ra cơ hội để mọi người trân trọng sự khác biệt, tăng cường quan hệ và thúc đẩy sự hòa hợp giữa các nhóm văn hóa.
3. Heading: Promoting Language Exchange Programs Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nhấn mạnh rằng ngôn ngữ là công cụ mạnh mẽ để kết nối văn hóa và các chương trình trao đổi ngôn ngữ giúp người học vừa luyện giao tiếp vừa mở rộng hiểu biết văn hóa. Vietnamese translation: Ngôn ngữ là một trong những công cụ mạnh mẽ nhất để kết nối văn hóa. Trường học và các tổ chức thường tạo cơ hội để học sinh, sinh viên luyện nói với người đến từ các quốc gia khác. Bằng cách thúc đẩy các chương trình trao đổi ngôn ngữ, cộng đồng giúp người học cải thiện kỹ năng giao tiếp, đồng thời phát triển nhận thức văn hóa sâu sắc hơn và tình bạn quốc tế.
4. Heading: Overemphasis on Commercial Tourism Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cảnh báo rằng truyền thống đôi khi bị điều chỉnh để thu hút khách du lịch và tăng lợi nhuận, từ đó làm giảm tính chân thực của văn hóa. Vietnamese translation: Mặc dù du lịch có thể hỗ trợ giao lưu văn hóa, nó đôi khi cũng tạo ra những tác động tiêu cực. Ở nhiều nơi, các truyền thống bị thay đổi để thu hút du khách và tăng lợi nhuận thay vì giữ lại ý nghĩa nguyên gốc. Sự nhấn mạnh quá mức vào du lịch thương mại có thể làm giảm tính chân thực và khiến các thực hành văn hóa trở thành màn trình diễn hơn là sự biểu đạt bản sắc thực sự.
5. Heading: Concerns About Cultural Preservation Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nêu rõ nỗi lo rằng những phong tục truyền thống có thể mai một dần và thế hệ trẻ có thể mất liên kết với di sản địa phương. Vietnamese translation: Khi các nền văn hóa tương tác với nhau thường xuyên hơn, một số người lo sợ các phong tục truyền thống sẽ dần biến mất. Thế hệ trẻ có thể tiếp nhận lối sống nước ngoài và mất đi sự gắn kết với di sản địa phương. Những lo ngại về bảo tồn văn hóa này đã khiến nhiều cộng đồng chủ động bảo vệ ngôn ngữ, nghi lễ và các giá trị lịch sử của mình cẩn thận hơn trước đây.
6. Heading: Building Mutual Respect Among Communities Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cho thấy khi con người tìm hiểu truyền thống và niềm tin của nhau, họ thường thông cảm hơn và bớt phán xét hơn, từ đó xây dựng sự tôn trọng lẫn nhau. Vietnamese translation: Giao lưu văn hóa có thể đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc tạo ra những mối quan hệ hòa bình giữa các nhóm khác nhau. Khi con người tìm hiểu về truyền thống và niềm tin của nhau, họ thường trở nên thấu hiểu hơn và bớt phán xét hơn. Theo cách đó, các hoạt động văn hóa góp phần xây dựng sự tôn trọng lẫn nhau giữa các cộng đồng và khuyến khích sự hợp tác lâu dài.
7. Heading: Focusing on Authentic Cultural Experiences Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói rằng du khách hiện nay muốn trải nghiệm kết nối sâu hơn, tiếp cận đời sống và truyền thống địa phương thật hơn thay vì chỉ đi ngắm cảnh. Vietnamese translation: Du khách hiện đại ngày càng tìm kiếm những kết nối sâu sắc hơn thay vì chỉ tham quan đơn thuần. Thay vì đến những điểm đông đúc, họ muốn trải nghiệm đời sống hàng ngày, truyền thống địa phương và sự tương tác có ý nghĩa với người dân bản địa. Khi tập trung vào các trải nghiệm văn hóa chân thực, du lịch có thể trở nên tôn trọng hơn, mang tính giáo dục hơn và có giá trị hơn cho cả du khách lẫn cộng đồng sở tại.

extra_data.title: Cultural Exchange

paragraphs.text: Globalization has changed the way people understand culture around the world. Today, cultural exchange allows individuals to explore customs, beliefs, and values beyond their own societies. This process helps redefine global cultural understanding by encouraging openness, curiosity, and deeper awareness of diversity in modern life.

Many communities now organize international events to celebrate diversity and connection. These gatherings bring together music, food, art, and traditions from different countries. By encouraging cross-cultural festivals, societies create opportunities for people to appreciate differences, strengthen relationships, and promote harmony among various cultural groups.

Language is one of the most powerful tools for cultural connection. Schools and organizations often create opportunities for students to practice speaking with people from other countries. By promoting language exchange programs, communities help learners improve communication skills while also developing greater cultural awareness and international friendship.

Although tourism can support cultural exchange, it sometimes creates negative effects. In many places, traditions are changed to attract visitors and increase profits rather than preserve meaning. This overemphasis on commercial tourism may reduce authenticity and cause cultural practices to become performances instead of genuine expressions of identity.

As cultures interact more frequently, some people fear that traditional customs may gradually disappear. Younger generations may adopt foreign lifestyles and lose connection with local heritage. These concerns about cultural preservation have led many communities to protect their languages, rituals, and historical values more carefully than before.

Cultural exchange can play an important role in creating peaceful relationships between different groups. When people learn about each other's traditions and beliefs, they often become more understanding and less judgmental. In this way, cultural activities contribute to building mutual respect among communities and encourage long-term cooperation.

Modern travelers increasingly seek deeper connections rather than simple sightseeing. Instead of visiting crowded attractions, they want to experience daily life, local traditions, and meaningful interaction with residents. By focusing on authentic cultural experiences, tourism can become more respectful, educational, and valuable for both visitors and host communities.

2. Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cảnh báo rằng tình trạng ít vận động đang nghiêm trọng hơn do thời gian dùng thiết bị điện tử tăng lên.

7. Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn so sánh giải pháp ít tốn kém và giải pháp cần đầu tư lớn để nhấn mạnh bài toán cân bằng giữa lợi ích và ngân sách.

extra_data.title: Children and Exercises

headings.text: Ways in which environment can influence behaviour
The success of a simple idea
A design for exercise and for study
The situation has the potential of being worst
The wider effects of regular activity

paragraphs.text: In recent years, children have been engaging in less physical activity. Instead, research has shown that the amount of time spent outdoors has decreased while the amount of time spent lounging on the sofa at home has increased significantly. While technology is often cited as the main cause, it is not the only reason. Urbanisation has limited the amount of space available for children to play. In today's world, children spend many hours doing homework. This forces them to spend more time indoors. The combination of screen time and lack of exercise is having a negative impact on children's physical fitness and overall health.

The phenomenon of children being sedentary is becoming more serious, largely due to the increase in time spent on electronic devices. The lure of smartphones and computers makes it difficult for both parents and children to reduce their screen time. As people become more aware of the benefits of exercise, it is imperative that we work together to find effective solutions to promote an active lifestyle.

An inspiring example is a teacher who started a program called Daily Mile, in which students are encouraged to run at least one mile every day. This simple idea quickly gained widespread support. Thanks to media coverage and positive feedback, the program has won numerous awards and is implemented in more than 3,500 schools in 36 countries. This initiative shows that small changes can have a big impact on children's exercise habits.

Daily Mile not only improves students' physical fitness, but also helps improve academic performance. Many teachers have noted that students who participate in this program become more focused and alert in class. Psychologists also agree that physical fitness contributes to mental clarity. The saying 'a healthy body is the foundation for a healthy mind' shows that regular exercise has a positive effect on children's ability to learn and remember.

The living and learning environment has a great influence on human behavior. For example, workplaces are often arranged to improve efficiency, while living spaces are designed to promote connections between members. Similarly, schools can be designed to encourage children to be active. Arranging open areas suitable for play and physical exercise can help students maintain an active lifestyle and fight the trend of being sedentary.

In Japan, an innovative architect designed a kindergarten in a very different way: the playground was built like a running track, allowing children to run and move freely. He said: “It is simple”, “Just start running” This innovative approach was not only successful but also won an award for its positive impact on children’s activity levels. Such thoughtful designs could inspire other schools to rethink how they create spaces that support learning while promoting physical activity.

Daily Mile and the Japanese architect’s playground design represent two different approaches to finance. The Daily Mile is virtually free, while the playground model requires a large investment. Local authorities need to consider many factors to balance promoting physical activity for children and managing their budgets appropriately. By finding creative but cost-effective solutions, communities can create environments that support children’s health and overall development.
