question_text: What does the radio presenter say about how the research on happiness has been covered by the media?
options: It has been accurately reported by the media
It has not been accurately reported by the media
It has been ignored completely by the media
explanation:
Today we're going to discuss a recent piece of research on happiness. A great many researchers took part in this project, and it has become a very popular topic of conversation — everybody seems to be talking about it. Now, some newspapers always prefer a shocking headline to a careful story, and that is exactly what happened here. The information given in the newspaper article was very limited, and it did not reflect the research fully or accurately. The researchers spent years collecting data and checking their results with great care, but none of that effort appears in the article. Readers were given a dramatic headline and very little else. So the research has certainly not been ignored — but it has not been reported accurately either.
So what does the research actually tell us? It can certainly help people to think about their own happiness, and it clearly gives the media plenty to discuss. But if you are hoping for a final answer to the question of what makes people happy, you will be disappointed. What determines happiness is, in the end, very difficult to define. Money, health, friendships, family — each of them matters to some people and much less to others, and the balance changes throughout our lives. A conclusive answer, a single formula that works for everyone, is the one thing this research is unlikely ever to give us.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It has not been accurately reported by the media — "The information given in the newspaper article was very limited, and it did not reflect the research fully or accurately". Bẫy: "ignored" bị phủ định ("the research has certainly not been ignored").
2. Đáp án: To find a conclusive answer — "A conclusive answer, a single formula that works for everyone, is the one thing this research is unlikely ever to give us". Bẫy: "personal happiness" và "discuss in the media" đều là điều nghiên cứu LÀM ĐƯỢC ("help people to think about their own happiness", "gives the media plenty to discuss").
👉 Mẹo: bài nói liệt kê những gì nghiên cứu làm được rồi mới tới "the one thing... unlikely" — đáp án nằm ở phần đảo hướng cuối.

question_text: What are the benefits of spending time in nature?

Stress falls partly because nature never demands a reply, which almost nothing else in modern life can claim. There is also a change of scale: standing under old trees makes a work problem shrink to its real size. An hour in the park near my house resets me better than an evening of television. question_text: Why do many people read fewer books than before?

A phone offers something entertaining every few seconds, while a novel asks for twenty quiet minutes before it becomes interesting. Concentration itself has also weakened, because most of us now read in fragments all day long. Tiredness finishes the job, since a demanding book is the last thing an exhausted person picks up. I read every night as a teenager and now catch myself scrolling instead, which I am not proud of. So the real change is not in books but in what our attention has been trained to expect.

Distance and cost quietly remove the rest, because a gym across the city will always lose to a warm house. Then there is the timing problem, since visible results arrive weeks after motivation has gone. So the honest answer is that people start too big and give up too early.

Tiredness plays a large role too, since exhausted people choose the option that asks nothing of them. And the social life genuinely lives there now, so putting the phone down can feel like leaving the room. So it is less about laziness and more about a system built to be hard to leave.

question_text: What should we do to protect animals?

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: I think protecting animals starts with protecting their homes. The main reason is that most animals disappear because forests and seas are destroyed, not because of one hunter. On top of that, tourists should not feed wild animals like the monkeys in the first picture, and shows with captive animals, like the second picture, should slowly end. For example, Vietnam now protects sea turtles on Con Dao island and their numbers are rising. Having said that, many people depend on fishing or hunting to live, so the change must be fair. So the best help is simple: leave wild animals wild.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Protecting animals is mostly about protecting places, because species rarely vanish one hunter at a time — they vanish when a forest is cleared or a bay fills with plastic. So the first job belongs to governments: protected areas, enforced laws, and penalties for the wildlife trade. The second job belongs to us, and both pictures show it. Tourists who feed temple monkeys turn wild animals into beggars, and every ticket to a dolphin show funds the capture of another dolphin; declining both is a form of protection. Con Dao's turtle programme shows that numbers recover surprisingly fast once nesting beaches are left alone. Admittedly, families who fish or hunt to survive need alternatives, not lectures. So the rule is simple even if the work is not: leave wild animals wild, and make that the profitable choice.

question_text: Why do many people prefer to travel with friends?

extra_data.imageDesc: Nhóm năm người bạn trẻ đang đi bộ trên con đường ven biển đầy nắng; chàng trai tóc đỏ đeo kính, mặc áo gi-lê đen trên áo sơ mi caro đi phía trước, hai cô gái (áo hồng, áo trắng đeo ba lô) đang cười nói phía sau, thêm một chàng trai áo caro đỏ và một cô gái ở mép trái; sau lưng họ là biển xanh, sóng vỗ vào vách đá.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: I think many people prefer to travel with friends for several reasons. The main reason is that there is always someone to talk to and laugh with, and you can share the cost of hotels and transport. On top of that, friends help when something goes wrong, and it is easier to try new things when you are not alone. For example, when I lost my wallet in Da Nang, my friend paid for everything. Having said that, it is hard to agree on where to go and what to eat. So for most people, friends make the trip.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: People prefer to travel with friends because, put simply, the company is half the holiday. There is always someone to talk to, someone to laugh with when the bus breaks down, and someone to split the hotel bill with, which matters when you are young and not rich. Friends also share the same energy and interests, so nobody drags anyone round a museum they hate. And when things go wrong — I lost my wallet in Da Nang and my friend paid for everything without a word — a friend is the difference between a disaster and a good story. Admittedly, groups argue about food and directions, and some people travel alone for exactly that reason. Even so, for most of us, the people matter more than the place.

question_text: Why is gardening a good hobby for many people?

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Gardening is a good hobby because it is relaxing and useful at the same time. Working with soil and plants helps people forget stress and stay away from screens. It is also gentle exercise, since you move a lot without going to a gym. Watching something grow because of your care gives a real feeling of success. For example, my neighbour says her garden is the only place she truly relaxes. So gardening is calm, healthy and quietly rewarding.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Gardening suits people because it moves at a speed nothing else in modern life does. Nothing can be rushed, so the hobby forces a slower rhythm on whoever practises it. It is also physical without ever feeling like exercise, which is why older people stay with it for decades. The reward is unusually honest as well: the plant either grew or it did not, and the answer belongs entirely to you. My neighbour says her small garden is the only place where her mind goes quiet. So gardening gives patience, movement and proof of your own care, all at once.

question_text: What are the benefits of traveling alone?

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Traveling alone has several benefits, especially for confidence. You decide everything yourself, so you can change your plan at any moment. Solo travellers usually meet more local people, because they are not always talking to friends. Dealing with problems alone also makes you more independent and confident. For example, my cousin travelled alone for two weeks and came back much braver. So traveling alone is harder at first, but you learn a lot about yourself.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Travelling alone teaches you things a group trip carefully protects you from. Every decision belongs to you, so the trip becomes an honest picture of what you actually enjoy. You also become approachable, and strangers talk to one person far more readily than to a laughing group of four. Problems hit harder, but solving a missed bus in a foreign language changes how you see yourself. My cousin went away alone for two weeks and came back noticeably calmer about difficulty. So the loneliness is real, and so is the confidence you bring home.

question_text: Why do some people prefer living in the countryside?

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Some people prefer the countryside because life there is calmer and cheaper. Houses cost much less, so families can have more space and a garden. The air is cleaner and there is much less noise and traffic. People also know their neighbours, so the community feels closer than in a city. For example, my grandparents moved back to their village after retiring and are much happier. So the countryside is slower, but for many people that is exactly the point.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: The countryside wins on the things cities quietly take away. Space is the obvious one, since the price of a small city flat can buy a house with a garden. Air, noise and traffic follow, and their effect on health is easy to underestimate until you leave. Community matters just as much, because knowing your neighbours is normal in a village and unusual in an apartment block. My grandparents returned to their village after retiring and have never once mentioned missing the city. So people move for calm and space, and usually discover the community was the real prize.

question_text: What can people do to reduce stress?

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: There are many simple things people can do to reduce stress. Exercise helps a lot, because the body relaxes after walking or playing sport. Talking to a friend or family member also makes problems feel smaller. Sleeping enough is very important too, since tired people worry much more. For example, I go for a short walk whenever I feel stressed at work. So small daily habits work better than waiting for the stress to disappear.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Most stress relief is unglamorous and works anyway. Movement comes first, because a walk changes the chemistry of a bad mood faster than any advice. Talking is second, since a problem kept inside the head grows, while a problem spoken out loud stays its real size. Sleep is the quiet foundation under both, as almost everything feels unsolvable at one in the morning. What rarely works is waiting, hoping the pressure will fade on its own. So the answer is small repeated habits rather than one big solution.

question_text: Why should we help other people?
Why is it important to have family meals together?

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: I think family meals are the glue that holds a family together. The main reason is that dinner is often the only time when everyone is in the same room, and people talk more naturally when they are eating. On top of that, children learn manners at the table, and parents notice problems early. For example, my parents always know when I am stressed because they see it at dinner. Having said that, busy work schedules make daily family meals very hard. So even one shared meal a week is worth protecting.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Family meals matter because they are the one daily moment when a family is forced into the same room with nothing to do but talk. Conversation flows far more naturally over food than in a scheduled 'family chat', so parents learn what is really happening in their children's lives, and small problems surface before they grow. The table is also where manners, listening and family recipes get quietly handed down. My parents can always tell when I am stressed, simply because they see my face at dinner. Admittedly, modern work hours make a daily meal difficult, and a silent dinner with everyone scrolling achieves nothing. So the goal is not perfection but one screen-free shared meal a week — a small habit with an enormous effect.

question_text: What do these two famous writers have in common?
options: They both wrote in the same genre
They both were born in the same country
They both make references to each other in their work
explanation:
In this week's literature lecture, we look at two writers who changed modern fiction — and at what actually connects them, because students always guess wrong. The first guess is that they wrote in the same genre. In fact, one spent his life on realistic novels while the other moved between fantasy, essays and poetry. The second guess is that they were born in the same country. Also wrong — an ocean separated their birthplaces, and they met in person only twice. What they truly share is more unusual: they make references to each other in their work. Open one writer's short stories and you will find the other's characters walking through them; read the second writer's essays and whole passages answer arguments the first had made years before. Across different languages and continents, their books carried on a lifelong conversation of mutual respect.
Now, what should you expect when you read them? Do not expect simple language and structure — anyone who tells you these are easy books has not read them. And do not assume their works are based on real events; both invented freely, even when history appears in the background. What is genuinely special is that the meaning of their work is not always easily identified. Both writers hid ideas beneath the surface — symbols, private jokes, arguments in disguise. You may finish a chapter unsure of what it truly said, return a year later, and find a different book waiting for you. That richness is exactly why we still study them.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 05 bài 2 — nhiễu khác: same genre / same country.)
1. Đáp án: They both make references to each other in their work. Bẫy: "same genre" và "same country" đều bị phủ định ngay đầu.
2. Đáp án: The meaning of their work is not always easily identified. Bẫy: "simple language" và "based on real events" đều bị phủ định.

question_text: Why is it important for families to keep memories together?

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Keeping memories together is important because it gives a family a shared history. Photos and stories remind everyone of good times, especially during difficult periods. Children also learn about their grandparents and their family background this way. Looking at old pictures together creates natural conversation between generations. For example, my mother tells the same story every time she sees one particular photo. So shared memories keep a family connected across time.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Shared memories are what turn a group of relatives into a family with an identity. Photographs and repeated stories give everyone the same reference points, which matters most when times are hard. They are also how children meet the grandparents they never had time to know properly. Old pictures create a rare thing as well: conversation between generations that starts naturally, without anyone forcing it. My mother tells the identical story every time one particular photo appears, and nobody stops her. So keeping memories is less about the past and more about holding the family together now.

extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: It is hot and sticky today, typical for this time of year: around thirty-two degrees with hardly a cloud, so the afternoon is best spent indoors near a fan. There was a pleasant breeze first thing, which made the journey here bearable. The forecast promises a storm this evening, and honestly I am looking forward to it, because the air always feels cleaner afterwards.

On the surface it is a children's comedy, but it says something quite honest about growing up — that sadness has a job to do as well. I first watched it with my younger sister, and we both ended up crying, which neither of us expected from a cartoon.

question_text: Why is it important for older people to stay active?

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Staying active is very important for older people, for health and for happiness. Gentle exercise keeps muscles strong, which helps them avoid falls and stay independent. Activity is also good for the mind and can reduce feelings of loneliness. Many older people exercise in groups, so they meet friends at the same time. For example, my grandmother walks with her neighbours every morning and looks ten years younger. So staying active keeps older people healthy and connected to other people.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: For older people, activity is really about independence rather than fitness. Strong legs mean fewer falls, and one avoided fall can save years of quality of life. Movement also protects the mind, which tends to fade fastest in people who stop leaving the house. The social side may matter most of all, because most exercise for older adults happens in groups. My grandmother walks around the lake with the same four neighbours every morning, and that hour is the centre of her day. So activity is not about staying young, it is about staying in charge of your own life.

question_text: Listen to an announcement at a railway station. Which platform does the train to Edinburgh leave from?

question_text: A man is calling his friend. Where will they meet?

question_text: A reporter is interviewing a woman about her shopping habits. Where is the woman going to shop today?

question_text: A woman is leaving a message for her friend. What time does she want to meet?
options: At seven o'clock
At a quarter to eight
At half past seven
explanation:
Hi, it's Laura. I'm calling to tell you that I won't be able to make it at seven, because I have a meeting this afternoon. It's a very long meeting, and it won't end until half past seven, so seven is impossible for me. Let's meet up at a quarter to eight instead. That way we'll still have about fifteen minutes to have some coffee before the show starts. So that's a quarter to eight, at the usual place. Sorry about the change — see you later!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – At a quarter to eight (7 giờ 45).
• Vì sao đúng: "Let's meet up at a quarter to eight instead" và nhắc lại "So that's a quarter to eight, at the usual place".
• At seven o'clock sai: giờ hẹn cũ, cô không tới được — "I won't be able to make it at seven".
• At half past seven sai: là giờ cuộc họp KẾT THÚC — "it won't end until half past seven".
👉 Mẹo: học chắc cách nói giờ kiểu Anh: "quarter to eight" = 7:45, "half past seven" = 7:30. Giờ đúng đứng sau "instead".

question_text: A man is talking about his family's weekends. What does the family do most weekends?

• Vì sao đúng: "We go for a walk together almost every weekend" — câu hỏi hỏi thói quen (MOST weekends).
• They go bowling sai: chỉ là đề xuất cho tuần NÀY ("this weekend, for a change").
• They go out with friends sai: là kế hoạch cho bọn trẻ tuần này, không phải thói quen.
👉 Mẹo: phân biệt "this weekend" (kế hoạch) và "almost every weekend" (thói quen) — câu hỏi hỏi cái nào thì chọn cái đó.

question_text: Jose is calling his friend about tomorrow. What will Luis and Emma bring?

Hi, it's Jose here. Tomorrow I'm meeting Luis and Emma at the bus stop at five o'clock in the afternoon. They're going to bring the food, so we don't need to worry about lunch or dinner. Do you want to meet us there? If you can, come at about a quarter past five. After that, we can go and buy a few things we still need — some fruit for the journey, and maybe some water. And don't forget to bring your own sleeping bag, because it gets really cold at night. See you tomorrow!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Food.
• Vì sao đúng: "They're going to bring the food, so we don't need to worry about lunch or dinner" — "They" = Luis và Emma.
• Fruit sai: là thứ CẢ NHÓM sẽ đi mua sau — "we can go and buy a few things we still need — some fruit".
• Sleeping bags sai: là thứ NGƯỜI NGHE phải tự mang — "don't forget to bring your own sleeping bag".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi hỏi AI mang gì. Ghép đúng chủ ngữ: "they... bring" (Luis & Emma), "we... buy" (cả nhóm), "you... bring" (người nghe).

And once it's all finished, of course, you must come round and see it. Call me back when you can!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – To ask where to buy furniture.
• Vì sao đúng: "I wanted to ask: where did you get your furniture? Is there a good shop somewhere nearby?".
• To give away her old furniture sai: cô nói rõ KHÔNG nhờ bạn lấy sofa cũ — "I'm not going to ask you to take our old sofa; Tom has already given it to his brother".
• To invite her friend to see the house sai: chỉ là lời hẹn cho SAU KHI xong, không phải mục đích cuộc gọi — "once it's all finished... you must come round".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "Why is she calling?" → tìm câu có "I wanted to ask" / "I'm calling to". Các ý phụ (từ chối, hẹn sau) là nhiễu.

question_text: A girl is talking about a film. Which scenes does she think are the best?
options: The fight scenes
The car-chase scenes
The mountain scenes
explanation:
Today I'd like to talk about my favourite film. Actually, I don't usually like action films, but this one isn't like the others, with car chases and fight scenes that go on forever. What makes it special is the mountains. The best moment is when they climb to the summit at dawn, and the view that opens up is absolutely spectacular. The ending is a bit predictable, but overall it's an amazing piece of work.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – The mountain scenes.
• Vì sao đúng: "What makes it special is the mountains. The best moment is when they climb to the summit at dawn".
• The car-chase scenes / The fight scenes sai: được nhắc với ý chê — "go on forever" — và là đặc điểm của phim hành động khác.
👉 Mẹo: cụm "what makes it special" / "the best moment" báo hiệu đáp án.

question_text: A man is talking about his plans for the weekend. What will the woman do on Saturday?
options: Go for a drive
Go to a party
Go for a coffee
explanation:
M: I'm going to celebrate my promotion this Saturday.
W: Oh, what are you going to do?
M: In the morning I'll have coffee with some friends at the hotel, and in the evening there's a party.
W: What about the afternoon?
M: I'll watch the football. And on Sunday I'm driving out to the countryside. Do you want to join me?
W: Sunday? Sorry, I can't make Sunday.
M: Then how about Saturday morning?
W: Yes, that sounds good.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Go for a coffee.
• Vì sao đúng: anh mời "how about Saturday morning?" (= uống cà phê ở khách sạn) và cô nhận "Yes, that sounds good".
• Go to a party sai: là kế hoạch tối thứ Bảy của ANH, cô không nói sẽ tham gia.
• Go for a drive sai: chuyến đi là Chủ nhật, cô từ chối "I can't make Sunday".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi hỏi về NGƯỜI PHỤ NỮ — chỉ tính hoạt động cô ấy đồng ý, không phải lịch của anh.

question_text: A man is calling his colleague Ruth about a meeting. How does he suggest changing the meeting?
options: Cancelling the meeting
Delaying the meeting
Having the meeting without him
explanation:
M: Hi, Ruth. I'm really sorry, but I've just had a call from an important client. They've suddenly come to visit our office, so I don't think I'll be able to make it to the meeting.
W: Oh, that's a problem. Should we delay the meeting until tomorrow?
M: I'd rather not. I've got a factory inspection scheduled for tomorrow morning, so I'll be busy all day.
W: Right, I understand. So what do you suggest?
M: I think the best thing is to have the meeting without me. You can discuss everything with the others and send me the notes afterwards.
W: That sounds sensible. I'll let everyone know.
M: Thanks, Ruth. Sorry about the situation.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Having the meeting without him.
• Vì sao đúng: chính người đàn ông đề xuất "I think the best thing is to have the meeting without me... send me the notes afterwards".
• Delaying the meeting sai: Ruth đề nghị hoãn sang mai nhưng anh từ chối — "I'd rather not. I've got a factory inspection scheduled for tomorrow".
• Cancelling the meeting sai: không ai đề nghị huỷ; cuộc họp vẫn diễn ra với những người còn lại.
👉 Mẹo: phiên bản này ĐẢO VAI so với Đề 37 (ở đó Ruth gọi và đề nghị họp không có cô ấy). Câu hỏi hỏi "how does HE suggest" — bám vào lời đề xuất của người gọi, không phải lời hỏi của Ruth.

question_text: A man is talking about taking a course. Which course will he take?
options: A computer course
A management course
A leadership course
explanation:
M: I'd like to take a course this year.
W: Sure. Which one?
M: I was thinking of the management course.
W: Hmm. We don't have many people with computer skills in the company. I think you should go for that one instead.
M: OK — I like technology anyway.
W: That's settled, then. You can always do a leadership course later, when you have more experience.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – A computer course.
• Vì sao đúng: sếp gợi ý khoá máy tính ("not many people with computer skills... go for that one") và anh đồng ý "OK — I like technology anyway", rồi "That's settled".
• A management course sai: là ý định BAN ĐẦU, bị đổi.
• A leadership course sai: để "later, when you have more experience".
👉 Mẹo: "That's settled" = chốt; đáp án là thứ vừa được đồng ý ngay trước đó.

question_text: Listen to a weather forecast. Where will the weather be best?
options: In the south
In the east
In the west
explanation:
And now the weather forecast. The heavy rain we've had all week is continuing across most of the country. In the north there's no sign of it stopping, so keep your umbrella ready. The south stays grey and cloudy, with more showers this afternoon. In the west, though, there are some positive signs: the weather is improving, and the sun has already started to come out in a few places. However, the best weather today is in the east. It's bright and dry there, with no rain at all — perfect for a family picnic.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – In the east.
• Vì sao đúng: "the best weather today is in the east. It's bright and dry there, with no rain at all".
• In the west sai: chỉ ĐANG TỐT LÊN, có nắng vài nơi — "the weather is improving" — nhưng câu sau có "However" đảo hướng.
• In the south sai: vẫn xám và có mưa rào — "stays grey and cloudy, with more showers".
👉 Mẹo: bản tin thời tiết đọc lần lượt từng vùng; vùng "tốt lên" là bẫy. Chỉ chốt vùng đi kèm từ so sánh nhất "the best".

question_text: Listen to an announcement in a supermarket. How much are the cleaning products?
options: One pound fifty
Two pounds fifteen
Fifty pence
explanation:
Good morning, shoppers, and welcome to our biggest sale of the year. In the kitchen section, every item is marked down by twenty per cent today. All our cleaning products are also reduced — they are now just one pound fifty each. That's one pound fifty for any cleaning product. And don't miss the bakery: our cakes are down to only two pounds fifteen, and bread rolls are fifty pence a bag. Offers end at closing time today, so hurry while stocks last. Thank you for shopping with us.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – One pound fifty.
• Vì sao đúng: "All our cleaning products are also reduced — they are now just one pound fifty each", được nhắc lại ngay sau đó.
• Two pounds fifteen sai: là giá BÁNH — "our cakes are down to only two pounds fifteen".
• Fifty pence sai: là giá bánh mì — "bread rolls are fifty pence a bag".
👉 Mẹo: thông báo giảm giá liệt kê nhiều giá liên tiếp. Ghép giá với đúng MẶT HÀNG trong câu hỏi (cleaning products), đừng chộp con số nghe rõ nhất.

question_text: A woman is calling her friend at a restaurant. What does she usually drink with her lunch?
options: Milk
Tea
Wine
explanation:
Hi Sally, it's me. I'm going to be a little late — I can't find anywhere to park the car. Could you order for me? I'll have the fish; I'm trying to eat healthily. And I usually have tea with my lunch, so could you order me a big cup? See you in about fifteen minutes.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Tea.
• Vì sao đúng: "I usually have tea with my lunch, so could you order me a big cup".
• Milk / Wine sai: không được nhắc.
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi có "usually" — bắt đúng câu có "usually" trong bài.

question_text: A man and woman are discussing their plans for the evening. What do the man and woman decide to do in the evening?
options: Make plans later
Go to the movies
Stay at home
explanation:
M: So — tonight. Any ideas? There's that new film at the cinema, the one everyone's talking about.
W: I checked already: sold out until the weekend. Every single seat.
M: Ah. Then we could just stay at home? Order food, watch something on the sofa?
W: We've done that three nights in a row! I can't look at that sofa any more.
M: Fair point. So no cinema, no sofa... what's left?
W: Honestly? Let's not decide right now. I finish work at five — let's just see how we feel and make plans then.
M: You know what, that's the best idea. No pressure, no booking.
W: Exactly. I'll call you at five!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Make plans later.
• Vì sao đúng: "Let's not decide right now. I finish work at five — let's just see how we feel and make plans then" — anh đồng ý "that's the best idea. No pressure, no booking".
• Go to the movies sai: phim đã hết vé tới cuối tuần — "I checked already: sold out until the weekend. Every single seat".
• Stay at home sai: bị loại vì đã ở nhà ba tối liên tiếp — "We've done that three nights in a row! I can't look at that sofa any more".
👉 Mẹo: đôi khi đáp án là "chưa quyết" chứ không phải một hoạt động cụ thể. Nếu cả hai phương án cụ thể đều bị loại, nghe kỹ câu chốt kiểu "let's decide later".

question_text: A woman is talking about her old manager. Why did she like George?
options: He looked after his staff
He was friendly
He taught her a lot
explanation:
A lot of people don't like their managers, but that wasn't the case for me. My manager George was really good at his job — he helped me know what to do in difficult times. He was a friendly manager, and he looked after his staff, too. But those aren't the main reasons I liked him. He taught me a lot, and he was like a teacher to me. That's what mattered most.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – He taught her a lot.
• Vì sao đúng: "He taught me a lot, and he was like a teacher to me. That's what mattered most".
• He was friendly / He looked after his staff sai: đều được nhắc nhưng bị gạt — "those aren't the main reasons".
👉 Mẹo: dạng "nhắc cả 3 rồi loại 2" — đáp án nằm sau "But... the main reason" / "That's what mattered most".

formalEmail.sampleAnswer:
Dear Manager,

Thank you for your email about the possible closure of the public library. I was very sorry to read this news, as the library has been an important part of our community for many years, and I believe our club should act quickly to help keep it open.

I would like to suggest two ideas. Firstly, the club could hold its monthly meetings at the library instead of at the community centre. Secondly, we could organise a reading festival for local schools, with storytelling sessions and a small book exchange. Children who enjoy the library today will become the readers of tomorrow.

I would be happy to help organise either event. Please let me know if you need any further support.

Yours sincerely,
[Your Name]

formalEmail.sampleAnswer:
Dear Manager,
Thank you for your email about the changes to this year's photo contest. I was pleased to read about the new categories, and I would like to share my thoughts.
In my opinion, dividing the contest into several categories is a very positive change. Last year, some younger members felt that they had no chance against experienced adults, so a separate category for children under 16 will encourage more of them to take part. It will also make the judging fairer.
I have two small suggestions. Firstly, the club could add a category based on subject, such as landscape or street photography, so that members can enter the area they are best at. Secondly, it would be helpful to publish the judging criteria before the contest begins.
I look forward to taking part this year.
Yours sincerely,
[Your Name]

question_text: There is too much information on the Internet
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
M: Have you read that piece about how the Internet has changed us? It's been on my mind all week.
W: Go on then. Though my first thought is always the same: there's simply far too much material sitting out there. Nobody could ever get through a fraction of it.
M: I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. You can't really have too much of it. It's just there, quietly waiting. Nothing is forcing you to open all of it.
W: Fair enough, but it does leave me feeling swamped before I've even started.
M: Well, here's what I would say. Digging out something decent takes proper technique. You have to know how to word a search, where to look, when to give up on a page.
W: Exactly, I agree with you there completely. Half the people in my office type in a whole sentence and then wonder why they get rubbish back.
M: Right. It's a skill like any other, and almost nobody sits down and teaches it.
W: Nobody teaches it at school either, which is odd.
M: Here's my bigger worry, though. I reckon all this has genuinely reshaped the way our minds work. We skim, we jump about, we never follow an argument through to the end any more.
W: I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. I'll accept that our habits have shifted, but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap. People were easily distracted long before any of this existed.
M: Hmm. I still think something has changed in here.
W: What I will say is that youngsters now have almost no tolerance for waiting. My nephew sighs if a video takes three seconds to load.
M: Oh, I completely agree with you on that one. I see it constantly at work. If a page doesn't open instantly, they've already given up and wandered off.
W: It's the on-demand culture, isn't it. Everything now, or not at all.

Key: Quá nhiều thông tin trên mạng = Woman · Tìm thông tin cần kỹ năng = Both · Internet ảnh hưởng cách ta suy nghĩ = Man · Internet khiến giới trẻ kém kiên nhẫn = Both
1. There is too much information on the Internet → Woman: Nữ nêu "there's simply far too much material sitting out there". Nam phản đối rõ: "I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. You can't really have too much of it."
2. Finding information on the Internet requires skills → Both: Nam nêu "Digging out something decent takes proper technique." Nữ tán thành: "Exactly, I agree with you there completely."
3. The use of the Internet affects the way we think. → Man: Nam nêu "I reckon all this has genuinely reshaped the way our minds work." Nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. I'll accept that our habits have shifted, but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap."
4. The Internet makes young people less patient. → Both: Nữ nêu "youngsters now have almost no tolerance for waiting". Nam tán thành: "Oh, I completely agree with you on that one."
👉 Mẹo: Bẫy nằm ở ý 3 — nữ nói "I'll accept that our habits have shifted" nghe như đồng ý, nhưng ngay sau đó bác bỏ kết luận ("but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap"), nên đáp án là Man chứ không phải Both.

question_text: Four people are talking about protecting the environment. Match each person to the correct information.

I take out what I need and leave the empty box by the door, and the next time the delivery comes, the driver collects the old one. The boxes are made from environmentally friendly material, so they're very easy to recycle. In the past I used to drive to the supermarket three or four times a week, so I'm sure this change helps in some way.

Speaker B: Water is something we all waste without thinking, and I decided I wanted to use less of it at home. The easiest change I made was in the bathroom. I used to fill the bath almost every evening, but now I take a shower instead. A shower is much quicker, and it uses far less water than a bath does. Clean water takes a lot of energy to treat and to pump into our homes, so saving it protects the environment as well as my bills.

Speaker C: My electricity bill used to be very high, but I've changed the way I live, mainly because most of our power still comes from burning fuel. I turn off all the lights whenever I go out, even if I'm only away for a short time. I also unplug the wifi before I go to bed every night. You may think these are small changes, but you'd be surprised. Less electricity used in my house means less pollution somewhere else.

Speaker D: The supermarket is just around the corner, so I walk there every day. I also live close to my office, and that makes a real difference. I don't have to drive to work; I cycle there every day instead. Cars are the main source of dirty air in this city, and short journeys are the worst of all. Since I stopped using my car for these trips, I hardly ever fill up the tank.

formalEmail.instruction: Write an email to the club manager. Write about your feelings and what you think the club should do. Write 120–150 words. Recommended time: 20 minutes.
formalEmail.sampleAnswer:
Dear Manager,

Thank you for your email about the group of foreign tourists who will soon visit our country. I was thrilled to read this news, as welcoming visitors is exactly why I joined the club, and I would be glad to help.

Yours sincerely,
[Your Name]

So I don't do anything complicated, like washing jars or recycling everything at home. The one thing I do manage to do is buy environmentally friendly food. When I'm on my way home from work, I usually stop at the shop and choose the greener option, even if it costs a little more. It's a small thing, but at least it's something I can do.

question_text: Four people are talking about listening to music. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My brother listens to music all the time — in the car, at work, even while he's cooking. I honestly don't know how he does it. For me, it's only after I wake up. Before I even get out of bed, I put on a few songs, and it helps me clear my head and get ready for the day. I never sing along, though. First, it's far too early, and second, my brother says I have a terrible voice. Once I've had breakfast and left the house, the music goes off until the next morning.
Speaker B: A lot of people like listening to music after they wake up, but I only listen when I'm studying. It helps me concentrate so much better — when I'm doing homework, and especially when I'm preparing for my final exams. I usually put my headphones on and focus as hard as I can. But it has to be music without any lyrics, like classical music. Songs with words just distract me.
Speaker C: I like pop music. I often listen to songs and pretend to be my favourite singers, singing along in my bedroom with a hairbrush as a microphone. People tell me I have a lovely voice, and that's exactly what I'm going to do: use my voice to express myself. Last month I joined a small choir at my college, and next year I'm planning to enter a singing competition. When I'm singing, I feel I can say things I could never say in normal words.
Speaker D: After a long day at school, nothing is more relaxing than listening to music and enjoying some time on my own. I usually lie on my bed, put on something slow and soft, and close my eyes. Within a few minutes, all the stress of the day just melts away. Sometimes I fall asleep before the playlist finishes, but I never put music on just to help me sleep — it's simply my way of switching off and calming down.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = After waking up: "For me, it's only after I wake up... it helps me clear my head and get ready for the day." Bẫy: A nhắc anh trai nghe nhạc "in the car" (không phải A) và nói "I never sing along" → không phải While singing.
B = While studying: "I only listen when I'm studying... when I'm preparing for my final exams." Bẫy: câu mở đầu "after they wake up" là thói quen của người khác.
C = While singing: "singing along in my bedroom... use my voice to express myself... When I'm singing, I feel I can say things..."
D = To relax: "nothing is more relaxing than listening to music... all the stress of the day just melts away... my way of switching off and calming down."
Nhiễu: While driving (chỉ anh trai của A nghe trong xe), Before going to bed (D có lúc ngủ quên nhưng "never put music on just to help me sleep").

The colour is wrong.

explanation:
W: Good morning. Can I help you with anything?
M: Yes, I'd like to exchange this jacket, please.
W: Oh, is there a problem with it? Is it faulty?
M: No, there's nothing wrong with the jacket.
W: Is the colour wrong?
M: No, the colour is exactly right, and there isn't any other problem with it. It's just that the arms feel a little uncomfortable when I wear it. It's a bit too tight around the arms, so I'd like to exchange it for another size.
W: Oh, I see. No problem. I'll help you find another size.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – The size is too tight.
• Vì sao đúng: Anh nói áo "a bit too tight around the arms" nên muốn đổi cỡ khác. Anh đã phủ nhận cả hai ý áo lỗi ("nothing wrong with the jacket") và sai màu ("the colour is exactly right").

question_text: A mother is calling her daughter. What time will she meet her daughter?
options: 2 o'clock
3 o'clock
4 o'clock
explanation:
Hi sweetheart, it's Mum. I'm sorry, but I don't think I can get to your school when classes finish at two. I have to go back to the office to finish my report first. I thought it might take me until four, but my manager says I can leave a bit earlier. So I'm going to meet you at three o'clock. Wait for me at the main door, OK? And call me back to let me know you're OK.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 3 o'clock.
• Vì sao đúng: "So I'm going to meet you at three o'clock. Wait for me at the main door".
• 2 o'clock sai: 2 giờ là giờ con tan học, mẹ nói không kịp đến lúc đó ("I don't think I can get to your school when classes finish at two").
• 4 o'clock sai: mẹ tưởng phải làm đến 4 giờ nhưng sếp cho về sớm hơn ("I thought it might take me until four, but...").
👉 Mẹo: nghe hết câu sau "but" và "So I'm going to..." — con số chốt luôn nằm sau từ nối.

question_text: What is the most important thing to help you sleep well?
options: Blocking noise and light is the key
Beds are best for sleeping
Resting sufficiently is necessary
explanation:
Let me begin this health talk with the question I am asked most: what is the single most important thing for a good night's sleep? People arrive with strong opinions. The furniture believers insist the bed is everything — invest in the perfect mattress and sleep will follow by itself. The common-sense camp simply says that resting enough is necessary, which is true but circular: telling a poor sleeper to rest more is like telling a poor swimmer to drown less. What the research actually crowns as most important is neither of these. It is blocking out noise and light. The sleeping brain monitors its surroundings all night, and every beam of light or burst of sound pulls it briefly toward waking. Seal the curtains, silence the notifications, and even an average mattress will serve you well. Comfort helps — darkness and quiet decide.
On insomnia, allow me to correct the record as well. It is not a condition caused only by physical health problems; anxiety, habits and irregular schedules cause at least as many sleepless nights as any illness. And the strange belief that insomniacs secretly sleep too much during the day is simply false — most get less rest in total, not more. What deserves everyone's attention is a quieter discovery: people cannot always recognise the symptoms of their own tiredness. The exhausted brain misreads its fatigue as restlessness, reaches for one more episode, one more scroll — and buries itself deeper in the very problem it cannot feel.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant thứ 4 của Sleep — options bộ Đề 03: Beds / Resting sufficiently.)
1. Đáp án: Blocking noise and light is the key. Bẫy: "beds are best" và "resting sufficiently is necessary" đều được nhắc rồi hạ ("neither of these").
2. Đáp án: People can't always recognize the symptoms of tiredness. Bẫy: "only physical health problems" và "sleep too much" đều bị bác.

question_text: Four people are talking about visiting a museum. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: I really enjoyed visiting the museum, especially because I'm quite interested in science and technology. There were so many different exhibitions that I wanted to see, from history and culture to modern inventions. However, I didn't want to spend too much time on the sections that weren't really my thing. I just had a quick look at some of them before moving on to the science and technology exhibitions that I was particularly interested in. There was so much to see that I knew I couldn't explore everything carefully in one visit.

Speaker B: I really enjoy visiting exhibitions and museums, so I was looking forward to seeing this one. Unfortunately, I had some problems with the organisation. The biggest issue was the map and the signs around the museum. I tried to follow the directions on the map, but I couldn't work out where the main entrance was. At one point, I thought I had finally reached it, but I realised that I was actually at another entrance. I kept checking the map and asking people for directions, but it took me almost the whole day to work out where I was supposed to go. Apart from that, I found the exhibition quite interesting.

Speaker C: I actually had quite an interesting experience at the museum. I lost my ticket before I arrived, so I had to go online and book another one. Fortunately, the museum has a really convenient website and a smartphone app where visitors can buy tickets easily. I also enjoyed some of the interactive games inside the museum. It was quite crowded, and I did get a little confused about where to go at first, but I could easily check the information on my phone. So, although there were a few small problems, I thought the technology made the whole visit much more convenient.

Speaker D: I was really impressed by the museum because there was such a wide range of things to learn about. I discovered a lot about history, science and society, and the exhibitions were much more impressive than I had expected. There were quite a lot of visitors when I went, so some areas were a little crowded and I sometimes had to wait to see certain displays. However, I didn't find the crowds too annoying because there was still plenty of space to explore at my own pace. In fact, I enjoyed the experience so much that I'd definitely like to come back when I have more free time. I think there are still many things I haven't had a chance to see.

Dạng sắp xếp câu: tìm câu mở đầu (không trỏ ngược), rồi bám vào đại từ, từ chỉ định và từ nối để nối dần.

  2. "It must include relevant pictures along with your own text about the topic." → "It must include" nói tiếp yêu cầu của dự án vừa nêu.
  3. "You will then use these pictures and your written work to create a presentation." → "these pictures and your written work" nhắc lại tranh ảnh và bài viết ở câu trước.
  4. "It should last about five minutes." → "It should last" nói về bài thuyết trình vừa được nhắc.
  5. "Afterwards, your classmates will have the opportunity to ask questions, and you will respond to them." → "Afterwards" là sau khi thuyết trình xong: bạn cùng lớp đặt câu hỏi.

▸ Music show at the park — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "Last Saturday there was a music show in the park." → câu cho sẵn.
  1. "The local authorities planned, sponsored and paid for everything." → "everything" chỉ toàn bộ buổi diễn ở câu cho sẵn; chính quyền tài trợ hết.

  3. "They came early and sat in nearby shops where they could see the performances." → "They" là 5.000 người vừa nhắc; họ đến sớm và ngồi trong các cửa hàng gần đó.
  4. "Although the staff had a busy day, they closed the shops early to watch the singer perform." → "the staff" là nhân viên của các cửa hàng ở câu trước.
  5. "The singer performed for two hours, and everyone had great fun." → Câu kết: ca sĩ biểu diễn 2 tiếng, mọi người đều vui.

Car ownership
Fires in the countryside
explanation:
Air pollution has been a hot topic on social media this week. Many people have blamed unusual atmospheric conditions, while others have pointed to the rising number of people who own cars. However, new satellite photos taken in the last few days show several hotspots in the countryside, where farmers have been burning their crops. Experts now say these fires are the root cause of the pollution in our city.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Fires in the countryside.
• Vì sao đúng: ảnh vệ tinh cho thấy nông dân đốt rơm rạ ở nông thôn và "Experts now say these fires are the root cause of the pollution".
• Atmospheric conditions sai: chỉ là điều "many people have blamed" — ý kiến trên mạng, bị bác bằng "However".
• Car ownership sai: cũng là ý kiến của "others", không phải kết luận của chuyên gia.
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi NGUYÊN NHÂN, ý kiến đám đông đứng trước "However" thường là bẫy; đáp án nằm ở kết luận của chuyên gia.

I've lived in my house for several years now, and I really like it because it's in a quiet area and quite close to my workplace. My old house has three bedrooms, which used to be enough when I lived alone. However, things have changed recently because I've got a child now. As you can imagine, we need more space for the family, so I started looking for a bigger place. After looking at several houses, I've finally found a new one. question_text: A man is calling a bakery. How many mini cakes are needed for the meeting?
explanation:
M: Hello, is this the bakery? I'd like to order some of your mini cakes for our meeting with a client this afternoon. I believe there will be four people at the meeting; however, I'm not sure whether they're bringing their assistants as well, so let's make it six mini cakes just to be safe. Could you deliver them by two o'clock?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án: 6. Người nói nhắc "four people" trước rồi tự sửa "let's make it six mini cakes just to be safe" — đáp án là con số ĐƯỢC CHỐT sau cùng.

extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Growing your own vegetables has quite a few benefits, and food safety is probably the biggest one. question_text: Jose is calling his friend about tomorrow. What will Luis and Emma bring?
options: Fruit
Food
Sleeping bags
explanation:
Hi, it's Jose here. Tomorrow I'm meeting Luis and Emma at the bus stop at five o'clock in the afternoon. They're going to bring the food, so we don't need to worry about lunch or dinner. Do you want to meet us there? If you can, come at about a quarter past five. After that, we can go and buy a few things we still need — some fruit for the journey, and maybe some water. And don't forget to bring your own sleeping bag, because it gets really cold at night. See you tomorrow!

question_text: What does she say about working at home?
options: There are no distractions
Not good as expected
Video calls are superior to face-to-face conversation
explanation:
Before I began working from home, I imagined paradise: no commute, no meetings that could have been emails, and above all, silence. I truly believed there would be no distractions once the chatting colleagues were gone. Reality re-educated me within a week. The distractions did not disappear; they changed uniform. The washing machine calls, the doorbell rings, the fridge whispers, and family members assume that being home means being available. As for video calls — useful, yes, but let nobody tell you they beat face-to-face conversation. Explaining a complicated problem through a frozen screen and a delayed microphone cured me of that idea permanently. So when friends ask for my honest verdict after a full year, I give them three words: not as expected. There are real advantages, but the dream and the reality live at different addresses.
Let me pass on what I have actually learned. First, forget the magazine photos — you do not need a big home office. My best work happens at a small desk in the corner of the bedroom. Second, do not believe anyone who says this lifestyle requires no self-motivation; with nobody watching, discipline is the entire game. And the biggest lesson: there is no universal answer. How well working from home goes depends on your situation and your personality. My neighbour thrives alone; I miss the noise of other humans. Learn which kind of worker you are — preferably before you sign anything.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 02 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: Not good as expected. Bẫy: "no distractions" ("changed uniform") và "video calls superior" ("cured me of that idea").
2. Đáp án: It depends on your situation and personality. Bẫy: "big home office" và "no self-motivation" đều bị phủ định.

question_text: Two friends are talking about a new apartment. What does the man find difficult about his new apartment?
options: The location
The neighbours
The rent
explanation:
W: How's the new apartment? You moved in last month, didn't you?
M: Yes, I moved closer to the city centre. It's far more convenient than my old place.
W: Wow, that's nice. The rent must be pretty expensive, though?
M: Actually, yes, rent around there is quite high. Luckily I know the landlord well and he let me have it at a much cheaper price.
W: So what's the problem?
M: The neighbours next door. They play loud music every night, and when I asked them to turn it down they were quite rude about it.
W: I see.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án: The neighbours. Location: "far more convenient" (tốt). Rent: đắt nhưng "he let me have it at a much cheaper price" (không phải vấn đề). Vấn đề thật: "The neighbours next door... play loud music... quite rude".

question_text: Two colleagues are talking about a new job. What does the man love about his new job?
options: The slower pace
The shorter journey
The work itself

W: So how's the new job going?
M: Well, I was used to the hectic pace at my old place, and the heavy workload made me really stressed. This new place is calmer, which is fine, and the work itself is OK.
W: What's the best thing about it, then?
M: The journey. It only takes me twenty minutes to get there now. I enjoy it, and my daughter loves it too, because I can drop her at school and still get to work on time every day.

question_text: A woman is talking about a town. What is the population of the town?
explanation:
This small town has a population of around ten thousand people. Twenty years ago, only about eight thousand people lived here, and many visitors still guess that it's around nine thousand. But it has grown a lot. It has many shops and a train station, which some big towns don't even have. It's a lovely place to live.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 10,000.
• Vì sao đúng: "This small town has a population of around ten thousand people".
• 8,000 sai: là dân số 20 năm trước ("Twenty years ago, only about eight thousand people lived here").
• 9,000 sai: chỉ là con số du khách đoán ("many visitors still guess that it's around nine thousand").
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi CON SỐ, gắn mỗi số với mốc thời gian/người nói — số hiện tại mới là đáp án.

question_text: A woman is talking about a family holiday. Where is she going to go?

The lakes

John wants to walk in the park, but I want to go to the mountains, and John is happy with that. So that's where we're going. I hope there'll be a river for the children to swim in.

question_text: Jack is calling his friend. What colour is Jack's house?
options: Red
White
Green
explanation:
Hi, it's Jack. I'm calling to let you know that my family has just moved to a new house. Now I live much closer to you, so we can meet up any time. The house is on White Street. There are lots of big houses in this area, but ours is quite small. Don't look for the green door — that's our neighbour's. You can easily find our house because it's red.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Red.
• Vì sao đúng: "You can easily find our house because it's red".
• White sai: "White" là tên đường ("The house is on White Street"), không phải màu nhà.
• Green sai: cửa màu xanh là nhà hàng xóm ("Don't look for the green door — that's our neighbour's").
👉 Mẹo: màu sắc có thể xuất hiện trong tên riêng (White Street) — đừng chọn chỉ vì nghe thấy từ đó.

question_text: A man is talking about a coffee shop. What does the customer complain about?
options: The wifi was too slow
The coffee was cold
The shop was too noisy
explanation:
I visited a coffee shop yesterday hoping to spend a few hours working on my laptop. Everything seemed perfect at first — the drinks tasted great, and the place was quiet enough to concentrate. The only problem was the internet. The wifi was incredibly slow, making it almost impossible to join an online meeting or download documents. Even the staff apologised and explained that several customers had experienced the same issue. Because of that, I probably won't return for work anytime soon.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án: The wifi was too slow. Cà phê "tasted great" và quán "quiet enough" → loại A, C. "The only problem was the internet. The wifi was incredibly slow".

question_text: A woman is asking a colleague about some work. Why can't the man finish the work today?
options: He has another appointment.
He doesn't have a colleague to work with.

explanation:
W: Are you able to finish the work today?
M: I'm afraid I can't.
W: Why not? Do you have another appointment?
M: No, that's not the reason. I'm just really busy today.
W: Are you short of someone to work with?
M: Right. One of my colleagues is absent today, so I have to do all the work by myself.
W: I see. That explains it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – He doesn't have a colleague to work with.
• Vì sao đúng: "One of my colleagues is absent today, so I have to do all the work by myself." Anh phủ nhận lý do có hẹn khác ("No, that's not the reason").

question_text: A mother is talking to her son about school. What subject does her son like studying?
